Midterms were difficult. Readings were typically alright, some were pretty good. Drops a good amount of your lowest scores on assignments which is nice.

American Heritage is really not about the professor but just yourself. He has a big study guide that helps a lot. He also gives prefecture videos( 5-10min) and 2 quizzes a week 1 lab a week. The midterms are harder than the material so just study. He is pretty funny and his lectures are pretty good

While Wilson was an alright professor, his course structure was horrendous. American Heritage is needlessly difficult for a first-year GE class. Most of the knowledge required for midterms came from the countless readings he assigned. Going to lectures felt like a waste of time, since most midterm questions were centered around the many readings.

The TA's really make or break this class. My TA was very unhelpful, so it was more challenging than it would have been. If you honestly do the 4 hours of reading and studying every night. You might pass. The lectures, reading, and tests did not really align with each other, so it was kind of pointless to prepare for tests. Do not take this class.

The lectures were very boring, tests were hard, and there was a lot of reading. There are NO study guides for the tests, so make sure you study the pre-lectures, lecture slides, textbook, and quiz questions (some test questions are copy-paste the quiz questions). The second-chance grading saved my grade, and there was a good curve at the end.

American Heritage sucks, but you might as well take it from Professor Wilson. No problems with him, the course, in general, is just awful. Lab assignments, SO MUCH reading, weekly quizzes, and difficult midterms and final. Just pray you get a good TA that reviews info well and provides study guides. There is a nice curve at the end for exams.

Honestly, I'm sure Professor Wilson is a great professor. My main complaint comes with the course. American Heritage has been a mandatory class at BYU for ages now and I don' think anyone know why. Readings can be really long and the lectures are super boring. Pray you get a good TA that covers the lecture materials well in your weekly lab.

Solid professor. Lots of reading and out of class material, but if you read it all and take notes you will do well. Tests are medium hard, but there is a great curve at the end of the class. He's a good lecturer as well, so class is fun.

Probably your best option for American Heritage professor. He does not require a lot of extra work or projects or anything, just 11 short lab assignments. Course structure is a little confusing at first, and test can be hard to study for, but overall a really good class. Lectures are pretty interesting.

Professor Wilson hasn't taught this class in almost 3 years and I can see why. Readings done on your own & barely uses any of that content in the lectures. The lectures hardly relate to the test and his tests are very detail oriented based off of specific readings and minute details you have to remember. I recommend anyone but him for this class.

All grading is done by TAs which is normally an issue, but they normalize it all with a curve at the end of the semester. My class's was a 3-4% curve, but it changes every semester. Prof Wilson did a great job of teaching the material and mad lectures entertaining and applicable to the course. Great choice for AHTG, gotta work for the A though.

Personally for me, I did not find American Heritage to be extremely difficult like everyone says. I found that most of those people who think its hard are usually from school systems where grades are extremely inflated. They expect As from minimal effort, which is not the way it works here. It's a manageable class and Wilson is a good choice!

Wilson is the way to go! (He only teaches in fall FYI) Less reading material, no papers: only short (250 words) weekly writing assignments. If you do the reading, memorize the study guide, study with other people, and make use of your TA, youll do great. The TAs are very helpful - attend the review sessions as often as possible.

Dr. Wilson gives amazing lectures. They are very unbiased and I had no idea what his political orientation was until he told us. I have never really liked history, but Dr. Wilson made it engaging and relatable. Tests are hard and there's a lot of reading, but the final grade is very heavily curved. TA reviews are very helpful.

He played funny clips that went along with the material as long as The Story of Us type videos, all of which was nice. He cares about the topic. American Heritage sucks, but Wilson at least knows what he's talking about and puts forth clear effort in making it enjoyable and useful.

I went into the course with a positive attitude. The material was interesting but the class was mostly a disappointment. Dr. Wilson didnt do anything to make it better. He has his theories of what makes a class fair but I do not agree with them. Good guy, just needs to be more aware of students and think of better ways to meet dept. requirements.

American Heritage is a brutal class but I would pick Wilson. This class is pretty hard and most of what you are graded on is not on the lecture but rather in the study guide and the textbook. The study guide the reviews are talking about is this 150 pg pamphlet with the bulk of what you need to know which is really helpful and exclusive to Wilson.

American Heritage is the worst, but if you have to take it, I guess this prof is okay to take it from. The exams consist of a combination of lectures, supplemental reading, and textbook stuff never discussed in class. I also thought his lectures got a bit dry at times, but maybe that's just because I don't care for history.

American Heritage is a brutal course to begin with but Sven makes it bearable. He is funny and inspirational in lectures. He does share his views a lot but he is good about it. I would recommend taking this class from him.

I did not like Dr. Wilson for American Heritage. He is extremely political and loves to share his views. I had a hard time with him sometimes because he acts like his beliefs are doctrine. It doesn't matter what your political beliefs are, I don't think teachers should share them, & he did like every class. Save yourself and don't take it from him.

I really enjoyed learning the material in this class and lecture was very interesting. However, I feel that this class does not accurately measure your knowledge as the tests felt like a game I did not know how to play. I attended every lecture, completed all reading assignments, and studied hours every week... and was left very discouraged.

Great professor, very difficult class. Lectures are interesting but the amount of information needed to be successful on exams felt impossible. I did all the readings, studied hours a week, and still did poorly on exams. This class seems like it was made harder than it needed to be.

I loved Professor Wilson's lectures and teaching style! American Heritage is a difficult class, but if you take it from anyone I would take it from him. The homework amount is reasonable, and the class is completely doable if you study hard and keep up with the readings. He compiles all of the lectures into a study guide, which is great!!

I would avoid taking American Heritage at all if you could avoid it. Professor Wilson is good, but the class is not worth it if you can find other things to fill the credit. It is overly difficult for a GE class taken primarily by freshmen. The tests are ridiculously difficult and designed to make you do poorly.

Dr. Wilson is very knowledgeable; however, AHTG is a difficult class. There is a lot of reading, and most his tests come from the readings. Review sessions will be your best friend. Also, he has you buy a packet with all his slides in it from lecture, super helpful! He is the only AHTG professor I know who does this.

Professor Wilson is the best American Heritage professor at BYU. His lectures are extremely entertaining. I am not kidding when I say he has the most organized class and syllabus of any I've seen at BYU. It is very clear what you need do to get an A. If you work, you get an A. This class is not that hard.

There was a lot of reading to do before each lecture, but less than Pope's class. The tests were equally weighted based on the readings and the lectures. Attendance is required, but he also provided a study guide with everything we went over in class that helped for studying. He isn't the best lecturer, but I liked how he showed videos.

This class is tough but doable. Study in groups, do all the reading, ask questions during lecture and lab and keep an open mind. The tests are ALL application based which was the hardest part (for me). The last midterm average was 71% for my section. It's definitely not easy. Take from Wilson! (I've heard Pope is good too). Final grade is curved.

American Heritage has been my least favorite class I have yet to take. I dont believe its Prof. Wilsons fault, but more of how the class has been organized over the years at BYU (I'm not sure how other prof. are ). Tests are extremely difficult and his lectures are all over the place. He does although provide a study guide, which is nice.

Take from Wilson, he's a great teacher. Shows lots of cool videos. Unlike others, he gives you a study guide, which has EVERYTHING you need to know. Go to the TA sessions, they grade your papers, so get their advice. Midterms were difficult, but the final was easier. MAKE SURE you get the concepts at the beginning, they're used the entire semester.

Professor Wilson is a solid choice for an american heritage professor. You will need to work for your grade but that is the case with any AmHer class. He does a great job of keeping lecture interesting and has weekly labs that help you apply what you've learned. He also provides a study guide that really helps on tests. It's really not that bad.

Wilson is the best AHTG100 teacher at BYU. It probably won't be you're easiest class, as you will have to go to class, and do the readings, and attend the labs if you want to get an A. It's a fair amount of work, but if you have to take the class, you will be less stressed and unhappy if you take Wilson as opposed to one of the other professors.

Honestly, take American Heritage from him. He's the easiest. No papers, just a little 300 word writing assignment a week. Weekly quizzes on reading and lecture. Don't get behind on reading. Tests are on lecture, lab, and reading. They can be hard, but if you really go over lecture and reading and make sure you understand everything, you're golden.

Avoid him if you can. I went to lecture, read the chapters, went to the review room at least 3 times a week and still did poorly on his tests. If you are not a good test taker then do not take from him. This was my least favorite class this semester, a whole lot of studying only to be tested on bogus things randomly from lecture.

Professor Wilson is probs the best professor to take American Heritage from! His lectures are always interesting (once he auctioned off a box of donuts!) and the subject itself is very interesting. If you do all your reading (no, not skimming) you will do good. I was scared to take this class, but it turned out to be my favorite class this semester

I was afraid to take this class because I had heard so many bad things about it. American Heritage with Professor Wilson turned out to be my favorite class this semester! Yes, you have to read a lot and study hard to do well on the tests, but he keeps the lectures really interesting. He is such a great person and I looked forward to going to class.

I really enjoyed this class from Professor Wilson. There are a lot of people ready to scare you about taking American Heritage, but if you do the readings, attend class pretty frequently, and go to the review room about once a week, you will do just fine. Wilson's lectures were really good and used a lot of multi-media stuff. Take him!

Professor Wilson is a really nice person, but his class is what it is. You really have to study to do well on tests (especially test #2). Interesting lectures, lots of videos. Careful of your TA because labs can be graded pretty harshly. iClicker quizzes every class period for attendance. Between Pope or Wilson, choose Wilson. quizzes are tough.

This class has a reputation for being difficult. It is. It isn't this guy's fault. He is passionate about what he teaches and it shows. This class was the most consistently fair, transparent, and useful class I took this year. Wilson is so happy to help you, and curves generously on his tests, which are admittedly difficult. Take him!

Honestly this is my least favorite class and the professor does not help. His tests are ridiculous because he wants to get a good curve. It is very frustrating because unless you can memorize 6+ chapters of the textbook, all of his lectures, and the additional readings its impossible. Svenny is the worst! Dont be fooled by his fun name!

I loved learning American Heritage from Dr. Wilson. He was very passionate and informed about the topics he covered which made lectures enjoyable. It is a work heavy class and you have to really understand the concepts in order to pass the tests. However, since it's a required class I would recommend taking it from Wilson.

Seriously Svenny is so hard!! He gives a ton of reading assignments and on the second midterm created questions from specific sentences in the textbook he knew a majority of the class would miss. He's actually a pretty nice guy, I think, but not very considerate when it comes to tests. SO rude honestly, avoid if you can ppl.

Svenny is the worst! I did poorly on the first two midterms so I went into his office asking what I could do to improve for the final and he basically said welcome to BYU people are smart here. You shouldnt be upset being average or just below. He does not care for the individual student or if they are learning anything. Only cares about his curve
Lots of reading, and tests are very difficult, but he is a great professor who made me enjoy what we were learning about! Definitely doable, but not an easy A unless you work really hard

American Heritage is going to be a hard class regardless of who you take, so yes this class was hard.  But the work load is NOTHING compared to other ahtg professors.  I loved professor wilsons lectures, and he often brought us sugar and fun treats for holidays.  Labs are great, go to those.  Take american heritage from prof wilson for sure!!!
He is really kind and passionate about what he teaches. Always has a positive attitude and you know what to expect from him. Good choice for obligatory class.

Brother Wilson is a great teacher! He was VERY generous with grades (especially curves on tests). There were scriptures we had to kind of memorize for tests, mostly just fill in the bank, but he gave us a study guide with them on there! So easy. Take this class!

I really liked the class. It was his first time teaching it and he was well prepared. I especially liked that he used present day examples to illustrate how the constitution applied today or how we still have places we can improve. He is an economics guy, so there was also some of that in class, esecially how it relates to the founding and ao now.

He has never taught BOM before and it was pretty obvious. This class was based on his opinions and hardly on the text in the book. His tests were difficult in the sense that he tested to his opinions and makes you memorize useless scriptures to do well. Not the best religion teacher
He's an amazing professor.  He went to Chicago for his PhD in Economics so he's been well trained and he's battled with the best of 'em.

Great teacher, I learned a lot about philosophy and how to live life. She is great at teaching and we had fun days where we would go to the duck pond if weather was nice enough. You can see the love she has for this subject.

This was my favorite class I've taken at byu, Sydney is the best, and I loved going to class everyday. You might never expect a general credit to be that great, but I'm so glad I took this class, it changed my life honestly.

Lectures were awesome. I loved the topics that we went over! I was always excited for class every day. There is a good amount of reading, but it's all interesting stuff and the most you usually do with it is have class discussions. Professor Ballif is amazing!

Professor Ballif is a great teacher. This online class was very organized, and it was always clear what was expected. The structure of the course made a difficult subject much more manageable. There were helpful support resources, including extra credit opportunities, which made a big difference in learning and performance.

Sydney is the apple of my eye. She cares for other people so deeply it's inspiring. It's amazing how engaging her lectures are. She is one of a kind. She is passionate about the world, especially love. In fact, she's an expert at it. Every time I went to her class, I left feeling inspired and motivated to dig into the material!
Kind, smart, funny, passionate, loving and an excellent teacher. As a both a graduating and transfer student, I can fully say that is the best instructor you will EVER have.
Wow. Speechless. Would follow her to the ends of the earth—the embodiment of pasión and all that is good in the world. Standing ovation was well deserved.

No words I could ever write here could begin to or properly express how much I love Syndey. Syndey is one of God's greatest gifts to humankind. Take ANY AND EVERY class she offers. Your life will forever be changed. 10/10, would adopt.

Sydney is, without a doubt, the highlight of my college experience. Every minute spent in her class was enriching. Sydney teaches with contagious passion and profound wisdom. The principles she taught resonated with me in a way I had never experienced in the classroom. Taking IHUM 202 with Sydney will change your life for the better, trust me.

I would never recommend taking her class.

Do not take 133 from Sylvia if you want any creative freedom. She makes you approve your plans for your projects, but I lost track of how many times she told me “no” to various ideas. Her assignments are super weird and too specific. She never gives 100s. Her expectations are unclear and impossible to meet. I know many other students feel the same.
Sylvia is a super great teacher! She has great creative feedback and is willing to work with you in tough circumstances. If you can take a 3D Art class from her, do it!

Too much work for only 1/2 a semester class. Felt rushed to finish projects instead of focusing on making them look good. Randomly grades easy on some projects and hard on others. There are 15 girls 1 professor and 1 tool for each thing you want to do. Almost impossible to work productively during class. Shes nice but pretty boring lecturer.

His class is amazing! Very chill and he doesn't just teach the language, but he teaches the Samoan culture as well! If you want to learn a language and get an easy 4 credit hours, this is the class for you! Usually not many students, so you can develop a personal relationship with him too! Great class!
He does his best to help you get a good grade, learn, and love samoan. Loved his class! Only regret was that I didn't take it earlier.

Honestly the easiest class I've taken so far. He explains things well during class and will go through the content again if you don't understand. He cares for his students and is patient. There is usually a quiz every week which he never fails to remind and prep us for. Homework isn't too hard and he preps you well for the final!

I LOVED this class. The class was honestly super laid back and chill. By far one of my easiest classes this semester and you don't have to stress at all. The homework load is super light and the tests and quizzes are super easy. There is also a lot of extra credit opportunity so no need to stress about your grade.

Brother Lesa is an AMAZING professor! Hes by far the easiest class Ive had this semester while at the same time having a moderate amount of homework. He explains everything thoroughly and always asks for questions. His extra credit is recording yourself a month apart saying prayer in Samoan. Theres assignments every class, but do more than need.

Brother Lesa is the best teacher ever! This is the easiest class you will ever take at BYU. I would recommend taking this class every semester. It's also really fun to learn about the Samoan culture and language. Brother Lesa is so funny. I always leave feeling uplifted and happy.

Absolutely loved learning Samoan with Professor Lesa. His ability to explain the language grammar clearly helped me excel in this class, as well as the wealth of information he had readily available about the language and culture. I am not a native speaker, and the classroom environment helped me feel really comfortable about practicing speaking.
Ta'au is so laid back. He teaches what students want to learn. The homework load isn't tough and assignments are easy and help your grade. Kuga'i is delicious
Ta'au is amazing! Learned tons in the vasega and there's a food party before mid-term and final. Take this if you have to take a language and get your Math GE done too. Easy A
He is a great teacher and everyone enjoys his class. Manaia le mafutaga o tagata e tautala faaSamoa i lenei vasega.
He is such an amazing professor! I absolutely loved his class
So kind and caring!!! Very easy A.

This was my last religion class, and I am SO grateful that Prof Welty was my last professor! Seriously, this class strengthened my testimony on eternal families and God's plan. I don't think this would have been my experience if I had taken any other professor. Super fun lectures and inspired discussions.

Brother Welty is the best! He is super nice and the classes are very spiritual. Also, reading was a very reasonable amount. He's usually a seminary teacher so I think that's why he's so caring and chill. There was lots of good opportunities to participate and learn from each other in class. He also invited us over for conference and cinnamon rolls.

This was the last religion class I took at BYU, and I am SO grateful I took it from Brother Welty. Every moment of his class was so filled with the Spirit. We had two 30-day reading challenges that were not too hard, and they changed how I read my scriptures. He honestly was the best religion professor I have had at BYU. 100% recommend!

Dr. Smith is amazing. He cares deeply about music and wants to create beauty and a spiritual experience for everyone involved. He made music meaningful for me again! If you are on the fence about auditioning for the symphony, I highly recommend doing it. Be brave; you will not regret it!

Dr. Smith is an OUTSTANDING conductor, professor, and disciple. I was in the Symphony Orchestra and was wowed by the constant focus on the Savior and our personal refinement, as people and as musicians. He puts his whole soul in the music. AWESOME class!

Dr. Smith is an amazing conductor! Absolutely loved being a part of his orchestra. He leads with care and wants to help us produce amazing music. Right before concerts can understandably be a little more stressful, but the reward for working hard and listening pays off. Always looked forward to rehearsals with him!

Dr. Smith is so talented at conducting and describing music! Lots of rehearsal time/1.5hrs a week of practice (for strings) for only a 1 credit class. Assignments inlcude listening to the pieces, attending 1 sectional per concert, personal practice, and sometimes a recorded playing test. Music was challenging for me but this was my favorite class!

I love dad
-Gabriel
If you love music you will love this class. You have to listen to the music, practice, and go to class, but I loved the class. The music is hard tho, so you actually have to put in time to learn it.
I love Dr. Smith. You can tell he really loves his job and cares for the students. He does fun music and answers emails really fast. Highly recommend taking this class if you love music!

Dr. Smith is fun to work with. He is passionate about music and knows how to apply the music past the classroom. He will not tolerate phones and talking, so if you aren't able to be respectful, don't take this class. You are required to listen to the music, practice 1 hr every week, have two sectionals per concert.
This is a great class. Don't feel scared if you aren't a music major, you'll do well if you put in some practice. For a music instructor, he has a calm demeanor and was very inspiring.
Excellent musician and conductor. Will get stressed and frustrated if you don't prepare-- he can tell.

He's very passionate about music, and it's only polite to express appreciation for the passion. So don't goof around in class, and he will like you! He likes everyone. He's so nice and patient. He does kind of make a big deal out of the strings being important and everyone else not so much, which makes me kind of upset as a horn player. But oh well

Dr. Smith is an amazing person.  I don't think it is possible for him to get mad and he expects the bests from everybody.  The amount of patience he has in incredible and he respects all of his students.  Playing under him is a great experience.

Dr. Smith is a phenomenal conductor. He's one of the kindest people I've met and I would take another class from him in a heartbeat. (I took symphony orchestra). There was not a day of class that he was rude to us or that e took his anger out on us, and we were even stuck in a pit with him for 3+ hours every day. Dr. Smith is AWESOME.

He is such a good teacher. I don't think it is possible for this guy to lose his temper b/c he was always very chill in class and very respectful towards everyone. Loved learning conducting from him. I'd recommend anyone to take a class from him b/c he was one of the nicest teachers I've ever had at B.Y.U.
What a great guy! Band was awesome with this Dr. Smith. Likes to laugh, compliments a lot--one of my favorite professors.
This is a great class.  It's a little frustrating at first, but as you get into it, the class gets really fun.  Prof. Smith really knows what he is doing, and you learn a lot.

Fun class. It is hard if you have any conducting experience prior to this class, you will feel like you are conducting in a straight jacket. Just go with an open mind, and have fun. Bro. Smith is a lot of fun, and makes the class interesting, most of the time.

This was an online Marriage Prep class. I loved what I learned and will definitely use it throughout my life! I love that it teaches about dating but honestly focuses more on personal development and growth (including perfectionism, time management, financial principles, communication, etc.) There was a lot of reading but none of it was hard!

She was kind; even though lectures were pre recorded from a different professor, she was involved in weekly updates. The class was amazing and very do-able, and if I could do one thing differently it would be to get to know Tamara better.
Professor Chamberlain is very caring, and provides a lot of different and interesting ways to learn about the subject in an online class! Tests were not hard, and neither were assignments.

The layout of the online class was very easy to follow and the professor was helpful with clarifying class content and deadlines! Grading was not super strict but up to a good standard. I enjoyed the class content and the activities used to practice the concepts!

Our professor is very good at talking about hard topics that may be uncomfortable. She also shared many stories that were very inspiring. She has a lot of expertise in the field of family/ marriage/ sexual relationships.

The material in this class was very insightful, and I felt I was learning applicable information. This was an online course I took over the spring semester, and it was fairly easy. The only challenging part of the class was the Exams. You have to actually put a decent amount of preparation into each exam to get a good grade.
She was cool! Lots to learn highly recommend. The class taught me a lot about marriage, and everything that comes with finding your eternal companion. It was awesome.
not willing to work with you even with months' notice. the exams are super nit-picky too. Not a bad course, just not my favorite.
This was a pretty easy and good class overall, but exams were very long and a lot of written response which took forever and they were super specific questions which made it worse.

This was a good class that I was able to learn from. If you are taking it in the spring or summer, just keep in mind that it really is an accelerated course because of the length of the semesters. All in all, I liked the course.

I think that a lot of the activities were well thought out and creative, it was nice to have a lot of different styles of things to do to help break up the usual class routine. I also liked how the course was a lot about developing and being comfortable with yourself so you can become the best partner you can be in marriage.

The content of this class was very good, and I think everyone should take this class! However, alot of the assignments were not helpful in learning and just a big time waster. I would take this class if you're getting married or need an elective, while theres a fair ammount of work its on the low end for BYU.
The course is super easy to navigate and flows well.
Didn't love her lectures. Felt like they took forever. She does this thing called Snazzy Sucess Points which in my mind is a complete waste of time.

She always responded quickly to my emails and helped anytime I had a question. The lectures are prerecorded from another professor, but I loved the content. Tests can get long with lots of short answer questions.

Professor Chamberlain was a great professor. She had a lot to say about the different topics that weren't necessarily important, but it was good to know. I took her online course in the spring term so there was more work than usual but I was able to stay on top of it. The workload wasn't too bad either.
I took this online, it was a very easy class. The only issues I saw were obscure assignment due dates.
Great class, it will help you become a better and more well rounded people if you act on the invitations.

This course was amazing. Dr. Chamberlain had some videos she would post to check in with us, and her TAs were amazing. Dr. Chelom Levitt was the one leading the lectures online, and they were very insightful! I would definitely recommend this course!

This was a great class with lots of amazing material. I learned so much in this course that I am excited to apply! The exams were pretty hard, so just make sure that you pay attention to details as you read, but the TAs in her class were super helpful. She does include extra credit and it was a pretty fun class overall!

Tamara is incredibly sweet, faithful, and genuinely cares about her students. The class is very easy with no exams and a light workload. There are optional readings if you want to learn more, and she offers extra credit opportunities throughout the semester. She does take attendance, so be sure to show up. Great professor overall!
This class was great but was a lot for an online class. Several weekly videos that were very long. Also the tests were simple but looked for word for word long explanations.

Professor Thomson is super funny and will often go on tangents about random things. She does a pretty decent job at explaining writing concepts but it does feel very rushed most days. Lots of essays in this class and she is a really tough essay grader but she is super lenient about due dates and essay requirements (# of pages, sources, etc.).

Professor Thomson is one of the best teachers I have ever had! She is very clear about the material, and truly cares about her students and their success. She makes class fun and can always make a hard day lighter. I would recommend her to anyone! She is the best! Take her class, you wont regret it!!

As far as Creative Writing goes, this was the easiest class I took. Her grading was easy, she's incredibly accepting, and the two books we had to buy for the year I didn't even need to open. The only issue is she didn't really teach anything and it seemed like she didn't want to be there. A few adult jokes here and there. Lightweight class.
She's awesome! Loved the writing exercise reviews! she's so funny haha.

Tamara is fantastic. She cares deeply about her students and the material. She is very fair and lenient. There are a decent amount of papers, but it's a writing class and I honestly didn't stress too much about this class and learned a lot. She is open about her politics but not pushy and is understanding of others. Would recommend her to everyone.

Tamara is very kind, and shows that she truly cares about her students personally, as well as their success. I wouldn't take this class if you're sensitive to political topics, as she does like to have discussions and papers occasionally related to some controversial topics. There is a textbook, but the author makes witty jokes, so it's a fun read.

This teacher is very harsh on grading. You will have to buy a text book, the essays are graded by how well the sentences link together, not the essay as a whole. She does cancel class for the week to work on the essay. Like everything there are certain bonuses. I would not take her class, but instead take it from another teacher if you can.
Tamara was amazing! If you have the option to take from her, I would 10/10 recommend. She gives great feedback but also respects you as a writer.

Tamara really cares about her students. She is effective in explaining writing topics and helpful over email when you have questions or comments. She can be political in class. There are three main writing papers that make up your grade, but she is a fair grader. For your last project you make a meme with another class member!!

Tamara is the bomb! She is so good at helping all her students to understand what we can do better and is very considerate of us. She wants to help everyone accomplish their goals and get the results they're working for. She's super fun and made class a positive experience.
He's pretty cool. By far the easiest class I've taken at BYU

Professor Eastmond is a kind professor. I appreciated his ability to integrate spiritual insights and prayer into the beginning of each session. His commitment to his faith was evident throughout his instruction. While this course is inherently challenging, he was deeply invested in the success of his students, offering support and accessibility.

One of the best professors I've had at BYU. If you have to take ECON 388, take it from Professor Eastmond. He explains concepts really well in class and is very willing to spend office hours helping to prep for exams (highly recommend taking advantage). The class is very manageable if you consistently review and understand the homework.

Dr. Eastmond is the GOAT. Turned a tough class into something super manageable and eye-opening--he has a GIFT for teaching simply. He's invested in all his students and wants them to succeed. He even knew everyone's name on day one and always addressed students by their name. Take 388 from him, you will be so glad you did!
I'm by no means intelligent and he made this class possible. Take it from him 100%, one of God's greatest gifts.

Dr. Eastmond is a newly minted PhD that did well at teaching very thoroughly the principles of 388 - this class will be a lot of work but I wouldn't hesitate to take this class from him if you're looking for the right professor to take it from.

Dr. Eastmond is an extremely good professor. Either 388 isn't as hard as people say or he's just that good. That being said, it'll be tough if you don't go to class. He has a gift at explaining difficult concepts and really wants to help students succeed. Practice exams are super similar to exams, so that was a plus.

By far the best econ professor at BYU. Lectures were super clear and very easy to understand. He made a hard class very enjoyable and a lot easier by clearly explaining everything. His goal is to help you learn and understand so he is always available to help and answer questions. Tests were very fair and he prepares you well for them.

I am not exaggerating when I say Dr. Eastmond is the best professor I've had in my whole BYU experience to this point. He has a gift for teaching concepts to the level of complexity you need while making it crystal clear. He is higher energy and engaging in lecture and is very fair and grounded in his approach to pretty much everything. 11/10.

An excellent professor, really knows his stuff and presents the material well. ECON 388 is hard but he will give you all the support you need. Try your very best not to miss class because everything builds on past lectures and catch-up is difficult. You've got this!

If I could give him a 6/5 rating I would. Econ 388 is brutal, but he made it genuinely fun and interesting. Incredible lecturer, truly good person. He assigns a lot of work, but no more than is necessary for you to learn the material. He is firm but fair. I cannot recommend him enough. Also try to get a group to work with for the data projects.

Dr. Eastmond is one of the very best! You can tell that he cares a lot about the class. Even though 388 is challenging material, he was really good about checking for understanding so I always felt like my questions got answered. He was really good at responding to questions I emailed as well. Seriously I can't recommend him enough! He's incredible

This is a really tough class, but Dr. Eastmond is incredible. From day 1, you can feel that he cares about each of his students. He is very responsive to questions over email and in class. Applies feedback quickly on things like class structure and test preparation. Helped me appreciate the value of good data and sound models. Super funny and kind.
Skousen walks you through every assignment in class so I would recommend going. He makes the hour enjoyable and both him and his TA's are very helpful!

I LOVE HIMMMMMMMMMM Super kind guy and easy class. You don't need to attend class, but you only have one assignment a week and he gives you the answers in class, so I would say go. Only downside is the textbook you need is $100...

His love of Excel is infectious. He explains things really well. Attendance is not required. But since he goes through the week's homework step-by-step, I would go and use the classtime to just do my homework. And then I would always get 100%!

Super chill, only went to class the first day, the rest of the course was pretty self explanatory. Do the practice examples before the graded assignments. You could knock this course out in 2 weeks at the beginning of the semester if you wanted. AI is helpful if you get stuck.

Professor Skousen is super funny and patient and helpful. Easiest class I've ever taken. Class is literally just a walkthrough of the homework for the week, and you can use AI on the homework and the final. Completely your fault if your don't get an A.

I think I spent a total of 5 minutes per 2 weeks on this class outside of class. Love this man to death and the class was actually super insightful and helpful! Loved his silly stories and getting to do spreadsheets with him. What a phenomenal experience.
He is so fun! If you ever struggle with the homework go to class and you will get the help you need! I did most of the homework outside of class and only went if I needed help! Awesome professor!

Prof Skousen is the most genuine person I've ever met. He wants all of his students to do well and it shows. Loved the format of his class, it let students go at their own pace. He played more of a supplemental role for anyone who needed help which was great. Would 150% recommend him for any course

Professor Skousen is the best. He is funny, caring and teaches the class well. Easiest class i've taken here. If you go to class, he literally gives you the homework for the week. On the tests you can use notes and past homeworks.
Awesome guy, great teacher. Explains simply and directly. Class is formatted in a way that helps you retain knowledge.

Class is just him going through the weekly assignments step by step so you always get 100%. Tests are open note, open AI so also easy. Skousen made class fun, he will sing to you every once in a while. He makes up songs about information systems. Not sure how many of the skills I retained long term but getting the credit was nice!
Hes a guy that likes to laugh, and have fun, but with time he will get the job done.

He is a very nice guy and the class is super easy, there is no homework outside of going to class besides the midterm and final which take 2-3 hours each. His lectures are very slow paced though and he talks a little like Dora the Explorer but they are worth not having any homework for the week. Very nice guy. Take it

He explained things very well in his lectures, and his energy helped me feel excited about something I never really enjoyed before. Attendance wasn't mandatory, but each week he went over the homework assignment with the class so it was very easy to get a good grade with him.

I would recommend either 1) completing this class before school starts because everything is online and accessible from day one or 2) attending class. If you go to class, Skousen will go through the work entirely in class and you will not have homework (except for the midterm and final). Lectures are super fun and give you useful shortcuts.
Very useful information to know and attendance is optional. Exams aren't too bad since they're open note.

This class was originally a little overwhelming because I had no idea how to use excel. Once I warmed up, it was predictable and I enjoyed the problem solving aspect of the lessons. This professor is very warm and welcoming. It is set up for you to learn how to do it at home, then do the assignment in class. The class isn't time intensive.
Effortless class. The assignments were completed during the weekly lecture. Dr. Skousen is funny, friendly, and real. IS 110 is a great class to take regardless of major.
Super easy A and I rarely went to class! Awesome guy!

If you don't get an A in this class, that is your own fault. He is so dope. He goes over the answers to homework in class before it's even due, so a free 100% for your assignments. His mid term and final combined are worth 30% which is so nice. His mid term and final were super easy. He's literally a free A, but he is also a great person.

THIS MAN IS GOING STRAIGHT TO THE CELESTIAL KINGDOM!! He is kind, caring, hilarious, entertaining, and passionate about IS. If you go to the class he does the homework with you, and even if don't need the help you should go. This class was honestly the highlight of my week. Love this man, and I feel like I learned how to use Excel pretty well too.
Professor Skousen is very caring! He is always looking out for his students and trying to make it as easy as possible to do well in the course.
Great professor. Very kind and caring.
Awesome teacher, super funny and entertaining. He likes to sing for the class. Easy course, very easy to get 100% if you do the assignments and use TA assistance for the midterm and final.
Super nice guy, very understanding. I am absolutely terrible at Excel, and I feel like this class is very doable.

This is the 1 credit Excel class and you will get as much out of it as you put in. You don't have to go to class and you can do the class as fast as you want. Meaning if you want to grind it out early you can and then be done with it. You basically watch some videos, do some practice, and then do the HW. Pretty chill class and professor.
I have him for IS 110 right now and he is a great guy. He is so kind and it's clear he cares very much about everyone who takes this class.

Prof. Skousen is fantastic; he was so fun to learn from, and his class was really well-structured so it was always clear what steps I should be taking to stay on top of things and enhance my learning process. He's great at explaining difficult concepts, and I can tell he really cares about our success. And sometimes he sings songs for us
His class is structured very well. He is also always willing to help students at any time. He gives test corrections and will make sure you're prepared for the test

Professor Skousen is AMAZING! He is so kind and cares so much about each of his students. He will do anything to help you succeed and goes through so many examples in class so that you really understand the material. He also writes fun songs to help you remember the concepts. He is so awesome!!
Super easy class. Seemed repetitive at times but contained some useful recruiting information.

If you are looking to go into finance, take this class. It will prepare you so much, and Tanya is the only one who teaches it. You do not interact with her too much, mainly the TAs, but they always have solid TAs for this course to help you succeed in the sector of finance you are looking to go into.

The TAs teach most of this class and the content wasn't super helpful. You learn everything taught in this class by going to clubs so it is just very repetitive. It is also very quick as it is taught on the term and everything they teach is really basic. I took it because it looks good on the finance application and it was good for networking.

She is super passionate about what she's talking about and really understands it. She really wants you to succeed and she gives actually useful advice which is really helpful for a pre-business major about to apply. Highly recommend, she's super nice and smart.

You'll get a ton out of FIN 180, whether you're pursuing finance or not. Be aware, that while this is a half credit class, there are assignments due every week and two mandatory 1+ hour lectures weekly.

I have had one conversation with Professor Harmon but she was very kind and helpful when I asked her questions. The class was easy and although only half a credit, it will probably be one of the most useful classes I ever take. Never be afraid to talk to her, she is there to help you.

I honestly didn't benefit much from this class. I only took it to look good on my finance application. Because they shove all the work in this class into one term it's kind of a lot of work. Also, the TA's I had for this class were very unhelpful.

This class was so much more difficult than it needed to be. It is a .5 credit class and I did 3+ hours of homework/reading per week. The reading quizzes are designed to trick you. Prof Harmon was quite rude to me when I asked her questions. Luckily the content was useful and the TAs were great, but I'll never take another class from her.

Tara is kind and passionate about the arts, as well as very accommodating. This class and the assignments can seem menial at times, but it was worth it to be able to practice more skills in an art room, and to be able to work with and teach art lessons to kids.

Love love love her! Tara is the sweetest person ever, has the best feedback, and makes class so fun! I'm not artistic AT ALL but learned SO MUCH from this class and grew to love art! Tara helped me realize that everyone is creative and I had a blast! Hands down would take this again!

Tara is the best person! She is so sweet and will allow you to retake anything. The class is super fun. There is a lot to do outside of class, but it is all fun. Great way to cover the Art GE credit and a great creative outlet. One of the best classes I have ever taken!

Tara is super sweet and a great teacher. I learned so much from this class and she makes it entertaining. You do not have to be good at art to do well. Just give your best effort and you can easily get an A. There is a project, readings, or paper every week, but none of them are difficult. I probably spent a max of 3 hours outside of class a week.

She is so great! Not judgy about others' artwork at all. Since it's once a week, you have to show up to class. The "textbook" was more of a reference for lesson plans. You have lots of fun and learn a lot. Definitely pick her!

Tara is aiight. Easy A so take from her. One thing I didnt like is in lesson plans she would doc me points for things not mentioned in the rubric. Just according to Taras opinion but you are able to resubmit for more points. However you only get like 1 pt back. Dont like her all that much but easy A ppl!

Although not a very artistic person, I really enjoyed taking this class from Tara. She is very understanding and caring. She always gives positive feedback and is very willing to help you find ideas for different projects. We were able to teach kids about art and do projects with them. That was super fun!

Tara is absolutely amazing! I loved her class! I went into it thinking that I wasn't creative and couldn't do art, and left feeling completely confident in my creative talent. I feel like everything I have learned from her class will help me to be a much better teacher than I would have been without it. I would gladly take this class again!

Tara was so awesome! I feel like I am not artistic at all, but I had a ton of fun in her class. She made it very fun and interesting for three hours. As long as you do the assignments and attend class you should be fine. She was also very willing to give feedback and advice for upcoming assignments.

Tara is a really good teacher. She is really good at encouraging students and giving positive feedback. You don't have to be super artistic to get an A. Just turn in all assignments in time and attend class to enjoy making arts and you will get a good grade!

Tara is such a sweet lady! A little scatterbrained at times, but a great teacher. I'm not artistic at all, but it was still fun for me and I learned a lot! Smallest work load I have ever had for a 3 credit class-probably an hour outside of class per week. Just do the assignments and you will get an A for sure.
Tara is a wonderful teacher. We did a lot of different and fun projects and she was always helpful and encouraging. For a 3 hour class the time went by fast.

This was a blended class and so we met once a week over zoom. Then every 4 weeks we went to the SLC center. Math isn't an easy subject. You have three midterms and a final. You have three homework assignments a week that are tricky. Her tests reviews are life savers and she tells you the tricky questions. Do her test review packets as well!!
Great teacher. Basically our classes were learning the concepts and then going over the homework as a class. As long as you're paying attention and asking for help, you'll pass.

Best teacher for Math 118 for sure. Students from the other sections would come to her reviews. She explains it super simply and does videos so you don't have to read through a super dry book. You have a fairly good handle on the material and she does a good job preparing you for the test. Would recommend. 10/10. Also a super kind lady.
Just eh. Not the best teacher but she's really nice.

Math 118 is a tough class, but Tara explains it in a way that is simple and easy to understand. I rarely needed to open my textbook because her lectures covered all of the important material. I highly recommend her as a professor!

She is a great teacher, but the material was difficult. She is fun and explains things really well, but for me (someone who is horrible at math), the class was pretty tough. I did well because I studied a lot, and because she was willing to go over certain topics with me to help me understand them. She is a great choice for this class.

Tara's the best! She teaches well, and is very lenient on grading - you only need 75% on most homework and quizzes to get full credit for them. The class is still difficult, however. There's no curve, so you need to work hard for the A. If you do all the HW and come to class, Tara will be merciful. She bumped me up 1% for an A. Take it from Tara!

Prof. Lewis is amazing! She works hard to help her students succeed. She gives lots of time in class to work problems. She holds outside of class test prep sessions. She makes herself very available to help when you are stuck on a problem through text or email. I wish she could teach every class I take! If you take math 110, take it from Lewis!

Tara Lewis is an awesome teacher! She really knows how to teach math and the harder topics that this class has. She takes her time to explains things and doesn't waste time on things that don't matter/ won't be on the test. She also makes class really fun and enjoyable. This is a hard class with a lot of work required but Tara made it a lot easier.

I love Dr. Ford! A bit disorganized at times and the tests were a lot, but so worth it and doable. One of the best classes I've taken. She gives extra credit and brings food and listens to the class when things are too hard. Best lectures and assignments. You will laugh, feel the Spirit, and learn to love others and other faiths as never before.

Dr Ford might be my most influential professor I've taken this far. She's so passionate about other religions and cultures, I'd argue that everyone should take this class or one similar to it, I learned so much in this class. Dr Ford is so funny and understanding- just talk to her if you miss an assignment and you can make it up.

She is a sweet lady and this class is easy - just as a religion class should be. I got to learn a lot in a low-stress environment and never felt worried about my grade. She makes class fun and interesting too so it doesn't get old by the end of the semester. Not too many assignments overall and she grades super leniently.

Dr. Rutherford is the sweetest and bubbliest professor I've had at BYU. She handled the tech challenges of online classes insanely well, and her lectures were seriously so enriching and intriguing. She has a great respect for religions of the world and really expects her students to embrace other faiths with an open mind and heart. Amazing lady.
She has been one of my best professors here at BYU. Such an amazing professor, she loves her students and it shows. I am definitely taking another class from here.

10/10 wish I'd taken this class from someone else. She speaks rather flippantly of other religions (and our own) which made me v uncomfy. If you're just here for entertainment she does the job, but I personally felt as if I was cheated of an important opportunity to gain empathy and understanding of other religions.

Dr. Rutherford is an amazing professor. I took her class during the summer and never felt like it was too much work. Her lectures are incredible and very insightful. She is also hilarious and very charismatic. She knows a lot about what she's talking about and is a spectacular person to get to know.

I've never regretted taking a class at BYU before. About 6 weeks in and I wish I had dropped it day one. She's the worst religion professor I've ever had. She mixes in too much opinion with doctrine and expects us to know what her opinion is. She expects way too much from a GE Religion course. Avoid taking her at all costs.

Rutherford Is passionate about world religions & very knowledgeable. Her passion is contagious! Interesting material. Gives easy "attendance" quizzes to help boost your grade. Easily accessible by email or after class. Graded on an inter religious worship service, a service project, and two tests. Plus quizzes. Easy grader if you do the work.

YOU FOUND THE PERFECT PROFESSOR FOR ANY RELIGION CLASS! She is by far one of the best religion professors I have ever taken and you'll regret not taking her class. It's not if you should take her class, it's WHEN!

She's hilarious and a wonderful lecturer because she is passionate about world religions. I never read the book, all of the essential info is in her ppts. Super straightforward tests with helpful study guides. 3 off-campus projects so don't take this class without a car. Highly recommend! I loved it so much I never missed it even at 8AM!

Best religion class I've taken by far. Dr. Rutherford was both knowledgeable and entertaining, and the course material itself is fantastic. Only two tests, but she's VERY straightforward about the material. There are two interfaith projects, so don't take the class if you don't have a car. She really wants her students to succeed
She is so awesome! Seriously has opened my eyes to other religions. So grateful for her fun spunky attitude in class. Its never boring!

The class is awesome and really helps you interact with different religions on a personal level. Dr. Rutherford was hilarious and she has a lot of personal experience with the material. I did feel she was a little overfocused on learning material and not focused enough on growing spiritually. I also felt it required more work than necessary.

Dr. Rutherford is skilled in informing her students, as well as making other religions interesting. If you want to learn about other religions, this is the class to take. Not easy, but if you pay attention and do the readings youll be fine.

Dr. Rutherford is an amazing professor! World Religions with her was the most inspiring and eye-opening class. She relates other religious 'traditions' back to concepts that members of The Restored Church can understand. She emphasizes service in her class, too.

Pro. Rutherford is awesome! Her lectures are great and she is welcoming of other's opinions and insights and she is very funny. Taking world religions with her was fantastic and the class gives double credit for religion hours and cultural awareness.

Dr. Rutherford is hilarious and witty! She's a classy, well-dressed, kind woman who is passionate and highly educated in world religions. (Specifically the religions of India) TAKE THIS CLASS! She has wonderful and powerful insights. She even shared her story of meeting Mother Teresa! A powerful, highly beneficial class and powerful professor.
Good teacher, fairly easy class. Good insight into religions.

Sister Rutherford is a former BYU cheerleader, and you can definitely tell. She is very cheerful.  She requires a lot of memorization for exams, and she has world religion project where you attend a (not LDS) religious service and write a paper. Lots of role play. Multiple choice is easy, and she really cares about her students.  Highly recommend!

Sister Rutherford was decent. The class is super easy so if that is what you are looking for, take this class from her. She tells you everything you need to know for the tests. My problem was that I was never inspired. I feel like I didn't really learn much about the gospel. If you want to be spiritually enlightened take from someone else.

She is a great teacher, lots of insight. However, she makes you memorize a ridiculous amount of passages. I assumed the class would be more centered on learning, teaching, and concepts but its honestly just how well you can memorize.
She's super funny and I had a great time and learned a lot. The reading was a little unclear, but if you talk to her you'll be fine.

Quizzes on reading after every chapter. Big project is attending a worship service for a faith not of your own. She really cares about what she's teaching, but sometimes she is confusing. Overall a really fun professor.

Sister Rutherford is so awesome. She's hilarious and very friendly. Her lectures are always entertaining and very interesting. It's a really tough class, and reading the text matters a ton. Always be prepared for a surprise quiz. But the class is definitely worth the hard work. I learned a lot!

Paper every week, quiz every class, 40-50 pages of pretty heavy reading every week, 7 page paper final, midterm, and a final exam. Not my favorite religion class despite how interesting the material actually was to me. Just seemed like overkill for a six week course for me.

I took this during the summer but the course outline was pretty intense. A paper every week, reading quiz every class,a midterm, a 7 page paper and a final exam. It wouldn't be as difficult if it was the same amount of course work spread out over a full semester but seemed like overkill for a religion class.

Easiest class ever. I completed the entire semester's assignments in a week, and with extra credit got 105% in the class. Her tests have a few trick questions, so unfortunately I only got a 98% on the final, but then she curved it to 100%. Downside -- attendance is mandatory.

Professor Rutherford is one of the best teachers I've ever had, she made sure we learned the material all while making it an environment for us to feel the Spirit. She's brilliant and knows what she's talking about and loves to help students with whatever they need.

This was a great class and I'd highly recommend it. It has a lot of memorization and reading, so that was difficult especially for tests when every small detail was tested on.  extra credit  our teacher was reasonable. recommend it, if you've got the time.

Super approachable and wants to help you learn. He did a very good job at inviting us to come talk with him during his office hours, and was very empathetic in helping us with the things we were having struggles with. The class has a very heavy workload, but Professor Greenwood is a good guy

Dr. Greenwood is a great professor. He knows everyone's names and genuinely cares about how you do in the class. The class itself is difficult not because of the content but because of how much time it takes, but Dr. Greenwood's class is significantly easier than other professors classes at BYU.

Dr. Greenwood is really great, I thought he did a great job teaching this class. The workload is heavy but doable, about what you would expect for learning to use CAD in 3 short months. I went from 0 experience in SolidWorks to feeling very confident on the exams. Dr. Greenwood has probably one of the easier 272 classes at BYU.

He's amazing, I loved this class! He knew all of our names and cared about our questions. The hardest part about the class is just the workload; the content isn't too difficult, there's just so much to learn. All of the homework and assignments took me FOREVER to complete, but I actually really enjoyed the content!

Professor Greenwood is one of my favorite professors. Any CAD class is just going to be a lot of work because you have to model the parts, but I felt like this class had one of the easier loads. He was super friendly and connected well with the class. He also spent a lot of class going over how to actually do what we needed for the tests.

Dr. Greenwood is such a thoughtful and caring professor. I really appreciated the time he took to help me understand and improve when I was struggling. This was a difficult class, but Dr. Greenwood is so great at making sure that you really get to learn and improve from your mistakes.

I took this class three years ago, and I'm coming back to rate because of how helpful this class has been at helping me in my professional career. Pay attention in this class and keep the materials for the future!

Absolutely condescending at all times, couldn't even ask a question without being roasted to the shadow realm. Entirely relies on memorization His tests are brutal too. He makes you do so much drawing in so little time. In fairness however, his tests are pretty much copy pastes of the quizzes he posts so if you ace those you're good to go.
Mr. Taylor is one of the best professors I have had. He genuinely cares about each of his students and will go above and beyond to help you do your best. I would take his class over and over again.

This is the best class Ive taken so far at BYU. Im not a business major, yet the skills I learned were completely relevant to me, and I feel they would be for any career. I left far better prepared for applying for jobs and with more confidence. I have so many positive things to say about Mr. T, but especially: he cares and wants you to succeed.

Mr. T. is awesome! If you need to take this class, don't take it from any other professor. Mr. T. is really good at teaching, and does really well to prepare you for real life situations. There was a lot of good application from this class. Pay attention during lectures, and study hard for the grammar test--it can make or break your grade.

The class itself is challenging, specifically the grammar portions. However, it is without a doubt one of the most helpful courses I have taken at BYU. Mr. T is a really good guy and genuinely cares about his students well-being. He is more than willing to help his students succeed both in and out of the classroom.

Mr T cares a lot about the success of his students; every assignment was given to help his students acquire useful, even essential, skills for success in the workplace. The textbook is online, digestible, and free.

The class Mcom is in general very hard. If I had the choice I would still take it from Professor Taylor. You really enjoy and learn from him. The assignments are very toughly graded so put time into them.

MCOM is a difficult class but Professor Taylor does his best to eliminate busy work and make the load manageable. He does a great job of teaching the curriculum which can be interesting and useful in your future career.

Mr. T is awesome! The class is difficult but also a lot of fun. You will definitely use what you learn in his class for the rest of your life. MCOM is hard anyways, so you might as well take it from a teacher who is invested in your progression, like Mr. T.
Professor Taylor is a great teacher, and the material he covers is useful even if you are not a business major. Many of the concepts I have learned in the class have been applicable in my daily life.

Prof. Taylor is a really awesome guy. I have a lot of respect for the guy because he really tries to practice what he teaches, and communication in management settings is not necessarily the easiest of topics. Anyway, you need to go to class to participate, be prepared for group projects, and be on the lookout for ambiguous assignment requirements.

Mr. T. does a great job preparing you for the business world by assigning realistic work. I would say that his grading techniques are unique, but won't hurt you from getting an A in the class. Very personable as well and is willing to help out his students in any way possible.
One of the best professors I've ever had. It is a tough class, but the material is stuff you can use every day of your life. Super important class to take.

MCOM 320 is a very useful class. All the assignments have a clear purpose and help you develop your communication skills. Mr. T does not give the clearest instructions for assignments and much of his Learning Suite schedule and assignment descriptions were out of date. Other than some disorganization, he is great and a fun professor.

I'm a junior at BYU and Mr. T is one of my favorite professors. He cares a lot more about you and your life than he does about the material. I learned valuable life skills in this class. I'm not a business major but I would advise that if at all possible take MCOM 320 from Mr T for your advanced writing class! PS if a phone goes off we get treats!
One of the best professors I've had at BYU so far. He is 100% genuine and caring with his students. A lot to learn from him so take any opportunity you have to pick his brain.

Professor Taylor is a great teacher who cares about his students and wants us to learn important life skills. The class is more about learning than just getting through the course material. I would definitely take another class from him again in the future.
Professor Taylor is great! He is fun and engaging. This class is hard and a lot of work. You have to be on top of assignments because it is a lot to handle sometimes. It is a very beneficial

He has a really great personality and the classes are a ton of fun. The course is hard and challenging especially the grammar portion, but I learned a lot and it is useful information. If you are in a business major it is perfect and he makes the course a lot of fun.

Professor Taylor is great! Lectures are awesome. I always left with interesting ideas to think about on my own. The only downside to the class is communication about homework. Instructions are ambiguous and assignments seem to come up out of the blue (because they aren't discussed in class). But overall I loved the class and would highly recommend!

Dr. Taylor is a great professor. Sometimes it's hard reaching him and assignment instructions are ambiguous but for a purpose. However, sometimes it's unclear HOW he wants you to turn it in. Lectures were very interesting, and Dr. Taylor definitely has strong personal views.

This class was a time for me to turn off distractions and really engage with the teacher and students. It was one of the best times of my day! You put in a good amount of work into it, but nothing terrible. Sometimes Mr. T wouldn't talk about upcoming assignments. All the info is on LearningSuite, so keep on top of it. Highly recommend!

Mr. T is a great guy who genuinely cares about his students. His door is literally always open if you have any questions or even just want to talk. The skills that I learned in his class are so valuable, I'll undoubtedly use them for the rest of my life. His grading seemed to be somewhat harsh at times, and he had a LOT of assignments, but still :)
Great teacher. Pretty chill assignments. Great final writing class to take.

Mr T. is an amazing professor. I wouldn't have wanted to have taken this class from anyone else! This class is hard but not hard at the same time. Assignments are very chill, but the grading is harsh at times. Lectures are fun and interesting, lots of group activities. So glad I had to take this class, I learned more than I ever thought I would.

Mr. T was an awesome teacher. He really focused on LEARNING rather than just assignments and grades. He has some really great perspectives and makes sure to focus on the most important. He will leave the topic to ensure the conversation is important and he removes assignments that are unnecessary. He is great! I did not get an A but I learned!

Dr. Taylor is awesome. I was in a serious accident early in the semester and he was awesome working with me. I had heard from multiple sources how hard MCOM 320 was and was surprised how manageable it was. He's engaging, fun, and understanding. Definitely take him for this class!
He is a super great professor. You will get so much from the class if you participate. This class is hard, but it totally prepares you for the real world after college.

Textbook is required, but it's free and online. Mr. T was a great professor and I'm glad I got to take MCOM 320 from him. Participation is mandatory, there are papers and group things to do, but overall he was lenient with deadlines and due dates, and very willing to adjust the schedule as needs arose. Would definitely take again from him!

He specifically makes the class ambiguous and unorganized to simulate what life will be like in the real world. For me, that made things pretty stressful, but it was good practice that I don't think we get very often in college.

I am not a big english fan and hate writing papers so I was seriously dreading taking this class. However, Mr. T not only made this class extremely useful and helpful, but actually made MCOM enjoyable. He is super funny and cares A TON about his students. I can't say enough about him - he is one of my favorite professors here at BYU.

He is great! I've never had a professor that is as focused on helping students in real-world situations. He cares that we succeed in the business world. I talked to a few friends who took M Com from other professors and Professor Taylor cuts out a lot of work that other professors will make you do.

One of the best professors I've ever had. He really cares about the students and his MCOM class is phenomenal. He is so much fun and so wise on all aspects of life. Wish he was my teacher for every class, his teaching style is very visual and makes everything really easy to learn and apply. The class is hard work but so worth it.

Mr. T cares about his students, he learned our names on the first week. He teaches great life skills of communication. Check LS often because he will move assignment due dates around. Go to class, do the reading, put in the work, and you'll have a great experience. Go Mr. T!

MCOM 320 with Mr. T is the most useful class I've ever taken at BYU. The wisdom Mr. T has to share will change the way you communicate and interact with people, and therefore will change you, your marriage, and the rest of your life. Mr. T loves his students and tells them so. He is available, heartfelt, and hilarious, and requires quality effort.

Okay, this RateMyProfessor website doesn't work for this teacher, cuz sure we all know why you're here, to find a easy teacher and get the best grade. I'm here to tell you that GRADES DO NOT MATTER! Prof T. is literally the best teacher you'll get. No matter what grade you get, his class alone will be worth every cent of your semester's tuition.

Mr. T is the greatest teacher I've ever had. He's extremely relatable and is more focused on giving you a great educational experience than just giving you a grade. The class is tough and grading can be tough at times, but he seriously cares about his students. One of my favorite classes at BYU.

Mr. T is a solid professor. He truly cares about his students. He will adapt lectures to teach to needs, which I highly appreciated. Check LS often because he will move assignment due dates around. Go to class, do the reading, put in the work, and you'll have a great experience. Don't wait until you're a Senior to take the class. Loved his class!

Professor Taylor really pushes you to learn how to more effectively communicate in a business environment. He is a teacher dedicated to YOU! My main struggle with the class is that assignment guidelines are confusing and hurt my grade because I interpreted instructions differently than expected.

Professor Taylor is awesome and he is very respectful of his students. This course is quite difficult, but if you are willing to work hard, Professor Taylor will make it worth it. This class is definitely one of the more useful courses I have taken here at BYU.
His class can be life-changing in the best way.

Mr T is a great professor. He makes his class intentionally difficult and ambiguous, which can be frustrating. But he teaches material that is extremely useful outside the classroom. He also cuts out busy work assignment that professors require in other sections. A lot of work, but well worth it.

This class was one of my favorite and most useful classes taken at BYU. I would highly recommend anyone to take this class, especially from Mr. T because it will improve your life. However, be prepared to put in effort to do well in the class, it's definitely not an easy A.
Mr. T is an awesome professor! His assignments can be tough but he makes sure you are prepared for them. I really learned a lot of things that I will take along with me the rest of my life.

Great professor. Always willing to talk and help however he can outside of class. Attendance mandatory!
Mr. T is a great professor. He cares about his students and he's really funny. The work load is rough and he is a tough grader. Don't skip class! The material is very applicable to life in general.
Professor Taylor does his best to make sure you leave MCOM 320 with the most important aspects taught in the course.

His class is hard and you really have to work for your grade, which is good, but be ready for to work. He gives really good feedback on your papers. He is willing to talk to you and help you work those any struggles you face with the class

Any MCOM class will be tough, but Mr T is a good teacher to take it from. You will learn a lot about how to communicate well. The things that I learned I was able to implement almost immediately in different emails that I was sending to potential employers.

Mr. T (what he goes by) cares more about giving you real life experiences and skills than your grade. Tough grader but your learn a good amount. He's a cool guy, class is interesting but you could probs find an easier teacher for this class.

Get ready to work! Grading for a few assignments seemed a bit too subjective (Im not sure peers should be grading some things), but overall it worked out okay. This is a hard class, probably because it isnt full of fluff and useless stuff. The course content is extremely useful! Mr. T is a very likable guy, and always willing to help students.

MCOM is the most practical course I have taken. I think Mr. T does a good job of teaching the concepts and helping you learn the material without making you drowned. That being said, it's a lot of work and you can't just breeze through the assignments. You have to know your stuff if you want to do well but the best part is the material is so good.

Great teacher. He really cares about the success of his students. Wants you to learn so he's challenging, but it's effective. Very valuable class, there wasn't a crazy ton of homework but you should be diligent and stay on top of things. Everyone should take his class, it's helped me with SO much more.
Does a fantastic job with the class. Very realistic and is in it for the students. One of the most valuable and applicable classes I have ever taken.

Professor Taylor is a great guy. His class was fine for the most part, but there are way too many assignments and he grades very harshly. He doesn't think that grades are important and tells you from the first day of class that almost no one gets an A. Assignments are very vague and he changed the due date of a big assignment after it was due.

The class was helpful. Professor Taylor was very helpful and eliminated from the given curriculum assignments he deemed unnecessary in the business world. The grading in this class is obnoxious. In my opinion, overly hard and sometimes the peer grading felt unfair. The feedback on the assignments was very useful. Ambiguous assignments everywhere!

Take Mr. T for MCOM320! He genuinely cares about his students. There are a lot of assignments with any MCOM course, but he only puts in the required assignments from the department. If you get a chance, meet with him outside of class. He's more interested in your future success than your grade. Wonderful Professor!

This class was so applicable to real-life situations. There are random quizzes at the beginning of class so attend and be on-time. Mr.T is a tough grader but gives good feedback. I think this class is difficult regardless but Mr. T makes it real and engaging. It has been one of the most interesting and useful classes I've taken at BYU.

I enjoyed this class. It is the kind of class where you feel like you are learning so many useful skills that you don't really care about your grade. If you do care about your grade I highly recommend visiting Scott during his office hours and he will point you in the right direction. Scott is very real. I had a great experience in this class.

Mr. T is a great professor. He's very practical and teaches you what you really need to know without all the fluff. He's also super accessible and is always willing to give feedback. This class is honestly one of the most helpful and applicable classes I've taken. It's hard and kinda ambiguous, so make sure you put in the time to get a good grade.
