The grammar test at the beginning of the semester is tough. It is standard across all M COM 320 classes. You get a re-take if you want. Scott Taylor is an enjoyable professor. The class discussions are interesting and applicable. There is a lot of homework, which also seems consistent with other M COM 320 classes. Not an easy A, but a great class.

The material that we covered in class was very interesting and very applicable to real life. Defiantly one of those classes that could have a big impact in your career if you take the time. Mr, T was a cool professor and very knowledgeable. But if your more worried about the grade then this class might be frustrating.

I am not a business major and just needed an English class to do my GE. That being said, Mr. T made this class very applicable to any field by making us see that this was real world stuff. He grades hard but with a purpose. You will learn a lot and you will be better prepared for life after graduation.

The course is tough, and he is a tough grader, but he also gives good feedback on your assignments. Class attendance is a must. He really cares about his students, and he wants you to learn principles that will help you for your entire career. He is funny and entertaining, and he shares a lot of practical and valuable experiences/stories.

Really awesome professor. He is a really tough grader-- he has to be. He does a lot of in-class group work, so coming to class is a must. The hands-on activities really drives home the lessons he's teaching in class. Always bring your computer as many times he'll ask for you to email him or type on a word document. Tough, but awesome.

I've recommended Mr. T to my friends who still need to take MCOM. The class was tough but probably one of my favorites in my college experience. Mr. T gave me the most helpful feedback and suggestions when I was trying to get an internship (better than the classes and workshops I've taken) and I think I might not have gotten it without his help.

Mr. Taylor is a great Professor, his lectures are engaging and interesting. The material is applicable to any career you may be interested in. He knows everyone in the class and is there to help you out however he can.

Very unprofessional. Prompts for assignments were changed last minute after I had started working on a couple. Prompts sometimes ambiguous too. I recommend double tasking while he lectures and taking notes as necessary, he won't tell you much what is not already in the textbook.

Scott Taylor was a great professor. The course is naturally designed to be difficult, vague, and challenging. Professor Taylor gives direct feedback, and if your project stinks, he'll tell you that it does, but he'll also tell you why and how you can improve. He's super funny, and loves deeply.

Mr. Taylor is a great professor. He has so much experience and so his insights are always very helpful. This class has taught me so much and I actually use all the things we learn on a daily basis. The class is really hard -- but it will make your life easier.
Mr. Taylor is very easy to work with. He gives good feedback and provides valuable experience to help learn principles of business communication.

Mr. Taylor is all about helping the students learn the material and applying it. All of his assignments have purpose and he is good about giving feed back on your graded assignments. Classes are always beneficial and inspirational. He expects that you give your best and he goes the extra mile to help you. I %100 recommend.

Scott helps students become good communicators and be successful in life. He likes to share personal examples and teach life lessons, and he wants you to know that grades don't matter that much. Scott can be blunt but really does care. He's willing to help outside of class and he knows your name and remembers you. The course is tough by nature.
Down to earth guy. Gives real world examples and is very knowledgeable.
It was a very insightful class. Good teacher, keeps your interested and gives real world examples.

Professor Taylor knows his stuff and gives real-world examples about communication which is very helpful. He cares about his students and makes sure that all their questions are answered. The class was very insightful but sometimes unclear and a perfect scores seemed intentionally out of reach, just because. Great professor for the course however!

Professor Taylor gives excellent real world advise and preparation. He gives amazing lectures, and helpful feedback. I felt challenged on every assignment. Overall I did not care what my grade was as I learned so much.
Scott Taylor taught effectively. He is a fair grader. This course is designed to be ambiguous. I would take another class from Scott. Meet with him 1 on 1 and you will learn so much about life!

Overall Mr. T is a really nice guy. He definitely cares about teaching students and helping them succeed. The only thing I didn't like about this course was I felt like it wasn't as relevant to me. I was not a business major and felt that the course was very specific to those pursuing business careers.

It is a privilege to have a class from Mr. T. The demands of the class were stressful at times, but Mr. T gives you a good grade if you put in effort, apply class principles, and adapt to the situation. He also took time outside of class to talk about my future and give me valuable life advice. Take this class!

This man is inspirational and has changed my perspective on life. His coursework is definitely difficult, but it's totally worth what you learn. It's not impossible to get a good grade, but you've really got to work for it.

Mr. Taylor is an amazing professor. He makes lectures entertaining and focuses on the most applicable information. This course is rigorous by nature, but he does not waste your time. Every assignment will benefit your future success. I definitely recommend taking his class, you will not regret it!

Scott is one of the most accessible professors I have ever had. MCOM 320 is, by nature, a difficult class. It doesn't matter who you take it from. However, Scott genuinely cared about us and our success. He cared not in a way that made the class easy, but in a way that made the class worth my time and effort. DEFINITELY take this course from him.

Great teacher! I would recommend him if you really want to improve your writing. You should know, he doesn't care about grades, and he makes that very clear. He uses lots of real-world examples of good and bad communication, which I really loved. He knows how to prepare you to get a job and is a great resource. Cool guy. Cares about his students.

Gives you every opportunity to be successful, but you have to work for it. The class takes time and commitment but if you put effort into it you can succeed. Uses lots of real life application. Motivates you to be your best and to improve. I felt comfortable trying new things and breaking outside my comfort zone. Really cares about his students!
He helps each student individually grow and communicate better. He is time invested in the class and cares about what we are learning. He is a great professor and I would highly recommend him.

M COM 320 is a tough class, but it's practical & applicable to the real world of business. Professor Taylor makes the class entertaining with his sense of humor. He is respectful, and does a great job at helping students, creating meaningful opportunities to participate,  & leading students to lifelong learning and service. Highly recommended!

Professor Taylor gives really good feedback and you can tell he really enjoys teaching. It is not an easy A, and sometimes assignment instructions are not always very clear, but the class is worth it.

He gives you very strict and defined grading criteria. You will have to work on your grammar a lot too. However, the things I learned in his class will be applicable in everything I do for the rest of my life.

Professor Taylor is great guy and great teacher. He is always willing to meet with you if you have any questions and is genuinely interested in how you're doing. His expectations can be a little blurry at times, but he teaches well and gives very practical advice and coursework that I feel is applicable to the working field.
Professor Taylor is an excellent professor and I would recommend him. He cuts a lot of useless assignments that other MCOM sections do and he shows how principals are relevant to the work place.

Mr T. is a good professor.  He taught the material very well.  This is simply a difficult class with tons of homework.  I have learned so much about how to write effectively in a business format.  However, this was the most labor intensive class that I have taken in my 6 semesters here at BYU.  I do think that Mr T makes it as bearable as possible.
One of the best classes BYU offers. He  is a solid teacher too. Tough grader, BUT the way he teaches the class is too rewarding to pass up!

Because he only teaches one class and owns several businesses, coaches varsity soccer for Timpanogos High School, and has a quail farm, he is usually only around for a few ours after class. He is a tough grader but he allows redo's on most, if not, all the assignments. He is super chill and overall a great guy and teacher

Best class I have taken at BYU. Every lesson is applicable to the real world. The class is a big time consumer, but it is never a waste of time. Mr. T is funny and engaging. If you work hard you can get a good grade, grading is fair. But don't take this class for the grade, take this class for the professional-level skills it teaches you.

Very inspiring teacher. Teaches principles that can be applied in real life. He does not hand out easy A's, but as long as you try and put in the work you will not receive a bad grade (in an already tough class). You can tell he loves what he does. One of my favorite classes and teachers at BYU. Participating in class helps you learn more.

Mr.T is a great teacher. The class is a lot of work and will really push you. His grading is harsh, but fair. Mr.T wants his students to succeed and truly gain skills that will help them in their future as professionals.

He is really a cool guy, and updated the syllabus during the semester to avoid any busywork assignments. He talks about real work experience and ties in subject matter into the real world. Sometimes I wasn't sure how to approach assignments, due to unclear explanations, but he'll answer questions about any assignments. All-around a great professor.

One of the most rewarding classes I have taken at BYU. My only complaint was the ambiguity of the assignments. The instructions were never clear and it was very difficult to contact him to get clarification about them and he doesn't have T.A.'s to help so my grade suffered. Other than that a great professor and life mentor.

This class really helped my writing, which was already good. He gives detailed feedback on your written work, which is SO helpful. Be prepared to take constructive criticism. Like any MCOM class, you will get nailed on tiny grammar mistakes, so check everything three times before handing it in. *Never start a sentence with "There is..." Haha

Mr. T is a great Mcom professor. He teaches because he enjoys it and he has cut everything out of the course that he doesn't think will be helpful for your future. He is a very difficult grader so make sure to follow the directions in the book and on each assignment carefully. If you will put in the time, you will have learn a lot and will do well.

It was one of the most useful classes I've ever taken. As long as you're okay with a little bit of disorganization, you won't have any problems. There's a lot of group work and what could be described as "busy work" but it is all useful and relevant to your future career.
Great feedback, class schedule is a little disorganized but it helps you stay on your toes. Overall, learned a lot but not a good class to take if you want to keep your GPA.
Fairly good teaching, very inspiring and quite funny. I felt he was unorganized and difficult grader but he was still a great guy. Had inspiring random stories I love when teachers do that.
Class helped me get practical skills in communicating and in business. He grades very hard, but the feedback you get is very helpful. I appreciated his class and think he is a great professor.
Great class. Very applicable. Be ready to read a lot and work hard for a good grade. Probably worth it.
This is just a hard class, there is no way around that. One of the best classes I have taken.
He's a great person but a hard grader. You'll learn a lot taking from him but you'll have you work for it!
Mr T was awesome. He totally cares about our learning and our personal lives

Professor Taylor is a great teacher. His classes and lectures were always interesting, as well. His class was difficult and he was a hard grader, so if you are looking for an easy MCOM 320 class, this isn't it. Overall it was a great class and I learned a lot from him.

Mr. T is awesome. His class is hard and time consuming, but worth it. He gives awesome feedback, and if you work hard, you'll come out of his class a much better writer and presenter. I would highly recommend taking his class.
Yes, he grades hard, but I really like how he said that you might as well get the grade now than fail in the future.

Mr. T is a smart guy and a good teacher.  His class was really difficult and time consuming, but it definitely got better throughout the semester.  His lectures were enjoyable.  Almost everything we learned is super applicable to our lives in the business world.  Overall I enjoyed the class, despite it's difficulty and very heavy work load.

He is a great teacher and I learned a ton in this class that is helpful for the real world. It's a lot of work and theres a ton of homework, he is a super tough grader. It's a great class just be ready to put a bunch of work into it.

Prof T is a good teacher, he applies the course to real life business experiences. He doesn't really care about grades, he wants you to learn and be better in the business world. I liked his examples and application to life, but he didn't explain concepts very well.  Also he takes forever to get feedback to you.

He really wants you to learn the material which does mean the class is a little harder than it could be but he is reasonable and it does make the class more beneficial. The level of difficulty was high for me but that is because I'm really not good at technical business writing at all.

I am not the kind of person who enjoys business classes or speaking in public so this  class proved a challenge from the beginning. Although I wasn't naturally good at anything in the class, I learned more applicable skills in this class than any other class I have taken at BYU. Professor Taylor really cared about my individual growth and inspired

Mr. T really cares about his students and wants them to succeed. His assignments are very straightforward, and he includes a rubric with each one so you know what to expect. This class will keep you busy, but you will learn more than you could ever imagine. Mr. T gives constructive feedback and does a great job of preparing you for the real world.

If you are looking for an easy A, this isn't it, but you do learn a lot about writing and presenting. Sometimes the assignment sheets aren't very clear, but Professor Taylor is always willing to answer questions and is prompt about getting back to you.
He is a tough grader, but I learned so much from him.  The things I learned in his class were the most applicable to real life, and most useful out of all of my classes.

Scott Taylor is a great teacher with real-world experience. He is a tough grader and expects a lot out of his students, I feel that his style of teaching and grading helped me learn the material better.  He is very helpful both in covering class material and helping students outside of class. Take advantage of his entrepreneurial expertise!

Professor Taylor is a fantastic teacher! The class is difficult and pushed me, but I learned a lot. Professor Taylor cares a lot about the students, and gives good advice for real-life situations. He wants us to be successful.  Professor Taylor is a difficult grader, and not always clear with assignment expectations, but he always answers questions

Professor Taylor was an extremely difficult but good teacher. He is purposeful in the things he teaches and in what you learn. He sincerely cares for the welfare and success of his students. His class is very focused on useful things that will make a difference in your life. He is an extremely tough grader and very straightforward.

Dr. Landon gives great lectures, and you can tell that he is invested in his students' success. He provided useful real world examples for every concept that we discussed. Since he is a newer professor,  he knows how to relate to undergrad students and gives solid advice regarding study strategies, etc. The textbook was not needed/useful.
Tough class, but very doable. Homework load was light, so personal study was required to stay up to speed.

Dr Landon is the best. Lectures are great. He refers the textbooks chapters for every class, but you don't need the book if you go to classes. His grading criteria is clear, participation and attendance is 5%, and tests are 70%. He learns everyone's names and calls people out to participate and makes sure you are comfortable. Take it from him!
Econ 380 is very difficult but Dr. Landon made me exited to come to class. He is soft spoken, smart, and extremely selfless. I would highly recommend taking classes from him.

Great professor. Econ 380 is a beast, but he's a good lecturer and is very willing to work with students one on one to clear up misconceptions. As other people have said (and he himself says), the textbook is dense and completely optional for this course; I did just fine using my in-class notes and the practice tests to prepare for his midterms.

Dr. Landon is awesome. Super smart but also super approachable, and he really cares about his students. He did a good job getting me excited about economics! Econ 380 is tough, but he made it a lot better and was very fair. Definitely take it from him if you can!

He's really solid. The material covered in this class is really tough, but he teaches it really well and makes it managable. The textbook is completely optional, I recommend going to his class a couple of times before buying it. I don't think you need it. Overall, Dr. Landon is super chill and makes a tough class about as enjoyable as possible
Really great class, was definitely a huge jump from 110, but Dr. Landon made the material digestible and was always available.

FIN425 with Taylor Nadauld and Bob Winder was one of my favorite classes at BYU. They genuinely care about students spiritually and temporally. It feels like two classes in one—but in a good way. The workload is average, the content is super relevant, and it preps you well for PE/VC interviews. Highly recommend despite a bit of disorganization.

This class was disorganized. They claim they've taught it for 7 years but it seems like it's the first year being taught. TAs run the class and they don't know what they're doing. 

Ex. one of the key points that was taught and the notes provided had major errors. Study guide as well. Errors were corrected about 16 hours before the exam started.

FIN 425 with Nadauld and Winder is a top tier class. Taylor does a terrific job of walking through terms and concepts you'll see a lot if you work in PE/VC. He is a super caring teacher and is very entertaining as well. He brings in a lot of super cool founders as well. Pretty light on homework and the tests are fairly easy. Would recommend! 10/10!

Great for PE preparation and the best exposure you can get at BYU to deal terminology, acquisition analysis, and fin modeling. He gave great lectures, and I enjoyed the class. Assignments were ambiguous, however, and it was difficult to study for lack of formal materials; the content is delivered as whiteboard scribble. Most students got an A or A-

Professor Nadauld, what isn't there to say about him? He is the only professor I have ever rated. Truly, he has been my favorite professor at BYU. He is extremely knowledgeable, teaches to understand, emphasizes the "why" and "how" instead of just the "what", etc. He intertwines the gospel into lectures in such an inspirational and beautiful way.

Professor Nadauld is amazing! He really cares about each of his students and takes time to teach you gospel principles/life insights as well not just finance. He is brilliant in finance and in every aspect of life but super humble. He has been my favorite professor at BYU so far.

This guy is actually the GOAT. I literally have never given a rating on here, but Professor Nadauld deserves it. I learned SO much from him, and almost everything was so enjoyable. He cares about us actually learning, and is not so concerned about just blowing through the material. Arguably the best professor I've ever had.

This was my favorite class I have every taken. Professor Naduald is such a great teacher and really focus on teaching the concepts not just the material. His lectures are entertaining and he really cares about his students.

You have to take this class from Taylor! I learned so much in this class because of his teachings. Midterms arent terrible if you take good notes during class. There were about five group cases that do take a long time. Taylor is super real with us and made his class manageable with COVID.

Class consisted of 2 midterms, a final, and like 5 cases (10 pages long). Homework was sometimes hard and not gone over in class, but if you put any answer at all you get full credit. Huge curve at end of semester so everyone gets at least B+.

Taylor was my first introduction to thinking critically and figuring out how to deal with ambiguity. The Harvard cases are an excellent way to learn, and I believe working on those cases in groups is the closest thing to being in the workplace post-graduation.
Professor Nadauld is the best professor I have ever had. He teaches students to think critically. He makes complex topics seem simple. The class is tough, but definitely worth it!

Best lectures I've been in, you have to take 401 from him. He explains complex concepts so clearly, you don't even realize they are complex. You just need to remember to take notes and study practice problems for his tests. His tests aren't too hard, you just need to make sure you know the concepts as well, he'll have free response questions.

Great lectures, he helps you really understand the material. It can be hard to take notes because you just want to listen to his insights. Incorporates a lot of humor into his lectures, explains concepts, and willing to help you one on one. Tests can be tough if you don't study the concepts or homework, but not that bad. Best teacher I've had.

I loved Professor Nadauld's class. He struck just the right balance between funny and serious, and he was always happy to slow down the pace of the class to help students really understand the concepts. I think I actually understand finance now! He also sometimes goes on hilarious tangents, and it makes class all the more enjoyable.

Professor Nadauld is an excellent professor. He does a great job of helping students understand the big picture AND the nitty gritty details. I have heard that his lectures can be hard to follow for some, but I had no problem with it. He's obviously passionate about finance and does a great job bringing that passion to his lectures.

Such a funny guy and smart professor. His class is very unstructured. He used power points only a handful of time.  You can tell he knows what he is talking about. Very engaging and cares about the students. If you don't do well in unstructured classes you probably will struggle. He is a total bro.

Prof. Nadauld seemed much more interested in his research than in his students. He frequently seemed unprepared to teach, and was often impatient with struggling students. Respected among faculty, but not among any students I've personally talked to. He seems like the kinda guy you want to hangout with, but not take a class from.

His teaching style was hard for me. He opted to move away from a structured course and chose instead to leave things up to us to figure out. He got frustrated twice during the semester when students asked him questions that he thought they should know the answer to. A bit on the arrogant side. If you like structured classes, don't take him.

There are a lot of case studies in this class and the tests are hard, but Nadauld is funny and competent at teaching difficult subjects, so the class is doable if you take time to make sure you know the subject.
Taylor is a true homie. Super smart and straight forward. Best professor in the junior core.
Taylor's class was amazing. This guy  might be one of the smartest people I have ever met. His lectures are clear and blew my mind every time. He is probably my favorite professor at BYU.
greatest teacher i've ever had

My all time favorite professor at BYU. Professor Nadauld has it all going for him, he prepares you to be a terrific analyst by giving you the specific skill set you need. He really cares and is willing to spend time helping you! Without a doubt best professor!

great professor! So knowledgeable and really cares about each student.  Goes out of his way to make sure everyone is getting the concept of the material. One of my favorite professors! The class has a lot of work, but none of it is busy work.

This class is a part of the Junior Core, so you will work in a group in this class as well as the other core classes. Professor Nadauld is smart, funny, and likes his students. He teaches to students' understanding very well and really cares about you getting the material. He cares about your lives outside of his class and offers advice. He rocks!

I had heard from seniors to take the track that had Nadauld in it, and I was not disappointed. He does an incredible job at letting you know why what you are learning matters and where it fits into the big picture. His passion for finance and concern for the students are evident in every class. His real-world experience adds tons of value.
AMAZING COURSE.   LEARNED SO MUCH AND LAUGHED A TON

Nadauld is one of my all-time favorite professors! He kept the class interesting and did a good job explaining difficult concepts. I enjoyed the case work we did and felt like they were great learning experiences, even though it was more unstructured than what I am used to. I really loved his class and he was a great professor!
Best teacher at BYU. This guy explains things in such a way that your mind will be blown into smithereens and then it will come back together and everything will make sense.

Naduald is a champ. Best professor I have ever had. He becomes your friend. He is respectful, helpful, inspiring and caring. He wants you to be happy and do what you love. The content is hard but he is the best teacher the subject. You will love the class and learn a ton!
Best professor in the Marriott School. Entertaining and inspiring lectures.

Taylor Nadauld is the best teacher I have ever had at BYU. He treats his students as equals, and explains concepts incredibly well. Finance 401 is a hard class, but if you take from Nadauld and do the work you will understand the material and do well.
He's the man.

Easily the best teacher in the Finance Core.  He understands the students.  Keeps the class interesting and explains the concepts very well.  So funny and very helpful.  I never missed this class because I always knew it was worth my time.   Amazing class.  If you are taking this class, don't take it from anyone but Dr. Nadauld.
Best professor I have had at BYU.  Insightful, entertaining, and very clear at teaching.  You learn a lot, yet you are not overburdened by homework and studying.  Highly recommended.
BUS M 401. Best professor I have ever had at BYU. Not easy but manageable course load. You should try to arrange your schedule so you have him.
This course taught me essential networking and cybersecurity fundamentals that I use daily at my job. Content was highly interesting.

Seems like his class has evolved since last year, because the labs/homework that last year's reviews said took super long were not bad at all. Usually not longer than a couple hours if you utilized AI to help (which was allowed). Tests were time-consuming but mostly reasonable. I liked Wells overall and would take another class from him.

Hardest class in the Junior Core. Labs didn't connect well to lectures and would have taken on average 10+ hours without chat. Despite the difficulty, Prof. Wells is a great guy who genuinely cares and puts a lot of effort into the class. His tests are tough, but he's dedicated to student success. The other reviews are fresh after a tough project.

Content is all over the place and says 'we'll talk about it later' to everything, so you have no idea what is important. You can't do the labs without chatting everything. Tests are the toughest and you basically have to rewatch every class lecture and memorize everything he's ever said. The only applicable thing was content from a few videos

The only Core Professor that I really didn't enjoy. He is proud that he grades tougher than the other professors, the labs are impossible without chat and you don't learn anything from them, and his tests are impossible unless you rewatch and memorize every class recording. Also, the only professor i've had at BYU that incorporates 0 spirituality

This professor is one of the most frustrating at BYU. His lectures rarely align with the tests, and the homework is long and unrelated to what's covered in class. He often goes off on tangents, making it hard to follow. Since he's part of the core curriculum, you can't avoid him—good luck getting through his class.

This class was my worst experience at BYU to date. He seems like a decent person, it's really a shame. But the class was exam heavy and his exams were full of trick questions that chucked your hours of studying out the door. Unless you really like some good mind gymnastics, go into this course knowing it's going to be the worst one in the core.

Professor Wells is nice but the lectures are so hard to follow. In between almost every sentece, he says "uhhh". It was a distratctingly large amount! His labs are time consuming and I didn't feel like I learned much from them because chatgpt had to do most of the work. Nice guy though, just not my favorite teacher.

He is very full of himself and he's not good at teaching class content. I went on to get my masters in information systems at a different school and I can say he was the worst professor that I've had for a cyber security class. He's unavoidable but I just wanted to give him a bad rating. Most unimpressive professor the the BYU I've had.

He is a good professor,but I didnt learn much. Everything I did for labs was chatGpt generated. He gives good study guide for exams but his notes and slides are terrible,I didnt even know where to study from. Got terrible scores even tho I spend hours studying.Exams are closed book/note and a lot of to memorize. I barely showed up in there.

Professor Wells was great. However, I felt like I didn't learn much from the labs. His instructions are clear for the most part so you can get them done but half of the time I didn't know what I was doing or why.

He presents the class in an interesting way. The class isn't too hard if you pay attention. He makes it very clear what you need to do in order to achieve full marks. I'd recommend taking IS 201 from him to a friend.

Favorite professor at BYU. His lectures are the funnest! They are really interesting and engaging, so they were easy to follow. The class is really well organize. His tests can definitely be difficult and require a lot of studying and technical skills, but he prepares you well for them and they are definitely doable. 

TAKE THIS MANS CLASS!!

Professor Wells was awesome! He structured class so we could learn to code along with what he was doing which was very helpful. He is very good at answering questions outside of class and explaining the concepts we need to learn. I would highly recommend taking his class!
Professor Wells is exactly what you would hope for - I'm so glad I got to take the class from him. He knows his subject very well, is always ready to help, and is genuinely just a great guy.

I was soooo worried about this class. I know nothing about computers and I'm not tech savvy at all. But I still did amazing in this class because it was made for people like me. The grading requirements were clear, TA's were helpful, and going to class in person helped a lot too. As long as you're trying your best and going to class, you're good.

Overall great class. Dr. Wells explains concepts extremely well and helps you learn useful business skills and practice them in class. Participate, watch the textbook videos, and find a fun study group and the class won't be too bad at all! The TA lab was super helpful when I still wasn't understanding something. My favorite class at BYU so far!

Professor Wells is a wonderful teacher! He is very responsive on Microsoft Teams and wants you to succeed. The class isn't too back except for the VBA and WebDev projects so start on them early and don't be afraid to ask the TAs or even him for help! Overall entertaining lectures and very caring professor!

Professor Wells is so awesome, and I definitely would recommend taking IS 201 from him. The quizzes/projects aren't bad at all except for VBA and Web Dev which were a lot of work and you should NOT procrastinate them. He is very responsive to answer questions over Teams which came in clutch for those two projects. Take this class from Wells!
Hard class, moves fast. Keep up and study hard for tests. Wells is a very nice guy, but can seem intimidating because he’s so smart. Very nice professor.

I loved Dr. Wells! From what I had been told, this class was meant to be a monster. But he does an excellent job of explaining concepts to someone who has no background with IS (me). Expect a good amount of projects and a few midterms, some harder than others. But if you attend his lectures and read the textbook, you'll do fine.

This class was rough. Very test and project heavy and you are expected to learn a lot very different and complex things very quickly. Attendance isn't necessary as all info can be found in the book online anyways. You'll spend quite a bit of time on this class, especially on the final project. That one is a doozy.

Professor Wells was very nice and knowledgeable. He was always willing to help his students and there were TAs available at almost all times during every day. Class was a lot of busy work but that is to be expected when learning skills over content. Leave lots of time for projects and do them early if you can so you can get TA help.

Wells is an awesome professor. I really enjoyed his class and thought he taught well. One of my favorite things is he zoomed the lectures then put all the recorded lectures on learning suite afterwards. Class is just as hard as every other is201 class which isn't bad. All tests are open book/notes. Take from wells he's great.

Professor Wells clearly cares about is student, and has always been available to me for questions on projects and extra credit. You for sure have to work for this class, but the final is a project instead of a quiz, and there is 1% extra credit offered for the class. ABSOLULTY recommend Wells for this class. Great professor, clearly cares for us.

Professor Wells is a really great IS201 teacher! He is so good about answering questions (in and out of class) and overall does a great job at teaching the material. If you know IS, you could never show up to class and use the online materials given to you (MyEducator) and you could still get an A.

Professor Wells is amazing, very energetic lecturer and classes were entertaining. The class is tough, VBA is no joke. My one complaint is that points were often taken off assignments without explanations, would've been nice to know why points were taken off. Use the TA lab, they're a big help.

Even though this class is difficult, professor wells really wants you to succeed. My friends scared me about this class and it has been a good experience. He goes through everything slowly and makes sure everyone understands

I tried taking IS201 a year ago and was met by utter failure. I withdrew and took it again this year and the difference has been night and day. Prof. Wells will really work with you and listen and he shows he really cares and is willing to accommodate if needed. There is no other choice but Prof. Wells! Good teacher and a good person overall!

Awesome teacher, don't overlook VBA, that is the only hard part of the course. You will inevitably bomb VBA, so be sure to meticulously study for the other parts of the course. He is so easy to work with, interesting teacher, and respectful of everyone.

His strength is manifesting his desire for all of his students to succeed. Many times during lectures, patiently he would review material or processes he had just explained not 5 minutes prior; he wants EVERYONE on the same page for learning. Possess the intellect of a graduate degree but also the passion for learning of your 2nd grade teacher.
Dr. Wells is very smart and his lectures could be a little confusing, but he goes over what you need to know, and makes sure you understand the material.

Dr. Wells did a great job at teaching this class, especially since most people had no programming experience. The only reason I got an A is because I actually went to his lectures. If you practice, you'll be fine. He's also available and super helpful outside of class, if you need help go talk to him. He's way more useful than the TA's.

Dr. Wells is a great teacher. The topic he teaches is not easy, however everything he teaches is clearly explained in video tutorials posted on MyEducator by Dr. Gaskin. If you watch the videos and attend class, Easy A. If you don't prepare for class, it will be hard to keep up.

Good teacher, but nature of the class doesn't rely on lectures. Online textbook and videos are the most important. Dr. Wells is easy to access outside of class and gives good examples. Expect to work outside of class.

This class was tough. Professor Wells was nice and willing to help you, however, class lectures were sometimes confusing. Online materials were often more helpful than class. He gave great real-world examples, though.

Dr. Miller is one of the best professors and Sin and Atonement is one of the most interesting and well structured classes. I learned so much and Dr. Miller exposed us to a wide variety of frameworks for understanding these ideas. As long as you do the readings and put forth effort, you'll get an A. Everyone should take this class!

I had a bad experience with the class.I went to Dr. Miller looking to plan how to catch up and he was rude and unkind. He accused me of refusing to take responsibility for my own learning and was not accommodating in the least. I didn't consider it worth the fight, and I'm retaking the class from another professor. Don't recommend.

Dr. Miller is an excellent and model professor at BYU. He is the epitome of clear and precise teaching with minimal fluff. Even though he is very knowledgeable and well-respected, he is also very friendly and helpful if you come to him for help. He and the TAs have done wonders in helping me excel at logic.

Miller is easily the best professor I've ever taken a class from. He structured his 305 class in a way that really emphasizes learning over busy-work. There were no tests, so the class was graded on weekly problem sets and a few papers, which were very straightforward. The material was difficult, but Miller is the path to success.

He is a fantastic professor, the only graded assignments are 4 written exams, taken in class. He is very fair about them as well, the class previous, he shows the 3 possible prompts that could be chosen for the exam so you could study them. His lectures are essential to understand what is going on. The TA is very helpful as well if meeting with him

I could not say enough good things about this professor. Dr. Miller is truly exceptional. He is so charitable and simultaneously helped me strengthen my testimony and open my eyes to different perspectives. He's the best BYU professor you could ask for. I hope this man knows how appreciated he is. I've taken an interest in phil now bc of him!

One of my favorite classes so far, lectures are very entertaining. He gives you the prompts of the exam essays beforehand, and will pick two out of the three for you to choose from on test day. Exam grading was a bit harsh, but not awful. Some reading before class, and he provides notes as well on a doc. Overall, a very fun and enjoyable course!

He is an incredibly precise and inspiring lecturer. He's also very funny, well-tuned into student's needs and questions and never made me feel like my questions were not worth asking. He's deeply committed to everyone succeeding but also expects high quality work. Highly recommend his classes.

This has been my favorite class that I've taken so far at BYU! Class is not mandatory but interesting and important to go to in order to understand the material. The class is graded by 4 tests and a paper, but he gives the exam prompts a few days prior. I would highly recommend taking this class from Dr. Miller and just taking this class overall!
Dr. Miller is the best. He cares about his students and is fair. The concepts in the course are difficult, but he teaches them well. He uses the most precise language of any professor I know.

Dr. Miller's class was great but the logic was hard for me. Its easy for this kind of class to be really boring but he made it feel fun and exciting. The TAs were amazing. I did all my HW in the lab. Take it from him

Dr. Miller is an exceptional logic teacher. He goes fast but will slow down and check for understanding and slow way down if needed. This class was easy to do well in if you put the time in to work with the TAs. The TAs are incredible, they do a great job teaching and are very patient. Homework expectations are very reasonable, there are no tests.

This is such a cool class. You have 4 exams and if you pass them all you get an A. But you get retakes. If you screw up it wont screw you. It was a hard class for me but he helped me so much after every time I didnt pass to learn the material. Ive never had a professor actually care so much about helping me learn

Super kind professor that was always willing to answer questions. Lectures are very important to attend, the only homework was readings but it was the lectures we were tested on. There were only 4 tests and 1 paper which I liked, but it also meant each were worth 20% of our grade. Overall though, great class.

Dr. Miller is a very solid choice for any upper level philosophy course. He lectures perspicuously and is very accessible outside of class to speak about the material or assignments. You're graded by only a few things (for us, it was a problem set, two papers, and participation) so pay attention to due dates and plan ahead lest your grade suffer.

Just pay attention in class and skim the readings. All that really matters is to be there in order to answer the 4 writing assignments (which are done in class). They are super easy and the answers are practically given to you before hand it took maybe an hour to feel prepared. Best class and easiest class I've ever taken in all 4 years at BYU!

Dr. Miller was a good dude and super chill, however he is so passionate about the material that he often used such complex and big words that no one uses. So you sat their like dawg what? l consider myself a relatively smart person but dang rough words. The reading to prep for classes were substantial also. Only 4 exams, you gotta take hecka notes

Professor Gray really wanted everyone to succeed. Grading criteria is clear and the test questions are given beforehand so you can literally write your answers using notes, memorize them, and write them down for the tests without any surprises. If you put in at least some effort you will get an A. Readings aren't necessary if attending lectures.
His classes are genuinely interesting and the class isn't extremely difficult.

Loved Phil110 with Dr. Miller. Provided compelling lectures in every class while doing a great job at incorporating modern ideas about religion and life with philosophy. Encourages class participation and can moderate discussions in a fascinating fashion. I would absolutely take his class again.

Had a super solid experience with Dr. Miller. Cool guy, knows his stuff for sure. The readings took 2-3 tries to sink in, but it is a philosophy class. I liked how he did his exams, 3 prompts given the class before, he picked 2 of the 3 prompts, and you choose 1 to write on. It's just the 4 papers and a final one for the grades. Solid lecturer too.

The class was very interesting and also pretty easy. They only things that are graded are 4 exams (he gives you the questions a few days before) and a final paper. Go to class and take notes and you will be fine. If you are taking this for a GE take professor miller.

Super relaxed class and a great atmosphere. he wants all of his students to do well and doesn't stress them out. No homework assignments and just 4 "exams" and a term paper. He's a really funny guy and makes the class very discussion based. If you're looking for an easy class take this one!

Very relaxed and chill, cares about the students well being and is a quirky type of funny. Very patient and willing to re-explain anything needed, loves discussion and makes the classroom relaxed and casual.

Very engaging. I love his enthusiasm, and he is so so patient. He really wants everyone to succeed. His teaching methods were refreshing and felt more modern compared to many other professors who stress students out. Super clear teaching. He doesn't want to stress students, just wants to teach them. Definitely take from Dr. Miller.

Prof. Miller is super eloquent, so sometimes simpler concepts can sound more complex when he teaches them. However, he's clear in what he says, so if you can keep up with what he's saying, it'll probably make sense. I enjoyed his lectures and appreciated the class structure - no required homework, all we got graded on were four retake-able tests.
lots of exams, but gives you test questions ahead of time, and all the answers are given in lecture. Basically just have to memorize notes but you gotta go to class to get the notes.

The grade was almost completely based on a few essays. No tests or quizzes, tho. His teaching style is a little bit inexperienced and sloppy and he talks too much, which takes up most of the class period. A different professor probably could have gotten through the material twice as fast. Still, it was pretty easy if you grasp philosophy easily

Took this class during COVID. Had issues turning in assignments cuz of family drama and wifi issues. He always accepted late work without marking down. He was super flexible to work with. I got kind of freaked out cuz the material was pretty hard and was lost in the class. I told him and he went over the stuff over and over with me until I got it

Professor Miller is good at explaining hard concepts. The material is kind of hard for an intro class. it seemed kind of advanced. Every test-paper is open note but he grades hard because of it. He gives you all the lecture notes, so basically all you have to do is copy what he says and you'll get an A. Idk why people had a hard time lol.

He is an ok professor. He's a nice guy but a tough grader. He doesn't admit to being wrong about things. Just make sure that you know what he expects on your papers because the only way to get an A is to agree with everything he says. There are four Essays in the class. The reading was not long. It was difficult to understand. Good Luck!
This was a fun approach to an intro class. Attendance matters because of pop quizzes. But if you miss class, he's happy to help if you go to his office during office hours.

Dr. Cannon is one of the best professors out there! She knows how to teach very well, and she knows how to make it applicable. We also had spiritual thoughts in every class which I LOVED. Dr. Cannon really cares about here students and respects there time so I never felt like there was any busy work. It was a very well balanced class.

Dr. Cannon made MATH 112 much more manageable with clear explanations and lots of support outside class. She offers exam retakes and extra credit, and the labs/homework closely matched test questions. Math is hard, but she really tries to help students succeed!
Great teacher and great class. Willing to answer any questions and takes time to make sure you understand the material.
Doctor Cannon was amazing!! I would take her again in a heart beat! She truly cares about her students and wants them to succeed!!

Calc II is a really hard class. Lectures and recitation help (kinda), but homework is where you really learn, and there's a lot (6 assignments a week). Midterms are difficult, but the final is manageable. You need a lot of time to understand the material. Cannon is kind, funny, and understanding, I just wish I had more time to fully get everything.

Dr. Cannon is probably one of the best calc professors you'll find at byu, or anywhere for that matter! It's a hard to teach class because you have a large range of students from Engineering/ Math majors, to education, business and premed majors who haven't done math in a while, but she find a good balance and does a great job with her class.

I really liked Dr. Cannon, although some youtube videos were much clearer than her lectures. Not a lot of homework, short online portion after every lecture and 1 written a week. Would reccomend to anyone taking Calc 1.

Dr. Cannon was an amazing professor who was passionate and great at teaching. Homework is participation-based; exams are easy if you do the study guide and study the review slides, and you can retake quizzes. It sometimes feels kinda boring because its ELED math.
hw helps a lot

I love Dr. Cannon! I went into the semester feeling nervous to take calculus since I hadn't taken a math class for a year. I should not have worried. Dr. Cannon is kind, patient, and does a great job explaining things. She cares about her students and answers any questions we may have. I also love her math-related spiritual quotes.

Dr. Cannon explains calc clearly and answers any questions students may have. Lots of opportunities in lecture to participate, which helped me learn better. Material is difficult, but the homework is useful and manageable. Willing to give extensions, extra credit, and makeup points for missed multiple choice exam problems. Take MATH 112 from her!!!

Very good professor. My only complaint is that I don't think lab attendance should be mandatory. If you don't go and get a bad grade because you didn't learn then that's your fault. But if you can get a good grade without labs and lectures you shouldn't be punished for being ahead.

Also having a midterm the week before finals is bad.
She is a great teacher, I love her teaching style. The class was hard but that's just because its calc. She explained everything very well in lecture and is very open.

I LOVE DR. CANNON.  She teaches very clearly and has clear expectations of what she wants you to get out of an assignment,  No busy-work; everything felt super important.  She also allows redos on homework for full credit.  You will actually LEARN in this class

Professor Cannon is awesome! She used to teach AP Calculus so she knows how to teach it in a way that is simple and understandable. There are lectures MWF with labs TTh. She provides guided notes for lectures and worksheets for labs. She lets us retake the MCQ section of exams. You'll get a great base understanding of calculus.

She is sincerely an amazing teacher. She does everything that she can to make sure that each concept is understood. The homework is graded off of participation so it really just depends on if you actually want to learn. The tests are very easy if you have done the homework and gone to class. I absolutely recommend her.

For Math305, pay attention in class and take good notes. For tests, there are great reviews by the TA and test corrections afterward, but those are graded too so make sure they're well done. She is a great instructor and really knows her stuff. She's funny, kind, and very eager to help her students.

Dr. Cannon is great! She teaches very simply and really wants to make sure that we understand the content. The class is very organized and you have 2 opportunities to go to elementary schools to ask students math questions. She's willing to meet with you outside of class to clarify things. Definitely take MTHED 305 from her!

Dr. Cannon's class is wonderful! She really focuses on you learning and understanding the content rather than getting a good grade. She is extremely respectful and kind to everyone. The homework was basically a participation grade only. Three tests, all of which were pretty simple and straight to the point. All together, Dr. Cannon is amazing!!

Take this course from Dr. Cannon!! She is extremely caring and wants everyone to succeed. Class is very engaging and the homework is easy and helpful. You'll have three exams that are not too difficult and she allows for test corrections. She teaches so well and her doors are always open for additional help. Take from Dr. Cannon!

I took Math 112. There were about 2-4 homework's each week, however you only have to get 80 percent on the homework, and she would manually enter in that you got a 100%. She also allowed you to request extension on the homework if didn't get it done. She has great study guides to prepare you for each test! I strongly recommend Prof. Cannon!

Professor Cannon is an amazing professor. She knows how to teach and teaches things WELL. The layout of the class is very organized, you always know what's expected of you, and she makes it easy to succeed. She prepares you well for the tests, but if something goes wrong, you can do test corrections! 10/10 do recommend taking MATH ED 305 from her!

Professor Cannon is AMAZING!! She teaches the content really well and genuinely cares for her students. I never realized a math class could be so spiritually strengthening. She hits on all of the aims for BYU and deserves recognition! This class wasn't hard at all!

I really enjoyed this class and Dr. Cannon was a great professor. She is super kind and really knows her stuff. I learned a lot in her class and felt that it was a perfect amount of workload. You have homework every class, but it's not hard and takes maybe an hour. Homework is based on participation and the tests are fair.

I really enjoyed this class with Prof. Cannon! She has a really kind and thoughtful heart! She is a very good teacher, and will work hard to help you understand. There are homework assignments every day after class, but none of them were too difficult.

I loved this class. I learned so much and I am more confident as a future teacher. She is a tough grader and needs specific answers on tests and etc. There are test corrections and you can get up to 1/2 back. The text book is very helpful. There are a few classes done in elementary schools. Very helpful but hard to get to if you don't have a car.

Dr. Cannon is great! I learned a ton about using technology to teach math, and I even learned some interesting new math. There was no busywork and the workload was very manageable. She clearly cares about her students and she's always willing and available to talk outside class. Also, she's pretty lenient about late work. Great professor.

Emery is a good professor overall, lectures aren't anything special but she teaches and doesn't waste time. She corrected her grading time, getting nearly all the lab reports in before the final. She will nit pick lab reports so be extra cautious with your formatting.

Its a very hard class but she does a great job as a professor especially being an adjunct who has to rely on Professor Sorensen's policies.
Very hard class with A LOT of homework but that's the nature of the class.
Only big problem is having a midterm the week before finals. Causes too much burnout in students especially when every class does it.

Most of the things students didn't like about her class were dictated by Dr. Sorensen who designed the course, and were out of her hands as an adjunct professor. She was very caring, and if you know how to make and use an equation sheet, then the tests are pretty easy too. Several HW, quiz, attendance are dropped and there's decent extra credit.

Gets a bad rap because the class is pretty tough. She was relatable and nice enough. Grading was strict, but marginal extra credit is offered. Her teaching is very straightforward. Being an adjunct, there are probably some policies outside of her control. Attendance quizzes can actually sway your grade a few percent.

She reads the other professor's slides and gives answers without any process. She doesn't have the enthusiasm to teach sometimes and tends to just do too much instead of explaining the basics and keeping it as simple as possible. Formulas are given but explanations are not so the best advice on how to pass would be to take Sorensen instead.

Dr Emery Mechanics class: Lectures felt VERY unprepared for. First she would read Dr. Sorensen's (a different professor) slides word for word. Second she would give you the equations you needed for the homework. and that was it. She never walked through a full homework problem and did not explain things. I found you-tube more helpful.

Dr. Bateman is a great professor. You can tell he cares about what he is teaching and he wants you to become the best foreign language teacher you can be too. I would take this course again. It really help me practice teaching techniques in a safe environment where I didnt feel judged. His feedback was always helpful.

This class has little assignments throughout the semester.  Overall, they are not tough.  If you do them you will do fine, only one test and it is only 10% of your grade.  It is an easy A, but does have lots of little assignments.  Great teacher and I really learned a lot and it was my favorite portuguese class.
Was super easy and he's pretty nice, very liberal though... that can get kind of annoying but you'll get an A without too much blood, sweat and tears...
She is so sweet and genuine. Handles hard topics in an aware way and cares a lot about the students.

Take a class from Professor Washburn. Honestly, the most enjoyable religion class I've ever had. Most of the class is a discussion. You have some readings prior to class and need to share a quote you liked from them and why. No final or tests. Just a project that you work on throughout the semester/term

Probably one of the nicest professors at BYU. Great at keeping things Christ-centered. You choose what to read from the provided list, completing a minimum of 45 minutes of reading and a reflection before each class. Class is Zoom-recorded so you can join remotely if needed or make up missed classes by watching and writing her an email about it.

She is so kind! She LOVES her students and the gospel and you can feel it in her classroom as she testifies and teaches. Her assignments are very meaningful, not busy work, and if taken seriously, will help you grow your testimony. It's very easy to make up absences and she's so willing to work with you.

Amazing teacher! Very loving and caring for all of her students. Very insightful and meaningful assignments and class discussions. The principles taught in her class are all very useful and applicable to everyone's lives!

She is seriously the best!! Super easy work and so willing to help out with any projects or questions. She requires and class prep and a few assignments per week and no finals just one big project that is so doable.
Very well-read, very understanding of student situations. Gives good feedback, but it comes in pretty late. One of the best professors I've had
Class preps did take some time but they were helpful for class enjoyed her lectures super caring

This was an amazing class. The discussions were great and she really cares about each and every one of her students opinions. There are easy weekly reeding assignments but overall I would take it again.

Dr Washburn is awesome and super sweet. The class had a lot of assignments, but they were simple and actually meaningful (not just busy work). There are no exams. She uses a variety of teaching styles (group work, individual reflection, activities). She is SO flexible and understanding of her students.
He's the best professor ever! He's so funny and makes class interesting. I would recommend him for writing 150. As you long put in the work, you'll do well. He wants to help in any way.

First of all, don't buy the textbook. There are 3 main papers, which are not very hard to do and he spreads them out so you have time to do them and avoid cramming. Professor Brown genuinely loves teaching this class and you'll never have a boring lecture. He also offers extra credit if you go to the writing center.

Prof. Brown is honestly amazing. He isn't too tough of a grader, makes his expectations really clear, and definitely genuinely wants to help you do the best you can. The 4 papers are really useful and he offers a lot of support (instructor conferences) as well as extra credit for going to the writing center. He's pretty funny to boot.

As a basic writing class, it was enjoyable. There are 4 main papers, reading that you can basically skim and easy (and infrequent) small assignments. He offers extra credit by going to the writing center for papers and is a relatively easy grader. His classes weren't SUPERB but weren't sleep inducing. Decent choice for a GE.

For MSB 494r, the internship was good, but the class was not. I learned nothing about dev or commercial real estate in class. The only grades were a couple of quizzes; he would say they were on a topic, and then they would be on something different. He also would get off on random tangents and was generally not clear about anything he taught.

Terrible, absolutely terrible. I thought that by taking this class I would actually learn about real estate. Every day he gets up and just talks about random things that have nothing to do with real estate and loves to talk about how corrupt the government is. Quizzes are impossible unless you've done the reading at least 3 times. Horrible class.
Not a fan of his behavior
He is down-to-earth, knowledgeable, interesting and really cares about his students. Take a class from him if you get the chance.

Excellent professor.Very entertaining and provides many real world examples.We are only in the beginning of the semester, but I have already learned a lot.Not a typical bookish professor.He touches briefly on boring text topic, and expounds on what is really important for you to learn. Highly recommended class to anyone wanting to be in Real Estate

Excellent professor!He teaches real world stuff which is what students need.  As an MBA student,I enjoy learning real world stuff than book theories.Peterson challenges your thoughts and he makes you think through your answers.If u are up for learning real world stuff, this class is for you. If you are a booky type, take boring accounting classes.

Tom was an awesome teacher.  I only took this class because it fit into my schedule, but he made me keep wanting to come back.  He really cares about the students and has many interesting stories and experiences.
Best class the Marriott School   offers! Take Prof Peterson's class if you want to learn how the real world works.
One of the best classes i have ever taken!

I never felt like we learned anything in the class.  He just liked to talk in front of the class about whatever he wanted and changed directions at the whim of a hat.  Fall 2008 was his first semester, so he is learning how to be a teacher.  He said next semester would be very different.  Only time will tell.

Prof Peterson did well in the real estate world so he has a strong network and real world experience. However, as a teacher, he is clueless. His class is random and disjointed. The tests are ill-prepared and frustrating. Fall 2008 is his first semester teaching so there's hope that he will get things straightened out (learn how to teach) soon.

Professor Wayment is one of my favorite professors so far! I'll admit, his lectures are kinda all over the place and easy to zone out to but it's actually really fun. The "textbook" is The Iliad, and we read it throughout the semester as well as some other texts and plays. Overall, it's a pretty easy class; just make sure you learn the myths.

Wayment was definitely one of my favorite professors this semester. He really cared about me and the other students, and challenged us to think outside the box in ways I didn't expect. Class was not very hard if you pay attention and do the readings, which made it easy to take things out of the class and apply them.

This class can be an essay A if you show up take notes, good amount of reading outside of class but nothing to crazy and I often enjoyed what I read. He is super chill, funny and genuinely care for his students. If it wasn't completely different from my major, I would definitely take his other classes in the future

This class was very informative and interesting, but his attitude felt very out-of-place at a religious university. Although attendance isn't taken, exams are graded majorly on what is said in lectures. Other than that, there were a few discussions, a recitation, and a creative project. It's an easy class, but I wasn't a fan of his teaching style.
I loved his ability to teach hard concepts and connect to the class. He really was a joy to have and learn from. 11/10 would take again!

Professor Wayment's lectures were my favorite to attend this semester! He was super engaging and such AN INCREDIBLE Professor! There were two papers that were our tests, and while there was a lot of reading you did not really need to do all of it. I would recommend going to the lectures to know what's going on.

Dr. Wayment is very knowledgeable about Greek myths and ancient Greek culture. Definitely a fun, easy credit and a great way to feed your inner mythology nerd! Overall grade consisted of a few exams, quizzes, and a large creative project, but honestly, as long as you read and generally pay attention, you will be just fine!

Professor Wayment understands that most are there for GE's and makes it easy to get an A. That being said, his attempts to broaden our views on the world often come from jabs at the LDS church, making it hard to share anything in class related to church. Interesting facts, but didn't feel like a class for a religious university.

This was a great class! It was super interesting, just make sure you go to lectures to know what's going on (even though attendance isn't taken). Tests were super easy and pretty short. Only one paper/project that basically everyone got an A on if you did it. Readings can be time-consuming but won't wreck your grade if you don't do all of them.

Professor Wayment speaks in such a kind and caring way, it's so clear that he doesn't want to trick you, he just wants you to consider other ways to look at things. This was more spiritually uplifting than any religion class I've taken. I looked forward to every class and am going to miss it a lot!

Professor Wayment has really fun, enjoyable lectures. There is a lot of discussion so if that isn't your thing, this may not be the best option. He said himself he wasn't trying to make it a hard class. He recognized most people are there for the GE. He did a great job explaining why myth was interesting and worked to apply it to our lives.

Dr. Wayment is far and away my favorite professor at BYU. For his Greek classes, we typically read the scheduled passages together as a class, taking turns reading a section. We were expected to come having already prepared the passage, but if you happened not to prepare for a day, it wasn't a big deal.

dr wayment is a nice guy and it's funny how on the first day he admits that he's extremely liberal as a disclaimer but that he's not trying to convert anyone to liberalism. Class is easy, no true tests just in-class quizzes that are a breeze if you're good at memorizing. I found the class interesting and it's a super easy A so I'd recommend

Professor Wayment is the best and I LOVED this Greek and Roman mythology class. It got me applying things outside of the classroom in the way I think and view the world, and if that's not a success, I don't know what is. I even read all of the assigned reading because he made it so enjoyable! (Audible audio books recommended unless you love paper)
Professor Hilton is amazing!

This is my favorite Professor at BYU. The class is incredibly organized and easy to understand. She is also a very understanding person and is willing to help with anything you need. Really can't emphasize enough how incredible she is.
Take this if you are bad at math.
Be ready to pace yourself. You need to make sure you have enough time to do the assignments each week.

I loved Professor Hilton! Most of the class is watching videos that would be the lecture if you were in person. The weekly assignments are predictable and not hard. There are a ton of rescources for sucess. The exams are open note and have 2 tries. The TA lab is amazing and Professor Hilton is amazing about meeting with you if you need help.

Dr. Hilton is incredible, and this class is super fun. You don't have to do any math since the R Shiny app does it for you. Lectures are a great length. Tests are open note, book, etc. Concepts were broken down and made very simple/clear to understand. I was afraid of this class for nothing - 10/10 recommend.
Super knowledgeable teacher and the exams are open notes. I thought this class would be harder but it is actually the class I am doing the best on this semester. Add the class without fear.
If you actually watch the videos and do the homework, you will be just fine. I was nervous to take stats but prof Hilton is actually the best and makes it easy to understand. Highly recommend!

I seriously cannot say enough great things about Professor Hilton!!! She was the most organized, involved professor I've ever had. She makes learning stats manageable and provides so many resources to help you succeed like guided notes, TA open zoom labs everyday which is great for asking homework questions and so much more. Take this class!!!
Take this class online from Prof Hilton! Tests are all open note with multiple chances! Lectures are easy to follow along and she starts each lecture with a spiritual thought and quote, which I love.

Professor Hilton is THE BEST! This class is an easy A, not because it's useless, but because she provides tons of resources, practice exams, and study guides you can use in the exam that actually help you learn, not just memorize. She has review videos, multiple exam attempts, and easy extra credit. I hate stats and I would take this class again.

This was a very well done online class! Prof. Hilton is a great teacher, and was very clear. It was one or two hw assignments a week that would take me maybe an hour, and studying for the exam was made very easy by well done study guides and information. Loved it and would highly recommend.
Great teacher. Be sure to put in the effort and watch all of her videos. She prepares her material very well!

Sister Hilton is a great professor. I took this class online over spring/summer semesters. It took me about 3-4 hours max each week to finish the homework and other assignments. The TAs are great and you get 2 chances on all exams and 3 on HW assignments.

Sister Hilton was great. I took this class over the Sprummer semester (spring/summer) online and it was pretty chill. I did the homework the week of and it probably took me at most 4 hours total to finish everything. You get two chances on all exams and the TAs are great.

Professor Hilton is the best STAT teacher at BYU. I took her class online. She is kind and good at helping students. Weekly hour long TA lab required. Challenging concepts but she explains them well. Lots of homework. Tests are difficult but open note and she provides lots of resources. Not my favorite class subject and not easy but very doable.
I would not have passed this class if the test wasn't open note!! I hated doing the homework and the lectures were hecka boring, but it was relatively easy to get an A.

If you need to take stats and don't have a lot of time available, this is the perfect course for you. The note guides are amazing, the midterms and the final are open book, and her video lectures are so good! The TAs she picks are also great, and she responds very quickly to emails.

Don't hesitate taking this class. Tiffany is one of the best math professors I have ever had. Her recorded lectures are clear, her class organized to succeed. You will not regret this class. I cannot imagine having to sit through 3 hours a week of this class now that I experienced the online version.

Dr. Hilton is the actual best professor for stats. I was scared to take a class like this online but she actually made it as smooth of a process as possible for us to be successful. Great explanations, multiple opportunities on tests and quizzes, and she makes a packet to guide your note taking. She is so awesome!

I was a little nervous to take this class online, but it was great! Prof. Hilton manages to show she cares even through video. There are guided notes that make working through the weekly material not too bad! You can take everything at your own pace. You have 3 tries on every quiz, 2 tries on every exam and it is all open note! Loved this class!

This class was the best! By far the best way to take STAT121. The amount of work was fair and I never felt like I was doing busy work which I feel is common for an online course. Tests are open note and class material. Would recommend!

An incredible professor! I usually really struggle with math, but I found this class super interesting and manageable. The workload is fair and feels applicable to real life. I think that this class improved my numerical abilities. There is also a lot of supports and helpful resources provided. A genuinely ideal online course.

Professor Hilton is the best! This is by far the easiest and best organized online class I have ever taken. It's hard not to get an A in this class. You get 3 attempts for the unit quizzes and the exams are open note and you get 2 attempts. She gives you fill in notes and walks you through how to do the homework. She's awesome!

Tiffany makes this class super easy. I honestly never spent more than 3 hours on it a week. She breaks down the material really well and I definitely got a beginners taste into stats. It is super easy to get an A+ if you do the work on time, take all the chances given to you (they take highest scores) and know how to navigate your notes!

AMAZING professor and easiest class I have ever taken at BYU.
Two attempts on exams, extra credit opportunities, and a million ways to succeed. Take online if you want to skip lectures. If you've taken higher-level math courses, this class will be a breeze.
So easy. Just take the class fully online to save time not going to lecture. Every test can be taken twice. I never studied for this class.

This was the easiest class I have taken (although I still feel like I learned a lot). Everything is super well organized and if you want you can work ahead of the schedule which is nice. The textbook is provided online and I never read it while still getting an A. Tests were open-note and easy. Piece of advice: Watch the lectures at 2x speed.

Dr. Hilton was great! I took STATS 121 online, and it was really well-organized. I spent maybe three hours a week total on all the lectures and assignments, and the TAs are all super helpful. She also allows for two attempts on all exams including the final, and this class was much easier than I thought it would be, especially after a mission.

Professor Hilton was an amazing professor if you want to complete the languages of learning credit, online, with a pretty easy A. She lets you use notes on tests and if you do the homeworks everything is pretty straightforward.

This isn't the most engaging class, but it's super easy. Two homework assignments and an online lab each week. You get three tries on homework assignments and two attempts on exams. Exams are open note, and as long as you take good notes you should be fine. I only put in 4 hours a week into this class and I still got an A.

Two homework assignments a week. One learning lab over zoom a week. (you can choose what day) Three tests throughout the semester. Hard concepts to grasp but if you follow her note taking then you'll be okay as you can use that in your tests. All tests are open note and proctored (NO AI or other humans, Or google). I didnt study, just used my notes

Usually online classes are difficult, but this one is so easy. Professor Hilton splits her videos up so that they don't feel long and boring. Quizzes are sometimes hard to score well on, but you get 3 attempts each time. The online labs are easy and helpful. I hate online labs, but I actually really liked these ones. The professor is super sweet.

This is one of the greatest classes I have ever taken. If you learn well in a Live Remote Delivery setting, this class is for you! She is an excellent teacher and everything is set up for you to succeed! If you put in the 6 hours a week, you will do well. I think every BYU Professor should learn from Professor Hilton how to create an online class.

Tiffany is an icon. She makes this class as easy to understand as she can. She also inspired me by her little spiritual quotes every video, they hit deep sometimes. This class was completely online and easy to navigate and super easy to understand. Plus she is low-key funny and enjoyable to listen to. Save yourself time and take it from Tiff!!!!

Tiffany's STAT121 class was well-organized with lots of resources to help you succeed, like the great study guide and helpful TAs. unstuck ai was a game-changer for my prep. Open-note tests made it manageable, just stay engaged and you'll do well.

I was nervous at first taking Stats because it's notoriously difficult, but Prof. Hilton really prepares you for exams and teaches the subjects clearly. Online class - attendance is mandatory for a 1x per week lab (there are so many different available times during the week, so I wouldn't worry about it). Definitely take the practice exams!
Super organized, very clear teaching. Always looking to improve the course and how she teaches. Very available and willing to work with you. Just a great teacher.

Took this class online, was organized very well. Broke her lectures into smaller videos so they didn't drag on forever. Very kind, always willing to help answer questions. TAs are super helpful, study guide is the BEST. If you struggle with stats, take her class; as long as you give effort you can totally pass!
