Such an awesome and organized class. She gave so many opportunities to ask questions if you needed help and did everything to help you succeed. Super easy online stats course. Watched 2 45 min lectures a week and took 1 quiz where you got 3 tries. 2 tries on tests, can use notes and internet on tests too. I learned so much in this class

Pro Hilton is amazing! Her online stats is 100% the best way to take it. 2 midterms, 1 final all open note and you get 2 attempts. She does great at explaining concepts and there are a ton of TAs who can help you understand things. There are many resources to help you succeed. I was worried about this class but it ended up being not bad at all.
She is the best. Got a lot out of the class and was successful due to the immense amount of resources and clear, easy-to-follow lectures.
Prof. Hilton's online class is one of the best I've taken. Clear instructions, accessible TAs, two attempts on open book/note exams, and no math required thanks to the university stats app.

Tiffany was one of the best professors I've ever had. 3 tries for homework quizzes, 2 tries on tests, open note and open internet tests. Always responded quickly to emails and was super willing to meet with you if you needed extra help. Did everything to help you succeed. Could not recommend her more. If you have to take STAT121 take it with her!

Pro Hilton was a great teacher and made everything super clear. I took the online version and you just have to watch some lecture videos then do the homework. The tests and open note and there are 3 total. You have to attend a lab every week which was kinda annoying but helpful. TAs are always available to help over zoom. Great class!!

I was not excited at all about stats, but I actually really enjoyed it because of Dr. Hilton. Idk if I would've enjoyed it as much with any other professor. She is so straightforward and teaches clearly and concisely. It's a decent amount of work but she provides you with all the tools to succeed. She is also so kind and is always available to help

Rly good teacher. But.. Ta zoom meeting once a week(they love to yap). Can't see practice exam answers which defeats the purpose of taking one to try and study. Most of all, you won't learn much unless you are specifically a stat major. Most of it is plugging numbers on the r-shiny app and letting it tell you the answer. Oh, and its just boring....

I struggled big time in this class. Professor Hilton is really nice but when you ask for help it's very "copy, paste" help. Meaning she just tells you to study and to ask TAs which is not really helpful when you are already doing it. Test are so hard and everyone struggles. She does not really take time to explain things just goes through it fast.

Boy do I love this lady. She is so kind and passionate about what she does. She is always offering help and her TAs are really great too. She teaches in a very clear and concise way. She also offers lots of extra credit, so please take advantage of it. If you put in solid effort, you should get a good grade. Also, study in advance for the final.

I finished with an A but I had to fight for my life. There are so many assignments and test but she is the most caring professor ever. DO THE EXTRA CREDIT! She cares and loves her students. 3 lessons and quizzes a week, 3 midterms, one final. Open lab and times to get a better understanding. Most organized and great online class set up.
Professor Hilton is super nice

Sister Hilton as a person is great, however I did not enjoy how her class was setup online. Lectures were pretty easy but were always formatted the same. I found it hard to grasp the minute differences between concepts because all the notes looked the same, all we learned to do was plug in numbers to a calculator or table.

Everything about this class was easy except there is a lot of busy work during the week so sometimes it felt like a lot but it wasn't hard, just time consuming. The exams were clear and the review was accurate. She explains everything super well in her video lectures.
best online class I've ever taken. I feel like I actually learned in her lectures, and she explained things thoroughly and clearly. 10/10 would recommend

She is a great professor; her lectures were the most helpful thing in this class. Stats was just extremely hard for me, but I promise, she is a great professor. almost everything is open note. Your test questions are similar to quiz questions. She gives you a lot of resources to help you. If you reach out, she always helps.

I took Accounting 200 with Professor Larson. If you liked that class. Don't take this. It's the exact opposite. It feels like so much information is being thrown at you all at once and they're just hoping something sticks. I don't feel like the goal is to help students truly learn. Disappointed.

I took Professor Hilton's Stats 121 class online over the summer and absolutely loved it. She is so good at explaining concepts and she was always encouraging us to talk to her or the TAs if we needed help. She offered plenty of extra credit and had plenty of review material for her exams. Professor Hilton is amazing!

I hate math. I loved this class. I'd never taken a STATS class before, but I really enjoyed Dr. Hilton's. If you're worried about taking this class, don't be. The material is fairly easy and her notetaking system is great! Quizlet was super helpful. 

(PS: I took this class through Independent Study)

This is a very forgiving class. There are extra credit opportunities offered all the time and you have every opportunity to succeed because of it. I did all the extra credit and my grade went nearly a whole letter. The material is challenging enough that you will need time to study before the tests but there are plenty of resources to be prepared.

By far the best professor I've had at BYU!! Was very caring and wants to see you succeed. Lectures are extremely clear and easy to understand with study guide notes provided. There were lots of opportunities for help through Zoom, weekly TA review sessions, and practice quizzes/ exams. As well as, extra credit points each week and on exams.

I don't have much to add to the other reviews. Tiffany will make you feel like she cares even though you'll probably only ever see a recording of her. She teaches clearly, has possibly the most organized online class ever created, and will help any student succeed that wants to. If you have to take stats, take it online from her.

I took stats online and it was a great experience. It was not too hard as long as you kept on top of the lessons. There were a lot of ways to get extra help in this class and she made all the topics easy to understand. Great class!

I took this course through BYU independent study. The course was set up very well! Each lecture was followed by a practice quiz (with unlimited attempts) and a credit quiz. Before each exam, there were practice exams and exam review lectures to ensure you knew each concept. The set up was so efficient, I didn't even take notes throughout the course

If you're taking stats 121 just stop looking. Take it from Tiffany. Lectures are extremely clear and she is so easy to work with. I bombed the first exam and she pointed out a syllabus section that allows a student to drop a test score and replace it with the average of the other three. She cares about your success!

I took stats online with Tiffany and it was a great experience. The lectures were great and there was always someone to ask questions to, whether it be Tiffany or a TA. When an assignment wasn't graded by my TA before an exam, Tiffany went in and graded it herself. Lots of extra credit opportunities and the tests weren't horrible.

3 midterms and a final exam that accumulate 70% of your total grade. Stay diligent and keep up with the course material and you'll get an A! Cramming before the tests won't work. Tiffany is helpful and knows what she's talking about. There's a textbook you can get but she never refers to it. You'll be okay with the study guides she provides.

Professor Hilton was amazing! The class online was so well organized and well paced. I was nervous because I'm terrible at math, but Professor Hilton explained everything so well and she and the TAs were super accessible to answer questions. I always felt very prepared for quizzes and tests, and there was also lots of extra credit available.

Be ready for multiple quizzes almost every day. I have had some issues with the TA and unfair grading, just watch your grade for that. I did not enjoy the time and I worked so hard for a poor grade. This class is offered by other professors and I highly recommend taking it from them, this is a level 100 but very hard.

This class is very well organized. She is a great teacher and responds to emails very quickly and respectfully. She is very helpful! You don't get to see what you got wrong on the test unless you go to the labs which I didn't love, but would strongly recommend.

Despite my grade, Dr. Hilton is a great. Great prerecorded lectures. Explains things well. Makes it easy to succeed and is accessible outside of class. Wish I had taken more time to study and master the material. For the first time in my academic career, I feel I earned the grade I deserved, and I should have done better (which was VERY possible).

I have never been good in math classes, but Tiffany made my experience so easy! The practice and credit quizzes are designed so expertly to help prepare us for the exam. She runs so many practice questions to allow us to practice doing the questions on the exams on our own. Her lectures are spiritually focused and compact with content.

Professor Hilton is amazing. If you want to do good in her class and are willing to put in the effort you will. She provides SO many recourses outside of the lessons to learn better. Just put in the work and take advantage of the resources she provides and you'll do great.

Took it as an online class.  It was pretty easy; just watch the lecture, take the credit quiz, and take the exams.  Easy A.  She definitely provides plenty of help resources so if you do run into issues there is help.  If you do have an issue she is quick to respond and wants to help.

This is the best online class ever. Is it hard? yes. but so is any stats class. Highly recommend this class online, you can complete the work on your own time as long as its before the due date. The TA's and Tiffany are EXTREMELY accessible its very nice. I got a B but just cause I'm not great at math. an A is completely achievable in this class.

She is the BEST. So good at explaining concepts. If you watch the video lectures and fill out her helpful note sheets, you'll do well. She is so helpful to meet with over Zoom, my classmate went over his previous test with her and she gave him points back because he demonstrated that he understood the concepts he missed points on. She really cares.

BEST ONLINE CLASS EVER, the optional textbook was NOT needed, save yourself the 25 bucks, but I have so many other friends that took stats and wish they did it with Tiffany. Im telling you she offers extra credit, awesome labs, TA's have a zoom link open almost the entire day, helpful recordings, better organized than all of my in person classes.

Tiff is so cute. Her smile in every lecture made my day. Loved the class. I hate math and i took stats in high school but she made it bearable. The only thing I didn't like about the class was that you have due dates every other day instead of Saturday at 11:59 like other online classes.

I would recommend Professor Hilton to ANYONE. She makes the course simple to follow and provides so many opportunities for help outside of the class - TAs are  ALWAYS, I was in office hours all of the time! Her exams are very fair and she simplifies the content as much as possible. I felt like I was learning but not overwhelmed

Prof. Hilton was fantastic as an online teacher. I'm not a math person, but this class felt so doable thanks to her video lectures and Canvas setup. Tests were harder than the review tests, but it still wasn't too bad. Only complaint is that she talks sooo slow, but I fixed that by watching her videos at double speed. Highly recommend for Stats!

This class requires consistent work, but it's pretty straightforward. 3-4 assignments/week, 3 midterms, and a final. Took it on demand, but never felt unprepared for any of the assignments. She did a very good job explaining and building on previous topics. Took this class as a prereq for my major, yet felt like the material wasn't too challenging

You might ask why I consider Tiffany inspirational? The concepts could've been much more difficult (like some other GE's at BYU), but she did an outstanding job teaching every single thing you would be quizzed on or tested on. No doubt in my mind that she is one of the most respected professors at BYU. Take from her!

Professor Hilton was grade but this class was pretty difficult. She made the assignment schedule very clear and gives a lot of extra credit opportunities. There were 4 exams though, which I thought was unnecessary, so be aware of that. Super great professor but I'm just really bad at statistics so I didn't enjoy it that much.

Professor Hilton is super organized. I knew exactly what was expected each week. She sends out an announcement each week listing everything we need to do and when it is due. Her lectures are straightforward and easy to follow, which is a godsend for something as complicated as stats. Highly recommend

Tiffany is one of the best professors ive had!! She makes a subject matter that can seem intimidating incredibly understandable and enjoyable. She really wants her students to succeed and gives lots of opportunities for extra credit and one-on-one help with TAs. Her lectures are so clear, and she makes stats fun!

Professor Hilton is truly the best professor I have ever had at BYU. I held this class off until the last bit of school because I had a lot of apprehensions but Professor Hilton has such a gift for explaining tough concepts. I would recommend this class to ANYONE, whether they are excellent at STATS or struggle. Make sure to watch the lectures!

I love Tiffany so much! She is so understanding and easy to reach when you have questions. Her lectures and exam-prep materials were so helpful, she offered so much extra credit, and the structure of the course was super easy to follow. I seriously only have great things to say about Tiffany. If you take STAT 121, it needs to be from her.

This class is difficult, but Professor Hilton makes it so much better. She offers lots of extra credit and makes review videos to help you on tests. She explains stuff so clearly, and it is easy to understand. You have to put in a lot of work to get a good grade, but that is just how stats is. I would definitely suggest taking this class from her.

Tiffany is the best Professor Ive ever taken at BYU. She made something confusing like statistics to something I could easily understand. Her video lessons are on point and are the highlight of this class. The TAs were whatever but visiting with Tiffany was always so helpful. You dont need the textbook but be sure to fill out the study guide.

If you are nervous to take stats, I highly recommend taking Tiffany's online class. The video lectures are clear and super helpful, there isn't a ton of work, and the tests are fairly easy (if you study). I thought for sure I would fail stats and I passed with a B+ thanks to this class. However, I found the open/active labs to be kind of pointless.

This is a tough class but take it from Hilton! I put in a lot of hours but getting an A is totally achievable! All the resources you need are available to succeed. There are weekly labs and open labs and office hours open every day to help you. Reading the textbook, memorizing the study guides, and doing all the practice work is what got me an A+!

Very well structured course, homework, and quizzes are short but help you learn the material well. I did not like the way tests were written however, they seemed more focused on memorizing her wording and phrases than about applying statistics.

Tiffany was amazing! I got to work at my own pace, which I loved. Her lectures are short, clear, and taught me everything so well. I would recommend watching them sped up. As long as you pay attention and study a little, you will do great on the tests. Don't procrastinate! I am so glad I took stats from Tiffany.

She is the most amazing Stats professor ever! You usually hear awful things about the dry lectures on statistics and how hard it is. Professor Hilton really explains the material well and sets you up for success. If you put in the time to understand the concepts, you will do just fine.

Dr. Hilton was one of my favorite teachers. Stats isn't always a loved subject, but she makes it fun and really helps you admire stats. Dr. Hilton is easy to get a hold of and always willing to help you. She's honestly like a mom- kind, willing to help, and always there for you! I would recommend her to anyone, she is super amazing!

The class is very structured and she explains everything super well. Most of my friends wish they would have taken stats online with her. You do about 2-3 chapters a week, which includes a 20-30 min video and quiz for each chapter. She makes a review video for the tests and provides a practice test. Also go to a learning lab 1x a week for xtra cred

This class is all online. She is extremely patient and either her or her TAs were always available for me. I felt like there weren't any surprises during the semester and the course outline was easy to follow.

Tiffany is wonderful! The class is set up nicely so that you're working on your study guide as you study throughout the semester. She even uses specific boxes on your testing guide so you know what will be on the tests. She's super willing to help, explains concepts well, and is a great teacher all around. The class was easy to understand.

She gives lots of extra credit opportunities and is so so sweet. She will meet with you outside of class if needed even though it was an online class. I felt like I always knew what I was going to be quizzed and tested on and she had practices quizzez and tests. I wouldn't buy the text book if you do online becuase the videos were sufficient.

Yeah, I didn't care for this class and found some of the concepts hard to grasp, but Prof. Hilton made the workload manageable and pretty clear to understand. If you do the homework and the extra credit you can at least get a B or higher.

Took this class fully online and it was well-organized with lectures, a corresponding study guide, and open-note credit quizzes for each class. Professor Hilton and her TAs are accessible outside of class and really want to help you succeed. Extra credit is offered frequently and tests honestly aren't bad as long as you look at the review material.

If you are doing Stat121 do it with Professor Hilton online. It is the clearest and best environment to learn this material. Don't buy the textbook, not worth it at all. Honestly can't express how amazing this class was for learning stats.

A great online class. It was super well organized and easy to follow at my own pace. I would do the homework each week and watch the recorded lectures and the tests were very manageable. She also gives out a fair amount of extra credit.

Prof. Hilton is amazing! I took AP Stats in high school so this course was a review from years prior, and her lecture videos were very well done to help explain harder concepts. She runs her online class in a flipped classroom style and it worked really well for me. She is very accessible and wants to do what she can to help you out!

Tiffany is a great professor who wants you to succeed. The class is not an "easy A," but is definitely a class you can get an A in if you put in some time and effort. I would recommend this class to anyone needing to get a STAT class done.

The class was very organized and clear. I didn't like that you had to go to Professor Hilton during her few office hours to see what you missed on a test. I would rather see what I missed on my own time. Maybe her class would have been better in person.

Although I did appreciate her excess of extra credit, I did not love Professor Hilton. She was nice; however, when she made errors on credit quizzes she was unwilling to fix her mistakes. The class was all prerecorded lectures, so it was easy to go back and revisit things. The tests were pretty hard but nothing crazy. Use the office hours and TA's!

This was an online course with an in person lab once a week. Honestly, the textbook for this class was awesome and the homework consists of a practice quiz and then a credit quiz which are both super helpful. The class is set up in a clear way and there are tons of resources to help you succeed. There is tons of extra credit too.

I took the on-demand version of this class, so I didn't have too much interaction with Sister Hilton. However, I did go to office hours and watch her lectures and review videos. She is really great and explains concepts very well. Her review videos for the exams were honestly lifesavers. Take stats from her if you can!

Prof. Hilton taught this course with Prof. Lynne Nielson. Together they were very caring professors and really helpful. Unfortunately for me, I failed this class but that's simply because I can't math. It was no reflection on the teachers. Prof. Hilton is a really wonderful Professor. I recommend her because she works hard to help you succeed.

I loved this class especially from Tiffany. I didn't think I would like stats at all but I ended up loving it. The way she teaches makes the class so much easier to understand. It has the same amount of work as any other stats 121 class but the way Tiffany taught and organized it was super helpful.

Tiffany is a great professor and she wants everyone to succeed. There are a lot of assignments but many of them are done during class with her so youll always get 100% on them. I felt very prepared for the tests with all the in class notes.

Professor Hilton is the best professor I have had at BYU! She is amazing at teaching Stat.! Definitely worth it to take this course from her at BYU's SLC. Very knowledgeable and likeable guy who makes you laugh every class. However, questions in lecture did not get answered very well, and TA's were a bit disconnected from the class. The class structure is straightforward and generally stress-free. If you are confident in your ability to teach yourself, take this class

Wasnt a huge fan of his lecture style lots of tangents and he didn't answer questions very well. I think using video lectures from covid was lazy. His tests were open note and internet which helped in keeping stress low. Most questions were pretty good and made me apply my knowledge.

Class time is spent discussing video lectures where Dr. Jenkins helps us walk through problems to extend our understanding; although attendance isn't mandatory, it is super helpful. The grading is only unit tests, midterms, and 3 easy projects. Dr. Jenkins is funny and has a inspirational approach to science and biology. 10/10 would recommend!

If you took AP Bio like I did, Dr. Jenkins' class will for sure be an easy A. He records video lectures to watch on your own, and class time is used to review the material (so not the end of the world if you miss it). All quizzes and tests are online and open note/open Google, so you are really tested on understanding vs just memorization.

Jenkins is awesome. Everything you need to know is in his videos. You get to use google on every test, so if you know the material good enough to know what to google you will be able to kill it. He also lets you replace your grade on the final as your grade in the class. Probably the most organised and professor I have had at BYU.

Dr. Jenkins is a very caring professor and shows the utmost respect for the students. He structures his class to be "flipped" so you watch the lecture before and then go to class to discuss. The format wasn't my favorite, but it was pretty good. The lectures are definitely boring if you didn't watch beforehand.

His classes are structured weirdly. Most of the material is covered online, and you go to class to understand it better. But most classes go on tangents into topics way outside the scope of the course. Tests are open- note and internet, but the questions are primarily conceptual, so knowing the material is required.

Honestly my favorite and least stressful class this semester. He tries to apply the material to real life and helps students to understand difficult topics. Also very fair on grading and quizzes. Amazing teacher, super fun and open. Would 10/10 recommend taking his class.

I loved Dr. Jenkins class. He structured it in a way that was very fair and it was pretty clear how to succeed in the class. The tests and quizzes make up most of your grade and apply what you learn in class really well. I loved his class and would absolutely take a class of his again!

Dr. Jenkins is by far my favorite professor. He was so understanding, helpful and knowledgable. His tests rely on application, not just memorization, so as long as you understand the principles and can apply them you'll do great (plus they're open notes and book). This class was amazing, I loved it. Definitely recommend taking it from him!

I took this class from Dr. Jenkins in my very first semester of college and was a little worried about how it would go. Honestly he is my favorite teacher so far as I go into my 4th semester. He has great lectures and youtube videos that help out a lot with learning the content from his lectures.

every two weeks there was a quiz and an assignment due. midterm replaced lowest quiz grade and my final ended up replacing my whole grade. Has great 20 minute prerecorded lectures. If you need to take PDBIO take it from him. You will learn at a super high level and it is never super stressful.

The class was super organized and he gives you a schedule of exactly what to do on what day, which helps a ton since this is an on-demand class. His tests are open-note, open-internet, but they test you on the application of the material, which is really good to LEARN the material. He is super caring and will do a lot to help students out. 10/10!
This class is organized very well. I felt that the lectures did not adequately prepare students for the level of difficulty that tests required.

I loved Dr. Jenkins! You should definitely take PDBIO from him. He's an absolutely amazing teacher and his class is structured in a way that really encourages learning. It's very evident that he cares about his students and wants them to learn. Great great teacher, would highly recommend.

Class was well designed with six unit tests, a midterm, and a final. Lectures were short but content rich, and most of what they cover is related to the tests. All of his tests use exam-level questions that require more than a surface level understanding of biology, but he is very patient and willing to help outside of class. Great class.

He has been my favorite professor at BYU so far. Honestly I doubt there is a better PDBIO 120 professor. Everything is so well organized in his class it is impossible to get lost. He has projects for every unit that are really simple. The way he tests is the best possible way for anyone wanting to succeed in his course. He really cares for students

Dr. Jenkins is the best professor at BYU by far, he was always willing to meet one on one to go over quizzes and tests, and even gave you points back if you proved that you understood the concepts being taught. He even did several calculations at the end of the semester to ensure we had the best grade we could get! Change your schedule to have him!

Dr Jenkins is anxious for his students to succeed. He is very accessible for questions and tests and assignments reflect the reality that scientists can look things up too (most things are open note). His lectures are clear and interesting and his personable and caring personality is evident in them. If you will put in the work, you will succeed.

Professor Jenkins is insanely nice, buuuut due to circumstances with classes being online this class was not a great experience for me nor the professor. There was not clear direction as to what was necessary for us to know in this class, and assignments didn't prepare us very well for the tests. It got better through the semester though!

Professor Jenkins has been my favorite STEM professor so far. He was very accessible outside of class and was always willing to meet with students. He really wants all of His students to succeed. He teaches all of the material you need in the videos. Quizzes and exams are open notes and internet, all because he really wants you to learn. 10/10

Such a great guy! Strengthened my faith while teaching Biology. He is the quintessence of what a BYU Professor should be. You dont need a book, I loved watching his videos because HE ONLY TELLS YOU THINGS THAT YOU NEED TO KNOW AND NOT THE UNNECESSARY THINGS IN THE BOOKS. Greatest Professor at BYU. Makes time for you if personal review is needed.

What saved my grade in this class (before the midterm I had a 72% in the class and I ended with a 97%) were STUDY GROUPS and Dr. Jenkins' lenient grading policy- replacing quiz scores. Honestly, after the midterm, I never attended class hours. I just watched the online lectures (about 3-4 hours worth every 2 weeks) and went to study groups.

I highly recommend taking from Dr. Jenkins! I took his class during the pandemic and, to accommodate for the changes, he constantly tried to make the material more accessible. He was always available to meet and personally address my concerns. He's a great teacher and very invested in the success of his students. Great choice.

I liked professor Jenkins, he was funny and kind! I took his class during covid and I think he did well, though it was a little hard because the material on the tests/quizzes was harder than the material taught in his online lectures. However I think that occurred because teaching online can be hard, and this was Jenkins first time. I recommend him

I love Dr. Jenkins. The best advice I can give is to be careful with the quizzes. The quizzes are a lot harder than the actual test. He specifically does this to prepare you for the tests. However, there are only two tests: the midterm and final. He lectures everything, but I would recommend you get the textbook to supplement what he gives you.

Dr. Jenkins is a great choice for PDBio 120! He really cares about his students and his lectures were entertaining. My one "critique" is that I would've loved to hear more about the research he conducts.

This class was great! It was super organized, 6 modules with an assignment and quiz in each, a midterm, and a final. He is super considerate of all the work that we were doing both inside and outside class and was always available to have one-on-one discussions. The final can also replace your grade! (Thats how I got an A) Take PDBIO from him!

Took it online with covid and it was a great class! It switched from blended to fully online at the beginning of the semester and the professor listened to students and adjusted the program to help us best. Not a lot of work, grading had a great system of replacing one of the first 3 quizzes with the midterm and the same with the final.

So grateful to Jenkins for the time/effort he put in to prep lectures. Makes complex topics simple and easy to understand! Lightbulb finally clicked for me taking this class from HIM! 6 units-HW/Quizzes for ea.+midterm+final. REALLY cares about students/helping them solidify info w/a lot of help avail ea. week. Most organized class ever. TAKE HIM!

Professor Jenkins is honestly one of the best professors I've had. He cares about each of his students and wants their success. His canvas is easy to navigate and he was able to change things that didn't work. All of his quizzes and tests are open book. The quizzes are application based and designed to be harder than the tests.

Dr Jenkins is great! This class has a great structure and clear expectations. Watch his lectures, take notes, and meet with a study group so you can talk through concepts/processes. He really focuses on making sure material is understood, not just memorized. Probably my favorite class I've taken at BYU

I can't even express how much I loved Dr. Jenkin's class. He had zero busy work, very mild homework assignments, and I learned SOOO MUCH. I would recommend to anyone and everyone to take his class(es). It's easy to tell how much he cares about his students and their success, because of a genuine care he has for them as individuals.

He does a great job teaching this class! Very enthusiastic about the material and willing to work with students when they need help. Tests are open notes but require a higher level of comprehension for the material than just watching the lectures. If you put in a little bit of work it will be a great class!

Professor Jenkins is honestly one of my favourite professors this semester. He provided concise, prerecorded lectures of all the content you need. This is also supplemented with optional TA sessions that re-teach the material in the videos. The best part is the open book, open internet tests that are easy if you utilize the internet correctly.

The teacher is a good guy and loves what he does. All of his lectures are prerecorded and are easy to understand. However the quizzes focus on applying the material learned from the videos and Jenkins nor the TAs ever teach us how to apply the material. Everything is open book/internet but it still doesnt really help.

Dr. Jenkins was one of THE BEST professors that I had during this past semester. This course is VERY organized, with 6 open-note unit quizzes (application-based) and 6 assignments. These are easy A's if you watch the lectures, do the review Q's, and show up. He holds Q/A sessions and TA sessions to help you. 1 open note midterm & open-note final.

Took this class in Fall 2020 (COVID year), so it might be different in a normal semester. SUPER kind prof., very accessible. 6 units, each unit has 1 quiz (basically a test, but open note), and 1 assignment (pretty easy mini-project). Content is taught clearly in video lectures, and TAs use the class time to review lectures. Prof. Jenkins is great!

Dr Jenkins was my favorite professor this semester. His class was very well organized and he did all he could to make himself available outside of class time. He tries to make his lectures interesting (and mildly humorous) and does a good job of explaining things well. You have to make sure you keep up with the video lectures and you'll be fine!

Honestly, not sure why students have rated him poorly. Everything is open note and Dr. Jenkins/the TA's are easy to work with OUTSIDE of class time. The class is geared for students to learn the material on their own so if you want to do well, it's important to avoid procrastination.

Class is broken down into 6 small units. Each unit has prerecorded lectures and live break out sessions led by the TA's (optional) during class time. Each unit contains a quiz and an assignment (hw) that you can complete at your own pace before the deadline. Concepts were tricky at times, but plenty of resources available to help. Not bad!

The class is prerecorded lectures, and then TAs will go over the recorded material on assigned class days. TA meetings were constantly canceled and rescheduled. The tests are based off of application, but you arent taught how to apply the material in the lectures or TA meetings. I spent hours outside of class time and it still wasnt enough.

Took Professor Jenkins' PDBIO class and it was extremely difficult. The lecture content was easy to grasp but the tests were nothing like what was talked about in lectures. His TAs consistently canceled zoom meetings and it was basically a do it on your own class. Tests were open note and I still consistently got C's and D's. He also loves his job

Professor Taylor was nice, though I only talked to her a few times. The TA did the grading and I got points off for small things on a lot of my assignments. The instructions for the assignments were often different than what the rubric said, which was frustrating. Lots of group work for an online class. Not the worst, not the best either.

The online format had a heavy workload with excessive homework and group projects that defeated the purpose of being online. TAs took off points inconsistently even when the rubric was met. Both the TA and professor took weeks to respond to emails, and replies were often unhelpful, usually just screenshots of the assignment

Took this class online; it was a lot of work but straightforward and simple. As an ELED Major, this was the most useful class I have taken so far, and it was insightful for teaching. TA's were really looking to take off points even if you did what was in the rubric, but if you do all the assignments on time you get an easy A.

Dr Taylor was absent from the entire class. Granted it was online but still all the lectures were prerecorded from another teacher. There is an absurd amount of homework and while non of it is hard, it takes TIME. There is also a lot of group projects that feel redundant. Not a hard class, but a lot of work.

Don't get me wrong, Dr. Taylor is SO SWEET, and kind. However, she is not the best with technology. The class has a ton of reading, discussion boards, and quizzes, however the course is very unorganized, so you're never really sure what she wants from you. We had more work/assignments/reading than any of my friend's UNIV 101 classes by a LONG SHOT.

Love Dr.Taylor! Met her at beginning. Then just completed these treacherous asynchronous modules by another pre-recorded teacher the entire rest of the semester. Hated how much work this class is. Takes a good 4hrs plus to complete one module. On top of that, a ton of overlapping group projects, side assignments, and volunteer hours you got to do.

Professor Taylor is a very kind person but besides that I didn't enjoy this class. There was SO MUCH reading and lots of quizzes that heavily affect your grade. We had lots of group projects and had to spend 10 hours in a classroom which was really hard for a lot of us to fit in our schedules. She is very unclear of what she wants.

I took CPSE 300 with her and it was really bad. She was impossible to reach outside of class, and did not answer the question asked. There are very few assignments, and they are pretty easy. You never really understand what is being asked, I would have failed without the other students.

Tina is such a kind and caring professor. Her class was so much fun to attend. My only complaint with the class was it was very unorganized, at one point we all missed a quiz because she never mentioned it to us. She waived it but there were a few instances like this where we just didn't know what was going on.

I loved her UNIV class. She is so sweet and was energetic. She cares about everyone and has you share about yourself and likes getting you involved. She took our feedback and changed the way we did the weekly discussion posts to how we wanted it. We did so many fun activities and she was a great teacher. She made UNIV fun, not just busy work. 10/10

Dr.Bronson is the best! This class was by far my favorite I have taken at BYU. Everyone says it is impossible to do well and usually choose Dr.Savage - CHOOSE DR.BRONSON. He is such an amazing guy and hilarious. If you put time into the class you will do well and he wants you to do well. 10/10 would recommend!

Dr Bronson did a wonderful job! His lectures are almost direct from the textbook. His exams are very fair (30 questions MC) It's a standardized final, which I found very easy. Overall, this class really isn't that hard. If you do the homework and practice problems from the textbook, you will be just fine. He also curves the entire class at the end.

We saw him once for 2 minutes. Class hinges on your TAs. My TAs were very kind. Workload is ridiculous, be ready to treat this like a 6 credit hour class. So many labs due each week, lab exams which are a total waste of time because they almost never make sense unless you go to the right TA review. I wouldnt take this alongside Ochem 2, doesnt help

Get a good TA I repeat GET A GOOD TA it will make or break your experience. Leave the room on day 1 if your TA gives you strict vibes. Rely on TAs for answers too. Go to TA reviews for exams, take good notes and you can use those during the exams. This class is way better than 107. I believe it is an easy A if you follow lab videos and use TA help.

Nothing against Dr. Bronson, but the Ochem lab is my least favorite class I've taken at BYU. Overall it's an exorbitant amount of work for a 2-credit class. The TAs are unhelpful - I would constantly ask questions about the procedure only for them to tell me I did it wrong with 5 minutes left.

This class was so easy. It is a lab so obviously you rely on the TA's but Dr. Bronson walked around and knew us by name even though it was during spring term. For the midterm and final... go to the TA reviews!! They really help (;
With this lab, you do not really get to know your professor. Overall, seems like a good dude; however, you will need to rely heavily on the TAs (going to test reviews highly important)

Bronson is the BEST, he is so funny I genuinely loved him. He wants you to do well and will answer/explain any question clearly for you to understand. This class is hard but doable. The TAs help so much and their exam/quiz reviews will ensure you score well. 70% of your grade is 4 exams and the final, so make sure to study hard for those.

You have to use the TAs to succeed in this course, and talk to other people to find out which TAs you should go with on day 1, it's an important decision. You may never interact with Dr. Bronson but he seems nice. Difficult and time consuming course, but it's doable!

Your TAs will be your best resources for this class. Very clear grading criteria. You don't interact with Dr. Bronson hardly at all, but he is a dawg! Cool guy. If you go to the TAs and exam reviews, this class is an easy A. DO NOT MISS ANY LABS THOUGH. This all being said, this class can be VERY time consuming, so just be aware of that.

His class is two hours, but it is totally worth it. Go to his office hours and review tests. Read the material before class so you can be ready to ask questions. He really cares about the students and takes the time to memorize names and faces. If you do everything he provides you with, you should be great.

Easy A. You absolutely cannot miss a single lab though. Making them up is such an insane pain. And talk to the TAs as much as possible. Every lab should be a free 20/20, just talk to the TAs to make sure. The exams aren't particularly hard, but they're basically all your grade depends on. Know how to identify IR peaks and H NMRs for an easy A

I liked Dr. Bronson, but this class was HARD. The exams and quizzes were difficult. The final was timed which was hard for me. This class was interesting though; he does a good job of applying it to everyday life.

I liked his teaching style, though the 2hr schedule could be tough. I didn't read the book before lecture, only for exams, and did fine, but many will need to do both in order to succeed on the exams. He uses the standardized final, which is very simple and general, and has a merciful curve at the end. If you put in the work, you'll be fine.

Dr. Bronson is a pretty stellar professor. I'm not going to lie, this class is difficult, but he gives you the resources you need to succeed. I appreciate that he constructed the class in a way where we were responsible for our own education/learning. He's a little scary the first day, but once you get to know him, he's hilarious! Loved his class!

This class was very difficult and would not recommend taking, have to retake this class for my major and very frustrated. Everything is based off of quizzes and exams so if you are not a good test taker, like myself, please don't take this professor. The lectures were 2 hours long and very exausting

You will never see him, the class is all TAs. Overall, not a hard class tbh, just time consuming for a 2 credit class, but thats not unique to this class. The prelab videos basically guide you every step. For exams, just go to TA reviews and you will be fine. Ask your TA literally everything and you should get an A.

There's definitely more work than there should be for a 2 credit class but the TAs will get you through. The lab is fun and it's very clear what is going to be on the test. It's a lot of work doing the pre-lab and the lab report, and especially HNMRS/CNMRs so plan for that.

Dr. Bronson is a quirky guy but I found him and his lectures entertaining. TAs were great and super accessible, their quiz and test reviews helped so much. Read the textbook and do your homework/practice problems!! Difficult class but doable and really rewarding.

Dr. Bronson is a great professor and if you do the work, you can succeed in his class. Lectures can be confusing and your grade heavily relies on your performance on his tests. The TAs are your best resource so USE THEM! Dr. Bronson wants all his students to do well and is willing to meet with you if needed.
The exams are dumb. So dumb. TAs are all you work with

Bronson is the best chemistry professor you will ever have. His lectures were entertaining and you could tell he cared for his students. Grading is fair, he lays everything out at the beginning of the semester so you know what to expect. One group project but have fun with it. Final is standardized, his tests prepare you. Overall, funny professor.

Dr. Savage is gone so this guy would be your next best bet. Definitely difficult class. Tests are 30 questions only so you gotta be careful. Quiz every week 10 pts. Final is standardized test and can replace your 4 tests average if you do good on it. TAs will help you succeed so go to them.

It was difficult to sit through 2 hrs. of Dr. Bronson's lectures. You need to attend class, read the textbook, and study with the TAs to succeed. Most of my learning happened in TA reviews. Dr. Bronson is organized and reasonable. He might not be the most inspiring teacher but he gets the job done. This class is doable if you put in the work.

Dr. Bronson was amazing!! The first day of class he tries to scare people off, but his class is not that bad! He is funny and willing to work with you when you need help. As long as you stay caught up with the readings and take notes, you shouldn't struggle too much!

Dr. Bronson uses slides in class that are accessible to all students. Homework is just the practice problems from the textbook and is it NOT required to do. That being said - there are weekly quizzes that are based on the readings and problems from the book. If you stay caught up with the textbook, you'll be fine!

DO NOT BE AFRAID TO TAKE HIS CLASSES! HE TALKS BIG FIRST DAY BUT HE IS A SWEETHEART (and his class is not as difficult as he says it is).  Professor Bronson was amazing! He learned everyone's names in a matter of days and treated us like his friends. I recommend sitting in the front of the class consistently if you want to be extra BFFs with him.

Bronson is funny and I laughed a lot in his class. It is heavy on the textbook reading but I guess it is technically optional. Weekly quizzes on Friday. Unit tests are hard but he weighs the class at the end so grades end up being much better. He totally prepared us for the final and you could tell he wanted every student to succeed and get an A.

I never met the guy but he was nice enough to round my grade up 0.4% so I could get an A, which was nice. The experiments are really long and the nmr practice is tough but it gets so much easier as the semester goes on. There are also some stupidly hard questions on the tests, but if you go to the good ta's reviews, you'll do fine.

Lecture reinforces & enhances what u read. 4 tests 1 final. Tests are easy if u go to lecture. The more u understand previous chapters, the easier it will be to understand future ones. U can tell he cares about his students &loves what he teaches. 10% of grade is showing up & an EASY presentation. just put in the work, go to class, & you'll do fine

This lab is run by TAs. Dr. Bronson replaced the lecture hour with a 20 min vid you were required to watch before coming to class so you won't ever see him in person. It's not a hard class, graded mostly on completeness of labs. There are 2 open note untimed tests worth about 30 percent of your grade. Overall a great class and lots of fun!

OChem Lab is WAY better than Chem 107 and a lot more engaging. The labs aren't to bad and the TAs will walk you through EVERYTHING. You really have to study for the exams and KNOW your stuff, but Dr. Bronson is super fair if you talk to him and explain your reasoning. I love the lab videos that allow you to work out everything before class. Great!

If you are taking this class you have taken a few other lab classes. At this point, you should know you won't meet the lab professor. Only student instructors and TAs. This is normal. If you don't like your TAs go to someone else's office hours or walk across to the other lab. People on here seem bitter. Expect to spend 6 hours in lab, 10 outside.

Like everyone else, I never met him. He makes himself totally inaccessible as he doesnt even have his email listed anywhere on learning suite or in the syllabus. I asked to makeup a couple points to maintain my grade due to extenuating circumstances and he sent me a rather unprofessional email response with weak arguments and misspelled my name.

I've never met the man - he doesn't teach any really relies on CHEM 352 to teach you everything, even if you haven't covered it in CHEM 352. Expect to spend  10 hours a week on this course, as its near impossible to complete post labs without getting answers from TAs. It should probably be a 3 or 4 credit class at minimum.

Dr. Bronson doesn't involve himself with this class at all. There is an enormous amount of work for a two-credit class: between lab prep, time in class, and post-lab reports, I probably spend ten hours a week on this class. Poorly structured, treat this like a three credit class.

Never met Bronson once. The head TA for my section was very arrogant and spent more time on the phone in lab. The other TA was phenomenal though, so it really just depends on who you get. 3/5 because at least the material was very organized and easy to follow, otherwise I'd say 2/5. Got done with labs at least 1 hour early almost every day though

Dr. Bronson is soft-spoken and not always terribly clear, but he knows his stuff and helps us learn it too. Lab reports are quite difficult to earn full points on, and the TAs played a big part in helping me earn an A. He was very accommodating once classes transitioned to online because of COVID.

Horrible professor. Openly mocks students in private and in front of the entire class for asking questions. Tests look nothing like what is taught in class, "because then we'd all pass." Impossible to talk to without being belittled and treated like an idiot. Impossible amount of work to complete if you're taking ANY other classes. DO NOT TAKE HIM!

I took this the coronavirus semester. The transition to online learning was so much easier. He literally cancelled the final (a relief bc the midterm was challenging!) and watching a video of the TA's doing a lab cut down on soooo much time each week that would normally be spent in lab which sometimes felt like busywork.

First of all NO ONE KNEW WHAT THEY WERE DOING IN THIS CLASS. Unfortunately if you need this class for a prereq then get ready for such a time consuming class with an extremely difficult midterm and thankfully no final this semester. I really liked my TAs and the experiments but it was a lot of busy work all together. IDEK who Dr. Bronson is

9 quizzes, 4 midterms, a final, and a participation section that's 10% of your grade (easy).If you get a better score on the final than the average of your 4 midterms, it will replace it. He was helpful and wants you to do well. Hard class, recommend him over the others. If you put in meaningful time and work, you will be able to get a good grade.

Dr. Bronson gets a 1 because he is nonexistent in the class and doesn't seem to care at all about students. However, all the TA's are great, and the labs are interesting. Lots of busy work, and tests are unneccesarily hard for a 2 credit class. It's a tough class, but if you put in the time, an A is possible. Befriend your TA's and you'll be fine.

This class is so hard! I was lucky enough to have Dr Bronson as my instructor. He is so fun, just talk about basketball and he'll love you! This was my most time consuming class this semester. Pray you get a good TA. The tests are very hard and very heavily weighted so prepare well. UNDERSTAND NMR! That is the real key. The labs are pretty fun.

Very heavily relies on the textbook. If you do not read the text, or practice problem there is no chance to be successful. Simple teaching, and usually easy to follow if you keep up with class schedule. Very little goes into grades, so be conscious of every assignment. Tests generally go beyond homework and quizzes so know CONCEPTS BACK & FORTH.

This class is hard. I did find it more enjoyable than CHEM 107. The test avg was 70% and they were hard. I didn't really learn anything from this class. Unfortunately if you are premed you have to take this class and Bronson is the only prof. that teaches it. It's not as bad as I thought, just very time consuming and confusing class!

a class full of busy work, tests that take 2x as long as a biochem exam. he makes students stick to syllabus but feels free to change anything that allows him to keep the gpa of the class where he needs it to appear like a "good" teacher... i guess??

Class is badly mis-managed. Poor teaching for exams. Exams  difficult but doable. Did not get to review Midterm. Hard to learn what you don't know when he hides your own work from you! More of a focus on keeping scores low rather than teaching. Huge disconnect between Bronson and students. Dr. Bronson lets his student instructors be his shield.
his changes for online curriculum were a joke. went back on his word in a few different ways. don't understand why he has to lie and change the syllabus with one month left of classes

switching to online classes you would expect professors to consider the students and how it would effect them. rather todd put more demands on his students and counters by saying its just as hard right now for me as it is for you and the withdraw deadline is today, so if you elect to stay you consent to these changes.. give us a break todd

Really sucks that you have to take this class if you are pre med. Bronson doesn't teach, he's non existent. All you have are the TA's. Tests are unbelievably hard for a 4 credit class let alone 2. Tests do not reflect what you learn. Such a joke. BYU needs to re-evaluate this course.

He's a very different kind of guy, and I liked him towards the end. A lot depends on your TA's - mine were awesome and helpful. The class can be a LOT of work at times, but I did learn a lot, especially about spectra. Study for the tests well, go to a review, and try to understand what is going on in the labs and you should be ok.

Poorly designed lab. The "lab book" was just empty graph paper, and for the pre-lab assignments you have to rewrite the entire procedure by hand which wasn't toooo time consuming, but it was not an effective way to prepare for the lab or the tests. Class average on the final was a 73 (and took 3-5 hours). Tests barely reflected what we learned.

Best choice for Chem 285! Weekly quiz that is almost exactly like the homework problems in the text book so it's easy to do well on the quizzes. We had 4 midterms and the final was a national standardized chem test that was WAY easier than any of the midterms. If we did better on the final it would replace the average of our midterm scores.

I took ochem lab while pregnant and I felt Dr. Bronson was a little sexist towards me. He asked to meet with me and then proceeded to tell me I really should think hard about taking this class because it could affect my baby. I told him I was graduating this semester and he kept pressuring me to drop the class.

Terrible class. The friends I made during the course made it much more tolerable. Working in a group was the only way I survived. Everybody hates this class. Anyone that tells you it's not that bad is just trying to act cool and smart. Take it only if you absolutely have to. Tests are ridiculous, long, and beyond the scope of the class. Good luck.

He is awesome! He made it really easy to understand topics with his lectures and I loved his lecture style. As long as you do the reading and assignments outside of class before lecture and come with questions you will understand everything.

Overall, pretty lame. Too much work for only a 2-credit lab and the tests were unnecessarily difficult. My rating is for the class itself as you will never actually see or hear from the professor. Unfortunately you have to take the class if you are pre-med/pre-dent etc., so just get it over with.

You will have to study a LOT. Took as much study / prep time as Chem 352. Pre lab takes about an hour, with post lab taking about an hour to an hour and a half. Tests were brutal. There are a few tremendously difficult HMNR questions (very point heavy too) on the tests that will wreck your souls. You've been warned.

I personally loved Dr. Bronson. It was a class jam-packed with information and the exams were EXTREMELY hard, but if you work for it, you'll get a good grade. He's really funny and keeps your attention exceptionally well during class. He taught the concepts clearly and answered questions to the best of his ability. 10/10, would take again.

Professor Bronson was an alright professor, but honestly the TAs were more helpful to me. He really worked with me when I went in for office hours and he'll work around special circumstances awesomely. The tests count for 50% of the grade, plus the final which counts for 20%. Lots of tests so beware.

This class was really hard because of the material but Prof. Bronson isn't the best lecturer. His lectures are boring and long and I didn't understand much after I left the classroom. There were four midterms and a standardized final in addition to a quiz each week over the chapters we read.

Awful, awful, awful class. Everything about this class is engineered to waste time: get ready to spend 1-2 hours a week copying handouts into your lab notebook, post-lab questions are designed to make you spend hours with the TA, and this doesn't even include test time. Clearly Dr. B didn't notice this is a 2 credit class. Worst experience at BYU.

There is really no way to describe how awful this man is. The problem is, he is the only real option BYU students have for their ochem lab credit. So we are all screwed, and with his tenure, he isn't going anywhere. Hopefully, he grows a soul and changes. Maybe he will realize that his job is to be helpful, but I am not counting on it.

This a 2 credit class. But that fact has slipped out of the empty mind of this awful instructor. To be fair, the hotness question I couldn't answer it because YOU WILL NEVER SEE HIM. He does not show up classes, the tests do not reflect anything gone over in class. Dr. Bronson is horrible, there is no question about it.

Dr. Bronson is horrible and has put together probably the worst class at BYU. He is a stickler for points on lab reports. Tests have almost nothing to do with what you learn and they are the hardest tests youll ever take at BYU. They take about 4 or 5 hours to complete and are so much harder than would seem a fair assessment of your knowledge.

Dr. Bronson is great. This is a lab so most of the interaction is with the TAs. Grade is based solely on lab reports and exams, a midterm and a final. Labs are fun, clear, and can be easy if you're prepared for them. Exams are killer. TAs are lifesavers for lab reports and exam prep. Ochem is tough, it is what it is.

Dr. Bronson was a great professor for this lab class. The spectroscopy for this lab is the only bad part, but you'll get pretty good at it by the end. The labs are fun and you can get 100% on them if you check your answers with the TAs, which can be a good thing or a bad thing depending on your personality. This was a fun class overall.

Love that he always posted powerpoints. Homework not required. Grades come from few, DIFFICULT tests that sometimes include minute details from pp slides. This semester he offered to replace midterm average with final exam score. Group project and attendance make for some easy but small points. Funny guy. HARD class because of memorization.

I was SUPER nervous to take this class and I also had no idea to take this class from although I definitely chose the right teacher!  He is always there to help and  the TA is awesome and helped a TON!  Super easy group project and quizzes if you study.  VERY tough class but if you study and stay on top of it you will do great! Read the textbook!!!
Dr. Bronson is a very engaging professor and his lectures are very helpful to listen to before the lab is done.
Just learn NMR well and you'll get an A. Lab part is easy - you're not graded on yield and TAs will basically give you post-lab questions.

This class is hard but not as hard as people make it seem. i got an A- in both my ochems but finished with an A here. this class prepares you extremely well for the mcat, something i did not expect while taking it, so don't put it off. its hard but i believe it pays its dividends. labs are easy and distribution is created by the two tests

He comes across pretty intimidating at first, but he's actually hilarious and is very helpful/legitimately understanding if you're having a tough semester. Also the clearest ochem professor I've had so far. Labs are a great experience and almost impossible to fail. Tests are tough but he prepares you well and curves fairly if necessary.

Chem 285 in general is just a hard class. Dr. Bronson understands the material, but his lectures are a little dry sometimes. He's pretty funny, but his lectures are still boring. The tests killed everyone's grade (watch out for the first test especially) but THANK GOODNESS for the curve! He usually curves grades 5-6% at the end of the semester.

Bronson is great; super friendly and funny and definitely knows his stuff. The class, however, was pretty rough. I'm used to getting As on most of my tests, but I got Bs and even a C on his tests. I probably would have done better if I had done the reading before class rather than after, so do that! Group project & participation are way easy.

I feel that a lot of the poor ratings for Bronson are fueled by poor students... Generalization? Maybe. But in all honesty Bronson rocks. This class is tough, but Professor B makes it a little less painful. He is very qualified in all aspects, level headed about expectations, and overall the best professor to take this class from at BYU. Promise.

Dr. Bronson is great for Ochem lab. His tests are super difficult though. Go to as many TA reviews as your possibly can! You can never study too much for his tests. The lab is super fun though once you get the hang of it and Bronson is the chillest professor on campus. He's hilarious too and not afraid to speak his mind.

Dr. Bronson is a good guy overall, but his test are not fun!  I got a 99% in chem352, but his test were much harder than any other ochem test I have ever taken, but the good news is you only need to average 84% on the tests to get an A so it is doable, but he will make you work for it.  The lab portion is super easy so the class is not too bad!

Dr. Bronson cares a lot about O-Chem, and he's obviously spent a lot of time preparing the labs for this class. His voice can be sleep-inducing at times, but he knows what he's talking about and his input is interesting and relevant.

Dr Bronson is a good teacher.  This material is just really difficult to grasp.  There are 4 hard midterms and a very hard standardized final.  He will help if you need it.  Reading and attending lecture are crucial.
The way he runs the exams are bad. He makes it so essentially you cant study what you did wrong, just so that he can reuse the exact same exam year after year. Not a good way to learn.

Professor Bronson was great. It is a very difficult class just due to its nature, but if you're willing to study and get help when you need it, you will do fine. One of the best things about taking it from Professor Bronson was that he helped our class bond and it felt like we had a mutual friendship between each other and with him.

Doesn't post answer key for midterm, he has a stupid system where you look at it during one period and then your test is shredded. This means you can't learn from your mistakes and make the same ones on the final. The tests don't line up with class material. Even other professors say that the test material is useless.

4 test drop you lowest onenot too hard but study! and then the final is some random standardized test that is one jacked up test well its not that hard but you have like 110 minutes to answer like 120+ Q the class is curved but you have to be on of the smartest or hardest working kids in class to get an A

It's hard to figure out what he's asking for in the labs. Tests are ridiculous and not an accurate reflection of what a student learned in class. He sits in the back of the lab with his arms folded waiting for someone to approach him rather than going out and trying to help. Not approachable in my opinion.

Hardest 2 credits ever. The tests are ridiculously hard and there's no curve. Become really good friends with the TAs and study your brains out for the tests.                           Signed - a former straight A student who got below a 60% on the final.

Really, really good professor. Bronson is very approachable and willing to help and he knows what's going on. Wanders the labs helping you troubleshoot and gets great TAs (easily the best I've had). I loved 353, it was so much more fun than Chem 107.

Bronson is a great professor. I dreaded taking this class, but actually really enjoyed it. Unlike chem 107, you usually are not rushed for time. And, even tho there is a lot of work, you do learn a lot. Bronson also teaches you the way it is in the real world which is nice. The TA's were also great which made the lab enjoyable. Study hard for tests

The hardest 2 credit class I have ever taken. Required a ton of outside classwork and the exams took several hours each. That being said, the TA's were extremely helpful and Dr. Bronson was always willing to help students. Just be prepared to put a lot of time into this class.

Bronson is the man! I loved this class, it was way better than 107. Tests are pretty hard, as others have mentioned. Dr. Bronson is very choosy about his TAs, so you get really good ones. He also circulates though the labs and helps you if you need it. He's very knowledgeable, wants his students to succeed. Get in one of his sections if possible!

Dr. Bronson is a great teacher, very approachable, knows his stuff so well, and wants you to learn, work hard and succeed. The tests are hard but the labs are easy and buffer your grade a lot. You'll probably like this lab more than most of the other ridiculous labs you have to take here.

This class was hard, but Dr. Bronson is the most approachable teacher I've ever had. Go talk to him for help! He likes helping. The labs are fairly ace-able but the exams are hard; it is the exams that Dr. Bronson uses to produce his grade distributions. Study your butt off for them.

You don't have a choice for who to take for O chem lab, but Dr. Bronson is great! I had a lot of fun doing the labs.  Much, much better than Chem 107! Tests are tough, but if you make sure to know everything about the labs, including post lab questions, you can do well.  Good class.

The redesigned labs are pretty good. They teach you a lot and he's done his best to cut down on frustrating busy work. Fortunately they are graded on your write-up quality, and not percent yields. Tests, however, are really challenging. You've got to become an NMR master. A's on most of the labs + class average on exams = B- in class.

Professor Bowen is amazing. I took the Adobe Premiere class. He made everything accessible for someone with no experience. Super friendly and willing to help answer questions. Weekly quiz based off lecture. Other than that it was just practicing and a few super short editing video assignments. Super creative opportunity. Absolutely would recommend.

Class is almost two hours long. I feel like, at most, it could've been an hour and fifteen. He's a great man and definitely knows his stuff - he works at BYUtv. I loved learning from him and his experience is invaluable - the main thing that separates his lessons from your average YouTube tutorials. Highly recommend!

Mr. Bowen works for BYU TV so he has a lot of experience. This is the only class he teaches outside of his job. It starts off pretty simple and moves at an easy pace. He does take attendance, there are 4 quizzes (nothing stressful) and 4 assignments that require a video to be made. It's a pretty chill class.

I took this class to learn more about Premiere Pro, and I did-- but honestly, most of this class was spent listening to dry lectures and doing easy quizzes/assignments. We did a couple longer video editing projects at the end, which I think we should have been doing throughout. You could probably learn the same with a couple of weeks of Youtube.

Dr. Nelson is one of the best ME professors I've had at BYU. He is really passionate about teaching, likes students and teaches very well. He is so funny and makes a tough class actually enjoyable. Definitely the move for machine design!

I don't typically rate professors on here, but Prof Nelson was such a good teacher this semester that I had to make sure other people would take him. Unlike Statics (the pre-req to Dynamics) professor Nelson felt like he wanted me to get a good grade and succeed in the class. Super nice guy, takes genuine interest in his students. Highly recommend.
Professor Pennington is the best and truly cares about each student!
Dr. P is an angel! The kindest professor I have ever had who helped me feel like me being a teacher actually made a difference! Take it from him, he is the best!

Professor Pennington is genuinely one of the kindest professors I have ever had. He is so caring, respectful, and ready to work with you. I loved all of his insights on teaching and education. Please take his class, he is amazing!
Best professor ever. Very inspirational and lenient if something comes up. Loved his lectures and learning about his personal experiences teaching. Would definitely take again!

Dr. P is an absolute asset and my favorite Professor in the PETE department. Like basically every PETE class, this one is very easy, but also very important. I learned a lot of applicable skills and enjoyed coming to class. Dr. P is kind, passionate, and caring. Highly recommend.

Due to classes being online, he had to adapt some of the homework assignments. They were manageable and there were only a few. The tests were multiple choice. He was good at communicating and answering questions. I would recommend.

Dr. Pennington is a very chill teacher, but a great one. The class itself was just hard because the technology rarely worked and he didn't really help out with that part. But his lectures are great - sometimes dragged on for too long in my opinion. He has the textbook online.

PETE 276 Gives good feedback. Cares about the students as individuals, doesn't feel like you are a burden. Respected by students. Hilarious. Amazing and inspiring lectures. There for you. Assignments are useful, simple, efficient. I would take any class you can from him because he is amazing. Didn't make us buy the text book but provided it online.

Dr. Pennington is such a great professor. He really cares about his students and understands if you turn assignments in late or whatnot. Goes off on tangents sometimes but he is really a great guy. Love him!

After 2 days of class you're thrown into the school. It's great but expect to struggle that first day. Learn from it and improve for next time. Class lectures tend to drag on.Refer to what you learned in PETE 169. Simple assignments. Textbook is expensive, use course reserve to prepare for online tests. Buy lesson plan book separately if poss.

Dr. Pennington was great. Don't buy the text until after the 1st day of class. The only problem is with the class itself. All 212 classes require a ton of time, completely different than 169. Exams were easy. I missed one exam and he let me make it up for minimal point deduction (5%!). Recommended.
Pennington is extremely helpful!

Todd is an awesome teacher! He gets into the lessons with you. He also accepts your ideas insteading of telling you you're wrong like other teachers will. If you go into the PETE program, you will have fun in this class.
Wonderful teacher! Not the greatest tennis player - but very very nice. Fun class.
Great v-ball teacher, tries really hard but isn't all that wonderful at volleyball.

He's fantastic. He wants his students to succeed and goes over everything you need to know. He talks about studying bears A LOT, I actually love him. Probably the GOAT of biology teachers. Everyone should take his class.
Very funny and knowledgable proffesor. Class was educational and entertaining. One 6 page paper. Thats your only assignment. 4 exams not to hard.

Tom Smith is the best professor I have ever had. This class was easy, but I learned a lot, and he did good at relating it to the gospel. There is a textbook, you can read it, but to be honest, I didn't, if you show up to class every day you can easily get an A. There are 4 exams, and 1 final project. No other homework, although he takes attendance.

I had a super fun time in this class. You definitely have to show up otherwise you won't pass. Professor Smith is funny and engaging; you can tell he's passionate about what he teaches. Pretty easy class for those taking it as a general. There are four exams, but if you study for each you'll be fine. TAs hold review sessions and post study guides.

Professor Smith is THE BEST. He is a Polar Bear scientist and has a real passion for what he teaches. He is hilarious, and delivers wonderful lectures. Exams are often curved, as he cares for his students dearly. Wonderful TA's as well. Take PWS 150 from Tom Smith! He wants you to succeed. I am a better man than I was before.

Absolutely hilarious, knows how to make a firehose of material enjoyable without diminishing its importance. Tests are fairly memorization heavy but the study guides should get you by. He knows most people are taking the class for the GE credits and balances it accordingly. Worth taking the class just for his stories.

I LOVE THIS GUY
Pretty easy, four tests, but I studied minimally and got low As in them. TAs are amazing and care, and tom does too. Tom is so fun and he lectures great, even though the material isn't like the most interesting. Would def take again

Environmental Biology counts as two GEs, and is pretty dang easy. 

Just skim the textbook readings and go to class. Tom goes off on tangents but is a very down to earth and pretty funny, and has like 20 years of experience studying bears, so he definitely knows the stuff beyond the textbook. 

Great way to knock out 2 GEs

Tom does not go by the syllabus. He makes changes without alerting students. There was no communication between the TA and the professor in regards to assignments and projects. Extremely disorganized and chaotic class.

Professor Smith is so funny. I enjoyed his lectures. DO THE READINGS and GO TO THE REVIEW SESSIONS and you'll get an A. This class is not a lot, and it's not hard UNLESS you get behind. There are four tests, one paper, and mandatory attendance.

Prof Smith is a great teacher! He gave the class so many opportunities to succeed. He is really passionate about everything he teaches so it makes the classes much more engaging. When taking the exams, go to the TA reviews!!! They are super helpful. It was a super easy general to take.

My favorite class I've taken at BYU and it's only a GE. Professor Smith is such an admirable scholar, he literally has done so many reputable things in his career outside of teaching which adds so much credibility to his class. He is the funniest person ever, I was always laughing in his class. Test heavy and one paper, but TA reviews help a lot.

1 large group project over the whole semester. Textbook questions every single day of class. Lab writeups. Two midterms, a lab final, and a lecture final. Lectures that are all over the place. Interesting class and not difficult.

This class was once a week and we got certified in multiple things like CPR and gun handling. He grades on attendance only, so you have to show up. I wouldn't want to miss the class anyway because it was fun!!

Tom Smith was one of my easiest professors at BYU. His grading was straight forward and the subject was interesting (his stories and personal work were highlights of the class). Loved his laid-back teaching style
Only graded on a few things: in class quizzes, one paper, and four non-comprehensive exams. The class is memorization heavy, and lectures are all over the place.

Tom Smith is fantastic! He's so funny & I always looked forward to lectures. The class has clear & easy expectations. TA test reviews and the study guides he provides makes it easy to get As on the tests. There's also a lot of extra credit opportunities! No reason not to take this class!!

I loved this class. The assignments, labs, and weekly reading questions are all really easy. The tests are really tricky, but if you visit the TA's they will show you know what you need to study. The two midterms and the final are the only difficult parts of the class. The labs were absolutely mind-blowing, I loved them!
I loved Tom. Coolest guy ever and best stories/experience ever. Favorite professor. I totally would have skipped/hated the safety class except for him and the way he teaches/the stories he tells.

Professor Smith is one of the best professors you could have a class from at BYU. I took this course my the Biology GE and it is the easiest thing. If you read the text and attend class, you will get a good grade- easily. He also fixes students' broken things to make sure they don't end up in the trash, including my short fused lights. He inspires!

Smith is an entertaining professor and this is a fairly easy class, just do all of the assignments and attend class and the reviews and you'll do well on the tests. Class attendance is important because iclickers will give you points and he makes test questions out of things discussed in class. He doesn't really have a filter but it makes class fun
Outstanding lectures. Dr. Smith is a pillar of unminced common sense, expertise, and practicality.
He says grades are based solely on attendance, but grades aren't in yet, so I can't say for sure that's right. Show up and you'll be fine.
