1 research paper (5-8 pages on anything biology-related), 4 tests (including non-comprehensive final), attendance points, and a lot of extra credit. A few test questions were tricky (or flat-out impossible), but that's my only complaint. His goal is for everyone to pass, so it's not a very difficult class.

I really enjoyed Professor Smith's Environmental Biology class. The lectures were actually really interesting, even though I'm going into Marketing, and the tests are a breeze if you go to class and the TA reviews. He is a total character, I loved it.

BIO 100 with Dr. Smith was a breeze. His lectures are long, but he is funny and he didn't make us memorize a bunch of useless processes that we would never need. (THANK YOU!) Take this if you are looking for an easy A in Bio 100.

Good teacher to take this from! His lectures sometimes seemed to drag, but he tries hard to make things interesting (One time he skyped us from Alaska for a study he was doing). You have to go to class for iClicker questions, but he offers a lot of extra credit and reviews/review sheets are way helpful. Hardly use the book if you have good TAs :)

By far the best Bio 100 teacher at BYU. Funny, caring, down to earth guy. Interesting lectures on relevant subject matter--and before, I really didn't like biology. Trust me, you don't have to read the textbook at all--the TA review sessions tell you every single test question and answer. Take it from him.

Smith is hilarious. You have to attend lectures because many test questions are only from in-class, but he always made them entertaining. TAs were always super helpful. He makes it clear what you need to know, so tests are manageable if you study. Recommend for all of those non-majors.
Super funny and fair. If you want an A it is so possible. You have to try to not get an A.

He is the best Bio 100 teacher. His lectures are very interesting, and you will do well on the tests if you just know the study guide well and go to the TA reviews (where they basically tell you test questions). He also gives tons of opportunitites for extra credit. If you get lower than a 70% on a test, he lets you have a take home test. The best!
Dr. Smith is the best bio 100 teacher at byu. Super easy, his lectures are accented by his tasteful sense of humor. I highly recommend him, especially if you don't want to do too much work.

Class was practically required because of iClicker quizzes, but many people skipped because it all seems so pointless. Prof. Smith is a nice guy, but I never learned anything in class. Your grade relies almost entirely on textbook reading. It's a pretty easy class, but if you're looking for a good lecture experience, DO NOT take from him.

He may not be the best teacher in the world, but he is a funny, interesting professor. His class was pretty easy. I didn't learn a whole lot in his class, but it was a freshman class. His teaching was a times a little unclear, but it was made up for by TA review sessions. He has some great stories. He gave a lot of extra credit opportunities.
This is a great class and Dr. Smith makes it very interesting and fun to learn.

Dr. Smith is a great Biology teacher. He cares about his students and does everything he can to make sure they succeed. Responded promptly to all of my emails, which rarely happens to me when I email the professor. I'm not a Biology person by any means, but he made the class interesting and manageable.
He is awesome and has awesome bear stories! Makes biology interesting and funny!

Dr. Smith is a really funny guy.  He likes to have fun and his class is pretty entertaining.  All his lecture material is from the book so it's easy to follow along.  Go to the TA review sessions, they helped a ton!  The tests are reasonable.  You're going to have to study.  Don't worry though, he offers a ton of extra credit to help your grade.
Brother Smith is awesome and really understanding of any problems you may have.

Dr. Smith is a funny guy, so class is fairly entertaining because of his stories. However, all his lecture material comes straight from the textbook--same pictures, same phrasing, etc. This would make coming to class unnecessary, but he uses daily iclicker quizzes to keep you coming. He said he was going to stop using iclicker though, so who knows?

Smith is a really funny guy to learn bio from. He has the best, although not always so relevant, stories about everything. He gives tons of opportunities for extra credit. it's just bio100 but as long as you follow the review guides you'll do just fine on the tests.

Brother Smith is great! I don't like biology. I have no interest in it at all. But because I had Brother Smith, I actually enjoyed this class! He's really funny, and casual. And I love that he doesn't know everything about the subject. It's great to have a teacher who learns with the class. Brother Smith is amazing! I would recommend him to anyone.
He is a bear biologist, and is not any good at Microbiology. Not recommended.
Tom Smith is a funny guy.  He did a lot of bear research in Alaska so you hear a lot of funny stories.
The online resources are great, but the lectures weren't great. I thought that the HW assignments were difficult and progress checks/the final were unreasonable.

Dr. Stephens is a great guy. He's very straightforward with his expectations. This class is harder than CS 111/142, but he rewards staying on top of the assignments and will give a small amount of extra credit for doing them early. The final this semester was an in-class coding project that was very manageable. He is very accessible and inspiring.

I really liked Dr. Stephens. It's really clear that he thoroughly understands the topics that he is teaching, even though he never got a degree in computer science. He also always posts the slides for each lecture and has video presentations from when he taught CS236 online.

The online section is not forgiving in the slightest. You have to do well on everything to do well in the class. Fortunately they let you turn in everything late for full credit and are quick graders. The time commitment is really inconsistent with some weeks taking an hour or two and other weeks taking like ten hours of work.

Grading in the online section is rough. You must meet a minimum in each category (HW, Projects, Progress Checks, Skill Assessments, Final), and your lowest category becomes your final grade. Teaching was okay, but you'll need solid Python skills to succeed. I did not do well on 2 Skill Assessments so I failed the class. Not very forgiving.

Most CS professors I've had overcomplicate their lectures and accidentally talk about things outside of the course curriculum that I don't understand. Dr Stephens is very good at giving clear lectures that follow the course content. He was very willing to answer questions and would sometimes work out the hw on the board during lectures.

I took CS111 online and it was probably a lot better to do than in person. You have to have some programming experience or this class will eat you alive. Also, the online lectures were a little hard to follow and sometimes didn't leave you very prepped for assignments and/or tests/projects. Lots of work to understand well.

I'm not sure if it was a department change or just him but a change to the midterms and final exam was implemented during my specific semester (winter 25) that definitely hurt my grade. The exam involved implementing a data structure with no notes instead of doing a multiple choice exam. I've heard some professors don't do exams like this

In all honesty the class content is pretty easy, but the professor and TAs made it so much more difficult. Dr. Stephens is a smart guy but he didn't explain the topics and code very well. Attending lectures honestly didn't help me learn the content, which is frustrating because that's what I pay lots of money for.

Tom Stephens is very knowledgeable and kind, but this online course is awful. The lecture videos are difficult to follow, assignments often feel unrelated to the material taught in the videos, so be prepared to teach yourself, and utilize ChatGPT extensively.

His lectures were boring, but it the assignments weren't that bad, you can submit as much as you want and he has all of his lectures posted, I got 103 in the class, and I am like average when it comes to cs. It is in c++, but you learn how to use it pretty well. I would definitely recommend taking it during either spring or summer term, by itsself
Very kind and inspirational professor. Awesome teacher.

The class was poorly organized. Instructions for labs, hw, and projects did not instruct well at all, even had typos and grammar errors. The last day of classes had the two biggest, most difficult projects of the semester due at the same time. Stressed out of my mind navigating that and my other hw and preparing for finals.

I'm sure Dr. Stephens is nice, but CS 235 online was HORRIBLY organized. Assignments not published or out of order, instructions that were wrong, and autograders that just didn't work. Once I reported the problems on the CS Discord, it would take several days to fix it. The content isn't hard, but the class was like banging your head into the wall.

The canvas course was horribly designed. At one point a semester long project changed from being extra credit to required, 3 weeks before being due. No remorse was given. The final was a blind live coding challenge, which really just required rote memorization, as no help in debugging or outside resources was allowed. How is that fair in coding?

I think this teacher was mostly trying to teach us how to memorize instead of how to be an actual programmer. There were several live-coding exams where we were not allowed to look at our notes or use any outside resources AT ALL. That is not what programmers do in the real world.

Dr. Stephens really knows his stuff. His lectures are great, and if you don't want to attend the lectures he posts videos online. The TA lab is a great resource for the class, and Dr. Stephens has office hours all the time.

CS111 is a great class. It has the same curriculum as the equivalent at UC Berkeley, which has a top 5 CS program in the nation. If you ever want to do coding, DO NOT USE CHATGPT for this course. You need to really understand this content and be able to do it all on your own for your long term success. It's an easy A if you care to work a bit

He organizes the class, but the TAs really run it. He is available though and tries to help as much as he can. Not a hard class and he tries to makes lab as little busywork as possible. First few labs are much harder (or maybe you just get used to them). Not a class to stress about.

The given notes are super helpful, and you can use them on tests. The tests are incredibly difficult to complete within the time limit, but there are rework points, and you learn a lot from those reworks.

CH EN 273 is a very difficult class, but it would have been a lot more difficult without Dr Knotts' organization. My notes have never looked better, which is very helpful since you get to use them in tests.
Dr Knotts is great at presenting the curriculum in a straightforward way. He helps break down what exactly you need to know about each topic and is clearly focused on your success!

Dr. Knotts really cares about his students! The material as hard, but he does a good job explaining it and used and online text book that was straight to the point. He also allowed for exam rework and getting points back, which was very kind of him. The final project was roughly. He shows that he cares and is there to help.

He makes the class rigorous. The formatting of the homework is specific. The tests are hard. My advice is to make sure you master the basic principles. That will make the quizzes easy and you won't be pressed for time on the tests.
Avoid taking this class from him if you can. It is in your best interest. At the end of the semester, he dropped my grade down to a 79.9%, then gave me a C+. Make of that what you will.
Dr. Knotts is great. He teaches very clearly and gives you plenty of practice on the homeworks. Be ready to work, but be comforted that he makes it very manageable.

Dr. Knotts did a very good job teaching this difficult course. He is good at drilling the main concepts and is always happy to help struggling students. The workload was a bit too much for some of the semester, but he made it less time consuming as this came to his attention. Dr. Knotts is a great lecturer and wants his students to be successful.

"You don't get paid to solve problems that have already been solved" . basic teaching philosophy. I disagree with that. His lectures are specific, but his notes/annotations are sloppy. He's accessible outside of class, but I didn't get good answers to my questions. He basically says, "It's the right answer because it's the right answer." Avoid.

He did a splendid job! Was always prepared for his lectures and he makes everything clear. He is awesome. You can do well in his class if you are well prepared for the final exam. The final was 35% of the grade and it took me to the grade of A- only because I messed up a VBA problem. Overall, he is the best professor in the department!

Good teacher. He truly cares about his students. He communicates very clearly and his lectures are easy to understand. Also, he teaches you how to solve general engineering problems, not just the stuff covered in the class.

He's a great guy, and I learned a lot from the class.  It's kind of hard to apply class to homework because the class is so fast paced, and it's hard to get good notes.  I would strongly suggest getting TA help so you don't have to stay up all hours of the night figuring out how to program in VBA  because you missed it in class.
Dr. Knotts is a really good teacher, and is always extremely helpful. You learn a lot from him. He does expect a lot from you--more than you might expect from a 2 credit class.
He is very helpful and willing to take time to explain things to you. Good teacher.

Dr. Stay is one of my favorite Psych/Neuro professors. He's extremely intelligent and knowledgeable, and easy to access with questions. Also just a great resource for general career advice! He is a little disorganized, but was open to feedback and would give points back on test questions and enough extra credit it didn't matter for the grade.

Not PSYCH 2375, but super rough. He's really unclear in the way he teaches and not consistent in his class content and exams. All of the students in this class have expressed having a difficult time with him and feeling like we're not learning much. I'm purposefully extending an extra semester so that I don't have to take another class from him.

Dr. Stay is a rollercoaster of a human. He is really fun to interact with and is really high energy, but also often too high energy. He'll get impatient during lectures and go REALLY fast. He also read his midcourse reviews to us, and proceeded to ignore all of the feedback.He gives out plenty of extra credit, which is how I still ended with an A.

Dr. Stay is one of a kind. He's funny, caring, and intelligent. His assignments are practical and related to the content, and tests aren't too difficult. If you read the textbook and go to class you'll be fine. Attendance is mandatory, but it's because he wants you to consolidate everything you read in the textbook. BYU is lucky to have Dr. Stay.

Dr. Stay is a really considerate and kind teacher. I thought all the assignments and tests were very manageable. The hardest thing for me was getting the essay done at the end of the semester, but you get to choose your topic so you can make things easier on yourself if you choose.

Dr. Stay is one of the best humans I know- what a gem. He cares about each one of his students, and our learning is his top priority. There were quizzes at the beginning of class over the textbook. So, read the book and come to class and you're good to go. Would definitely take from Dr. Stay again. As someone else here said,BYU is lucky to have him

Dr. Stay was brand new this semester, and he did a great job. He regularly asked for our feedback and input about the class, which was appreciated. He was kind and gave engaging lectures with lots of examples. I wish the research paper had been organized differently, but he might change things next semester! Overall, had a great experience!

This class was really easy, definitely the easiest one in the Japanese minor. I liked the content of what you learned, including business Japanese, etiquette, useful vocab, etc. Andreason sensei is extremely understanding and fair.

She is really kind but sometimes I felt like there were some concepts that weren't explained well. I'd say the things you learn are purely based on memorization to the very detail so that's why I didn't feel like I truly "learned" much, felt very robotic/tedious. It's a very manageable class though and easy to get a good grade in.

Great class. I was nervous because I did not serve a mission in Japan, but Andreason-sensei was there to support me. She was always available after class to talk. If you do all of the assignments and participate in class, getting an A is very achievable. Overall, great class! Do not hesitate to add!

As long as you fully participate in class and do the assignments, this class will be a breeze! Prof. Andreason does really well in teaching all the material and preparing you for tests and quizzes. She also offers some extra credit opportunities. This was a great class for learning higher level (keigo) Japanese conversation skills!

Traci Sensei is nice and wants you to do well. Some people get frustrated by class organization and felt like we sometimes wasted class time. I just took it to have a low stress class that helps me keep up with Japanese. There are a few vocab quizzes, a midterm, oral presentation, mock interview, 1 take home test, and a final. VERY manageable.

Prof. Andreason is a kind, patient, competent, and altogether great professor. Despite slight disparities in ability level in our class, she helped all of us to learn and progress, and gain confidence along the way. I felt that I learned a lot of useful things in her class, and enjoyed doing so, too. Would recommend to anyone.
Great Professor. She cares about the students who care about her class. Put in the effort and you will get an A.

I just finished this class and really loved it! Great real-life application and I was always interested in what we talked about in class. Everyone has to do a presentation, not my favorite thing but it wasn't bad. I would recommend this class to anyone!

While this class is unbelievably easy, and the content of the textbook is pretty good, this class feels like a seminary class or sunday school more than anything else. You can get an easy A, and get away with not going to class pretty easily, but when you do go get ready to hear about church newsroom stories for a couple hours.
This is a great class. Keep up with textbook reading (usually 6 medium chapters a week) and go to class for lectures and you'll do great! We never took the full 3 hours of class.
I'm in this class now and I love it! It's one of my favorites I have taken at BYU. If you are debating taking it, it's totally worth it.

This was a great class with really relevant content. You need to show up and participate to really get the most out of what she has to offer. But Tracie is so kind and loving, she really wants her students to find success in her class. I loved the text, it really opened my eyes to a lot. Her class has been one of my favorites at BYU.

I was impressed with Tracie and how she used her real life experience in her lectures. She is a passionate teacher and knows what she is talking about. The class was valuable and I think it was more than fair as far as work load goes. I enjoyed learning from her and I felt like the class was totally worth taking.

I thought that the textbook for this class(Gender, Race, and Class in Media by Dines) was so interesting. Lectures were, on the other hand, very underwhelming. Since Tracie works for Church newsroom, we talked a lot about church news and it often felt like a Sunday School lesson. 4 papers(really easy), quizzes, midterm, final and class presentation

Tracy is the most amazing professor! She is so knowledgeable and also so kind. She genuinely cares about each student and is always happy to chat outside of class. I also loved her lectures! They were engaging and super informative. We did lots of hands-on activities during class.

Pro. Liu is the purest sole and AMAZING. That being said, this class is HARD. It is test and quiz heavy so there isn't a ton of room for error. The amount of info to learn is comparable to lecture of CELL 220 at the same pace. 2 tests, a final, a quiz about every week, and 4 "case studies" that are easy. TAs and Pro Lui are always ready to help.

Professor Liu is AMAZING! She is kind, intelligent, and genuine. She uses personal experiences in the medical field to provide meaning to course content. She is inspiring and loving towards everyone. Although the quizzes are 10 questions free response, you can do well if you study the slides well. One of my fav classes this semester.

This was a great class, and the professor did an excellent job making Organizational Behavior engaging and relevant to us personally. He used real-life experiences and examples to explain concepts which made the material much easier to understand and apply.  I would definitely recommend Tracy to students taking Organizational Behavior.

I thought that Dr. Maylett was an outstanding professor that taught about what he knew from his professional background. The classes were always useful and even though there was a lot of psychology taught it seemed to apply perfectly to business. I recommend his classes to business students but also for any organization.

Dr. Maylett is organized in his teaching and syllabus (Organization Effectiveness class so you would think he should be) but focuses more on helping students learn than sticking to covering everything in the syllabus. Classes are fun and have good points that we can use in business. Attendance isn't mandatory but he does have quizzes.

Maylett is the best! Seriously a great professor that wants students to learn. He applies the topic to business and personal life, also other organizations like church and government. He made it understandable. Classes were surprisingly useful for what I thought would be a fluff class.

I changed my major because of Tracy's class. Tracy teaches in a very practical way based on his experience and also the texts and reading. His classes were always prepared and his teaching was enthusiastic. He was willing to spend time with me outside of class. He also trusted us to learn and believed in his students.
I would rather shove a cactus up where the sun don't shine than spend another minute listening to Tracy promote his book or company. If he wants to be a marketer, he should do that instead of HR.

Tracy is a good teacher overall. He is a fair grader (although many of the assignments on a weekly basis are graded by a TA). The classes were always interesting and even entertaining because he didn't always just teach from the text and slides. He used a lot of outside examples and examples from his own work to help teach.

This was one of the most practical courses I have taken at BYU. Readings and assignments were fine but classes were always very interesting and relevant. You can tell he is prepared and wants students to learn. TAs were picky about what was included in the weekly assignments.

So much busy work in this class. the only point of it was to promote his book and business.
Tons of papers that are graded harshly. Lots of meaningless groupwork. 
He preaches "Engagement MAGIC" but can't even engage a class of students. People only showed up because of random quizzes. Take this class from literally anyone else.

He is good but he is one of those professors that has written several books and forces his students to buy them so he gets a profit. I refused to pay for the books because I thought he was being greedy, Turns out, he rarely even references the book in class... so my grade was fine. Good teacher thought. But dont buy his books, find a pdf online.

Class is just busywork. Diff teachers are easier. We had to write 4 essays 7-9 pages each. TA's and Tracy are super nitpicky graders and don't give you feedback. Tracy also heavily promotes his company and makes you buy his book which you definitely do not need. In my class of 50+ kids only 1 person got full participation points for the semester.

I really enjoyed lectures! I found them very interesting. There are "pop quizzes" but he often gives you a hint the class beforehand. The TAs grade kind of hard, you have to write a lot of fluff. 2000 word essay on a SMART goal you created for the semester. Couple of group projects at the end.

Don't buy the Organizational Behavior textbook---just find an old version on Reddit. It doesn't make a difference. To get good grades on written assignments, just cite things like crazy to show you did the reading. Tests are open note. I really enjoyed this class!!!!

This class seemed hard at first because I did not understand his system of pop quizzes and reflection questions. Tip: Studying powerpoint slides before class will help you do well on pop quizzes and being very thorough about citing your prep work and readings will help on reflection questions. Overall, fairly easy class and a very caring professor.

Prof Maylett is a good teacher. He has real world experience that he applies to his teaching. There are a lot of random assignments in this class, but none of them are ever very hard. He makes it easy to succeed in this class.

For being a morning class I am amazed he was able to keep us all awake. Dr. Maylett did a great job with such a big class (that's my one piece of negative feedback, the class was really big) keeping me coming and awake. Assignments were due most weeks but they were questions we had to answer. The professor works in this subject area.

This class was required for me so I wasn't very excited to take it. But Prof Maylett made it enjoyable and something that I can use. He seemed to care about both the class and the students and met with me a couple of times outside of class. He used lots of practical examples and his personal professional experiences to teach. Requires reading.

Great professor, knows the subject and works in the HR field. I have had two classes from him now, Organization Behavior and a Leadership class, and each was excellent. There is quite a bit of writing, which was a surprise, but the assignments were helpful. Great entertaining lectures, easy to listen to. Highly recommend.

He did as good of a job as you can teaching an HR class, I feel like I didn't learn anything and wish I didn't have to take it. Class is super easy and offers extra credit. I pretty much just showed up and worked on other homework. He strongly promotes his own books which I found odd. He puts a lot of effort into the class.

This class is essentially just common sense. Prof. Maylett gives a lot of busy work and requires minimum lengths on his essays of around 1500 - 2000 words. The midterm and final both were worded quite poorly and no one got 100% on either. Prof. Maylett made this class a drag and it felt like a complete waste of my time.
Great info.
I enjoyed the connections to real-world companies, as well as the variety of readings, videos, and activities used for homework. Just do the work, turn everything in on time, and you'll pass.

Professor Maylett cares deeply for his students and incorporates personal growth projects into the class. I feel like I learned and grew a lot. Be aware that he is a really tough grader! Also, your class participation is a big part of the grade and you really have to work for that credit. Make sure you do the pre-class work because it is worth alot

I would avoid taking this class from tracy. I have never met a more self righteous person in my life. He uses this class as a platform to promote himself, his book, and his company. Most of the class is filled with useless assignments and information. I am not one to complain or write reviews like this. I enjoy most my classes and teachers.

There is quite a bit of classwork for this course, but it is all pretty easy. Your grade depends a lot on what kind of TA you get to grade your papers. The class is really interesting and Dr. Maylett does a great job teaching and explaining new concepts.

Dr. Maylett is a good Professor and has a lot of experience in Organizational Experience. The class is interesting and the assignments aren't to tough. Most of the time he tells you when you will have a quiz. His tests cover a lot of material from all sorts of places. The thing that makes this class a bit tough is that the A is a 95%.
Dr. Maylett's class is interesting and helpful - real world application. If you are engaged you will learn so much. Its great having a CEO of a successful company teach you about business.

Tracy has a lot of great experience and knowledge. Was a really good class, but I honestly expected more from a CEO. The class was mostly on leadership theory, not real world application, which I didn't expect.
Fairly interesting class

I think the subject matter carries a lot in this class, it's just so fascinating. Dr. Anderson's lectures are good, but you have to really pay attention to both the lectures and the readings to get what's going on. It's a lot of reading but it is worth it.

Poorly organized and turned fascinating material into dull lectures. This class includes a film unit, but is mostly memorization of technical terms without any film clips as demonstrations of the vocabulary. Even as a film buff, I was bored to tears. He's kind and caring and occasionally passionate about the material, but ultimately ineffective.

Anderson is nice. Checked in when I didn't do well on midterm. But for midterm & final I studied the study guide for days & still did poorly. There's often reading quizzes worth 2 points so it's very easy to do bad on them cause the reading makes no sense. I thought ethics would be easy, I never understood it. Lectures are dry and easy to get lost

The content itself is primarily a history of philosophies and their accompanying philosophers. Expect a quiz based off of the readings in almost every class. He does give extra credit for exemplary work. Attend the test reviews at all costs. It's a fine enough class for the Letters credit, but I wouldn't recommend taking it in your first semester.

Professor Anderson is a great guy, he really shows he cares for his students... the class is just not it:/ The lectures are dry and there are 2 question pop quizzes almost every day. Take good notes and make sure you know EXACTLY what he's talking about. Overall, he's a great guy, and I would recommend the class if you really like ethics.

Travis's lectures are generally derived from his life experiences, and I really like how helpful they are in explaining hard philosophy concepts. He's lived a full life and I really like hearing about his experiences. He usually assigns a lot of reading, but the lectures are so worth attending.
Passing Grade. He's pretty busy but leaves good feedback on my resume. Not an official philosophy major but still believe some stuffs are pretty useful for my future career.

He's so sweet. There were very few grades, but the tests are relatively easy if you study. There is only one paper, about 4-5 pages. I actually had a lot of fun in this class. He gives study guides too.
Terrible. Never take one class from him.

Professor Anderson gives great feedback and he really cares about his students learning the material. He is incredibly smart and really knows his stuff. He can be a bit dry / old school in his teaching style, but overall I would definitely recommend.
Most caring professor at BYU. Unfortunately he had some biases that seemed unfair when grading papers. His lectures were very stale and boring but usually ended with a lot of thought and feeling.

Great class. Lectures could be a little monotonous at times and he would often go off on tangents answering questions. Only had to write one paper all semester, the rest of your grade is made up of quizzes, 1 midterm, and 1 final. A good introductory class to ethics and philosophy. I would recommend this class.

By far the best professor I've had at BYU who teaches in a very thorough manner such that you will understand the material well by the end of class. He cares about every individual and wants them to succeed. This can be a tough class, but I found it very worth it and doable, especially with his teaching methods. Not an easy A but very enlightening.

Professor Anderson is one of the most caring professors I've ever had. He really makes an effort to get to know and help students to the best of his ability. He doesn't use slides so lectures can consist of a lot of rambling, but he adequately prepares you for assignments and exams if you are paying attention. Overall, an interesting class.

He told us not to worry about using sources in our first paper and then proceeded to take off points from all of our papers for not using enough sources. This class is a general, and he teaches as though none of us know anything. He's a good man and cares for his students, so if you have time to talk, he'll work with you, but lectures are a slog.

A great guy but he is just not a great professor. A lot of his explanations are very circular. He spends the whole time saying the same thing in different ways but it sounds like different things which really confuses students. His class lectures are convoluted subject outlines with no real application or interesting conversations.

I loved this class so much! He was so nice, super caring, and an amazing teacher. It was totally online, and he did so well with accommodating with the changes from covid. His lectures were extremely detailed, and he is extremely intelligent so listening to his lectures were really fun. The papers are hard and long, but not too bad.

I personally loved Doctor Anderson. He creates a very positive discussion environment, separate from religion but not in a bad way . His classes are mainly just discussions over the textbook reading. The way the class is set up is fairly straightforward, and if you ever need help he would do anything to assist you out of class. Would take again!

Prof Anderson is my favorite professor that I have had at BYU so far. He cares about his students above anything else, and the course content is really easy if you do the readings. He will take time in class to ensure that you understand concepts and to help you fill out a chart that you will use for studying for exams. I miss going to this class!

Professor Anderson really cares about his students and will do whatever it takes for them to succeed. This is a great class for the Letters general. The tests are taken in class and are not too difficult if you study that table that you should be working on the whole semester.

Professor Anderson the nicest professor you could get. His classes are generally smaller so the structure of the class may be different than some of the other bigger classes. There is usually one quiz a week that is only 2 questions. He does not use slides and the material is heavily reliant upon the readings.

Professor Anderson really cares about his students and wants to make sure everyone has an opportunity to succeed. He's brilliant and knows a lot about philosophy. He's always willing to help students even if it means helping them on his own time. One of the kindest and funniest professors I've ever met. You'd love him!

Professor Anderson is a phenomenal teacher with sincere concern for your success. His lectures are very interesting and comprehensive. Each class hour has a homework quiz associated, each worth 1.7% of the grade, so be there. His tests are based on the application of course material, but the lecture material will adequately prepare you.

Professor Anderson is very kind and cares about class discussion. Going to class isn't super important if you do the reading every week and show up for weekly quizzes. Class itself was very easy. The tests are not too bad if you review the study guide and read carefully.

Two tests and two essays all semester. Brother Anderson loves teaching and it shows, he really encourages us to get to know him outside class. Super engaging class discussions all the time. Good classmates matter a lot. Tests can be tricky because they're specific and not exactly what's in class. Recommend if you're taking philosophy as an elective

Heidegger was arguably the best class I enrolled in at BYU. I believe Dr. Anderson was a big reason why.  The material coupled with Anderson's explanations are incredible.  Staying on schedule was often difficult. Material was challenging so consequently, papers and tests were too. Heidegger is now my favorite philosopher. Life-changing class.

Professor Anderson, and his horrific mustache, give very bland lectures. He also likes to make sure you know he is smarter than you. He gave us our final paper requirements and proceeded to tell us how easy the essay would be for him to complete.

Take Anderson, whether or not you are a philosophy major. When it comes to Philosophy Lectures, you will learn so much in a mere weekly 45 minutes. His rubric and grading makes it mandatory that you put in an effort to improve your writing. I appreciated how I was welcome to raise my hand and ask questions.

Professor Anderson is the most caring man I've ever met. The class itself was a little unorganized, there was a lot of reading, and the tests were a little on the hard side, but it was a fairly easy GE. If you put in the time you will get an A.

His Philosophy class is not terribly hard, but you don't feel like you're learning a lot throughout and Dr. Anderson seems a little in over his head in a teaching setting. He's super nice though and wants to help, just inefficient with time.

Team-taught with Faulconer on Being and Time. Loved it. Didn't do well, which was my fault for late papers. Heidegger might change your life, and these guys know Heidegger up and down. I graduated three years ago and wanted to leave this review because the class meant that much to me. Difficult concepts, not for lightweights.

Professor Anderson is one of the nicest people I have ever met, and spent unbelievable amounts of time and effort in helping his students succeed.  This was a film class, and was very interesting and fun.  We had a few papers, but they were fairly easy.  He even helped answer study questions on our GoogleDoc to help us on the test. Great professor!
Professor Anderson was great for the Honors Summer program I took with him. He really cares about his students and went above and beyond the course requirements to give us extra help and advice.

Nice guy, but his class was really unorganized. You had to keep asking questions about curriculum or he would let the class devolve into arguments hidden as "discussions" about theories. READ THE TEXT BOOK. It will save your life during the tests. The exams were MC, but the questions were so long you had to read them three times to understand.

Don't take this class. Dr. Anderson seems nice-ish, but his course organization is poor and his syllabus is verbose and confusing. He contradicted himself and the syllabus multiple times. When students asked questions about paper 1 because he kept contradicting himself, he sent a nasty email to the class insulting everyone. Tests aren't bad though.

Dr. Anderson is great. This class is really interesting and informative. It is a bit tricky to maintain a decent grade, but it is worth taking. Dr. Anderson  is more than willing to help and genuinely cares about his students.

My suggestion: run and hide.  Dr. Anderson seems sincere in his desire to teach, he just doesn't know how to do it well.  Why?: 1) extremely inefficient with time 2) no formal assessment 3) poorly designed curriculum 4) assessment content not consistent with course content
He really cares about his students.

Prof Anderson is a smart guy, but you have to ask him questions in class to get him to teach the material. Otherwise he lets the classes become a discussion from class members and you learn NOTHING! He is very disorganized. Attendance is mandatory, but just bring your book and study it if you must take this class. Tests were MC but HUGE questions.

Pretty good class.  My only problem is that it seemed like there wasn't a whole lot of organization.  Travis has a very hard time if you disagree with him... he seems to have a complex that a student could not possibly know as much about anything as he "the teacher" does.

The class is somewhat difficult because the ideas are so abstract.  However, Dr. Anderson does a good job in explaining them to you.  He is very fair and works hard to help students understand the concepts.  Good teacher.

I have so much respect for Professor Anderson!  He is such a great teacher and will go out of his way to help you.  He is a genius when it comes to philosophy and is also an amazing artist.  He does a great job of clearly explaining difficult material.  I strongly recommend this class to anyone!

Took a class on Emmanuel Levinas and loved it.  The material was difficult, but Anderson did an excellent job of explaining everything.  He also was very flexible on deadlines to give us more time to think things through.  Ended up being one of my favorite classes from one of my faorite professors.

He is the man. The class is way fun. Professor Anderson is smart and passionate about what he teaches. He is very helpful and has helped me create amazing films though continual improvement. He takes a good interest in his students.

Ok class.  Some of the lectures were really good.  Don't bother going for help, he's too self-conscious to offer any.  Really too concerned with art to be a philosophy professor but not good enough at art to be an art professor.  I guess he chose the easier of the two.  Not surprising
Very interesting class.  Liked listening to the lectures.  Material was very difficult though.  Tests not bad.  Teacher has very good insights and is fun.
Super easy class!

I want to give Travis a 5, but I wasn't a fan of the tests. We would randomly have to memorize some big facts and "Pillars of Psychology" that just felt a little meaningless and rote. Those were only talked about for maybe 20 minutes in the total semester. His lectures were great though and I learned a lot. He definitely cares!

Trav was the best! He cared about our success and provided lots of opportunities to succeed. Good extra credit options, and I always felt well-prepared for the exams. The only feedback I have is that the UnQuizz assignments seemed like a little more work than they were worth.
Dr. Travis is amazing! I recomend taking this class from him : )

Just a chill class, interesting textbook and kind of boring lectures. He's a super fun guy and we did a dope class March Madness bracket for extra credit and guess the score with prize every weekend of BYU mens basketball. The nicest ever and a really easy class with straightforward assignments

He gives a lot of extra credit opportunities, He is hilarious and super kind. Go to class because there are some on class assignments and because it worth it. But attendance is not mandatory for him, you mark your own attendance, don't forget to do it though. A bunch of TAs.

This class was a little boring, honestly, but that's just how the class is. The tests were fairly easy if you watched the TA reviews, and you don't even need to get the textbook because you can check it out from the library. Would definitely recommend Prof. Blackwelder to anyone taking the class!

Homeboy Travis is a real one. I was kinda scared for this class since I don't like history, but it doesn't even feel like a history class. Travis is hilarious and always makes class fun. I would definitely recommend him for any psych class.

Frequently goes on long side tangents that have little to do with class material. The textbook does most of the teaching, and he tends to just summarize it during lectures. The best lectures are the ones taught by the TA's, and the criteria for writing assignments is vague to nonexsistent. He does have good extra credit though.
Incredible professor. Incredible class. So kind, respectful, and funny. Genuinely one of the most Christ-like professors on campus.

This professor is one in a million! I loved his class so much and the energy and vibes he brought are unmatched. He is so sweet and teaches with the spirit. Hearing his story and the way he makes everyone feel important and loved is so good. I would take any class from him. Extra credit each game week if you just guess the final score

Travis made this class fun and he's very knowledgeable. You know what you're going to be tested on, and the TA's are easy graders. Go to the TA reviews, they basically give you all the answers for exams. Don't worry about this class if you take with Travis, just enjoy learning cool new things about psychology.

If I could describe Travis in one word, it would be delightful. His lectures are very chill. Participation is VERY important, huge chunk of the grade. Cons: The TAs suck, they often have no clue what they are talking about content wise. Their reviews do almost 0 to help. However, the tests are easy if you use the slides and study guide:) loved it!!

Wonderful professor! He will emphasize gospel connections. You do have to refer to the textbook for some assignments. His lectures are fast, but you learn the material better by attending and asking questions. The best advice is to do your research paper early and have your TA review your APA citations; also, fill out the study guides as you go!

This class was easy and time spent in class was mostly focused on learning APA format and tips on writing the final paper. There's also a final presentation but it isn't too bad and there's a lot of help. The TAs and Travis were helpful and provided good feedback. The lectures were a little boring but everyone in the class grew close together.

Professor Blackwelder is awesome and super chill, but the way the class is set up is pretty poor. There's too much leeway but then grading on the last paper is harsh. You're tested on things before they're taught, and lectures are boring and not always focused on things you'll actually be tested on. Content is great though, take from someone else

Travis is such a kind and caring professor. I'll admit that oftentimes, going to lecture felt a little pointless because there wasn't a lot to learn - we were just writing a paper - but the community among the students in this class is unlike any other. I would 100% recommend taking PSYCH 307 from Travis!!

Took PSYCH 306 from Travis. Great guy, but definitely just reads off his slides. There's an occasional in class assignment, so attendance isn't mandatory, but you'll probably get more out of the class if you go. Awesome guy and cool class, but not super exciting. Assignments are easy enough, nothing too crazy.

Travis is such a nice person. Lectures are kinda boring and pointless for 307 because there is hardly any material to cover. You work on the final paper throughout the whole semester, so it isn't too overwhelming.

Didn't seem to care about the success of his students and is impossible to get in contact with. Even the TA's said he is impossible to reach, so good luck getting help if you need it. While the course content itself was great, he didn't seem prepared for lectures and canceled class frequently. He is a very kind guy, but not a great teacher.

Blackwelder is nice but a bad teacher. He never responds to emails, wasn't prepared for lecture, and had his TA's do everything. I asked to meet with him after having a medical emergency to get caught up in class, followed up with him over email and in person, and he didn't reply until a days before the. Even the TA's said they couldn't reach him.

Worst class ever! I thought I was going to lose my mind. Class was so boring and pointless and he gave no feedback until the very end. His TAs did all the grading and he seemed unprepared for lecture so I really don't know what he did. He cancelled class a lot which was nice but he also cancelled meetings with us. Nice guy but terrible professor

This man is hilarious!!! He is such a caring and kind professor entirely willing to work with you. He makes the content interesting. Be aware that there is a lot of reading, but you can skim and still pass the class. In class he will focus in on specific parts from the reading and that is what will be on the test. Start working on the paper early.

Great professor! Most of the lectures were interesting and he was pretty clear about what is expected on papers and assignments. The final and midterm seemed stressful but the TAs went over everything that would be on the tests beforehand. Really enjoyed his class and would love to take another one from him!

Super sweet man. Didn't love him as a teacher. Lectures weren't super interesting and didn't seem to have a lot to do with tests and assignments. A lot of busy work. One huge paper, graded pretty harshly. TAs tell you what you need to know for the exams, and if you just study what they say you'll do fine even without the textbook or lectures.

Travis was an amazing professor. His lectures were very entertaining and I could learn the information very well. He provides many extra credit opportunities and cares about all the students. The midterm and the final felt daunting but the TA reviews were helpful and I got good grades on both. Awesome professor!!

Travis is literally the sweetest man alive and such a funny guy too. Everything is super easy besides the 1 midterm and 1 final-- they basically make sure you've been attending class and can get a little tricky if you haven't (guilty). Besides that, you'll have a great time in his class. You do need the textbook for certain assignments.

Professor Blackwelder is very nice, and you can tell that he cares about his students. He tells you exactly what is going to be on the midterm and final and is very clear about grading. He gives lots of opportunities for extra credit and make-up work. He canceled class at least four times because he gets sick easily. Overall, great teacher!

This was a fantastic class! I would highly recommend this class to anyone who is considering it. It is a 349 course, but I took it as a freshman, and it wasn't too difficult compared to my other classes. Do pay attention to the reading quiz questions, names of psychologists, and the various lists you go over in class, they show up on the test.
Just an overall amazing guy with fun and straightforward lectures. All of the topics covered in this course are very interesting.

He was sick for a good portion of the semester, but class was pretty straightforward. Slides are a copy of the reading. Tests are a lot of memorization but it is possible. Not the hardest class overall, but you do need to do the readings and fill out the study guides

Professor Blackwelder is an amazing professor! He really cares about helping you not only succeed in his class but in your future endeavors as well. The workload wasn't too much and the assignments were interesting. The final paper was graded pretty hard but there were also many resources shown to help you during the writing process.

(PSYCH 307) Professor Blackwelder is one of the nicest and humblest people! He genuinely cares about his students. 307 with him means weekly writing, but it's relatively manageable. His expectations are clear with samples for each paper. Put a lot of work into the final paper! He takes forever to respond to emails so just talk to him in person.

Travis is the best! One of the most selfless, Christlike and humble people I've ever met. Worth taking just for him. Long readings, but easy overall and extremely enjoyable. I swear you won't regret taking this class! Would recommend to anyone, psych major or not. No prerequisites and he keeps it relaxed for people of all majors/backgrounds

Amazing professor, one of the kindest, humblest people there is. His lectures were eye opening and also relaxing. This is kind of like a self-help class. Its all fairly easy except for the first test is extremely hard and almost pure memorization. But after that its a breeze!

This class is perhaps the best class I'll ever take at BYU! Stellar professor and a stress free class, actually a stress reducing class. You have a few quick papers and he really cares about every single student and your wellbeing. There is a reading book that is your textbook, but this class can change your life!!! Everyone should take this class

Travis is the kindest professor to ever work at BYU. He gives so many chances for extra credit and wants you to get an A no matter what! The tests are very easy. The class is also beneficial to create a happier life style. I learned so much from his lectures, but also from his character of being such a good genuine man.
Best prof on campus. Hands down. So caring. Knows you by name and actually cares. So amazing!
He is so genuine and one of the best teachers on campus. Take him for sure if you can!

What a wonderful professor! Seriously this man is what got me through this semester. Very inspiring class and focuses on helping you be a happier person. He is very caring and tries the best to make you feel important! TAKE HIM!
Professor Dyer is an incredible professor! The class topics are very engaging and very real-world applicable. He is down to earth, but very intelligent, he knows how to explain topics well. 10/10!
Travis is the man. We were in a small class and the lectures were so engaging. It was a lot of activities and cases which were so fun. He really cares and wants you to succeed.

This was a good class. The annoying thing was that 70% of the points were earned within the last week of class (semester-long project and final exam), so it was really hard to have any idea how your grade would turn out. But, it was easy to get an A by studying his slides before taking the final and following the rubric for the project.
This was a fine class, but it was hard to know what was going to be on the Final Exam. The final project isn't that bad if you choose a good company.

Assuming this was his first time teaching this course at BYU. We are still waiting for a final exam score nearly two weeks after the test. The class did not have much substance and the professor went off on tangents many times during our class period ranting about randoms topics. More work then 1.5 credit class should typically be.

This class is genuinely just busywork. Rather than being able to actually listen and pay attention in class, all you do is fill out worksheet upon worksheet that are clearly supposed to be helpful but are really just mind numbing and distracting. Probably my least favorite religion class I've taken my entire time at BYU.

Prof. Searle's Restoration class is mind-numbingly easy, with that in mind, the lectures are insanely grueling and there is so much busy-work that it is impossible to learn anything. If you show up, you will get an easy A, there are 0 tests/essays, and there is hardly any out of class work, but I would NOT recommend this professor for this class.

Great class and choice for a religion credit! Most of the assignments were filling out pre-made slides about each prophet / apostle. Info needed was covered in class, so I got most homework done during lecture. Super easy but learned so much about the prophets' lives and teachings. Highly recommend!
class is a little dull. easy to sleep through. but he is such a sweet man and really cares for his students. No final too, which was nice. Just doing the work and you'll be just fine.

Professor Searle really cares about his student and he has a great testimony of the restored gospel. I enjoyed his lectures and he tells a lot of fun stories related to living prophets. There is no final in this class but you have to work on a semester long project and you have slides to submit every week.

Brother Searle is the sweetest. He had quite a few assignments, but none were extremely hard. The class is very focused on helping you build your testimony of the Savior through the teachings of the living prophets! Would take this class again!
Brother Searle doesn't have any tests, just requires you to take notes during class, which had very well thought out lectures. I loved this class.

This religion class was very easy to follow and understand, and had no final exam. Attendance is a major part of the grade. I don't personally love the way Professor Searle addressed certain difficult questions or issues in Church History, he is very orthodox which I know some people appreciate, but it's not for me personally.

Brother Searle is awesome! He treats a religion class the way it should - learning focused and not grade focused. His lectures are almost always engaging, I was never bored. He focuses always on the spiritual aspects, and my testimony was definitely strengthened. He's extremely smart as well

Probably the easiest religion class I've taken at BYU, but very informative and well-structured. Before/in-class reflections that are ~50 words, slides ab 2 apostles due every 2 weeks with a final culmination at the end, and a simple semester-long project. Super easy to get a good grade if you just put a little thought into it. Highly recommend.

If you want any easy religion class, take it with Professor Searle. I honestly didn't pay much attention but  his lectures were really interesting when I listened haha. Homework is super easy. There are no tests or final. He's a good guy

Class was easy, no exams or quizzes. You have fill out a module and have to do an activity every two weeks and write 2 essays total. The only downfall is the modules you have to fill out in class. Sometimes it was hard to focus on his teachings or feel the spirit when we were too busy trying to make sure we got the notes filled out.

Brother Searle is awesome! Love his stories! You just read short things about each apostle and create Slides on them. You don't present them. No midterm. Semester long project that is very manageable. Final project is creating a cumulative slide of some slides you've already created. He is funny and shares great personal experiences and stories!

Very easy class, but also very informative - I learned lots about each apostle. No tests at all. Just pre-class reflection questions, a slide deck about each apostle every other weekend, and then a project spread throughout the semester about finding answers to questions. I love Brother Searle - so kind and sincere!
Want an easy A class with no tests that tackles difficult church historical topics with sensitivity and an eternal perspective? Take his class. Wouldn't take this class from anyone else.

I think overall this was a good class. There was a semester long project about finding answers to our questions, and I feel like it wasn't super clear what he wanted sometimes. My class was once a week, so I don't think that sometimes it was adapted very well for our class compared to the twice a week class. Really cool class though!
I loved this class!
Easiest religion class I've taken. Good lectures and insight. Caring and tries to connect with students.

Lectures were quite boring, only created more confusion among the students than actually answered questions, and he constantly tried to do too much, hardly giving students any time for the in-class discussions he assigned. The homework assignments were nothing but busy work that forced you to repeat yourself constantly.

I learned a lot in this class, but I struggled to grow besides that. Lectures were stressful and most of it was spent frantically try to fill out charts. Outside of class there were more charts to fill out and it was a bit boring since we did the same thing every single time.

This class was the most seminary- like religion class I have taken at BYU and I loved it for that. I feel like I learned a lot being able to study how I wanted while also having specific things to learn about in a  structured way. Classes did require partner work and participation. Would recommend!
This class is so boring. It's just busy work but it's an easy A.

He is a great professor I learned a lot from his class. He has a lot of knowledge and you can tell he loves what he teaches. Not a ton of homework and a very manageable class. There were no actual exams which is the way I think religion classes should be done.

Travis Searle was a great professor. Even when i took the class with a ton of other students he still tried his best to talk with everyone. I loved the class living prophets because i gained a deeper understanding of them. There is only a project, 8 slide show every 2 weeks, and a final witness slide show. No test.
Enjoyed this class! He is a great professor who does a really good job answering questions in a clear and respectful way. Really organized.

He is a great teacher! He does a great job discussing difficult topics related to the Restoration and makes his lectures interesting with lots of discussion and real-life examples. Attendance is mandatory, but I enjoyed attending class! Homework is very easy and very interesting! No tests, just some simple writing.

Brother Searle is a good teacher, and you won't be disappointed with his classes. There were no exams, so that was nice. Just smaller projects here and there. Definitely do readings so you can share it class because there are many group discussions. All around, good experience.

Awesome class! He dives deep into so many church history topics that are interesting and controversial. Professor Searle is so awesome and extremely kind and helpful, he is willing to help you improve your grade if needed and cares about his students. Easy A
Easy class and can learn a lot. I really appreciate this type of religion class. Good faith building classes.

My only complaint was that I took this as a night class and those turn 2 hours really long. Other than that, Brother Searle is great. His lectures are very inspiring and he cares about his students. I feel that I learned a lot. The out of class work was pretty light. I would recommend this class anytime.

He is a great professor and teaches really well. He's willing to answer any questions you have without making you feel stupid for asking them. He is also really good at talking about the difficult topics like plural marriage. I've learned so much from him and you can't go wrong with his Foundations of Restoration class.

Best thing about this class is that he doesn't do exams. I really enjoyed the desire assignments and before class study. Some assignments were just busy work, and he had some strange requirements that don't appear on the rubric. Nice enough guy - he's not great with the hard questions and frequently searches for a specific answer in discussions.

I LOVE Prof. Searle. This was my 3rd religion class I'd taken from him, and I'd take a million more. This class, along with REL 250, aren't test-based, which is how every REL class should be imo. He is super funny, puts a lot of heart into his lectures, and jumps to help students when needed. Just show up to class, read, and you'll get an A.

I loved Brother Searle! Attendance is mandatory, but you can make up two absences. There are two major projects throughout the semester, and weekly quizzes and short essay "what did you learn" assignments- I received full credit on all of these assignments! Exams are straightforward, and his extra credit quizzes are a great help. 10/10 recommend!!!

I have taken three different classes from Brother Searle at this point, I wish I could take more. His teaching is very focused on helping students learn good habits for lifelong learning. He is very kind and responsive to questions and concerns, inside or outside of class.
He knows his stuff and is super supportive and helpful. Sometimes class can be a little dry. He does well at preparing students for the exams. The class projects were also pretty tame.

I would not recommend him. He's a nice guy, but this class was WAY too hard and demanding for a religion class. You can def get things done, but seriously this class was ridiculous. Don't take it unless you want to stress about unimportant details and be super unclear about everything that is taught.

Prof. Searle was amazing! Lots of reading, but it's not hard. Attendance is mandatory!! His exams are Low-key hard sometimes but are only 10% of the grade, so It's not a huge deal if you bomb them. He is really nice, and provided many resources to help us study and prepare for the exams. Homework is easy, you just have to read:)

This class has lots of reading. The tests are closed book and pretty hard. He tries to make up for it in extra credit. You'll do fine if you pay attention but its pretty boring. He wants you to do well though and is always willing to meet. I wouldn't take again though.

This class was primarily graded on two large assigments, and then pre-class work and in class attendance quizes. Honestly this class felt like an institute or seminary level course with 10x the amount of required readings. The tests were closed scripture, and required you to memorize certain sections.

Such an easy, but inspirational class. If you're not sure who to take foundations of the restoration from I would highly suggest Bro.Searle! Weekly before class work, attendance, 2 largish (but easy) assignments, 2 midterms (easy enough), and 1 final (but graded the same as the midterms). Great class and lectures! Highly recommend.

The main homework is a preparation assignment before every class that is easy to keep up with. He goes a bit fast in the lectures at times, but his review questions in the beginning of the class will help to clarify what is needed to know. He goes in depth on the topics and answers questions very thoroughly.

Professor Searle gives out a lot of pre-class study material, but if you PAY ATTENTION in lecture and take notes, then there is no reason why you shouldn't succeed in this class. He will explicitly say "you will need to know this for the exam" all the time. There are like two time-consuming assignments the entire semester and a couple midterms.

Professor Searle is a good teacher and his lectures are entertaining; however, his tests are much too difficult. He sometimes will answer the test questions in class, but expects us to find the rest in the hour's worth of reading before each period. This class made me feel like I was drowning due to the difficulty of my more important classes.
Brother Searles class was very easy, as a professor he was excellent, I wish the class was not mandatory attendance because based off the readings you can crush the exams.
My favorite class I've taken so far.  It was super easy but I feel like I learned a lot.  Some assignments but they aren't hard at all.
Easy course, but some very discriminatory opinions shared as fact

Loved this class! The project we worked toward the whole semester seems daunting at the start but at the end of the semester I was so proud of how far I'd come and what I'd learned. What you put in is what you take out. Br. Searle is incredibly spiritual.

Searle once put two columns on the board, "Men" & "Women". On the left were words such as strong, independent, breadwinners, etc. On the right were words like dependent, caring, nurturing, etc. 

If you don't see an issue, Searle will be fine for you.
If you do, expect this kind of thing daily.

That said, you can expect an A with minimal effort.

Brother Searle is awesome. Really invites the Spirit. He really cares about the Gospel, his family, and his students. Great at sharing words of prophets as well as personal experiences. He does assign a lot of reading and assignments. They aren't hard but can be time consuming. Very easy grader though. Wants students to succeed and enjoy the class

Loved The Eternal Family, it was a low stress class but I also feel like I learned so much. The content wasn't memorization or specifics but rather gospel concepts and connecting the concepts to my life. This is how all BYU religion classes should be!

Not sure if there is a different prof named Travis Searle but my class had exams unlike others leaving reviews. They weren't bad though if you just fill out and study the study guide. No papers to write, but two mid-length assignments throughout the semester that weren't bad. Really nice guy and would take again.

If you want a super easy Eternal Families credit, this is the one for you. He has NO final exam. You will write little journals every week based on the readings and lectures, and occasional larger assignments, but still easy. At the end of the semester, you will compile everything into one doc and turn it in. Didn't learn a lot tho tbh.
There were no tests and assignments were easy. As a senior, this was the easiest class I've taken at BYU.

Easy religion but I did not learn anything. The readings were more beneficial to my learning than the class. The class was confusing and not pieced together well. They were all over the place and I had to multitask in order to survive from boredom in class. The assignments & papers were nice though. The format was helpful to learn from out of class
Be prepared to talk to the person sitting next to you. Every single class he had us discussing something with others. Wasn't the most fun thing for an introvert.

Super nice professor. Super easy. The only reason I didn't give him a 5/5 is that he is a little boring in the lectures. I found myself falling asleep in his class sometimes, but honestly, there are no tests in his class and you can still get an A without paying attention to the lectures. If you are looking for an easy religion credit this is good
His course just confused me a little bit. Wasn't the most organized and lots of work.

This was the strangest religion class I've ever taken. If you're used to the Utah Bubble, you'll be fine. If your testimony is so much as shaky, this class might make you leave the church. Apparently, heaven is for RMs, dating is a game, women aren't people, and divorces can be prevented with self-reliance classes. I wish this was a joke. Avoid.

Brother Searle is a great professor and takes care when teaching about hard topics which I appreciated. The exams were fairly difficult and if you have a hard time memorizing which scriptures are about which topics, I would recommend lots of studying! Other than that, lots of extra credit opportunities and a great religion class overall.
This class was a circus. There are so many assignments that don't actually help you learn. Least favorite religion class I have had at BYU.

I absolutely loved Prof Searle. Easily my favorite class I've taken at BYU so far. He's very respectful about difficult topics and always focuses on teaching the doctrine. There are before class readings but they are always just some short scriptures and a couple talks, nothing you can't do in 30 min. You don't have exams and the projects are easy

Anyone looking for a religion class at BYU, take it from Travis Searle! Very simple and easy. I cannot recommend him enough! He was very inspiring, and I loved the layout of his class. His class was exactly how a religion class should be. You will not regret taking a class from him.

Brother Searle is excellent. The two tests are difficult but everything else is super easy. Just show up to class, take notes, and do the 40 minutes of homework before class each day. This can be an incredibly easy class if you put in 40 minutes of work and fill out the study guide. If you mess up, no worries! THERE IS SO MUCH EXTRA CREDIT!
He has 2 tests and 2 big projects. The tests are pretty hard because you have to memorize what truths are in what scripture. The projects take up alot of time too but his lectures are great!

Professor Searle is very nice, but the class is annoying. It's a two-credit religion course with daily work, plenty of reading, and multiple midterms. You will complete work before class, during class, and after class. It is far more work than is necessary, and it follows any basic seminary course.

Brother Searle is one of the worst religion professors I have taken as a convert to the Church. I let him know I was a new member and he assured me that would be okay. His exams are deceptively difficult for new members, couldn't follow his lectures, and forgot about me and my appointments I had with him. He also posts 1/2 filled out slides.
This professor waste time too much.

Boring, but easy. I took Eternal Family from him, and I didn't show up for some days. Depending on the TA grading can be easy or tougher. Either way if you're looking for a religion credit on the easier side, I'd say this ones good.
Bro. Searle gives an ideal religion class.  The work is very manageable and the focus is on our own spiritual growth and learning.  He handles difficult topics very well and his lectures are great!

I learned so much from this class and Brother Searle's lectures. This is by far the easiest religion class I have taken, but you'll only get from it as much as you put into it. Show up for lectures and read the materials and you'll have a great, spiritual, stress-free experience.

So far my absolute favorite religion teacher. His lectures are amazing and he is always willing to answer questions in and out of class. He opened my eyes to the restoration even though I had been learning about it my whole life. Would 100% recommend him to anyone and take another class in a heartbeat.

He's a good teacher, he just wasn't the best fit for me. He repeated himself so much and talked very softly, so I had a hard time staying awake in his class. He also really loved partner work so if you're an introvert beware. You get out what you put into this class, I really like the talks we had to read but I'm glad I'm done with this class
Not too loaded with assignments. You can tell he cares for his students. He's always willing to answer questions no matter what they are. Take him! Especially to feel the holy spirit
The class was pretty easy overall. I didn't find his teaching style to be very engaging or interesting. The tests were harder than I expected, but after an hour of studying I aced them.

Everyone who has the chance should take Restorations from Prof. Searle. He knows the content so well but teaches simply, inspiring spiritual growth without stress. There are pre-class readings with great discussions and stories in class. He has a study guide available with every concept for the exams. Weekly reflections are easy by going to class.

Really easy class for me, and attendance wasn't mandatory but I often used the class time to lock in and turn assignments in. Professor Searle is nice, but doesn't get to know his students at all, but this didn't bother me. I was able to sit in the back of the class and not really talk to anyone, bc thats what I prefer.

Make sure to do the pre-class readings! And attend office hours if you have a question. He has a clear structure of the class in his mind, but wasn't always clear to me personally until I went to office hours. He's a really kind person, really helpful and accommodating. Great at tying in historical examples to modern principles.

Brother Searle is honestly amazing! He is one of the best religion professors that I have had at BYU. He knows how to bring the spirit and is very inspirational! Class work load is pretty light and easy to keep up with.

Brother Searle's class was pretty good. There is a bunch of small assignments, but those go by pretty fast. Some classes are very boring, but with class participation/discussion and everybody in a fun or good mood, the classes were great! We talked about good topics, and Searle explained them pretty well.

Professor Searle is great! There is a lot of homework; it's super easy, but make sure to do it. Online tests are easy as long as you review material. Half way through the semester Professor Searle even changed some organizational things after a mid class survey. If you've read the Saints books before you'll already be familiar with some content.

My least favorite professor that I have had so far. He would curb difficult questions and I would often feel tension in his class. Scraped by with an A- due to his first test. Would not take another class from him.

Professor Searle is a very nice guy who is passionate about the students and what he teaches. I wasn't personally fond of his writing style and the way he explained a few topics, but he ultimately is very organized and has the best of intention. Tests aren't graded super heavy, so as long as you do the home work, you should get a pretty good grade.

Bro Searle is so so so nice but his class was absolutely not for me. Stopped going to class mid semester and ended with an A. I did not like the organization of the class at all and didn't feel like I really learned anything which was disappointing because I was really looking forward to the class. Go to the TA test reviews & the exam will be fine

Had the class at 8am, so I lost a lot of points for being late to class, but if you attend you will mostly do fine. The material helps you resolve common questions about the foundations of the Church. He asked for feedback mid-semester and made lots of changes based on the feedback, he cares about the students.

Professor Searle is a super kind individual! I took his Living Prophets class online. Overall, very straightforward course and grading. Tests were open book open note; however, the tests are RIDICULOUSLY long. I spent over 2 hours on the midterm and almost 3 hours on the final. You can get great grades, it just takes some time investment.

Engaging & interesting lectures, but VERY homework heavy. To understand the material or do well on exams you have to read everything he assigns outside class. No extra credit. Projects were great, make sure to be aware of their deadlines (they come up fast).
Very responsive to class needs; changed the whole class setup after a mid-semester survey.

super great class!!! listened to the student's feedback at mid semester course survey and literally changed the set up. super organized class structure and easy weekly assignments. otherwise there are three papers in the class and final is non cumulative! loved this

Prof Searle was a fantastic teacher.  He was good at making class interactive and addressing touchy subjects in a Christlike manner.  He is super caring and shares impactful experiences.  There's assignments for each class, but you can knock them out in 10min.  Would recommend!

This has been by far the worst religion professor at BYU I've had. There is a pre class assignment, during class assignment, and post class assignment due every in class day. They take 1.5 hrs to do. The tests are the worst I have seen. Everything he wants you to do is so convoluted and if you don't do it his way he'll give you a bad grade.

REL C 225 is a heavier religion course and Brother Searle does a really good job of breaking down the material and dealing with uncomfortable Church topics. The class was harder than my other religion classes, but still pretty easy, and the test review materials were super helpful.
