Bro Searle was a good enough professor but his teaching style wasn't really for me. The TA said the tests would be easy but most people in my class did poorly on the first midterm. Luckily the majority of the grade comes from assignments and not exams because the midterms and finals were not as easy as religion tests should be.

Professor Searle was awesome! He always made sure we knew he cared about our comments and he was super nice! The tests weren't too hard, if you fill out the review he gives you then you'll be set! I loved this class and think everyone should take a class from Searle!

Course structure was very simple and organized which I loved, nothing too complex. when reading try to answer the objectives along the way, there are weekly personal insight assignments and daily assignments which takes 5 mins. tests can be meticulous but very simple, no difficult questions are being asked. great prof!

Loved him. Some readings took forever and quiz before every class w two attempts (easy). Tests are easy if you look at the ppt the TA sends out and the study guides and memorize that info. Writing assignments are graded easy and not tough. Lectures were good too. Graded on attendance and two make ups. Won't excuse sickness without makeup assignment
Brother Searle is very kind and a great professor. Class is quite easy if you stay on top of it, it's all about personal accountability.

Brother Searle is amazing!! I always felt the spirit and he very clearly explains some hard truths about church history. He is also very clear about what he expects on the few homework assignments and tests. I would take any class for him you can!

Professor Searle's class was exactly what a religion class should be! The tests weren't very hard, the study review sessions were super helpful, class wasn't boring or overwhelming, and the workload wasn't over the top! Honestly one of my favorite religion classes that I've taken and I would highly recommend taking it! Professor Searle is awesome!

This class is graded based on self reported book reading, attendance, a few self improvement type assignments, 2 midterms and the final. Tests are online and proctored- the study guides generally follow the tests very closely so it is easy to get a good grade. Prof Searle is really understanding and open minded. He makes an effort to know names too

Searle is a good teacher with a deep and passionate testimony. He cares about his students but is a serious man.
Everything on the test is said in class and he prepares you for all questions. Homework is very doable, takes 30 minutes.
Tests can be slightly stressful but with moderate studying and going to the test review, it is more than doable.

Brother Searle is a very spiritual teacher who gives good lectures. Soft spoken, so sometimes the in-class discussions didn't go far, but he did great at clearly giving us the content and preparing us for exams. The reading assignments weren't too heavy, I usually completed them the morning before class. I hope to take his class on living prophets!

Brother Searle is my favorite religion professor! Instead of overcomplicating things like many religion professors do, he focuses on the simplicity of the gospel. He doesn't try to invent some new profound idea, he just focuses on building faith. He's excellent at creating personal applications for church history and teaching by the Spirit.

I attended almost every class and did all the homework. It took me a month or so to get used to the class and to catch on to what information would be on the tests. The study guides helped. The work and syllabus are very organized. I did about 3 hours (on average) every week. Lectures were a little slow, but there were enlightening discussions.

There's quite a bit of reading, but it's not too bad. You can tell Professor Searle really wants to do well and see his students succeed, but his tests are everything a religion test should not be: detail focused and memorization heavy. However, it's hard to say whether this class was disappointing because of the course or the instructor.

Bro. Searle is a nice guy who knows the content well. He can go over the slides too fast, so be ready to take notes. the ungraded practice quizzes really help you get ready for the tests. the class is very straight forward and an easy A if you stay on top of things.

Most religion classes at BYU I feel like aren't super spiritual based. However, this class was a very good mix of spiritual and learning. There are assignments in class, so attendance is necessary. However, the daily assignments aren't difficult and the tests weren't too bad. Brother Searle is a fun, kind man.

He was great at addressing difficult topics, class was super easy, tests were straightforward, mostly copied the questions off the practice quizzes. Two big assignments seemed to be graded more on completion than competency. You can tell he is still trying to refine what class should look like but is good about being open to feedback. Great guy!

Prof. Searle is a great guy and you can tell that he cares about the content and his students. The coursework was very easy. If you do the practice tests you'll do great on the exams because it's practically a copy and paste of the questions. Overall, the lectures weren't super engaging, but I learned a lot about church history I didn't know before
Professor Searle is genuine and you can tell he really cares about his students. This class is not difficult but I still feel like I learned a lot. I'd take this professor again in a heartbeat.

go to class! study guides weekly are helpful. He answers any question. If you have questions about the restoration or about controversial content from that period, this professor knows how to address those in a courteous and logical way. Course content was mostly organized

The lectures in class are very material heavy. If you don't show up the lectures are posted online but the slides are not very detailed. Frequently he will ask you to turn and talk to partners about anything from answering a question on the board to very personal experiences.

This class is genuinely just busywork. Rather than being able to actually listen and pay attention in class, all you do is fill out worksheet upon worksheet that are clearly supposed to be helpful but are really just mind numbing and distracting. Probably my least favorite religion class I've taken my entire time at BYU.

Prof. Searle's Restoration class is mind-numbingly easy, with that in mind, the lectures are insanely grueling and there is so much busy-work that it is impossible to learn anything. If you show up, you will get an easy A, there are 0 tests/essays, and there is hardly any out of class work, but I would NOT recommend this professor for this class.

Great class and choice for a religion credit! Most of the assignments were filling out pre-made slides about each prophet / apostle. Info needed was covered in class, so I got most homework done during lecture. Super easy but learned so much about the prophets' lives and teachings. Highly recommend!
class is a little dull. easy to sleep through. but he is such a sweet man and really cares for his students. No final too, which was nice. Just doing the work and you'll be just fine.

Professor Searle really cares about his student and he has a great testimony of the restored gospel. I enjoyed his lectures and he tells a lot of fun stories related to living prophets. There is no final in this class but you have to work on a semester long project and you have slides to submit every week.

Brother Searle is the sweetest. He had quite a few assignments, but none were extremely hard. The class is very focused on helping you build your testimony of the Savior through the teachings of the living prophets! Would take this class again!
Brother Searle doesn't have any tests, just requires you to take notes during class, which had very well thought out lectures. I loved this class.

This religion class was very easy to follow and understand, and had no final exam. Attendance is a major part of the grade. I don't personally love the way Professor Searle addressed certain difficult questions or issues in Church History, he is very orthodox which I know some people appreciate, but it's not for me personally.

Brother Searle is awesome! He treats a religion class the way it should - learning focused and not grade focused. His lectures are almost always engaging, I was never bored. He focuses always on the spiritual aspects, and my testimony was definitely strengthened. He's extremely smart as well

Probably the easiest religion class I've taken at BYU, but very informative and well-structured. Before/in-class reflections that are ~50 words, slides ab 2 apostles due every 2 weeks with a final culmination at the end, and a simple semester-long project. Super easy to get a good grade if you just put a little thought into it. Highly recommend.

If you want any easy religion class, take it with Professor Searle. I honestly didn't pay much attention but  his lectures were really interesting when I listened haha. Homework is super easy. There are no tests or final. He's a good guy

Class was easy, no exams or quizzes. You have fill out a module and have to do an activity every two weeks and write 2 essays total. The only downfall is the modules you have to fill out in class. Sometimes it was hard to focus on his teachings or feel the spirit when we were too busy trying to make sure we got the notes filled out.

Brother Searle is awesome! Love his stories! You just read short things about each apostle and create Slides on them. You don't present them. No midterm. Semester long project that is very manageable. Final project is creating a cumulative slide of some slides you've already created. He is funny and shares great personal experiences and stories!

Very easy class, but also very informative - I learned lots about each apostle. No tests at all. Just pre-class reflection questions, a slide deck about each apostle every other weekend, and then a project spread throughout the semester about finding answers to questions. I love Brother Searle - so kind and sincere!
Want an easy A class with no tests that tackles difficult church historical topics with sensitivity and an eternal perspective? Take his class. Wouldn't take this class from anyone else.

I think overall this was a good class. There was a semester long project about finding answers to our questions, and I feel like it wasn't super clear what he wanted sometimes. My class was once a week, so I don't think that sometimes it was adapted very well for our class compared to the twice a week class. Really cool class though!
I loved this class!
Easiest religion class I've taken. Good lectures and insight. Caring and tries to connect with students.

Lectures were quite boring, only created more confusion among the students than actually answered questions, and he constantly tried to do too much, hardly giving students any time for the in-class discussions he assigned. The homework assignments were nothing but busy work that forced you to repeat yourself constantly.

I learned a lot in this class, but I struggled to grow besides that. Lectures were stressful and most of it was spent frantically try to fill out charts. Outside of class there were more charts to fill out and it was a bit boring since we did the same thing every single time.

This class was the most seminary- like religion class I have taken at BYU and I loved it for that. I feel like I learned a lot being able to study how I wanted while also having specific things to learn about in a  structured way. Classes did require partner work and participation. Would recommend!
This class is so boring. It's just busy work but it's an easy A.

He is a great professor I learned a lot from his class. He has a lot of knowledge and you can tell he loves what he teaches. Not a ton of homework and a very manageable class. There were no actual exams which is the way I think religion classes should be done.

Travis Searle was a great professor. Even when i took the class with a ton of other students he still tried his best to talk with everyone. I loved the class living prophets because i gained a deeper understanding of them. There is only a project, 8 slide show every 2 weeks, and a final witness slide show. No test.
Enjoyed this class! He is a great professor who does a really good job answering questions in a clear and respectful way. Really organized.

He is a great teacher! He does a great job discussing difficult topics related to the Restoration and makes his lectures interesting with lots of discussion and real-life examples. Attendance is mandatory, but I enjoyed attending class! Homework is very easy and very interesting! No tests, just some simple writing.

Brother Searle is a good teacher, and you won't be disappointed with his classes. There were no exams, so that was nice. Just smaller projects here and there. Definitely do readings so you can share it class because there are many group discussions. All around, good experience.

Awesome class! He dives deep into so many church history topics that are interesting and controversial. Professor Searle is so awesome and extremely kind and helpful, he is willing to help you improve your grade if needed and cares about his students. Easy A
Easy class and can learn a lot. I really appreciate this type of religion class. Good faith building classes.

My only complaint was that I took this as a night class and those turn 2 hours really long. Other than that, Brother Searle is great. His lectures are very inspiring and he cares about his students. I feel that I learned a lot. The out of class work was pretty light. I would recommend this class anytime.

He is a great professor and teaches really well. He's willing to answer any questions you have without making you feel stupid for asking them. He is also really good at talking about the difficult topics like plural marriage. I've learned so much from him and you can't go wrong with his Foundations of Restoration class.

Best thing about this class is that he doesn't do exams. I really enjoyed the desire assignments and before class study. Some assignments were just busy work, and he had some strange requirements that don't appear on the rubric. Nice enough guy - he's not great with the hard questions and frequently searches for a specific answer in discussions.

I LOVE Prof. Searle. This was my 3rd religion class I'd taken from him, and I'd take a million more. This class, along with REL 250, aren't test-based, which is how every REL class should be imo. He is super funny, puts a lot of heart into his lectures, and jumps to help students when needed. Just show up to class, read, and you'll get an A.

I loved Brother Searle! Attendance is mandatory, but you can make up two absences. There are two major projects throughout the semester, and weekly quizzes and short essay "what did you learn" assignments- I received full credit on all of these assignments! Exams are straightforward, and his extra credit quizzes are a great help. 10/10 recommend!!!

I have taken three different classes from Brother Searle at this point, I wish I could take more. His teaching is very focused on helping students learn good habits for lifelong learning. He is very kind and responsive to questions and concerns, inside or outside of class.
He knows his stuff and is super supportive and helpful. Sometimes class can be a little dry. He does well at preparing students for the exams. The class projects were also pretty tame.

I would not recommend him. He's a nice guy, but this class was WAY too hard and demanding for a religion class. You can def get things done, but seriously this class was ridiculous. Don't take it unless you want to stress about unimportant details and be super unclear about everything that is taught.

Prof. Searle was amazing! Lots of reading, but it's not hard. Attendance is mandatory!! His exams are Low-key hard sometimes but are only 10% of the grade, so It's not a huge deal if you bomb them. He is really nice, and provided many resources to help us study and prepare for the exams. Homework is easy, you just have to read:)

This class has lots of reading. The tests are closed book and pretty hard. He tries to make up for it in extra credit. You'll do fine if you pay attention but its pretty boring. He wants you to do well though and is always willing to meet. I wouldn't take again though.

This class was primarily graded on two large assigments, and then pre-class work and in class attendance quizes. Honestly this class felt like an institute or seminary level course with 10x the amount of required readings. The tests were closed scripture, and required you to memorize certain sections.

Such an easy, but inspirational class. If you're not sure who to take foundations of the restoration from I would highly suggest Bro.Searle! Weekly before class work, attendance, 2 largish (but easy) assignments, 2 midterms (easy enough), and 1 final (but graded the same as the midterms). Great class and lectures! Highly recommend.

The main homework is a preparation assignment before every class that is easy to keep up with. He goes a bit fast in the lectures at times, but his review questions in the beginning of the class will help to clarify what is needed to know. He goes in depth on the topics and answers questions very thoroughly.

Professor Searle gives out a lot of pre-class study material, but if you PAY ATTENTION in lecture and take notes, then there is no reason why you shouldn't succeed in this class. He will explicitly say "you will need to know this for the exam" all the time. There are like two time-consuming assignments the entire semester and a couple midterms.

Professor Searle is a good teacher and his lectures are entertaining; however, his tests are much too difficult. He sometimes will answer the test questions in class, but expects us to find the rest in the hour's worth of reading before each period. This class made me feel like I was drowning due to the difficulty of my more important classes.
Brother Searles class was very easy, as a professor he was excellent, I wish the class was not mandatory attendance because based off the readings you can crush the exams.
My favorite class I've taken so far.  It was super easy but I feel like I learned a lot.  Some assignments but they aren't hard at all.
Easy course, but some very discriminatory opinions shared as fact

Loved this class! The project we worked toward the whole semester seems daunting at the start but at the end of the semester I was so proud of how far I'd come and what I'd learned. What you put in is what you take out. Br. Searle is incredibly spiritual.

Searle once put two columns on the board, "Men" & "Women". On the left were words such as strong, independent, breadwinners, etc. On the right were words like dependent, caring, nurturing, etc. 

If you don't see an issue, Searle will be fine for you.
If you do, expect this kind of thing daily.

That said, you can expect an A with minimal effort.

Brother Searle is awesome. Really invites the Spirit. He really cares about the Gospel, his family, and his students. Great at sharing words of prophets as well as personal experiences. He does assign a lot of reading and assignments. They aren't hard but can be time consuming. Very easy grader though. Wants students to succeed and enjoy the class

Loved The Eternal Family, it was a low stress class but I also feel like I learned so much. The content wasn't memorization or specifics but rather gospel concepts and connecting the concepts to my life. This is how all BYU religion classes should be!

Not sure if there is a different prof named Travis Searle but my class had exams unlike others leaving reviews. They weren't bad though if you just fill out and study the study guide. No papers to write, but two mid-length assignments throughout the semester that weren't bad. Really nice guy and would take again.

If you want a super easy Eternal Families credit, this is the one for you. He has NO final exam. You will write little journals every week based on the readings and lectures, and occasional larger assignments, but still easy. At the end of the semester, you will compile everything into one doc and turn it in. Didn't learn a lot tho tbh.
There were no tests and assignments were easy. As a senior, this was the easiest class I've taken at BYU.

Easy religion but I did not learn anything. The readings were more beneficial to my learning than the class. The class was confusing and not pieced together well. They were all over the place and I had to multitask in order to survive from boredom in class. The assignments & papers were nice though. The format was helpful to learn from out of class
Be prepared to talk to the person sitting next to you. Every single class he had us discussing something with others. Wasn't the most fun thing for an introvert.

Super nice professor. Super easy. The only reason I didn't give him a 5/5 is that he is a little boring in the lectures. I found myself falling asleep in his class sometimes, but honestly, there are no tests in his class and you can still get an A without paying attention to the lectures. If you are looking for an easy religion credit this is good
His course just confused me a little bit. Wasn't the most organized and lots of work.

This was the strangest religion class I've ever taken. If you're used to the Utah Bubble, you'll be fine. If your testimony is so much as shaky, this class might make you leave the church. Apparently, heaven is for RMs, dating is a game, women aren't people, and divorces can be prevented with self-reliance classes. I wish this was a joke. Avoid.

Brother Searle is a great professor and takes care when teaching about hard topics which I appreciated. The exams were fairly difficult and if you have a hard time memorizing which scriptures are about which topics, I would recommend lots of studying! Other than that, lots of extra credit opportunities and a great religion class overall.
This class was a circus. There are so many assignments that don't actually help you learn. Least favorite religion class I have had at BYU.

I absolutely loved Prof Searle. Easily my favorite class I've taken at BYU so far. He's very respectful about difficult topics and always focuses on teaching the doctrine. There are before class readings but they are always just some short scriptures and a couple talks, nothing you can't do in 30 min. You don't have exams and the projects are easy

Anyone looking for a religion class at BYU, take it from Travis Searle! Very simple and easy. I cannot recommend him enough! He was very inspiring, and I loved the layout of his class. His class was exactly how a religion class should be. You will not regret taking a class from him.

Brother Searle is excellent. The two tests are difficult but everything else is super easy. Just show up to class, take notes, and do the 40 minutes of homework before class each day. This can be an incredibly easy class if you put in 40 minutes of work and fill out the study guide. If you mess up, no worries! THERE IS SO MUCH EXTRA CREDIT!
He has 2 tests and 2 big projects. The tests are pretty hard because you have to memorize what truths are in what scripture. The projects take up alot of time too but his lectures are great!

Professor Searle is very nice, but the class is annoying. It's a two-credit religion course with daily work, plenty of reading, and multiple midterms. You will complete work before class, during class, and after class. It is far more work than is necessary, and it follows any basic seminary course.

Brother Searle is one of the worst religion professors I have taken as a convert to the Church. I let him know I was a new member and he assured me that would be okay. His exams are deceptively difficult for new members, couldn't follow his lectures, and forgot about me and my appointments I had with him. He also posts 1/2 filled out slides.
This professor waste time too much.

Boring, but easy. I took Eternal Family from him, and I didn't show up for some days. Depending on the TA grading can be easy or tougher. Either way if you're looking for a religion credit on the easier side, I'd say this ones good.
Bro. Searle gives an ideal religion class.  The work is very manageable and the focus is on our own spiritual growth and learning.  He handles difficult topics very well and his lectures are great!

I learned so much from this class and Brother Searle's lectures. This is by far the easiest religion class I have taken, but you'll only get from it as much as you put into it. Show up for lectures and read the materials and you'll have a great, spiritual, stress-free experience.

So far my absolute favorite religion teacher. His lectures are amazing and he is always willing to answer questions in and out of class. He opened my eyes to the restoration even though I had been learning about it my whole life. Would 100% recommend him to anyone and take another class in a heartbeat.

He's a good teacher, he just wasn't the best fit for me. He repeated himself so much and talked very softly, so I had a hard time staying awake in his class. He also really loved partner work so if you're an introvert beware. You get out what you put into this class, I really like the talks we had to read but I'm glad I'm done with this class
Not too loaded with assignments. You can tell he cares for his students. He's always willing to answer questions no matter what they are. Take him! Especially to feel the holy spirit
The class was pretty easy overall. I didn't find his teaching style to be very engaging or interesting. The tests were harder than I expected, but after an hour of studying I aced them.

Everyone who has the chance should take Restorations from Prof. Searle. He knows the content so well but teaches simply, inspiring spiritual growth without stress. There are pre-class readings with great discussions and stories in class. He has a study guide available with every concept for the exams. Weekly reflections are easy by going to class.

Really easy class for me, and attendance wasn't mandatory but I often used the class time to lock in and turn assignments in. Professor Searle is nice, but doesn't get to know his students at all, but this didn't bother me. I was able to sit in the back of the class and not really talk to anyone, bc thats what I prefer.

Make sure to do the pre-class readings! And attend office hours if you have a question. He has a clear structure of the class in his mind, but wasn't always clear to me personally until I went to office hours. He's a really kind person, really helpful and accommodating. Great at tying in historical examples to modern principles.

Brother Searle is honestly amazing! He is one of the best religion professors that I have had at BYU. He knows how to bring the spirit and is very inspirational! Class work load is pretty light and easy to keep up with.

Brother Searle's class was pretty good. There is a bunch of small assignments, but those go by pretty fast. Some classes are very boring, but with class participation/discussion and everybody in a fun or good mood, the classes were great! We talked about good topics, and Searle explained them pretty well.

Professor Searle is great! There is a lot of homework; it's super easy, but make sure to do it. Online tests are easy as long as you review material. Half way through the semester Professor Searle even changed some organizational things after a mid class survey. If you've read the Saints books before you'll already be familiar with some content.

My least favorite professor that I have had so far. He would curb difficult questions and I would often feel tension in his class. Scraped by with an A- due to his first test. Would not take another class from him.

Professor Searle is a very nice guy who is passionate about the students and what he teaches. I wasn't personally fond of his writing style and the way he explained a few topics, but he ultimately is very organized and has the best of intention. Tests aren't graded super heavy, so as long as you do the home work, you should get a pretty good grade.

Bro Searle is so so so nice but his class was absolutely not for me. Stopped going to class mid semester and ended with an A. I did not like the organization of the class at all and didn't feel like I really learned anything which was disappointing because I was really looking forward to the class. Go to the TA test reviews & the exam will be fine

Had the class at 8am, so I lost a lot of points for being late to class, but if you attend you will mostly do fine. The material helps you resolve common questions about the foundations of the Church. He asked for feedback mid-semester and made lots of changes based on the feedback, he cares about the students.

Professor Searle is a super kind individual! I took his Living Prophets class online. Overall, very straightforward course and grading. Tests were open book open note; however, the tests are RIDICULOUSLY long. I spent over 2 hours on the midterm and almost 3 hours on the final. You can get great grades, it just takes some time investment.

Engaging & interesting lectures, but VERY homework heavy. To understand the material or do well on exams you have to read everything he assigns outside class. No extra credit. Projects were great, make sure to be aware of their deadlines (they come up fast).
Very responsive to class needs; changed the whole class setup after a mid-semester survey.

super great class!!! listened to the student's feedback at mid semester course survey and literally changed the set up. super organized class structure and easy weekly assignments. otherwise there are three papers in the class and final is non cumulative! loved this

Prof Searle was a fantastic teacher.  He was good at making class interactive and addressing touchy subjects in a Christlike manner.  He is super caring and shares impactful experiences.  There's assignments for each class, but you can knock them out in 10min.  Would recommend!

This has been by far the worst religion professor at BYU I've had. There is a pre class assignment, during class assignment, and post class assignment due every in class day. They take 1.5 hrs to do. The tests are the worst I have seen. Everything he wants you to do is so convoluted and if you don't do it his way he'll give you a bad grade.

REL C 225 is a heavier religion course and Brother Searle does a really good job of breaking down the material and dealing with uncomfortable Church topics. The class was harder than my other religion classes, but still pretty easy, and the test review materials were super helpful.

Bro Searle was a good enough professor but his teaching style wasn't really for me. The TA said the tests would be easy but most people in my class did poorly on the first midterm. Luckily the majority of the grade comes from assignments and not exams because the midterms and finals were not as easy as religion tests should be.

Professor Searle was awesome! He always made sure we knew he cared about our comments and he was super nice! The tests weren't too hard, if you fill out the review he gives you then you'll be set! I loved this class and think everyone should take a class from Searle!

Course structure was very simple and organized which I loved, nothing too complex. when reading try to answer the objectives along the way, there are weekly personal insight assignments and daily assignments which takes 5 mins. tests can be meticulous but very simple, no difficult questions are being asked. great prof!

Loved him. Some readings took forever and quiz before every class w two attempts (easy). Tests are easy if you look at the ppt the TA sends out and the study guides and memorize that info. Writing assignments are graded easy and not tough. Lectures were good too. Graded on attendance and two make ups. Won't excuse sickness without makeup assignment
Brother Searle is very kind and a great professor. Class is quite easy if you stay on top of it, it's all about personal accountability.

Brother Searle is amazing!! I always felt the spirit and he very clearly explains some hard truths about church history. He is also very clear about what he expects on the few homework assignments and tests. I would take any class for him you can!

Professor Searle's class was exactly what a religion class should be! The tests weren't very hard, the study review sessions were super helpful, class wasn't boring or overwhelming, and the workload wasn't over the top! Honestly one of my favorite religion classes that I've taken and I would highly recommend taking it! Professor Searle is awesome!

This class is graded based on self reported book reading, attendance, a few self improvement type assignments, 2 midterms and the final. Tests are online and proctored- the study guides generally follow the tests very closely so it is easy to get a good grade. Prof Searle is really understanding and open minded. He makes an effort to know names too

Searle is a good teacher with a deep and passionate testimony. He cares about his students but is a serious man.
Everything on the test is said in class and he prepares you for all questions. Homework is very doable, takes 30 minutes.
Tests can be slightly stressful but with moderate studying and going to the test review, it is more than doable.

Brother Searle is a very spiritual teacher who gives good lectures. Soft spoken, so sometimes the in-class discussions didn't go far, but he did great at clearly giving us the content and preparing us for exams. The reading assignments weren't too heavy, I usually completed them the morning before class. I hope to take his class on living prophets!

Brother Searle is my favorite religion professor! Instead of overcomplicating things like many religion professors do, he focuses on the simplicity of the gospel. He doesn't try to invent some new profound idea, he just focuses on building faith. He's excellent at creating personal applications for church history and teaching by the Spirit.

I attended almost every class and did all the homework. It took me a month or so to get used to the class and to catch on to what information would be on the tests. The study guides helped. The work and syllabus are very organized. I did about 3 hours (on average) every week. Lectures were a little slow, but there were enlightening discussions.

There's quite a bit of reading, but it's not too bad. You can tell Professor Searle really wants to do well and see his students succeed, but his tests are everything a religion test should not be: detail focused and memorization heavy. However, it's hard to say whether this class was disappointing because of the course or the instructor.

Bro. Searle is a nice guy who knows the content well. He can go over the slides too fast, so be ready to take notes. the ungraded practice quizzes really help you get ready for the tests. the class is very straight forward and an easy A if you stay on top of things.

Most religion classes at BYU I feel like aren't super spiritual based. However, this class was a very good mix of spiritual and learning. There are assignments in class, so attendance is necessary. However, the daily assignments aren't difficult and the tests weren't too bad. Brother Searle is a fun, kind man.

He was great at addressing difficult topics, class was super easy, tests were straightforward, mostly copied the questions off the practice quizzes. Two big assignments seemed to be graded more on completion than competency. You can tell he is still trying to refine what class should look like but is good about being open to feedback. Great guy!

Prof. Searle is a great guy and you can tell that he cares about the content and his students. The coursework was very easy. If you do the practice tests you'll do great on the exams because it's practically a copy and paste of the questions. Overall, the lectures weren't super engaging, but I learned a lot about church history I didn't know before
Professor Searle is genuine and you can tell he really cares about his students. This class is not difficult but I still feel like I learned a lot. I'd take this professor again in a heartbeat.

go to class! study guides weekly are helpful. He answers any question. If you have questions about the restoration or about controversial content from that period, this professor knows how to address those in a courteous and logical way. Course content was mostly organized

The lectures in class are very material heavy. If you don't show up the lectures are posted online but the slides are not very detailed. Frequently he will ask you to turn and talk to partners about anything from answering a question on the board to very personal experiences.

This class is genuinely just busywork. Rather than being able to actually listen and pay attention in class, all you do is fill out worksheet upon worksheet that are clearly supposed to be helpful but are really just mind numbing and distracting. Probably my least favorite religion class I've taken my entire time at BYU.

Prof. Searle's Restoration class is mind-numbingly easy, with that in mind, the lectures are insanely grueling and there is so much busy-work that it is impossible to learn anything. If you show up, you will get an easy A, there are 0 tests/essays, and there is hardly any out of class work, but I would NOT recommend this professor for this class.

Great class and choice for a religion credit! Most of the assignments were filling out pre-made slides about each prophet / apostle. Info needed was covered in class, so I got most homework done during lecture. Super easy but learned so much about the prophets' lives and teachings. Highly recommend!
class is a little dull. easy to sleep through. but he is such a sweet man and really cares for his students. No final too, which was nice. Just doing the work and you'll be just fine.

Professor Searle really cares about his student and he has a great testimony of the restored gospel. I enjoyed his lectures and he tells a lot of fun stories related to living prophets. There is no final in this class but you have to work on a semester long project and you have slides to submit every week.

Brother Searle is the sweetest. He had quite a few assignments, but none were extremely hard. The class is very focused on helping you build your testimony of the Savior through the teachings of the living prophets! Would take this class again!
Brother Searle doesn't have any tests, just requires you to take notes during class, which had very well thought out lectures. I loved this class.

This religion class was very easy to follow and understand, and had no final exam. Attendance is a major part of the grade. I don't personally love the way Professor Searle addressed certain difficult questions or issues in Church History, he is very orthodox which I know some people appreciate, but it's not for me personally.

Brother Searle is awesome! He treats a religion class the way it should - learning focused and not grade focused. His lectures are almost always engaging, I was never bored. He focuses always on the spiritual aspects, and my testimony was definitely strengthened. He's extremely smart as well

Probably the easiest religion class I've taken at BYU, but very informative and well-structured. Before/in-class reflections that are ~50 words, slides ab 2 apostles due every 2 weeks with a final culmination at the end, and a simple semester-long project. Super easy to get a good grade if you just put a little thought into it. Highly recommend.

If you want any easy religion class, take it with Professor Searle. I honestly didn't pay much attention but  his lectures were really interesting when I listened haha. Homework is super easy. There are no tests or final. He's a good guy

Class was easy, no exams or quizzes. You have fill out a module and have to do an activity every two weeks and write 2 essays total. The only downfall is the modules you have to fill out in class. Sometimes it was hard to focus on his teachings or feel the spirit when we were too busy trying to make sure we got the notes filled out.

Brother Searle is awesome! Love his stories! You just read short things about each apostle and create Slides on them. You don't present them. No midterm. Semester long project that is very manageable. Final project is creating a cumulative slide of some slides you've already created. He is funny and shares great personal experiences and stories!

Very easy class, but also very informative - I learned lots about each apostle. No tests at all. Just pre-class reflection questions, a slide deck about each apostle every other weekend, and then a project spread throughout the semester about finding answers to questions. I love Brother Searle - so kind and sincere!
Want an easy A class with no tests that tackles difficult church historical topics with sensitivity and an eternal perspective? Take his class. Wouldn't take this class from anyone else.

I think overall this was a good class. There was a semester long project about finding answers to our questions, and I feel like it wasn't super clear what he wanted sometimes. My class was once a week, so I don't think that sometimes it was adapted very well for our class compared to the twice a week class. Really cool class though!
I loved this class!
Easiest religion class I've taken. Good lectures and insight. Caring and tries to connect with students.

Lectures were quite boring, only created more confusion among the students than actually answered questions, and he constantly tried to do too much, hardly giving students any time for the in-class discussions he assigned. The homework assignments were nothing but busy work that forced you to repeat yourself constantly.

I learned a lot in this class, but I struggled to grow besides that. Lectures were stressful and most of it was spent frantically try to fill out charts. Outside of class there were more charts to fill out and it was a bit boring since we did the same thing every single time.

This class was the most seminary- like religion class I have taken at BYU and I loved it for that. I feel like I learned a lot being able to study how I wanted while also having specific things to learn about in a  structured way. Classes did require partner work and participation. Would recommend!
This class is so boring. It's just busy work but it's an easy A.

He is a great professor I learned a lot from his class. He has a lot of knowledge and you can tell he loves what he teaches. Not a ton of homework and a very manageable class. There were no actual exams which is the way I think religion classes should be done.

Travis Searle was a great professor. Even when i took the class with a ton of other students he still tried his best to talk with everyone. I loved the class living prophets because i gained a deeper understanding of them. There is only a project, 8 slide show every 2 weeks, and a final witness slide show. No test.
Enjoyed this class! He is a great professor who does a really good job answering questions in a clear and respectful way. Really organized.

He is a great teacher! He does a great job discussing difficult topics related to the Restoration and makes his lectures interesting with lots of discussion and real-life examples. Attendance is mandatory, but I enjoyed attending class! Homework is very easy and very interesting! No tests, just some simple writing.

Brother Searle is a good teacher, and you won't be disappointed with his classes. There were no exams, so that was nice. Just smaller projects here and there. Definitely do readings so you can share it class because there are many group discussions. All around, good experience.

Awesome class! He dives deep into so many church history topics that are interesting and controversial. Professor Searle is so awesome and extremely kind and helpful, he is willing to help you improve your grade if needed and cares about his students. Easy A
Easy class and can learn a lot. I really appreciate this type of religion class. Good faith building classes.

My only complaint was that I took this as a night class and those turn 2 hours really long. Other than that, Brother Searle is great. His lectures are very inspiring and he cares about his students. I feel that I learned a lot. The out of class work was pretty light. I would recommend this class anytime.

He is a great professor and teaches really well. He's willing to answer any questions you have without making you feel stupid for asking them. He is also really good at talking about the difficult topics like plural marriage. I've learned so much from him and you can't go wrong with his Foundations of Restoration class.

Best thing about this class is that he doesn't do exams. I really enjoyed the desire assignments and before class study. Some assignments were just busy work, and he had some strange requirements that don't appear on the rubric. Nice enough guy - he's not great with the hard questions and frequently searches for a specific answer in discussions.

I LOVE Prof. Searle. This was my 3rd religion class I'd taken from him, and I'd take a million more. This class, along with REL 250, aren't test-based, which is how every REL class should be imo. He is super funny, puts a lot of heart into his lectures, and jumps to help students when needed. Just show up to class, read, and you'll get an A.

I loved Brother Searle! Attendance is mandatory, but you can make up two absences. There are two major projects throughout the semester, and weekly quizzes and short essay "what did you learn" assignments- I received full credit on all of these assignments! Exams are straightforward, and his extra credit quizzes are a great help. 10/10 recommend!!!

I have taken three different classes from Brother Searle at this point, I wish I could take more. His teaching is very focused on helping students learn good habits for lifelong learning. He is very kind and responsive to questions and concerns, inside or outside of class.
He knows his stuff and is super supportive and helpful. Sometimes class can be a little dry. He does well at preparing students for the exams. The class projects were also pretty tame.

I would not recommend him. He's a nice guy, but this class was WAY too hard and demanding for a religion class. You can def get things done, but seriously this class was ridiculous. Don't take it unless you want to stress about unimportant details and be super unclear about everything that is taught.

Prof. Searle was amazing! Lots of reading, but it's not hard. Attendance is mandatory!! His exams are Low-key hard sometimes but are only 10% of the grade, so It's not a huge deal if you bomb them. He is really nice, and provided many resources to help us study and prepare for the exams. Homework is easy, you just have to read:)

This class has lots of reading. The tests are closed book and pretty hard. He tries to make up for it in extra credit. You'll do fine if you pay attention but its pretty boring. He wants you to do well though and is always willing to meet. I wouldn't take again though.

This class was primarily graded on two large assigments, and then pre-class work and in class attendance quizes. Honestly this class felt like an institute or seminary level course with 10x the amount of required readings. The tests were closed scripture, and required you to memorize certain sections.

Such an easy, but inspirational class. If you're not sure who to take foundations of the restoration from I would highly suggest Bro.Searle! Weekly before class work, attendance, 2 largish (but easy) assignments, 2 midterms (easy enough), and 1 final (but graded the same as the midterms). Great class and lectures! Highly recommend.

The main homework is a preparation assignment before every class that is easy to keep up with. He goes a bit fast in the lectures at times, but his review questions in the beginning of the class will help to clarify what is needed to know. He goes in depth on the topics and answers questions very thoroughly.

Professor Searle gives out a lot of pre-class study material, but if you PAY ATTENTION in lecture and take notes, then there is no reason why you shouldn't succeed in this class. He will explicitly say "you will need to know this for the exam" all the time. There are like two time-consuming assignments the entire semester and a couple midterms.

Professor Searle is a good teacher and his lectures are entertaining; however, his tests are much too difficult. He sometimes will answer the test questions in class, but expects us to find the rest in the hour's worth of reading before each period. This class made me feel like I was drowning due to the difficulty of my more important classes.
Brother Searles class was very easy, as a professor he was excellent, I wish the class was not mandatory attendance because based off the readings you can crush the exams.
My favorite class I've taken so far.  It was super easy but I feel like I learned a lot.  Some assignments but they aren't hard at all.
Easy course, but some very discriminatory opinions shared as fact

Loved this class! The project we worked toward the whole semester seems daunting at the start but at the end of the semester I was so proud of how far I'd come and what I'd learned. What you put in is what you take out. Br. Searle is incredibly spiritual.

Searle once put two columns on the board, "Men" & "Women". On the left were words such as strong, independent, breadwinners, etc. On the right were words like dependent, caring, nurturing, etc. 

If you don't see an issue, Searle will be fine for you.
If you do, expect this kind of thing daily.

That said, you can expect an A with minimal effort.

Brother Searle is awesome. Really invites the Spirit. He really cares about the Gospel, his family, and his students. Great at sharing words of prophets as well as personal experiences. He does assign a lot of reading and assignments. They aren't hard but can be time consuming. Very easy grader though. Wants students to succeed and enjoy the class

Loved The Eternal Family, it was a low stress class but I also feel like I learned so much. The content wasn't memorization or specifics but rather gospel concepts and connecting the concepts to my life. This is how all BYU religion classes should be!

Not sure if there is a different prof named Travis Searle but my class had exams unlike others leaving reviews. They weren't bad though if you just fill out and study the study guide. No papers to write, but two mid-length assignments throughout the semester that weren't bad. Really nice guy and would take again.

If you want a super easy Eternal Families credit, this is the one for you. He has NO final exam. You will write little journals every week based on the readings and lectures, and occasional larger assignments, but still easy. At the end of the semester, you will compile everything into one doc and turn it in. Didn't learn a lot tho tbh.
There were no tests and assignments were easy. As a senior, this was the easiest class I've taken at BYU.

Easy religion but I did not learn anything. The readings were more beneficial to my learning than the class. The class was confusing and not pieced together well. They were all over the place and I had to multitask in order to survive from boredom in class. The assignments & papers were nice though. The format was helpful to learn from out of class
Be prepared to talk to the person sitting next to you. Every single class he had us discussing something with others. Wasn't the most fun thing for an introvert.

Super nice professor. Super easy. The only reason I didn't give him a 5/5 is that he is a little boring in the lectures. I found myself falling asleep in his class sometimes, but honestly, there are no tests in his class and you can still get an A without paying attention to the lectures. If you are looking for an easy religion credit this is good
His course just confused me a little bit. Wasn't the most organized and lots of work.

This was the strangest religion class I've ever taken. If you're used to the Utah Bubble, you'll be fine. If your testimony is so much as shaky, this class might make you leave the church. Apparently, heaven is for RMs, dating is a game, women aren't people, and divorces can be prevented with self-reliance classes. I wish this was a joke. Avoid.

Brother Searle is a great professor and takes care when teaching about hard topics which I appreciated. The exams were fairly difficult and if you have a hard time memorizing which scriptures are about which topics, I would recommend lots of studying! Other than that, lots of extra credit opportunities and a great religion class overall.
This class was a circus. There are so many assignments that don't actually help you learn. Least favorite religion class I have had at BYU.

I absolutely loved Prof Searle. Easily my favorite class I've taken at BYU so far. He's very respectful about difficult topics and always focuses on teaching the doctrine. There are before class readings but they are always just some short scriptures and a couple talks, nothing you can't do in 30 min. You don't have exams and the projects are easy

Anyone looking for a religion class at BYU, take it from Travis Searle! Very simple and easy. I cannot recommend him enough! He was very inspiring, and I loved the layout of his class. His class was exactly how a religion class should be. You will not regret taking a class from him.

Brother Searle is excellent. The two tests are difficult but everything else is super easy. Just show up to class, take notes, and do the 40 minutes of homework before class each day. This can be an incredibly easy class if you put in 40 minutes of work and fill out the study guide. If you mess up, no worries! THERE IS SO MUCH EXTRA CREDIT!
He has 2 tests and 2 big projects. The tests are pretty hard because you have to memorize what truths are in what scripture. The projects take up alot of time too but his lectures are great!

Professor Searle is very nice, but the class is annoying. It's a two-credit religion course with daily work, plenty of reading, and multiple midterms. You will complete work before class, during class, and after class. It is far more work than is necessary, and it follows any basic seminary course.

Brother Searle is one of the worst religion professors I have taken as a convert to the Church. I let him know I was a new member and he assured me that would be okay. His exams are deceptively difficult for new members, couldn't follow his lectures, and forgot about me and my appointments I had with him. He also posts 1/2 filled out slides.
This professor waste time too much.

Boring, but easy. I took Eternal Family from him, and I didn't show up for some days. Depending on the TA grading can be easy or tougher. Either way if you're looking for a religion credit on the easier side, I'd say this ones good.
Bro. Searle gives an ideal religion class.  The work is very manageable and the focus is on our own spiritual growth and learning.  He handles difficult topics very well and his lectures are great!

I learned so much from this class and Brother Searle's lectures. This is by far the easiest religion class I have taken, but you'll only get from it as much as you put into it. Show up for lectures and read the materials and you'll have a great, spiritual, stress-free experience.

So far my absolute favorite religion teacher. His lectures are amazing and he is always willing to answer questions in and out of class. He opened my eyes to the restoration even though I had been learning about it my whole life. Would 100% recommend him to anyone and take another class in a heartbeat.

He's a good teacher, he just wasn't the best fit for me. He repeated himself so much and talked very softly, so I had a hard time staying awake in his class. He also really loved partner work so if you're an introvert beware. You get out what you put into this class, I really like the talks we had to read but I'm glad I'm done with this class
Not too loaded with assignments. You can tell he cares for his students. He's always willing to answer questions no matter what they are. Take him! Especially to feel the holy spirit
The class was pretty easy overall. I didn't find his teaching style to be very engaging or interesting. The tests were harder than I expected, but after an hour of studying I aced them.

Everyone who has the chance should take Restorations from Prof. Searle. He knows the content so well but teaches simply, inspiring spiritual growth without stress. There are pre-class readings with great discussions and stories in class. He has a study guide available with every concept for the exams. Weekly reflections are easy by going to class.

Really easy class for me, and attendance wasn't mandatory but I often used the class time to lock in and turn assignments in. Professor Searle is nice, but doesn't get to know his students at all, but this didn't bother me. I was able to sit in the back of the class and not really talk to anyone, bc thats what I prefer.

Make sure to do the pre-class readings! And attend office hours if you have a question. He has a clear structure of the class in his mind, but wasn't always clear to me personally until I went to office hours. He's a really kind person, really helpful and accommodating. Great at tying in historical examples to modern principles.

Brother Searle is honestly amazing! He is one of the best religion professors that I have had at BYU. He knows how to bring the spirit and is very inspirational! Class work load is pretty light and easy to keep up with.

Brother Searle's class was pretty good. There is a bunch of small assignments, but those go by pretty fast. Some classes are very boring, but with class participation/discussion and everybody in a fun or good mood, the classes were great! We talked about good topics, and Searle explained them pretty well.

Professor Searle is great! There is a lot of homework; it's super easy, but make sure to do it. Online tests are easy as long as you review material. Half way through the semester Professor Searle even changed some organizational things after a mid class survey. If you've read the Saints books before you'll already be familiar with some content.

My least favorite professor that I have had so far. He would curb difficult questions and I would often feel tension in his class. Scraped by with an A- due to his first test. Would not take another class from him.

Professor Searle is a very nice guy who is passionate about the students and what he teaches. I wasn't personally fond of his writing style and the way he explained a few topics, but he ultimately is very organized and has the best of intention. Tests aren't graded super heavy, so as long as you do the home work, you should get a pretty good grade.

Bro Searle is so so so nice but his class was absolutely not for me. Stopped going to class mid semester and ended with an A. I did not like the organization of the class at all and didn't feel like I really learned anything which was disappointing because I was really looking forward to the class. Go to the TA test reviews & the exam will be fine

Had the class at 8am, so I lost a lot of points for being late to class, but if you attend you will mostly do fine. The material helps you resolve common questions about the foundations of the Church. He asked for feedback mid-semester and made lots of changes based on the feedback, he cares about the students.

Professor Searle is a super kind individual! I took his Living Prophets class online. Overall, very straightforward course and grading. Tests were open book open note; however, the tests are RIDICULOUSLY long. I spent over 2 hours on the midterm and almost 3 hours on the final. You can get great grades, it just takes some time investment.

Engaging & interesting lectures, but VERY homework heavy. To understand the material or do well on exams you have to read everything he assigns outside class. No extra credit. Projects were great, make sure to be aware of their deadlines (they come up fast).
Very responsive to class needs; changed the whole class setup after a mid-semester survey.

super great class!!! listened to the student's feedback at mid semester course survey and literally changed the set up. super organized class structure and easy weekly assignments. otherwise there are three papers in the class and final is non cumulative! loved this

Prof Searle was a fantastic teacher.  He was good at making class interactive and addressing touchy subjects in a Christlike manner.  He is super caring and shares impactful experiences.  There's assignments for each class, but you can knock them out in 10min.  Would recommend!

This has been by far the worst religion professor at BYU I've had. There is a pre class assignment, during class assignment, and post class assignment due every in class day. They take 1.5 hrs to do. The tests are the worst I have seen. Everything he wants you to do is so convoluted and if you don't do it his way he'll give you a bad grade.

REL C 225 is a heavier religion course and Brother Searle does a really good job of breaking down the material and dealing with uncomfortable Church topics. The class was harder than my other religion classes, but still pretty easy, and the test review materials were super helpful.

Bro Searle was a good enough professor but his teaching style wasn't really for me. The TA said the tests would be easy but most people in my class did poorly on the first midterm. Luckily the majority of the grade comes from assignments and not exams because the midterms and finals were not as easy as religion tests should be.

Professor Searle was awesome! He always made sure we knew he cared about our comments and he was super nice! The tests weren't too hard, if you fill out the review he gives you then you'll be set! I loved this class and think everyone should take a class from Searle!

Course structure was very simple and organized which I loved, nothing too complex. when reading try to answer the objectives along the way, there are weekly personal insight assignments and daily assignments which takes 5 mins. tests can be meticulous but very simple, no difficult questions are being asked. great prof!

Loved him. Some readings took forever and quiz before every class w two attempts (easy). Tests are easy if you look at the ppt the TA sends out and the study guides and memorize that info. Writing assignments are graded easy and not tough. Lectures were good too. Graded on attendance and two make ups. Won't excuse sickness without makeup assignment
Brother Searle is very kind and a great professor. Class is quite easy if you stay on top of it, it's all about personal accountability.

Brother Searle is amazing!! I always felt the spirit and he very clearly explains some hard truths about church history. He is also very clear about what he expects on the few homework assignments and tests. I would take any class for him you can!

Professor Searle's class was exactly what a religion class should be! The tests weren't very hard, the study review sessions were super helpful, class wasn't boring or overwhelming, and the workload wasn't over the top! Honestly one of my favorite religion classes that I've taken and I would highly recommend taking it! Professor Searle is awesome!

This class is graded based on self reported book reading, attendance, a few self improvement type assignments, 2 midterms and the final. Tests are online and proctored- the study guides generally follow the tests very closely so it is easy to get a good grade. Prof Searle is really understanding and open minded. He makes an effort to know names too

Searle is a good teacher with a deep and passionate testimony. He cares about his students but is a serious man.
Everything on the test is said in class and he prepares you for all questions. Homework is very doable, takes 30 minutes.
Tests can be slightly stressful but with moderate studying and going to the test review, it is more than doable.

Brother Searle is a very spiritual teacher who gives good lectures. Soft spoken, so sometimes the in-class discussions didn't go far, but he did great at clearly giving us the content and preparing us for exams. The reading assignments weren't too heavy, I usually completed them the morning before class. I hope to take his class on living prophets!

Brother Searle is my favorite religion professor! Instead of overcomplicating things like many religion professors do, he focuses on the simplicity of the gospel. He doesn't try to invent some new profound idea, he just focuses on building faith. He's excellent at creating personal applications for church history and teaching by the Spirit.

I attended almost every class and did all the homework. It took me a month or so to get used to the class and to catch on to what information would be on the tests. The study guides helped. The work and syllabus are very organized. I did about 3 hours (on average) every week. Lectures were a little slow, but there were enlightening discussions.

There's quite a bit of reading, but it's not too bad. You can tell Professor Searle really wants to do well and see his students succeed, but his tests are everything a religion test should not be: detail focused and memorization heavy. However, it's hard to say whether this class was disappointing because of the course or the instructor.

Bro. Searle is a nice guy who knows the content well. He can go over the slides too fast, so be ready to take notes. the ungraded practice quizzes really help you get ready for the tests. the class is very straight forward and an easy A if you stay on top of things.

Most religion classes at BYU I feel like aren't super spiritual based. However, this class was a very good mix of spiritual and learning. There are assignments in class, so attendance is necessary. However, the daily assignments aren't difficult and the tests weren't too bad. Brother Searle is a fun, kind man.

He was great at addressing difficult topics, class was super easy, tests were straightforward, mostly copied the questions off the practice quizzes. Two big assignments seemed to be graded more on completion than competency. You can tell he is still trying to refine what class should look like but is good about being open to feedback. Great guy!

Prof. Searle is a great guy and you can tell that he cares about the content and his students. The coursework was very easy. If you do the practice tests you'll do great on the exams because it's practically a copy and paste of the questions. Overall, the lectures weren't super engaging, but I learned a lot about church history I didn't know before
Professor Searle is genuine and you can tell he really cares about his students. This class is not difficult but I still feel like I learned a lot. I'd take this professor again in a heartbeat.

go to class! study guides weekly are helpful. He answers any question. If you have questions about the restoration or about controversial content from that period, this professor knows how to address those in a courteous and logical way. Course content was mostly organized

The lectures in class are very material heavy. If you don't show up the lectures are posted online but the slides are not very detailed. Frequently he will ask you to turn and talk to partners about anything from answering a question on the board to very personal experiences.

This class is genuinely just busywork. Rather than being able to actually listen and pay attention in class, all you do is fill out worksheet upon worksheet that are clearly supposed to be helpful but are really just mind numbing and distracting. Probably my least favorite religion class I've taken my entire time at BYU.

Prof. Searle's Restoration class is mind-numbingly easy, with that in mind, the lectures are insanely grueling and there is so much busy-work that it is impossible to learn anything. If you show up, you will get an easy A, there are 0 tests/essays, and there is hardly any out of class work, but I would NOT recommend this professor for this class.

Great class and choice for a religion credit! Most of the assignments were filling out pre-made slides about each prophet / apostle. Info needed was covered in class, so I got most homework done during lecture. Super easy but learned so much about the prophets' lives and teachings. Highly recommend!
class is a little dull. easy to sleep through. but he is such a sweet man and really cares for his students. No final too, which was nice. Just doing the work and you'll be just fine.

Professor Searle really cares about his student and he has a great testimony of the restored gospel. I enjoyed his lectures and he tells a lot of fun stories related to living prophets. There is no final in this class but you have to work on a semester long project and you have slides to submit every week.

Brother Searle is the sweetest. He had quite a few assignments, but none were extremely hard. The class is very focused on helping you build your testimony of the Savior through the teachings of the living prophets! Would take this class again!
Brother Searle doesn't have any tests, just requires you to take notes during class, which had very well thought out lectures. I loved this class.

This religion class was very easy to follow and understand, and had no final exam. Attendance is a major part of the grade. I don't personally love the way Professor Searle addressed certain difficult questions or issues in Church History, he is very orthodox which I know some people appreciate, but it's not for me personally.

Brother Searle is awesome! He treats a religion class the way it should - learning focused and not grade focused. His lectures are almost always engaging, I was never bored. He focuses always on the spiritual aspects, and my testimony was definitely strengthened. He's extremely smart as well

Probably the easiest religion class I've taken at BYU, but very informative and well-structured. Before/in-class reflections that are ~50 words, slides ab 2 apostles due every 2 weeks with a final culmination at the end, and a simple semester-long project. Super easy to get a good grade if you just put a little thought into it. Highly recommend.

If you want any easy religion class, take it with Professor Searle. I honestly didn't pay much attention but  his lectures were really interesting when I listened haha. Homework is super easy. There are no tests or final. He's a good guy

Class was easy, no exams or quizzes. You have fill out a module and have to do an activity every two weeks and write 2 essays total. The only downfall is the modules you have to fill out in class. Sometimes it was hard to focus on his teachings or feel the spirit when we were too busy trying to make sure we got the notes filled out.

Brother Searle is awesome! Love his stories! You just read short things about each apostle and create Slides on them. You don't present them. No midterm. Semester long project that is very manageable. Final project is creating a cumulative slide of some slides you've already created. He is funny and shares great personal experiences and stories!

Very easy class, but also very informative - I learned lots about each apostle. No tests at all. Just pre-class reflection questions, a slide deck about each apostle every other weekend, and then a project spread throughout the semester about finding answers to questions. I love Brother Searle - so kind and sincere!
Want an easy A class with no tests that tackles difficult church historical topics with sensitivity and an eternal perspective? Take his class. Wouldn't take this class from anyone else.

I think overall this was a good class. There was a semester long project about finding answers to our questions, and I feel like it wasn't super clear what he wanted sometimes. My class was once a week, so I don't think that sometimes it was adapted very well for our class compared to the twice a week class. Really cool class though!
I loved this class!
Easiest religion class I've taken. Good lectures and insight. Caring and tries to connect with students.

Lectures were quite boring, only created more confusion among the students than actually answered questions, and he constantly tried to do too much, hardly giving students any time for the in-class discussions he assigned. The homework assignments were nothing but busy work that forced you to repeat yourself constantly.

I learned a lot in this class, but I struggled to grow besides that. Lectures were stressful and most of it was spent frantically try to fill out charts. Outside of class there were more charts to fill out and it was a bit boring since we did the same thing every single time.

This class was the most seminary- like religion class I have taken at BYU and I loved it for that. I feel like I learned a lot being able to study how I wanted while also having specific things to learn about in a  structured way. Classes did require partner work and participation. Would recommend!
This class is so boring. It's just busy work but it's an easy A.

He is a great professor I learned a lot from his class. He has a lot of knowledge and you can tell he loves what he teaches. Not a ton of homework and a very manageable class. There were no actual exams which is the way I think religion classes should be done.

Travis Searle was a great professor. Even when i took the class with a ton of other students he still tried his best to talk with everyone. I loved the class living prophets because i gained a deeper understanding of them. There is only a project, 8 slide show every 2 weeks, and a final witness slide show. No test.
Enjoyed this class! He is a great professor who does a really good job answering questions in a clear and respectful way. Really organized.

He is a great teacher! He does a great job discussing difficult topics related to the Restoration and makes his lectures interesting with lots of discussion and real-life examples. Attendance is mandatory, but I enjoyed attending class! Homework is very easy and very interesting! No tests, just some simple writing.

Brother Searle is a good teacher, and you won't be disappointed with his classes. There were no exams, so that was nice. Just smaller projects here and there. Definitely do readings so you can share it class because there are many group discussions. All around, good experience.

Awesome class! He dives deep into so many church history topics that are interesting and controversial. Professor Searle is so awesome and extremely kind and helpful, he is willing to help you improve your grade if needed and cares about his students. Easy A
Easy class and can learn a lot. I really appreciate this type of religion class. Good faith building classes.

My only complaint was that I took this as a night class and those turn 2 hours really long. Other than that, Brother Searle is great. His lectures are very inspiring and he cares about his students. I feel that I learned a lot. The out of class work was pretty light. I would recommend this class anytime.

He is a great professor and teaches really well. He's willing to answer any questions you have without making you feel stupid for asking them. He is also really good at talking about the difficult topics like plural marriage. I've learned so much from him and you can't go wrong with his Foundations of Restoration class.

Best thing about this class is that he doesn't do exams. I really enjoyed the desire assignments and before class study. Some assignments were just busy work, and he had some strange requirements that don't appear on the rubric. Nice enough guy - he's not great with the hard questions and frequently searches for a specific answer in discussions.

I LOVE Prof. Searle. This was my 3rd religion class I'd taken from him, and I'd take a million more. This class, along with REL 250, aren't test-based, which is how every REL class should be imo. He is super funny, puts a lot of heart into his lectures, and jumps to help students when needed. Just show up to class, read, and you'll get an A.

I loved Brother Searle! Attendance is mandatory, but you can make up two absences. There are two major projects throughout the semester, and weekly quizzes and short essay "what did you learn" assignments- I received full credit on all of these assignments! Exams are straightforward, and his extra credit quizzes are a great help. 10/10 recommend!!!

I have taken three different classes from Brother Searle at this point, I wish I could take more. His teaching is very focused on helping students learn good habits for lifelong learning. He is very kind and responsive to questions and concerns, inside or outside of class.
He knows his stuff and is super supportive and helpful. Sometimes class can be a little dry. He does well at preparing students for the exams. The class projects were also pretty tame.

I would not recommend him. He's a nice guy, but this class was WAY too hard and demanding for a religion class. You can def get things done, but seriously this class was ridiculous. Don't take it unless you want to stress about unimportant details and be super unclear about everything that is taught.

Prof. Searle was amazing! Lots of reading, but it's not hard. Attendance is mandatory!! His exams are Low-key hard sometimes but are only 10% of the grade, so It's not a huge deal if you bomb them. He is really nice, and provided many resources to help us study and prepare for the exams. Homework is easy, you just have to read:)

This class has lots of reading. The tests are closed book and pretty hard. He tries to make up for it in extra credit. You'll do fine if you pay attention but its pretty boring. He wants you to do well though and is always willing to meet. I wouldn't take again though.

This class was primarily graded on two large assigments, and then pre-class work and in class attendance quizes. Honestly this class felt like an institute or seminary level course with 10x the amount of required readings. The tests were closed scripture, and required you to memorize certain sections.

Such an easy, but inspirational class. If you're not sure who to take foundations of the restoration from I would highly suggest Bro.Searle! Weekly before class work, attendance, 2 largish (but easy) assignments, 2 midterms (easy enough), and 1 final (but graded the same as the midterms). Great class and lectures! Highly recommend.

The main homework is a preparation assignment before every class that is easy to keep up with. He goes a bit fast in the lectures at times, but his review questions in the beginning of the class will help to clarify what is needed to know. He goes in depth on the topics and answers questions very thoroughly.

Professor Searle gives out a lot of pre-class study material, but if you PAY ATTENTION in lecture and take notes, then there is no reason why you shouldn't succeed in this class. He will explicitly say "you will need to know this for the exam" all the time. There are like two time-consuming assignments the entire semester and a couple midterms.

Professor Searle is a good teacher and his lectures are entertaining; however, his tests are much too difficult. He sometimes will answer the test questions in class, but expects us to find the rest in the hour's worth of reading before each period. This class made me feel like I was drowning due to the difficulty of my more important classes.
