Brother Searles class was very easy, as a professor he was excellent, I wish the class was not mandatory attendance because based off the readings you can crush the exams.
My favorite class I've taken so far.  It was super easy but I feel like I learned a lot.  Some assignments but they aren't hard at all.
Easy course, but some very discriminatory opinions shared as fact

Loved this class! The project we worked toward the whole semester seems daunting at the start but at the end of the semester I was so proud of how far I'd come and what I'd learned. What you put in is what you take out. Br. Searle is incredibly spiritual.

Searle once put two columns on the board, "Men" & "Women". On the left were words such as strong, independent, breadwinners, etc. On the right were words like dependent, caring, nurturing, etc. 

If you don't see an issue, Searle will be fine for you.
If you do, expect this kind of thing daily.

That said, you can expect an A with minimal effort.

Brother Searle is awesome. Really invites the Spirit. He really cares about the Gospel, his family, and his students. Great at sharing words of prophets as well as personal experiences. He does assign a lot of reading and assignments. They aren't hard but can be time consuming. Very easy grader though. Wants students to succeed and enjoy the class

Loved The Eternal Family, it was a low stress class but I also feel like I learned so much. The content wasn't memorization or specifics but rather gospel concepts and connecting the concepts to my life. This is how all BYU religion classes should be!

Not sure if there is a different prof named Travis Searle but my class had exams unlike others leaving reviews. They weren't bad though if you just fill out and study the study guide. No papers to write, but two mid-length assignments throughout the semester that weren't bad. Really nice guy and would take again.

If you want a super easy Eternal Families credit, this is the one for you. He has NO final exam. You will write little journals every week based on the readings and lectures, and occasional larger assignments, but still easy. At the end of the semester, you will compile everything into one doc and turn it in. Didn't learn a lot tho tbh.
There were no tests and assignments were easy. As a senior, this was the easiest class I've taken at BYU.

Easy religion but I did not learn anything. The readings were more beneficial to my learning than the class. The class was confusing and not pieced together well. They were all over the place and I had to multitask in order to survive from boredom in class. The assignments & papers were nice though. The format was helpful to learn from out of class
Be prepared to talk to the person sitting next to you. Every single class he had us discussing something with others. Wasn't the most fun thing for an introvert.

Super nice professor. Super easy. The only reason I didn't give him a 5/5 is that he is a little boring in the lectures. I found myself falling asleep in his class sometimes, but honestly, there are no tests in his class and you can still get an A without paying attention to the lectures. If you are looking for an easy religion credit this is good
His course just confused me a little bit. Wasn't the most organized and lots of work.

This was the strangest religion class I've ever taken. If you're used to the Utah Bubble, you'll be fine. If your testimony is so much as shaky, this class might make you leave the church. Apparently, heaven is for RMs, dating is a game, women aren't people, and divorces can be prevented with self-reliance classes. I wish this was a joke. Avoid.

Brother Searle is a great professor and takes care when teaching about hard topics which I appreciated. The exams were fairly difficult and if you have a hard time memorizing which scriptures are about which topics, I would recommend lots of studying! Other than that, lots of extra credit opportunities and a great religion class overall.
This class was a circus. There are so many assignments that don't actually help you learn. Least favorite religion class I have had at BYU.

I absolutely loved Prof Searle. Easily my favorite class I've taken at BYU so far. He's very respectful about difficult topics and always focuses on teaching the doctrine. There are before class readings but they are always just some short scriptures and a couple talks, nothing you can't do in 30 min. You don't have exams and the projects are easy

Anyone looking for a religion class at BYU, take it from Travis Searle! Very simple and easy. I cannot recommend him enough! He was very inspiring, and I loved the layout of his class. His class was exactly how a religion class should be. You will not regret taking a class from him.

Brother Searle is excellent. The two tests are difficult but everything else is super easy. Just show up to class, take notes, and do the 40 minutes of homework before class each day. This can be an incredibly easy class if you put in 40 minutes of work and fill out the study guide. If you mess up, no worries! THERE IS SO MUCH EXTRA CREDIT!
He has 2 tests and 2 big projects. The tests are pretty hard because you have to memorize what truths are in what scripture. The projects take up alot of time too but his lectures are great!

Professor Searle is very nice, but the class is annoying. It's a two-credit religion course with daily work, plenty of reading, and multiple midterms. You will complete work before class, during class, and after class. It is far more work than is necessary, and it follows any basic seminary course.

Brother Searle is one of the worst religion professors I have taken as a convert to the Church. I let him know I was a new member and he assured me that would be okay. His exams are deceptively difficult for new members, couldn't follow his lectures, and forgot about me and my appointments I had with him. He also posts 1/2 filled out slides.
This professor waste time too much.

Boring, but easy. I took Eternal Family from him, and I didn't show up for some days. Depending on the TA grading can be easy or tougher. Either way if you're looking for a religion credit on the easier side, I'd say this ones good.
Bro. Searle gives an ideal religion class.  The work is very manageable and the focus is on our own spiritual growth and learning.  He handles difficult topics very well and his lectures are great!

I learned so much from this class and Brother Searle's lectures. This is by far the easiest religion class I have taken, but you'll only get from it as much as you put into it. Show up for lectures and read the materials and you'll have a great, spiritual, stress-free experience.

So far my absolute favorite religion teacher. His lectures are amazing and he is always willing to answer questions in and out of class. He opened my eyes to the restoration even though I had been learning about it my whole life. Would 100% recommend him to anyone and take another class in a heartbeat.

He's a good teacher, he just wasn't the best fit for me. He repeated himself so much and talked very softly, so I had a hard time staying awake in his class. He also really loved partner work so if you're an introvert beware. You get out what you put into this class, I really like the talks we had to read but I'm glad I'm done with this class
Not too loaded with assignments. You can tell he cares for his students. He's always willing to answer questions no matter what they are. Take him! Especially to feel the holy spirit
The class was pretty easy overall. I didn't find his teaching style to be very engaging or interesting. The tests were harder than I expected, but after an hour of studying I aced them.

Everyone who has the chance should take Restorations from Prof. Searle. He knows the content so well but teaches simply, inspiring spiritual growth without stress. There are pre-class readings with great discussions and stories in class. He has a study guide available with every concept for the exams. Weekly reflections are easy by going to class.

Really easy class for me, and attendance wasn't mandatory but I often used the class time to lock in and turn assignments in. Professor Searle is nice, but doesn't get to know his students at all, but this didn't bother me. I was able to sit in the back of the class and not really talk to anyone, bc thats what I prefer.

Make sure to do the pre-class readings! And attend office hours if you have a question. He has a clear structure of the class in his mind, but wasn't always clear to me personally until I went to office hours. He's a really kind person, really helpful and accommodating. Great at tying in historical examples to modern principles.

Brother Searle is honestly amazing! He is one of the best religion professors that I have had at BYU. He knows how to bring the spirit and is very inspirational! Class work load is pretty light and easy to keep up with.

Brother Searle's class was pretty good. There is a bunch of small assignments, but those go by pretty fast. Some classes are very boring, but with class participation/discussion and everybody in a fun or good mood, the classes were great! We talked about good topics, and Searle explained them pretty well.

Professor Searle is great! There is a lot of homework; it's super easy, but make sure to do it. Online tests are easy as long as you review material. Half way through the semester Professor Searle even changed some organizational things after a mid class survey. If you've read the Saints books before you'll already be familiar with some content.

My least favorite professor that I have had so far. He would curb difficult questions and I would often feel tension in his class. Scraped by with an A- due to his first test. Would not take another class from him.

Professor Searle is a very nice guy who is passionate about the students and what he teaches. I wasn't personally fond of his writing style and the way he explained a few topics, but he ultimately is very organized and has the best of intention. Tests aren't graded super heavy, so as long as you do the home work, you should get a pretty good grade.

Bro Searle is so so so nice but his class was absolutely not for me. Stopped going to class mid semester and ended with an A. I did not like the organization of the class at all and didn't feel like I really learned anything which was disappointing because I was really looking forward to the class. Go to the TA test reviews & the exam will be fine

Had the class at 8am, so I lost a lot of points for being late to class, but if you attend you will mostly do fine. The material helps you resolve common questions about the foundations of the Church. He asked for feedback mid-semester and made lots of changes based on the feedback, he cares about the students.

Professor Searle is a super kind individual! I took his Living Prophets class online. Overall, very straightforward course and grading. Tests were open book open note; however, the tests are RIDICULOUSLY long. I spent over 2 hours on the midterm and almost 3 hours on the final. You can get great grades, it just takes some time investment.

Engaging & interesting lectures, but VERY homework heavy. To understand the material or do well on exams you have to read everything he assigns outside class. No extra credit. Projects were great, make sure to be aware of their deadlines (they come up fast).
Very responsive to class needs; changed the whole class setup after a mid-semester survey.

super great class!!! listened to the student's feedback at mid semester course survey and literally changed the set up. super organized class structure and easy weekly assignments. otherwise there are three papers in the class and final is non cumulative! loved this

Prof Searle was a fantastic teacher.  He was good at making class interactive and addressing touchy subjects in a Christlike manner.  He is super caring and shares impactful experiences.  There's assignments for each class, but you can knock them out in 10min.  Would recommend!

This has been by far the worst religion professor at BYU I've had. There is a pre class assignment, during class assignment, and post class assignment due every in class day. They take 1.5 hrs to do. The tests are the worst I have seen. Everything he wants you to do is so convoluted and if you don't do it his way he'll give you a bad grade.

REL C 225 is a heavier religion course and Brother Searle does a really good job of breaking down the material and dealing with uncomfortable Church topics. The class was harder than my other religion classes, but still pretty easy, and the test review materials were super helpful.

Bro Searle was a good enough professor but his teaching style wasn't really for me. The TA said the tests would be easy but most people in my class did poorly on the first midterm. Luckily the majority of the grade comes from assignments and not exams because the midterms and finals were not as easy as religion tests should be.

Professor Searle was awesome! He always made sure we knew he cared about our comments and he was super nice! The tests weren't too hard, if you fill out the review he gives you then you'll be set! I loved this class and think everyone should take a class from Searle!

Course structure was very simple and organized which I loved, nothing too complex. when reading try to answer the objectives along the way, there are weekly personal insight assignments and daily assignments which takes 5 mins. tests can be meticulous but very simple, no difficult questions are being asked. great prof!

Loved him. Some readings took forever and quiz before every class w two attempts (easy). Tests are easy if you look at the ppt the TA sends out and the study guides and memorize that info. Writing assignments are graded easy and not tough. Lectures were good too. Graded on attendance and two make ups. Won't excuse sickness without makeup assignment
Brother Searle is very kind and a great professor. Class is quite easy if you stay on top of it, it's all about personal accountability.

Brother Searle is amazing!! I always felt the spirit and he very clearly explains some hard truths about church history. He is also very clear about what he expects on the few homework assignments and tests. I would take any class for him you can!

Professor Searle's class was exactly what a religion class should be! The tests weren't very hard, the study review sessions were super helpful, class wasn't boring or overwhelming, and the workload wasn't over the top! Honestly one of my favorite religion classes that I've taken and I would highly recommend taking it! Professor Searle is awesome!

This class is graded based on self reported book reading, attendance, a few self improvement type assignments, 2 midterms and the final. Tests are online and proctored- the study guides generally follow the tests very closely so it is easy to get a good grade. Prof Searle is really understanding and open minded. He makes an effort to know names too

Searle is a good teacher with a deep and passionate testimony. He cares about his students but is a serious man.
Everything on the test is said in class and he prepares you for all questions. Homework is very doable, takes 30 minutes.
Tests can be slightly stressful but with moderate studying and going to the test review, it is more than doable.

Brother Searle is a very spiritual teacher who gives good lectures. Soft spoken, so sometimes the in-class discussions didn't go far, but he did great at clearly giving us the content and preparing us for exams. The reading assignments weren't too heavy, I usually completed them the morning before class. I hope to take his class on living prophets!

Brother Searle is my favorite religion professor! Instead of overcomplicating things like many religion professors do, he focuses on the simplicity of the gospel. He doesn't try to invent some new profound idea, he just focuses on building faith. He's excellent at creating personal applications for church history and teaching by the Spirit.

I attended almost every class and did all the homework. It took me a month or so to get used to the class and to catch on to what information would be on the tests. The study guides helped. The work and syllabus are very organized. I did about 3 hours (on average) every week. Lectures were a little slow, but there were enlightening discussions.

There's quite a bit of reading, but it's not too bad. You can tell Professor Searle really wants to do well and see his students succeed, but his tests are everything a religion test should not be: detail focused and memorization heavy. However, it's hard to say whether this class was disappointing because of the course or the instructor.

Bro. Searle is a nice guy who knows the content well. He can go over the slides too fast, so be ready to take notes. the ungraded practice quizzes really help you get ready for the tests. the class is very straight forward and an easy A if you stay on top of things.

Most religion classes at BYU I feel like aren't super spiritual based. However, this class was a very good mix of spiritual and learning. There are assignments in class, so attendance is necessary. However, the daily assignments aren't difficult and the tests weren't too bad. Brother Searle is a fun, kind man.

He was great at addressing difficult topics, class was super easy, tests were straightforward, mostly copied the questions off the practice quizzes. Two big assignments seemed to be graded more on completion than competency. You can tell he is still trying to refine what class should look like but is good about being open to feedback. Great guy!

Prof. Searle is a great guy and you can tell that he cares about the content and his students. The coursework was very easy. If you do the practice tests you'll do great on the exams because it's practically a copy and paste of the questions. Overall, the lectures weren't super engaging, but I learned a lot about church history I didn't know before
Professor Searle is genuine and you can tell he really cares about his students. This class is not difficult but I still feel like I learned a lot. I'd take this professor again in a heartbeat.

go to class! study guides weekly are helpful. He answers any question. If you have questions about the restoration or about controversial content from that period, this professor knows how to address those in a courteous and logical way. Course content was mostly organized

The lectures in class are very material heavy. If you don't show up the lectures are posted online but the slides are not very detailed. Frequently he will ask you to turn and talk to partners about anything from answering a question on the board to very personal experiences.
Very funny professor and very interesting class. Take it from him!

He cares so much about his students and wants them to succeed. There are readings for every class, but he chooses amazing pieces that are enjoyable to read! I loved this class, and he is an awesome professor who loves what he teaches. This is definitely a very helpful course for learning how to read different types of literature. He is hilarious!

This class is mostly lectures and class discussions with a few group activities. Prof Hickman tells great stories and leads the discussions very well. But take notes and pay attention so you're ready for the final essay

Dr. Hickman is a great professor to take for literary history classes! He picked a great variety of books to read over the semester, and his lectures about them were very informative. Would recommend!

My favorite professor I had in my freshman year. You basically just do the reading and discuss it in class. There were a few essays, which were graded fairly harshly, but overall not too difficult. Occasionally you'd write a little in class. It was a very fun class, and most of the reading was very interesting and entertaining.

Loved this class, lots of reading, but he makes it so comprehensible and exciting. He knows his stuff. Not many assignments; do the reading before class and you'll be good! His tests are very well formatted and he is a fair grader, so read & show up and it's hard to fail! Overall Trent is an great professor who cares for his students & material.

Professor Hickman is hilarious and knows a lot about the course material. There are random assignments throughout the semester that count as attendance, so make sure to be in class! The material is fascinating and Professor Hickman makes it easy to understand. Very clear criteria for tests, which are half of your grade. A reading-heavy course.

Professor Hickman was fantastic! This is the second class I have taken from him, and he is by far my favorite professor at BYU. He is caring and realistic, and his lectures are super engaging! I found that if I didn't enjoy a passage, he would find a way to make me love it! I never imagined I would love Eliot's The Waste Land, but now I do!

I loved Professor Hickman's classes! This was the second class I have taken from him and every lecture is funny and insightful. He can meet with you if you're struggling. He cares that you know the material. I would highly recommend taking any of his classes!

Hickman is probably the best literature professor at BYU. You read a lot, but you go over the readings in pretty good detail in class to make sure you understood everything. The tests and papers were hard, but he provides study guides and peer reviews to give you the best chance at doing well. I would recommend meeting with him, get to know him.

Hickman was my favorite professor this semester. Class discussions were genuinely fun. He cares about his students, I'd feel safe going to him for anything. Few assignments, with most points in four essays throughout semester, but he will work on them with you in office hours (except final). I love this man. Take his classes.

Professor Hickman is the best professor I have ever had. He makes what we are learning so applicable and stretches it beyond face value. He is caring, knowledgeable, and prepares you to pass his class. It is not hard to earn a good grade if you try hard.

I took English 303 from Prof. Hickman as a freshman and it CHANGED MY LIFE! He taught the class a lot about how to come up with an idea for a research paper and execute it effectively. It has made me a much better writer, and more importantly, I really enjoy it now! I'm so grateful for this class and he's the first teacher I recommend to people.

Professor Hickman actually made enjoy lit history! I usually hate this subject or struggle with is and he made all assignments and exams pretty straightforward and easy. As long as you read and pay attention in class you'll be fine. He is actually funny and not like cringe funny, real funny! I definitely recommend his class!

He is such an awesome professor!! Highly recommend his class! If you do what he says to prepare for class and the tests, there is no way you can fail. The tests are extremely fair and as long as you pay attention in class you will pass with flying colors.

Professor Hickman is one of my favorite professors. He is so funny and his class is structured so that you do some reading outside of class and then discuss the reading in class. He has occassional rush writes, but if you do the reading you pass. He does have papers due throughout the semester and they are graded difficult, but overall low stress.
He is incredible at communicating the concepts in an understandable way. Every lecture flowed easily through my brain. This was my favorite class this semester, even over Creative Writing.

I love Professor Hickman. He's super nice and gives you excellent advice and feedback. And I LOVE how he structures the essay writing process. He will improve your writing. I love the way he interacts with his students---he's so helpful and understanding. Take any class from him to learn interesting things and become a better writer.

Trent was HILARIOUS. I loved his class so much and he made every lecture so interesting. He picked things for us to read that he truly thought we'd enjoy and was so caring. 3 tests (which aren't hard if you do the reading) and a rushwrite to start every class where you write about what you read the night prior (he grades them super easily)

I've taken two classes from Trent now because he's that awesome. He has clear expectations, a kind heart, an articulate and quick-witted mind, and a fantastic sense of humor. You learn a ton but also enjoy the work, and he gives you all the tools you need to succeed. He's simply one of those professors you just love.

Clear structure. Assigned readings & time period are discussed. Prepare for random "Rushwrites" (a question that has you reflect on the reading), so take notes as you read. Fair amount of exams and essays--the study guide is helpful. Mix of video clips, presentations, white board, groups, & lecture. He is knowledgeable & makes super funny comments

Professor Hickman is just the coolest guy. He is a mental health advocate so I always felt safe talking to him about anything and everything before class started. Lots of reading, but it's GOOD. He picks assigned readings that he knows his students will love. I always left the class feeling inspired.

Dr. Hickman is one of the kindest and funniest professors I've had at BYU. He is incredibly articulate and provides thorough feedback on writing assignments. He has a contagious love for poetry and literature and makes coming to class easy due to his engaging lectures. Can't recommend him enough.

Class attendance is important in this class because of rush writes. If you do a rush write, you get the credit. It is an easy class and I highly recommend this class for anyone. This class teaches you how to read in different ways and how to analyze things differently than you have ever done. One of the best classes I have ever took.

I love Professor Hickman! His lectures are the best and he really wants his students to succeed. He is a fantastic professor (and I loved EVERY SINGLE ONE of the novels we read this semester!). I loved his class so much that I'm already taking another one from him!

Trent Hickman is an amazing man. He is a mental health advocate in his classes and will work with students who struggle so they can still succeed in his class. He is so willing to talk to students about class material and how to succeed during office hours and goes out of his way to avoid triggering students in class.

Prof Hickman is a great guy. Clearly loves his subject and does his best to get students to get involved with the reading. The only reason I didn't like his class is because I'm not a huge fan of modernist poetry, the class's focus. Make sure you keep up with the readings and pay attention. I struggled only because the material didn't interest me.

Professor Hickman is outstanding. He teaches the material in a clear but interesting way. He assigns two essays (the average for this course) but they are both small in size and he gives clear expectations on how they are graded. I would definitely recommend taking this course from Hickman.

Prof Hickman is amazing. He's a very entertaining and sensitive professor, and his grading is clear. The lectures/discussions in class were truly fascinating and engaging. The class has lots of reading, but it's really interesting. Just do the reading and pay attention when he discusses key points and you'll do great.

Professor Hickman is, BY FAR, my favorite professor. He is hilarious, our class discussions are always incredible. He guides us, as a class, to answers for our own questions. His semester organization is also the best I've ever seen Now, this doesn't mean it's an EASY class. There's still reading to do and a paper or two to write, but it's worth it

Prof Hickman is a great teacher. His lectures are great and he makes time for students outside of class. He genuinely cares about whether his students are doing well and learning. Students are also very involved in the lectures. I would definitely recommend him to anyone.

He is an amazing teacher who is hilarious, kind, genuinely interested in his students, and passionate about what he teaches. There is lots of reading because it is a literature class, but the discussions are fantastic, he will work with you on the two small papers you write, and tests are straight forward.

Honestly, he might be the best professor I've ever had.  He is incredibly funny, spiritually sensitive, and deeply passionate about the material.  The only reason I put that you should be prepared to read is because it's an English class for heaven's sake.  It's all worth it. Do it.

There is a lot of reading, but even when you don't like it initially, Dr. Hickman can make you like it in the lecture. He's a funny, interesting and intelligent professor. He has in class quizzes that are easy (half the time, if you showed up he gives you the points anyway). Do the reading and show up to class, and you'll have it made.

Be on time. Come to class. You have to read a lot, so if you aren't willing to do so, I wouldn't take this class. The professor is HILARIOUS, and I LOVED what we learned! I really recommend this class. Tests are easy, and they TA's fairly lenient on grading.

Hickman really gets college students. He doesn't give worthless homework, but helps you not procrastinate. The books we read in American lit 1960-present were really great and inspiring which is hard for post-modern. Because of him, my papers were my best work. good balance between lecture and discussion. you won't regret it.
Professor Hickman is hilarious and you can tell that he loves the subject. He's a fair grader and actually listens to recommendations from students. I would definitely recommend this professor.

I was taking Stephen Walker for Brit Lit while I was taking Prof. Hickman for American. This guy beats the pants off of Walker, who is quite the professorial celebrity. Hickman is hilarious and kind. He really had me rolling sometimes. Seriously. Great lecturer. Do the reading, show up and pay attention, get an A. He's one of the best.

Professor Hickman is seriously, seriously awesome. His lectures are always engaging, his assignments are always explained clearly, and he's just a great guy. I'd take a million classes from him if I could.

He is a fantastic teacher! He is truly interested in the students and how well they are doing in the class. He knew most of our names the second class period and he knew all of them by the second week. I never liked to participate in class discussions before, but he made me feel as if what I had to say added to it. I would reccommend him to anyone.

I'm a multiple Hickman taking student.  People aren't kidding when they say that he is one of the best.  He remembers what it was like to be a student and he tries to create his classes accordingly.  Very interesting and funny.  Very organized and fair.  Will do everything he can to ensure you succeed.

Best teacher I have ever had. VERY inspiring--makes you really want to learn and know the material, if not purely because he teaches it in such an interesting way. VERY funny and kind, and a very fair grader. I would take every English class from him if I could!

I took 293 and the Post Modern class from him. One of my fav teachers. He is very helpful and interested in his students. There are random "Rushwrites" so you need to go to class-- but you'll want to! Really fun lectures and he gives a great study guide for the tests. Take him if you are lucky enough to get into his class!! (esp. Post Modern!)
Awesome Awesome!
If you need this class, take Hickman! He's a lot of fun, has a sense of humor, and the grading is fair and accurate. I really enjoyed my time in his class and looked forward to it.

Trent was way cool. After having classes from arrogant/overworked/boring english teachers, he was a youthful breath of fresh air. He's not annoyingly conservative, so discussions could go more in depth. He is super fair and easy to talk to. He knew my name even though i had only talked to him once in a class of 90 people!
Awesome teacher: fair, interesting, has a sense of humor. If you keep up with the reading schedule, you'll do fine. Tests are accurate assesments of what you know.

I had Dr. Hickman for American lit and Latin American lit, and I loved both classes, and I looked forward to class every day.  You do need to make sure and go to class, but it is very worthwhile.  He is funny, and he sincerely cares about the students.  I highly recommend taking any class from him.

Awesome teacher. I now love American literature, before this class I didn't. His lectures are great and he is clear about what you need to do to get a good grade, which isn't that hard. Very helpful and VERY funny. I would definitely take his class again.

Definitely one of the best English professors at BYU.  Very clear about his expections, helpful, funny, intelligent, organized, etc.  He responds to your emails very quickly and is easy to work with.  I would go out of my way to take a class from him again.
Fun professor. Class is fun, and the assigned readings are interesting. Go to class, do the reading, and write the papers- you'll be fine.

Prof. Hickman really cares about his students -- at the beginning of the semester he scheduled appts. with EVERYONE (80+ students) to meet so he could get to know us. Personable, likable, funny, and so knowledgeable. He is very passionate about what he teaches. If you are considering him for a class, TAKE IT! You won't regret it.
Prof. Hickman was a professor who not only genuinely cared about both his students and the subject, but made the lectures fun and interesting.  If it is at all possible, take a class from him.

Great teacher!! His classes are very fun. He knows a lot about his subject and he makes it really interesting. His tests are very reasonable, he is always willing to help you and give feedback on your papers.
really knowledgeable and helpful, but also made class fun.  tests are reasonable.  definitely take him!!

I had an online class from him and he left very helpful comments on my work- I could tell he had really paid attention to what I had done. This class is interesting, I liked it so much I finished it in 2 weeks! Would recommend Hickman!
Smart, personable, open-minded, engaging and all-around great teacher. You can't go wrong here.
Take a class from Trent.  You won't regret it.  Legitimate humor and good insight.  Well prepared.

Excellent teacher. Informative, organized, entertaining. Open about his expectations. Takes subject seriously but still fun(ny). (Won't let you off easy.) Willing to meet w/ students about anything. Great style. You'll love his class(if you can get in).

Hickman is the only Professor in the English major I have ever had who actually cares about the students ideas.   He cares a lot, and is always open to help.  He is so funny and he choses great stuff to read!
One of the best teachers I've had. Class-really interesting. Teacher-SO nice, always open and available, really helpful, truly cares about his students. Makes American Lit History really interesting.

I loved, loved, loved this class. Professor Hickman is a wonderful lecturer--very interesting, funny, good discussion. The tests are very fair. The papers are graded toughly, but he'll help you improve them if you ask.
He's a great teacher. Very helpful with a great style! You'll love him

You get out what you put in for this class. Plan on reading about 10 pages a day. About 2-3 hours of homework a week. Thoughtful and deep discussions in class. What impresses me about Dr. L is his willingness to adapt his course, assignments, and class discussions to further engage his students. He's constantly refining and takes feedback seriously

He is a very kind teacher and does care deeply about literature. I took 201 from him! The projects are heavy and the readings are really long. I would spend an hour everyday just to read everything assigned so make time for that. Way better than exams and we did get to do groups which I loved, this helped to make friends in class.
Hard tests, but really good study guides. So much reading. He is super nice though, and cares a lot about helping students.
Dr. Leinenbach was good. He really dives deep into the readings and makes you think. I wouldn't take again but everyone in my class liked him.

He tries to make things interesting and is available if you need help. But he talks in circles. Whenever I asked a question I never got a real answer. I don't like poetry anymore. We would talk about intense topics without a clear warning. Multiple times I wanted to leave class. To each their own.

Leinenbach understands how to direct a lecture/conversation to engage with students and what they want to discuss. He wants you to succeed and likes to think about education in non-traditional ways. Generally super positive experience.

He is a very inspirational teacher and helped me understand english. That is saying a lot for someone who hates English. There was no papers or tests but lots of readings. He helped me learn how I read and study best. So glad he is continuing to teach at BYU! Everyone should take his class.

Prof Leinenbach's discussion topics are obscure and lack connection to the assigned text. He clearly loves literature, but it feels like he read the assigned texts ages ago and designed the class content around his memory. He was also very set on his own topics and if a student tried to offer other, more compelling, topics he stayed set on his own.

I could not recommend this class with Professor Leinenbach more! It is a heavy reading class but with the structure of his class he tries to make readings more enjoyable and interactive! Class discussions were interesting and very interactive. Other than readings there isn't much outside of class work, but definitely put the effort in, its worth it

I loved ENGL 202 with Dr. Leinenbach! He really cares about his class material and his students, like he is a total sweetheart. Attendance is mandatory and the readings are super manageable. He also had no midterm/final exam which was really really nice. Overall I loved this class with Dr. Leinenbach! He is so awesome!

Had Prof L for British Lit. Lots of reading (duh), discussion posts were manageable, creative project & final paper weren't as bad as he made them seem. More lenient on grading than I expected. Discussions were mind opening and very engaging, it's obvious that Prof L knows his stuff. As a non-lit major, loved this class way more than I expected to.

Couldn't think of a better way to run a British Lit. class. Homework was mostly reading (it is heavy and fast...read 6 books in one semester). Class is just a group discussion, ungraded but you get what you put in. Plenty of time to do papers and he holds consultation sessions for them. Creative project was the best! Take this if you love reading

Dr. Leinenbach helped me grow into such a great writer throughout this semester. He starts his first class pretty intimidating to try to scare you, but the class isn't too hard if you show effort in your work! He is funny and really gets to know the students. Overall, I would absolutely take this class again or take another writing class from him.

Dr. L is a genius. You will learn SO MUCH in this class. I took ENGL 303 from him and he completely changed the way I percieved William Blake and literary criticism. That being said, this class will take up a huge amount of your time, perhaps more than really makes sense. Plan with caution. Only take if you have the time and emotional fortitude.
Honestly cannot say enough good things about this guy. Such a stud. Love him.

For ENGL 236. He gives excellent feedback and his lectures are funny, engaging, and educational. There is quite a bit of reading and sometimes the grading can feel a bit harsh. The class was fascinating and I really enjoyed it. He builds a great environment for his students.

I actually took Professor L's ENGL 236 class, British Literature, and it was amazing! He's so nice and caring for all of his students. He is passionate and energetic about what he teaches. There's a lot of reading, but that shouldn't surprise anyone considering it's an English class. Grading is clear and the material is great! Take Professor L!

I actually took Dr. Leinenbach for my Brit Lit 2 course. And he was amazing. I had to get used to the fast paced nature of the course, but that came with the nature of a summer semester. Dr. Leinenbach is kind, involved, and a genius. He helped me considerably outside of class and always explained what I thought unexplainable. Highly recommend!

He is a bit quirky but uses that to his advantage while he teaches. He is very open and accepting of each student and their opinions. The workload is a bit stretching, but nothing over the top for a college writing class. The feedback he provides is extremely helpful and he does a great job at keeping the majority of the lectures very engaging.
If you actually want to learn and become a better writer, take his class! he's incredible, and honestly became like a friend by the end of the semester!

He was really nice in person. His assignment descriptions were pretty confusing and he didn't have a clear grading rubric though. Overall I think I would take his class again, but I'd make sure to use his office hours more.

Dr Leinenbach was a fantastic teacher. He graded clearly and fairly, he made time for the students, and it felt like he truly valued each student. He also made class interesting with random activities and fun content. 10/10 recommend
He is FANTASTIC! I loved his class so much. It was hard, but he cares about you and is rooting and helping you to do the best you can. Go to his office hours and class, he's amazing.

Dr. Leinenbach is a great professor. His love of writing and rhetoric is clear through his excitement to teach the class. Lectures are well organized with opportunities for students interaction. A heavy workload class, somewhat of a tough grader however rubrics are assignment expectations are always clear.

He is a good professor and really cares about what he is teaching. I would recommend him as a writing 150 teacher, he is not the easiest but your going to learn and it is not going to be too stressful.

Trent is great. If you put the simple effort in to do the consultations and go to the writing center at least once you can easily pass this class with a great grade. I have always felt like a terrible writer and Trent turned that around. Would take from him again.

Trent's awesome! He's very passionate about what he does and fills his lectures with emotion. I've never liked writing very much but I enjoyed his class a lot. He cares about his students and is always willing to help you. He had a few pop quizzes, but they were simple and he usually warned us about them. I highly recommend him!

I don't personally enjoy writing, but the class discussions were pretty interesting and Trent is a very caring teacher. He is very understanding if you need to turn in a paper a day or two late as long as you let him know ahead of time. You have to read in order to do well on class quizzes. Trent doesn't kill your grade with essay scores.

I personally think Trenton is a great professor. He really cares about his students. As for homework, you'll read out of the book and write a lot, which is pretty  much ideal in learning how to write.  He's willing to meet with you to work on your writing and to help you out. He's a younger professor so he's a bit more approachable than others!

Love this class! Only take it if you are an organized person and enjoy writing already. Trent doesn't teach you to like writing--he just makes you a better writer and he is a brilliant lecturer and fantastic teacher, and he really does care about your success. The class is hard and you have to really try, but if you're motivated you'll be just fine

Even though I didn't really enjoy this class, Trent was a very good professor. He was always willing to help students with their writing. Although sometimes not very clear, as long as you asked questions, you'd be fine. I didn't like writing all the papers for this class, but I enjoyed the class discussions that we had. Take this class from Trent.

I was scared for this class, but Dr. Merkley made it very doable! There's a lot of material to cover, but her tests aren't tricky so long as you study and attend the review sessions. She's good at explaining lecture material, but definitely read the textbook before class. Final exam and paper were worth a lot, but not too hard. Take it from her!

I took this class during the summer semester so it was a beast! PSYCH 381 is commonly known as the hardest course in the major Dr. Merkley did a group job making it easier. Tests are 90-100 multiple choice with short answers and two essay questions. It seems daunting but the tests aren't crazy hard. Take it from her if you want a good grade.

I loved Professor Harding! She cares about the course material and wants to spread that passion. There were three major papers, but we worked on them a ton in class (peer reviews, writing conferences, etc.) which made them pretty easy and doable. There's a lot of reading, and it's all required (you have to annotate) but I loved this class and her!

Troy is a nice guy and communicates well. That said the lectures are somewhat useless as he lets the students distract him but he still grades really hard on attendance. In our class at least, he got really far behind the first half of the semester and then crammed us the second half to try to catch up. Still he clearly cares about the students.

o.m. gosh!  Troy is the most INCREDIBLE professor ever! Seriously, don't even question it, just take his class! And oh my, he is like, the CUTEST guy I've ever met! I kept dropping hints hoping he'd take me on a date, but he said that wasn't appropriate. After I met him, I went to look at rings! He's AMAZING! I could stare into his eyes ALL day!

Troy was an AWESOME teacher. If people really aren't getting something, he'll stop and help the class out. He's really chill and relaxed, makes you feel comfortable. Tells funny stories, but always gets through the lesson too. Honestly didn't learn that much, but got a good foundation. Show up for the weekly quizzes and you'll be golden. Take Troy!

I loved Troy! He was really fun and chill. He used fun games to learn vocab and concepts, and was always willing to give help. He told fun mission stories and cool cultural stuff. His class is easier than other 101 classes because he writes his own tests, which really aren't bad and he grades super easily. Feel free to make fun of him. :)
Extremely fun class. He's really laid back and will help you with everything. If languages come easy to you this class is a breeze, otherwise some studying is needed.

Troy was an easy teacher in the classroom but i found his quizzes were difficult.  I guess he leads you into false security, so make sure you study before the quizzes, even if you think they will be easy. Good class overall, i'm glad i took it.
Troy is a great professor. Oral Exams are quick and easy. Hes a cutie and I am going to take the class again just because it was so fun.
Great class, a lot of fun.  I wish we could've spent more time speaking together, but, all in all a great experience.

troy is the most sensitive, sexy, amazing teacher ever to live. I would recommend people of all walks of life to take one class from this godsend. I AM telling you YOU WILL NOT regret it! to bask in the glory of his knowledge is a privilege i will never forget!
He was a great teacher, really nice, really easy. We had fun in class this semester! Take italian from troy!

Troy is fabulous - it is an extremely easy class if you consistently study on your own. He shares hilarious stories from his mission in Italy. The oral exams aren't intimidating; instead of being one on one in his office, you go on a short walk around campus or just talk with a group in class. Also, he's very cute.

class was so much fun he taught us so much. made me so excited about italian! has such a passion for the language, culture, country, and passed it on to students. really cares about students too always went out of his way to help. wants everyone to succeed and learn. oh and he's cute too! if you want to learn italian, take it from prof gulbrandsen!

Very well organized and clear about expectations. As a numbers person, this class was easy. Be prepared to really use the book and take notes. If you learn the material in the book and go to class, there it's not tricky to do well.

This is a reverse classroom course, so it doesn't matter who you take it from; you'll watch the same videos and take the same quizzes as every other section. Master Lewis gave great lectures when we worked through the in-class worksheet, and he decreased the grade cutoffs by 0.5%! This saved me, as I was just 1 question short of 94% on the final.
Troy lewis is the goat! I took him two years ago and I loved his class. One of my favorite professors at BYU.
This class is hard but Master Lewis does a great job teaching it. The vast majority of your grade is exams. Thank goodness for the curve.

Professor Lewis is a fantastic teacher and excellent role model. While the tests were difficult, his lectures prepared me very well for them. He breaks down the subject to be easily understandable and is always willing to help.

Professor Lewis is amazing. I have been so impressed by him in every way - his standards are high and clear, his lectures are engaging and comprehensive, and he is genuine and understanding toward his students. I admire this man. He needs a raise!
The class is hard but he is easily the best professor I have had at BYU. Not even close.

I would argue that Professor Lewis sacrifices more compensation than any other professor to teach at BYU. He knows more than anyone out there about tax and yet he spends his days teaching students at BYU because he genuinely cares about his students. him. I left this class with more enthusiasm for tax than I ever thought possible.

Professor Lewis is probably one of the smartest people you will ever meet. He knows everything about taxes and explains things incredibly well. The Junior Core is hard and this class is very difficult, but professor Lewis makes this class possible.

Professor Lewis is my favorite professor I've had at BYU. He is so kind and caring--he gives all his students his cell phone number and you can call him anytime. He is also HILARIOUS. He doesn't have a PhD so he tells students to call him Master Lewis. Not only does he know everything about taxes, but he's human Google with all information.

My only qualm with Professor Lewis is that he uses a LOT of industry slang for an introduction to tax class. Sometimes he is really hard to follow, but he makes up for it with how much he cares for his students and how accessible he is to review things. This class is not easy, but he is an enjoyable professor.

Prof Lewis is an incredible professor. He was very accommodating during a crazy COVID semester. He cares for his students and is always willing to help outside of class. The material is technical, but Prof Lewis breaks it down in a way that students understand. He is by far the best tax professor at BYU. Take as many classes from him as you can!

Professor Lewis is by far my favorite professor at BYU. He is VERY knowledgeable about tax and he really cares for his students. He always makes time to be available. I once had a question the day he was flying out for a conference. Instead of directing me to a TA, he called me while traveling and spent an hour answering my question. He's awesome!

He just talks at you and expects you to absorb everything. But he talks incredibly fast, uses tons of incomprehensible (albeit cool) industry slang, and doesn't use any slides, and in the rare cases he draws something on the board, it's also incomprehensible. So it's impossible to take accurate notes. And he's exactly the same if he's one-on-one.

Professor Lewis is one of the best teachers I've ever had. Tax is super hard for me, but he does a great job of explaining hard topics and is always available to meet with you one-on-one if you're still struggling. If tax isn't your thing, the class is still going to be very hard, but Prof. Lewis is probably the best ally you can have to learn tax.

Professor Lewis is a professor that is really invested in his students' future. His lectures are always fun, he knows how to teach to your understanding, and he make complex things seem simple. Sure this class is hard. Learning tax is hard no matter which teacher you have. Professor Lewis makes it bearable.

Hands down, best tax teacher at BYU. Take as many classes from him as you can. Professor Lewis gets how students think and speaks our language. The material in this class is pretty complicated, but he's funny and expert at the same time. He does anything he can for his students, too. Absolutely the best.

He is a great lecturer, very enthusiastic and fun. The course is prepared by another professor which the whole school uses, tests as well. If you don't watch Norm online, it is a hard pass. Lewis cares about the students and wants them to pass.

Prof Lewis truly was a great teacher. He was always easy to follow in lectures, his grading was always very clear and consistent. Not a very easy class, but decent effort can earn you an A. Keep up with the work though, as it may accumulate very fast. He makes good occasional jokes. I recommend him to any student,and I would take it again from him

Professor Lewis is one of the most amazing professors on campus. Not only is he extremely helpful, his lectures are always the perfect blend of entertaining and informative. Although his resume is intimidating, he is extremely approachable, and is a master of breaking down the most difficult tax concepts.

Dr. Munro is very caring and teaches very well. This was a hard class and he taught us fairly clearly. The tests were hard and the homework was long and challenging. He really knows what he's talking about and is really fun in class. He really knows and cares about all his students. You have to spend a lot of time in the textbook.
Great professor, knows the material very well.

Really nice guy but not the best teacher. Lectures are super disorganized and hard to follow, and it was hard to keep track of random assignments that didn't really contribute to my learning. Labs were great. Most of my learning was done in the two days before each midterm by looking through the review material.

Doctor Munro is a great guy! He is funny and is always saying movie quotes. But as teacher, he is not great. He is scatter brained and tries to enhance learning with "helpful methods" and pointless learning objectives. Class had too many pointless assignments and projects were confusing. Labs were great. Luckily the TA's carried the class.

Dr. Munro knows his material very, very well. He understands that what he's teaching is difficult, and does his best to anticipate misunderstandings, but you *have* to ask questions if you want to know what you're doing. That isn't his fault: materials science is just a hard class. He's also one of the most kind and caring professors I've ever met.

Pretty difficult class, but Dr. Munro is one of the best professors I've had at BYU. He explains things really well and is very organized with course material. He also makes sure to take some time in every lecture to stop and tell a funny/inspirational story to break up some of the lecture, which I really appreciated.

Dr. Munro is alright, but his lectures are terrible. They're dry at best and he does a horrific job of teaching new material, the textbook is the only way to learn. Luckily the work load is pretty light, but tests are a doozy. Daily in-class Iclicker quizzes, EZ hw every week, 4 simple labs, and group project. Take some1 else if u have a good one.
Fantastic teacher. Highly recommend.

He is one of the best professors on campus. He is knowledgeable, kind, and reasonable. What more could you ask for from an ME professor and yet it is rare to find. I would recommend taking any class you can from him.

Dr. Munro does a solid job teaching a broad class. The homework was very reasonable and fair. The in-class lectures were dry but thats material science for you. Tests were hard but there was a curve at the end of the semester. He is a very nice guy does his best. I do think the TAs grade way too harsh though...

This class was solidly alright. Tests weren't super well-written (i.e. questions were unclear and had to be rescinded after the test). Labs were cool. Lecture wasn't very helpful, but there were iClicker quizzes, so you have to go if you don't want to drop your grade several points. Some extra credit given.

This guy expects you to know everything right off the bat. I felt like he was doing a review for the final in his very first lecture of the term. His class structure is unclear and he gives tons of homework. Other than that... nice guy.

Dr. Munro is great! Make sure to do the reading and ask questions if you don't understand something as it can be easy to get confused and fall behind. Overall this class isn't as bad as some other engineering courses.

Took him in the summer and I would not recommend. He went way fast over the material and expected us to know everything. He did offer extra credit and got better as the semester went on but he wasn't much help at all when it came to studying for the tests. He also gave us a ton of homework 3 assignments a night and a lab report/journal once a week.

Don't get me wrong he's a nice guy but the class was just NOT IT. He would change the required readings without warning, boring lectures, obscure test questions, SO MANY READINGS. I spent more time reading for his class than my reading-heavy history class. Oh and half the time I swear we didn't talk about anything related the eternal family.

Professor Mansfield is one of my all time favorite professors here at BYU, and his class one of the most influential I've ever taken. He is the most kind, thoughtful, and loving teacher I have ever had. Every time I walked out of his classroom my spirits were lifted and my heart was full. My life is better because of Ty Mansfield. Take his class!!!

Probably the most influential class I've taken at BYU. Prof mansfield is very passionate about the subject and is excellent at teaching in a way that is applicable to your life. The course structure is simple: do the readings, go to class, 4 tests throughout the term which are really easy if you do the readings and study the slides. Amazing man.
easy to get a good grade in, a little boring. a class to take if you just want the credit and nothing else out of it. sweetheart guy for sure
Lots of vague ramblings. Never gets to his point and plays A LOT of "guess what I'm thinking". Doesn't really teach, kinda just talks.

Brother Mansfield is the most confusing religion professor I have ever had. I might just be dense, but I always left his lectures more confused than when I walked in. It seemed like he never got to the point in the lecture; he just talked about broad, fluffy concepts. He gives way too much reading homework and gives little notice before due dates.

Mansfield is probably the worst professor I've had at BYU. His class is full of constant busy work that makes it impossible to learn, and he regularly mixes in his own opinions with actual doctrine, so you can't ever be sure that he's saying something that actually reflects church views. Do not take from him.

Professor Mansfield teaches this class so that it is directly applicable and helpful in life. He teaches basic principles and tackles questions and the culture relating to family. There were two big(ish) projects, but they didn't feel like busywork because they helped me see how what he taught worked outside the classroom.

Classes are great, and he's the best lecturer I've had. This is offset a little by a poor out of classroom experience. The study guides were usually published late, and there was a lot of reading. More than other similar religion classes I've taken. He is a very lenient grader though, so as long as you put in the time, you can get a good grade.

I took this spring term, and there was a ton of reading (up to 8 conferences talks/ articles before each class)
The content was very interesting and pertinent to understanding the divine role of relationships in the Plan of Salvation
His background as a marriage and family therapist makes his lectures very interesting
But it can be a lot to take in

This is by no means and "easy A" class. You will read A LOT, there are four exams, and two papers. However, this was the only religion class in my ENTIRE undergraduate degree where I felt like I actually LEARNED! Dr. Mansfield is a good teacher, and he CARES, but he won't let you slack off. If you're ready to actually LEARN take the class.

Brother Mansfield was a great teacher for eternal family, my only complaint is that there were sooo many readings and the course load felt a bit more than a 2 credit class. 4 exams, not comprehensive, 2 big essays. Overall he was an easy grader on the essays. He did have a lot of interesting insights and personal stories in his lectures!

While I consider this class life-changing, sometimes I felt the organization stifled the learning. As example, study guides include hundreds of possible questions from readings but only ~10 will be on exam. It's definitely possible to get a good grade, but I'd like less mass memorization and more intentional learning. Bro Mansfield is great tho.

Professor Mansfield is so unorganized and is constantly changing the timelines on things. Lectures are required but pointless, except for the 5 seconds that he says something that he wants you to have 100% memorized. When I asked him for help on something he said no. Feels like he cares more about flexing his knowledge than teaching gospel truths.

I learned so much from this class! It completely changed my perspective on marriage, love, chastity, and relationships. He draws on psychology and his experience as a therapist, but teaches the doctrine clearly and bears testimony. Though the 2 papers are a lot of work, I enjoyed them and learned so much. I thought the 4 exams were pretty easy.

He is smart and has interesting points but makes the class way too much work for a 2 credit religion class. Four tests, two essays, three interviews to conduct, and two books to read on top of weekly journal responses and massive amounts of reading for every class. He approaches the class from a very scientific approach stifling spirituality.

Professor Mansfield's class changed my life and perspective. His lectures are incredibly thoughtful and based on doctrine and research. Tests and papers aren't too bad because he gives you clear rubrics and study guides with all the questions you could expect to see. He really cares about his students and answers questions very thoughtfully.

As a preface, I rate all my professors. 
I would 100% recommend this class, it was inspiring and helpful in helping me look at and improve my life. The sensitive topics were handled straight on without hesitance which was refreshing. The exams were a bit tricky though, they came straight from the study guide. The projects: easy A + learned lots.

Really interesting lectures from the perspective of a therapist. Fair warning, there are lots of things to read before each class, which will come up in the quizzes, but sadly didn't get brought up in the lectures themselves. So I was left not really knowing where the readings fit into the context of the class. But they will be on the exams!

Professor Mansfield was great, he had interesting things to say and I learned a lot from him, especially about relationships with people It was hard to see where he was going with topics and he kinda goes on tangents. There were a LOT of readings but lots of extra credit opportunities. So lots of pros and cons, overall it was a good class though!

I loved Professor Mansfield, he made the lectures very interesting and was very caring. His stories were very cool as well. I was not a fan of his organization and I felt that his tests didn't really test for what we were learning, it tested more memorization but they were not terrible.

Professor Mansfield has been one of my all-time favorite professors. I was inspired by his lectures each time I came to class. He knows so much about human relationships and development it blows me away. There are extra credit opportunities and only one project that I had a fun time doing. He tries to not make his class super difficult.

Dr. Mansfield is very knowledgeable about his subject and speaks about it so eloquently. The readings and lectures changed my outlook on life! There are quite a lot of readings and attendance is graded. He also provided ample extra credit opportunities that proved to be very meaningful.

His lectures are so good and I loved them, and felt like I learned a lot. However, there are a ton of readings & the midterm & final are pretty much 100% based on them. I honestly didn't do all of them b/c we don't cover them in class, but I paid the price when I had to fill out the study guides. Exams were very close to the study guides though.

I took Eternal Families from Professor Mansfield, and on the whole it was great. He has a cool perspective that comes from both his therapy background and the gospel. Very chill workload, but the midterm and final are both pretty subjective and have monstrous study guides. Class is him lecturing, but he does a good job of answering questions.

It wasn't the easiest class ever but I loved that he made us think about how all of this really applied to us personally and tried really hard to apply the material to our personal lives.
Great Professor. I loved this class. His tests were open scriptures and he focused specifically on content in the scriptures. I thought the class was fairly easy. I would definitely recommend.

This class had a lot of good material to learn about but was WAY too much work for a 2 credit class. TONS of reading every week, 2 papers that required interviews and reading 2 books, and tests that required a ton of studying, way more than my engineering classes. I wouldn't recommend if you are looking for an easy, two credit religion course.

I absolutely loved this class! You have to write 1 page reflections everyday after class but it is all your own thoughts and testimony. There is a bunch of readings assigned before every class, but it is all fun readings. There are two short papers throughout the semester and two open  book, 10 question tests. Lectures are extremely interesting!!!
Brother Mansfield is incredible. His class is very good and he teaches very interesting things. It's EXTREMELY easy to get an A in this class!!!!!!

Professor Mansfield is an incredible teacher. Lectures were engaging, and I always felt like I was learning something important. Exams weren't too hard, but they took forever (5 hours)--a series of free response questions.

He is a great teacher. It was very phyllisophical and idea based rather than practical abotu marriage. You do a reading "journal" each week, telling him what you learned. LOTS and LOTS of reading of articles online!! Be prepared. You ahave 2 projects (Book report and fun couple questionnaire) The test - 10 essays open book

Bro. Mansfield is honestly the most down to earth professor.  While there was some reading for the class, it was interesting and easy reads (mostly talks from general authorities).  Lectures were insightful, personal, funny, and some of the best real-conversation I've ever experienced in a classroom setting.  Very clear and doable grading system!

Brother Mansfield is a good teacher. He spent a little more time taking about personal relevance and feelings than I would have liked, but that's not bad for everyone. I would have liked more textual analysis and context, but he knew his stuff. Personally I wouldn't recommend, but it was a good class.

Finally, a breath of fresh air in the BYU religion department. This guy is sensible, realistic, down to earth, and understanding. Such a welcome relief after all the male religion professors that act like it's still 1960. Hopefully this he is at the forefront of future leadership in the church. He knows what's going on in the world and understands.

While Marriage and Family is his forte, I would still highly recommend taking Doctrine and Covenants from Brother Mansfield. He is not afraid of finding real, doctrinal truths, even if it shatters some of his student's traditional beliefs. Awesome class.

Professor Mansfield was very insightful. I felt very uplifted  after every class, and always looked forward to hear the next lecture. This class broadened my understanding not only of gospel doctrine of marriage and family, but of how to improve my relationship with my Heavenly Father, family, and friends. My favorite BYU class so far!

This was BY FAR the best religion class, possibly the best class of any kind I've taken at BYU. It was uplifting, inspiring, empowering, funny, and fascinating. I really felt that it prepared me for my future.

Brother Mansfield is a very intelligent, spiritual and well-spoken man. I really enjoyed this class, and learned a lot about life. It was more than just a marriage prep class. He really expanded my understanding of God and how I relate with Him and my brothers and sisters on this Earth. He's a great choice to take this class from.

Super nice professor, very knowledgeable and keeps lectures interesting. Its hard material, but his grading is fair and the workload isn't too bad at all. Just be sure to keep up with the material and ask questions early on. Solid class.

is lectures can be boring at times, but the slides contain most of the information you need for the exams. There is one midterm and one final, each with 25 multiple-choice questions. I highly recommend visiting him during office hours or scheduling a time to ask questions. He explains concepts very well in a one-on-one setting.

Professor Shumway is an outstanding professor who genuinely cares about his students. The class is challenging, but he's understanding, brilliant, and always willing to help. Highly recommend talking to him.

Professor Shumway is kind, genuine, and truly wants students to succeed. He knows options inside and out. Lectures could flow better with more worked examples, but if you stay engaged and review the slides with ChatGPT, you'll learn a lot and do well in the class.

Shumway is an awesome guy. Kinda corky but really does care about getting to know his students and being there to help. He is VERY accessible outside of class. Homework was pretty straightforward and he only has one assignment due every week so workload was easy. His exams are not too bad but the material itself is really hard.

Professor Shumway is a funny guy but doesn't teach in a clear way to understand. This was my last core finance class and I felt lost the whole time. Would recommend taking this course from someone else.

Derivatives is simpler than you think if you remember basic finance (buy low sell high, DCF, etc.).
The hard thing for me was Prof Shumway's difficulty at breaking down tough subjects. He teaches like everyone knows what he's studied for 25+ years. If you can, take 411 in the Fall w/ Prof Mitton instead if you want to have a smoother experience.

Professor Shumway is awesome! Financial Derivatives is a fun class. The course was based around simulations and homework assignments. I believe the class was set up perfectly. One midterm and a Final. Homework assignments are helpful and not too much. The perfect amount of coursework. Definitely go to his class. Great guy!

Professor Gardner is one of my favorite teachers I've ever had at BYU. Super motivational, really cool guy. Cares about you and wants you to succeed. Really interesting assignments, not a boring writing class at all. Highly recommend!
Do yourself a favor and take this class. The teacher is very good and cares. No busy work.

Professor Gardner was kind and you could tell he loved literature. I was a little frustrated by the grading on the four short essays we did throughout the semester (especially the first one). Luckily, they aren't worth too much and the midterm balances it out. There were also mini quizzes once a week on the reading so make sure you do the reading!

This class was amazing and I found all of the lectures so interesting. There's a decent amount of reading but no other homework except a short essay every few weeks, plus the midterm isn't difficult and the final is open note. Even when the reading seems boring, Prof Gardner made it feel really deep and discussions were great.

Professor Gardner was one of my favorite BYU professors so far. I have never liked writing classes my whole life, but he took a different approach that made this subject so much more enjoyable. Taking the Writing 311 class from him made it feel like I was writing my own stories and topics in the way I wanted to. He is an amazing professor!

Prof Gardner is a gem! He's chill and fun, but also keeps authority as a teacher. He gives honest feedback but says it in a way that motivates you. Honestly one of the best BYU professors. 10/10 would recommend.

Professor Griffin is the best, his class was very easy and self explanatory. He is very inspirational and keeps his assignments, midterm, and final are very easy, its open notes and scripture. Hands down best religion professor.
Lectures: 10/10, Workload: perfect, Exams: totally doable, Grading: super lenient, Jokes: never-ending.

I liked Brother Griffin's class, I learned a lot and would say that my testimony grew. I do feel like there was a lot of busy work but maybe that's just every religion class. Brother Griffin does love his dad jokes which I didn't love as much but some people do haha

This religion class changed my life! Would definitely recommend taking a class from Bro. Griffin. He knows so much historical context about the NT that really gives it a lot of depth. There are 2 tests that are pretty hard, but they are open-scripture + open-notes (as long as those notes are in your scriptures). Try to write down everything he says

I cannot say enough good things about Prof Griffin!! He is so passionate about the gospel and is hilarious with his dad jokes. There are a solid amount of assignments but super super doable and his classes are so fun! I looked forward to each class and can't wait to take another class by him!

Brother Griffin is the best religion professor I've had at BYU. He's so smart and such a skilled teacher, and you can tell that he really cares about his students. If you do the readings and pay attention in class, it's really easy to get an A.
This was my second class by Brother Griffin. He is extremely in tune with the spirit, and really cares about each of his students. He is an awesome teacher!

He is such a sweet guy and truly loves his students. I only wish he would have more confidence in his teaching. There were so many time he would say sorry for lecturing to us or sorry for this or for that, even though I feel the Spirit so much in his class. Constantly saying sorry defers from the Spirit a little bit.
Second-worst religion professor, I've had. I'm not sure I can get an A in this class.
One of, if not my favorite professor I've had
Great professor, cares about students and makes assignments and tests easy to learn from.

I loved brother Griffin!! He always taught by the spirit and I grew spiritually through taking his class. He is seriously genuine and a dedicated disciple. If you stay on top of the weekly assignments you'll be good. Better than a grade though, this class can change your life.
I didn't enjoy class, it wasn't a very safe place for someone reexamining their faith. Lots of the doctrine came across as sensational. I didn't go very often, but an A- was well worth not going.
I loved Brother Griffin! I learned so much from his lectures and his class helped me grow spiritually. He is so knowledgeable about the gospel and is very fun to listen to.

This class is good and you definitely learn a lot! Griffin is a super sweet guy and his lessons are engaging but I would say his tests are pretty specific. To do well on them you have to take really good notes, especially on the things he says because chances are you won't remember everything said in class. You have to do good on tests for an A.

Professor Griffin is very kind and gives amazing lectures. I enjoyed his teaching, and the course layout was excellent. My only complaint is that the grading was way too tough! I never in my life thought I'd get below an A in a religion class, but this class proved me wrong. You will be graded more harshly than you think, so beware.
Such an awesome teacher! Very caring and loving towards all his student. He is truly there for us. He is passionate about helping us learn and understand the scriptures.

Professor Griffin is such a great teacher! He cares about his students and teaches about things that really matter. There are weekly assignments, essays, and tests, but they aren't too hard. I learned a lot of important things in this class.

Brother Griffin is the best! He knows what he is talking about and I learned so much in his class. His lectures are entertaining and so spiritual. He is also hilarious and I love hearing his dad jokes everyday! One paper, a semester long project, and weekly attendance quizzes, but not too much work.

Professor Griffin is the best of the best! He truly cares about each one of his students and their success in growing their testimonies. He is a a gifted storyteller and pun enthusiast whose love for the Savior shines through all of his words and actions. Take from him if you want the best Univ 101 class the way it was designed to be.

Great religion professor! The class got better as it went along & most of your grade is self reported. It was nice to examine my own spirituality & set my own goals than have someone tell me what to do. Much of your grade is on the honor system. The tests are very specific to class, so make sure you pay attention & take good notes.

Honestly one of the best religion teachers at BYU. You must take a class from him once and I can promise you that you will learn lots of new things and grow your testimony. If you keep up with the assignments and do them, you will get an A

Great class! I learned a lot, not only interesting facts, but how to find out more using online resources. He is such a kind teachers and you can feel his testimony as he speaks. Attendance does matter and you are expected to read scriptures every day. There is also a semester long project you work on, but you pick what you do, so it isn't bad.

Brother Griffin is hands down the best religion professor I've taken from so far at BYU. He offered so much insight into the standard works and made them applicable to my life. His classes were Spirit-filled, and I was genuinely so sad to walk out of the last lecture. I would highly recommend his classes to anyone who is really willing to learn.

Brother Griffin is a great professor. His lectures are amazing and spirit-filled. The tests are pretty difficult, but if you pay attention in class and take good notes, you should be fine. Not a bad class to take. He is very smart and adds many scholarly insights into his lectures, if you are interested in that type of thing!
