I attended this class for no credit. Just out of curiosity since I took 112 (Coach Dorff) last semester. Even after passing with an A, I was lost with his class. He writes on the whiteboard and it's hard to understand what is going on. His practice tests are very old and im not sure how that is helpful. Even after the class, you teach yourself

For some reason he likes to be called Coach Jarvis, but he is an exceptional math teacher. I did poorly in his class partly because of some health issues, but Coach Jarvis was super helpful and willing to help me out to succeed. He really does care and want his students to succeed, and is willing to sit down with students to really help.

He is going to try and convince you to do ACME. There is a lot of homework for this class, but that's just how it is. He is a super respected professor and maybe isn't the best 112 professor, but there are a ton of resources to help. The lectures were never super helpful because he wanted to help everyone with their questions first.

Students should get a B if they listen to the class carefully but must put extra effort into getting an A.  The professor will provide study materials such as past exams for students to get ready for exams. The class is heavy homework, so be ready to take more than one hour each day to complete the homework assignments.

Coach Jarvis loves math and wants you to love it, too. He does a remarkable job at allowing for questions and participation, even in a huge class. He moves fast during lectures, and teaches with proofs, so if you don't learn that way, he might not be for you. I loved his class though, and would highly recommend!!!

I took this class because on RMP it said 100% would take again, but I wish I looked further into his reviews. If you need more structure to your lectures then his are very difficult to follow. He only utilizes the whiteboard and does not have any PowerPoint slides. I never missed class, but I got nothing out of the lectures. I had to teach myself.

Dr.Jarvis is hands down the best professor I've ever had! He really cares about his students and is passionate about what he teaches. He is able to explain things so simply and he always takes the time to make sure that everyone understands what is being taught. Would take another class from him in a heartbeat.

I took Professor Jarvis in Fall 1999 and still remember him as one of my most impressive & helpful teachers at BYU.  A huge group of us would crowd in his office for office hours every week and he'd help us understand the homework on the white board.  I don't remember that dynamic with any other professor. I'm trying to get my kids to take him now.

If you ever have the opportunity to take any class from him, you'd be a fool not to. Coach Jarvis is hands down the BEST professor I've ever had for any class I've taken at BYU. He explains content clearly and is so available to help his students. His Saturday office hours were such a help, and he provided lots of learning opportunities for us.

Dr. Jarvis is a great professor! He cares a lot about his students and always offers help. If I ever couldn't make it to class my TA would send me a recording of the class which was so nice. There were daily quizzes (easy points) but also daily hw assignments. My only complaint is that Dr. Jarvis sometimes struggles saying what's on his mind.

He is the nicest professor ever and even had office hours on Saturday morning to help out. He was honestly pretty scattered in his work in class and sometimes it was hard to follow, but recitation and the homework always cleared things up.

It's a hard class but Jarvis is Super smart, explains everything clearly, always willing to help individual students struggling in the class, loves what he does. Really good at motivating students to do math. Knows how to help students succeed. If you have the chance to take math 112 from Jarvis absolutely do it. Not sure how he isn't 5/5.

371's a beast but Dr. Jarvis makes it doable. Lectures are good, but he expects you to have already read the chapter, so he designs lectures to supplement the reading. I wish he'd focused on teaching material himself and let the textbook be the supplement. Great professor, though. Gives extra credit for catching his mistakes. Available out of class

Jarvis is a great teacher and communicator. He wants to help, so go to his office hours. His tests are very reasonable and fair. The class may first seem intimidating, but it's definitely doable, even if you got a B- in 290 (like me). He gives extra credit for pointing out errors during lecture.

The class was hard; I frequently felt completely lost on the homework. In spite of that, the tests were more doable than I expected. Lectures were always great. He really knows his stuff. He was always busy with writing the new ACME textbooks, etc., but when I could talk to him, it was always helpful, be it for homework or for advice for the future
He literally sounds like Jerry Seinfeld. Brilliant professor. Knows hows to answers questions well & explains things clearly. I'd recommend Dr. Jarvis for any class really.

Jarvis is a great teacher. He cares about his student, and probably the smartest person I have ever had teach me, but more importantly, he engages the students, and answers their questions. It also doesn't hurt that the ACME material is so interesting. 10/10. Would buy again.
Dr. Jarvis is a bro.  I mean, he teaches like a boss, loves what he does, is a great dad, and even let me take a selfie with him one time.

Jarvis is one of the best math professors I've had. ACME is HARD but his is teaching techniques help make difficult concepts understandable, so attend class. Expects us to know EVERYTHING for tests but they're pretty short. He's hard but fair and helps you learn at the most efficient and effective rate, if you'll follow his advice.

This man works hard and is insanely smart. He's the master of all trades in math. He's merciful with grades and he's a great mentor. The material is challenging. He is crystal clear if you come with the right questions. You are largely responsible for your learning in his class. So prepare well.

Tyler was a great teacher and was consistently at his office hours. It's important that you attend class as well as be sure to be ready to discuss the homework BEFORE class. He was diligent in answering questions and all around shows care and love for his students. If you take him make sure you are diligent and pay close attention.

Dr. Jarvis globally optimized our learning, happiness, and personal growth in this class. That's all you really need to know, since this is an optimization class. Also takes April Fools jokes like a champ.

Dr. Jarvis teaches math by day and protects the city of Gotham by night. Teaching this class was  superhuman since it was the first time he taught it, the textbook was still being revised, and the material was very challenging. Through all that, Jarvis still gave us tons of help in office hours and individual help. We all dressed up as him one day.

Dr. Jarvis  an upstanding gentleman. He is laser focused on everything in his life: teaching and mentoring students, dominating research, and coaching cross country at Timpview. I haven't met a professor I respect more than Dr. Jarvis. He is always ready to teach you more and give you outside opportunities to learn: ask away.

Dr. Jarvis  an upstanding gentleman. He is laser focused on everything in his life: teaching and mentoring students, dominating research, and coaching cross country at Timpview. I haven't met a professor I respect more than Dr. Jarvis.  He is a good man and a great teacher. ACME is hard, but more worthwhile than anything else you could be doing.

Dr. Jarvis is a great teacher.  I didn't go to office hours for the first half of the semester because I was shy but once I did he helped me a ton.  He doesn't just give you the answer but helps you along and answers questions and explains things you got wrong.  He is super willing to talk to students who have concerns or questions.
Dr. Jarvis is an awesome professor. His class isn't easy but he will make sure you understand the material. He is really enthusiastic during the lectures which is really helpful.
Prof Jarvis really cares about his students and is a really good teacher. His tests are fair and the homework helps you learn.
I am pretty sure that Dr. Jarvis is the best professor ever.
Dr. Jarvis is one of the best math teachers I have ever had. He sincerely cares about his students and is very willing to help you understand. Go to office hours! It is well worth your time.

Dr. Jarvis really cares about his students. I've never been as comfortable asking for help or advice about other classes to take. The class is hard but doable, and the material is useful important stuff to know. He explains things very well and is always willing to spend time outside of class to give help. One of the best teachers I've ever had!

I feel like Dr. Jarvis really cared about our learning and our class experience. He put in a lot of time to help us. That said, he was also very fair, and had no problems challenging us. I feel like I learned a lot, and I have really enjoyed his classes.
Dr. Jarvis is one of the best teachers I have ever had. He is very sincere when it comes to helping students learn. He expects the best of students and raises their vision.

Prof. Jarvis is way awesome. Math is challenging, but he really understands the learning process and will help you learn the math, and learn how to learn the math. An excellent teacher, but you must be prepared to work, and go to his office hours for help.

Dr. Jarvis cares more about his students and their understanding than any instructor I've ever met. He puts in the time (both in class and out) to ensure that anyone who wants to understand will get it. The material that he teaches is by no means easy, but I can't think of anyone better to do it. I recommend him over any professor I've ever had.
Prof. Jarvis is a math wizard

Professor Jarvis is a great professor who really cares about his students. His office hours are really helpful. The material is hard, but Professor Jarvis explains it really well. The material is interesting. I recommend taking this course. I recommend taking a course from Professor Jarvis

Best teacher I have had at BYU. Very enthusiastic about what he teaches. By the way he teaches concepts, I can tell that he has a lot of experience with the best ways to explain things for the first time. Helps students focus on HOW to solve problems, not just the answer. Any difficulty comes from the subject, not from Dr. Jarvis.

Awesome math professor. Genuinely interested in the success of all the students, or at least all the students who have any interest in the course. Really good at breaking down fundamentals of calculus so that just about anybody who paid attention could understand. You'll get out what you put in to the course.

Very honestly the best math professor I have ever had.  He was extremely concerned with whether or not we actually understood, and wouldn't move on until he was pretty sure that we did.  If I could, I would take every theory class from him, as he explains very well, and never gives up on his students.

Professor Jarvis was pretty good at teaching concepts to death. There's no way you can leave a lecture without getting a decent understanding of his lessons because he goes over things step by step. At times, it made me a little sleepy, but I think his elaborate explanations were appropriate.

Ok, he is all about reading the math book, so if your really into reading a math book then this class is for you. But if you want to actually learn calculous I'd take math from Dr. Purcell who is the best math teacher I've ever had. P.S. Purcell doesn't teach this next winter semester. But don't take calc from jarvis, unless you don't want to learn

Jarvis is extremely enthusiastic and explains Calculus in understandable terms, working problems several different ways. He is very patient and makes sure everyone understands what he is talking about. Brilliant and down to earth - I recommend him

Based on the reports so far I suppose I should mention that Dr. Jarvis has a teaching style; he introduces principles from a visual understanding, then he shows how to derive the formula from scratch, then he gives examples of how to do the homework. If you don't care enough about math to understand anything but how it works, take it elsewhere.

Dr. Jarvis knows his stuff but he does not know how to teach.  I felt that going to his lectures was a waste of time, and I taught myself mainly out of the textbook.  The only reason I did well in the class was because I took AP Calc in high school.  Avoid Jarvis at all costs.

He makes math fun.  He does a great job keeping the student attention and is very willing to help. He will do his best to work around you. He also does a great job explaining difficult principles. I didn't like math a ton before this class but I can really see the importance of it now.

Extremely smart guy and he tries to help his students understand. He puts a huge emphasis on office hours and will help if you're willing to make the effort. Not too helpful if you have medical emergencies during the year. Pretty good teacher, but he'd probably be more understandable in a smaller classroom setting.

Jarvis is really good at making Calculus easier to understand.  He explained WHY in a comprehensible manner instead of telling you to simply memorize. He makes lectures interesting, which is tough considering its Calculus.

Professor Jarvis is extremely smart and passionate about the subject. He makes even math interesting, and he explains things really well, even simple things that you might be embarrassed not to know, he explains those too. He's funny too, and extremely helpful. I really liked his class, and enjoyed the lectures far more than the labs.

After a few of his lectures you'll find out your time is better spent in the math lab instead of in his lectures.  This didn't bother me one bit though because I had calc in high school and I still knew a fair bit of stuff.  If she's still around make sure you go to Natalie Wilde's reviews for the test, that's what'll get you through the class.

Jarvis is awesome.  I would definitely recommend him.  His office hours are awesome, and he'll help and explain if you need help.  He asks if everyone understands, and helps you think, not just memorize, but helps you understand chemistry.

He is a great teacher.  And the days between with the TAs are awesome, and help explain everything.  The tests are harder they you would expect so you have to go to test preps but the class is really good.
Good, Nice, Funny, Nerd, Cool Prof. ^_^!
wonderful proffesor,makes clear understandings of the concepts,but solves very few problems in class

He is a very good professor, he often goes to fast but then backs up to re-explain concepts, and yes he loves proofs, although they may seem useless, they are fairly helpful in understanding why we do certain things in Math. I would recommend him, and his TA's are very qualified and helpful!

He's a terrible teacher that is too obsessed with proofs to get the main point across.  The whole mandatory class and recitation period was quite annoying when you aren't learning much, I highly recommend a different teacher for this course.

Prof. Jarvis is a great teacher.  He explains the concepts clearly and gives plenty of examples of the problems.  The class layout is a little different, with recitation periods every other day, but the TAs he has are good too.  The exams are challenging, but if you understand the proofs and ideas, it is alright.

Tyler was a very nice guy and I could tell he knew a lot, but I haven't really learned anything in this class. His TA's aren't that good, they will never give full points even if you get all questions right, because the answers are written responses. Especially Kepler Ridge, pray you don't have her as a TA. Easy class though

If you are going to take biology 100, take it from this man. He is amazing and I actually learned alot even though I only took this for a GE. Very great class and I enjoyed learning from his knowledge.

Dr. Kummer was extremely accommodating and helpful in both 1-on-1 settings and in lecture settings. I could not recommend him enough for BIO 100. He understands that most people are in the class for the GE, so he does not throw too much at you like other professors do. He is here for your success!
The class was very lecture heavy. If you did not understand something you would be left behind. Also the tests were super difficult

The only reason I'm giving this a 4 instead of a 5 is because it felt like the learning activities were very easy and half the time, attendance was almost totally unnecessary. Your average week would look like two classes, with a learning activity and quiz over class material, then a lab class at the end of the week, w/ its own quiz and activity.

This is a easy class! I would recommend for a GE credit. There are no readings (other than a short 100 page book throughout the semester). There are small quizzes each lecture but he gives multiple attempts and you can usually do it in 5 minutes. It is a very well organized course.
Great class! I recommend having a friend in that class to help with homework.
Good teacher to take this GE with. Attendance is only mandatory for recitation labs; however, all of the homework is covered in class and is also how you take notes. Pretty chill class if you study.
Very disorganized. Instructions are not clear.
This type of classes should be eliminated from BYU. No meaningful learning. Just a lot of meaningless homework, quizzes, and tests.

Professor Kummer was awesome, definitely one of the better BIO 100 classes if not the best. Be sure to take notes in class. Each class has an assignment to fill out during class and a quiz at the end. He really cares about you learning the material so the mastery checks can be retaken at the TA lab as many times as needed! Would recommend for sure

He cares about his students and he wants you to succeed. Multiple attempts on all assignments including mastery checks (more too if you go in and meet with TA's) with open note midterms and 2 attempts averaged. But the final is closed note one attempt. The TA's were taught the recitations and I often left more confused which was frustrating.

Professor Kummer was wonderful and I felt like he had the student's interest at heart. The class was intuitive and the homework wasn't hard. Professor Kummer was a bit slow at times, and things were explained multiple ways which could be a bit of a drag, but you will understand the material if you pay attention and the material isn't difficult.

Professor Kummer breaks down Biology into lots of easy to understand segments. He gives out follow along notes with lectures which are very helpful. The you get multiple tries on unit tests and the midterms are open note. However, beware that the final is one try, closed note.

Dr. Kummer's class was incredible this past semester. Expectations are clear, and the class is doable as long as you put in the effort. Lectures aren't mandatory, but attending them makes the assignments and quizzes easier. Dr. Kummer responds to emails regularly, and the TAs are very willing to help. You get out of this class what you put into it.
Solid teacher but you have over 100 assignments in one semester. Seemed like just busy work that I spent more time on than any other class.
He is very knowledgable and cares a lot about the students. The class is oriented towards the lectures as well as the TA recitations, so you should do your best to attend.
Great and easy class but sometimes material was taught rushed and confusing.

Dr. Kummer is so caring for his students. His class is totally set up for you to succeed. Use the TA labs to learn what you're doing for the Mastery Checks on each unit, and you'll do great on the exams. The only downside is that the lectures can be pretty boring.

I thought I kind of liked Biology before this course haha. Lectures were hard to understand and I ended up doing the actual learning during homework/quizzes. I just feel like it doesn't need to be this hard. You can tell he cares about his students though.

The class just got reorganized this semester.  It is everything you could dislike about a gen ed at byu.  The busy work is crazy.  you will have up to 4 assignments due on saturdays.  Expect lectures to just be the professor talking about random stuff.  no real learning occurs, and expect to be doing pointless busy work every single day.

This was a really easy class, but it was very unorganized. I learned nothing. He teaches like a high school teacher. You can redo most things as many times as you want which is how I got an A, but I never understood any of it. He just moved fast and seemed to never fully explain everything. I'm glad to have this GE done, but I wish I learned more.

Definitely the best professor for Bio100 (the TAs agree). He gives no homework and instead has small quizzes on what was taught in class. The quizzes all give multiple attempts. The midterm is open notes, open internet (no AI) and lets you correct mistakes for half points. The final allows a page of notes. He is friendly and lectures were engaging.

I think Professor Kummer did a great job teaching Bio 100! He is passionate about what he talks about and clearly knows, but I will admit it is difficult to follow lectures and taking notes is impossible with the way he structures the in class assignments. I understood the material in class, but I got to the tests and knew a lot less.

Dr. Kummer is a great professor; Bio 100 is a surprisingly tough class, take the mastery checks as many times as you want I encourage you not to just take them til you get 80%, go beyond that and strive for higher scores. The midterms were very forgiving, the same with the final curve.

Professor Kummer was super awesome, but the class is far from easy. Attendance isn't mandatory, but he goes through assignments in class, so to stay caught up, you should try to get to class. Exams and mastery checks are a huge part of the grade to get ready to study. Overall, he's a great professor, but BIO 100 is pretty tough.

Kummer's class was super fun and relatively easy, although it often felt like a bunch of memorization for the test. Assignments were engaging though, and the workload is pretty dang light, but still an engaging class! Definitely would recommend if you're just trying to get the GE.

This is a great professor for biology! If you go to class and pay attention you will be able to get all of the assignments done. There is very minimal homework as you do most of it in the class. He is super understanding and wants you to pass this class. Midterms and Final are online.

He does a good job with the content he has to teach. This was also nice because there was no lab and you just need to show up to class and pay attention, if you do that the out of class assignments are easy. This class sometimes made me want to throw my head though a wall, Professor K makes it as bearable as possible.

Professor Kummer is very knowledgeable but helpful. BIO 100 is a very very difficult course and I felt like he was a very fair teacher of it. Although it was a ton of work to do online, I'm glad I did since I was able to do labs virtually instead of having to go in everyday and every week to do them.

I took the online version and there was a lot of work. Online is set up so that you can see everything due for the entire semester. Tests are open note, which is way nice. Sometimes it felt pretty disorganized with the content of the assignments not matching up with the quizzes. Some of the videos are super grainy and impossible to decipher also.

I saw the reviews for BIO 100 online and decided it'd be an easy GE. It absolutely has not been. The structure of the course is incredibly confusing and essentially you will be teaching yourself. Tests are much harder than you'd think and the averages are pretty low. If you're trying to knock out your Bio GE, take it in person or from someone else!

For the Online Class: This class is run through learning suite and most of the homework is graded by completion. I found it very easy. It felt like more work could be spent on making the class better and more organized.

I'm sure he's a good professor but do not take the online course. I don't know if I was missing something but instructions weren't clear and I honestly ended up googling most of the information. He's decent at responding to questions/emails, but I am not a science person and took this for GE, would not recommend.

Professor Kummer is a good teacher but not a good professor. Briefly introduces topics in class, with frequent quizzes covering material. However, tests cover very little, with low averages and heavy curves. Only three tests and a final in the course.

Prof Kummer was so caring and always willing to help his students. You do your learning through learning activities that can sometimes be confusing since it is your first look at material but he does weekly reviews and his TA saved me. His tests are very fair and as long as you take time to do the work you will succeed! Not a high stress class

Most poorly organized class I've ever taken. Lessons were out of order &  help material wasn't labeled so you'd have to click on every video & PowerPoint (dozens) to see if they related to what you were learning. Learning activities were extremely juvenile, yet oddly difficult because  professor wanted to expose you to concepts w/ zero context.

I really love professor Kummer's online Bio class! The structure of it is focused on helping you learn and he even has multiple grading options so you can have the best chance of succeeding in the class! He provides a textbook to use for reference but most of the learning is done through great activities in learning suite and weekly reviews!

Professor Kummer focuses on the students learning how to think scientifically and understand broad concepts. He does not make students memorize lists of terms. He designs lessons really well to get you thinking. The class started out super easy and got a little bit more difficult over the semester, but was still quite easy by the end.

I wouldn't say I like this class' on-demand structure: weekly lectures cover only a small part of the contents, and there are no exact answers for learning activities. This class is not hard as a 100-level GE class, and he is a nice guy, but if you are a lecture learner, consider switching to another section.

I took this during a spring term. There were 5-6 assignments and 4-5 quizzes due every week. There were 4 exams. The first 3 exams are open note and you can take them twice. You can also take the quizzes twice. You take do the homework assignments 2-3 times. I appreciated how the professor set up the class to help each student do the best possible.

This class is very disorganized and seems to cover random biology concepts. There are no lectures and you have to teach yourself everything. Really heavy on evolutionary biology and we didn't even cover the fact that the mitochondria is the powerhouse of the cell. I would rather take Econ 110 than take this class again.

One of the most considerate professors ever! The textbook is free, you get 2 chances for all exams which are open book/internet (except for final), 93%A, quizzes are easy and done during class, and he's very accessible through email. But Learning Suite setup felt pretty disorganized and no study guides. Still recommend taking from Kummer though.

I took this class on-demand and I felt like the structure was set up well. HIs weekly zoom review sessions are a great way to make sure you've got the previous week's concepts solidified. He also is great about getting back to you through email if you have questions or concerns. Tests are open note, so take good notes and you'll do fine!
This class was mainly hard due to the online format. But he does explain concepts in review videos.

Professor Kummer is awesome. I took his class over zoom due to Coronavirus, and he made it good. The lectures were only 40 minutes on average, so I did not get too bored. You also go over the quizzes in class so as long as you show up you get 100 on all the quizzes. Just do the HW. You get 2 tries on each test, except for the final, which is good.
A great professor! Take BIO from him. Straightforward, wants all his students to do well, doesn't do busy work.

One of the most chill professors I've ever had. I was a COVID student while taking his class, so everything was online. You can take the exams and quizzes twice which is super nice. Just do the learning activities and you'll definitely get an A.
He's way chill. Just go to class because there are quizzes in class. Tests are online

Taking BIO 100 from Professor Kummer is the best thing you can do for yourself. Professor Kummer has really helped to make science understandable and manageable for me. Tests are open notes, online, and taken twice. The quizzes are also taken twice, once alone, once with the classmates. The final is open notes!

Professor Kummer is SO great! He made BIO 100 a breeze! The tests are open-notes, the quizzes are done in class with two trys and you get to work with a neighbor, and not a ton of homework. He is super helpful, gives extra credit opportunities, and is super chill! LOVED this class! I would definitely take it again!!!
Whatever you do, take Bio 100 from Professor Kummer!!!

Amazing Teacher. Lets you take midterms twice with open note and averages them both. Attendance is mandatory since you go over all the material in class, but if you miss just get the notes from someone. He seriously is the best teacher and he teaches so simply and the assignments are lowkey really easy. He answers emails quickly. Take his class!!

I signed up for Dr. Kummer's evening bio 130 course without any idea what to expect. Turned out being the greatest decision I could've made. We had a small class which ment he was able to help us more individually. Never read the text book. Open book/note exams with test corrections. He really wants you to succeed and understand the content.
Easily one of the best professors I have had at BYU-- very kind and a subject matter expert. His expectations were clear and he was consistent and fare.

Professor Reeder is a great professor! He taught extremely well over the summer semester. He keeps his lectures quick and easy to understand. I had a friend get married over the semester and he worked with them to stay caught up when they missed a week. Take Professor Reeder!

I took him instead of having to take american heritage and he was pretty good. The class workload is manageable and is pretty nice. You just need to read a lot of material, but overall a fun and good class. He was a fun nice guy as well.

Professor Reeder is such an amazing guy! His lectures are so full of amazing content and if you take notes and really participate, you'll do great! The content quizzes in the second term are super easy if you just read the readings and go to class. The 3 papers that are required in the class are very fairly graded and are not hard if you study.

I have taken Dr Reeder three times and that's no mistake: he is an amazing teacher. He has a level-headed and optimistic grasp on history, is willing to discuss just about any question, and always give clear expectations for assignments. I can't recommend Dr Reeder more highly.

Professor Reeder is an excellent professor! His enthusiasm made every lecture engaging, even on topics I don't usually enjoy. He's also genuinely funny and incredibly supportive of his students. He's always available to help, willing to work with you, and very understanding of mental health and family issues.Tests are pretty easy if you go to class

Amazing teacher, great guy, really enjoyed taking his class and going to his lectures. Be prepared to take reading quizzes, but they are usually announced in advance and aren't too difficult. Stay on top of the papers, (3 total), they come up quickly but they aren't that bad. He's very clear about what is important to know for tests.

He is a really amazing professor! His lectures are super interesting and he is always willing to work with you to improve your grade! He grades tough on papers but if you work hard you can get a good grade on them. There aren't many assignments which is nice but at the same time it makes it so every assignment counts so don't miss any!!

This was the worst teacher I have ever had. He only had two assignments before mid-November that were barely worth anything, and most of the class grade came down to one midterm and one final paper. He was a terrible grader and when I asked him questions about a writing assignment, he would say it looked like an A and then give it a worse grade.

Toughest class I've taken and the only class I didn't get an A in but that's not a reflection of the professor. He's caring and very nice. You'll learn a lot from the class. Take it for the learning experience, especially if you plan to go to law school

Boy he sure likes James Madison. Heavy reading, but all super interesting. Lectures were pretty engaging. We spent most of the class focusing on 18th century constitutionalism, which makes sense given his research expertise. Just be ready for that and for the lectures to be perpetually behind the schedule in the syllabus.

Pro. Reeder is a good guy and I learned a lot from his lectures. The class is lecture-heavy and near the end of the semester, you need to read about 100 pages a week to answer 5 content quizzes.  He's also a strict essay grader. No one scores 100. However, it's perfectly possible to pass his class.

I actually really enjoyed his class. His class was engaging and I enjoyed the topics. My problem is that the way he graded his assignments seemed to change in the middle of the semester and his standards just changed without any warning, so my grade dropped because the instructions became unclear. The same thing happened to my friend.
DO NOT TAKE!  I took in place of the American hettirage credit and I should have just taken that.

Good professor, but lectures could get boring. There were 2 primary analysis papers and 1 final paper instead of a final exam. There were content quizzes that weren't too difficult over the readings after the first midterm. There were many easy chances for extra credit that give extra points to later assignments.

One of my favorite professors this last semester. He gave great lectures and was really good with responding to emails. If you keep up with the readings and attend lectures you'll be just fine. I definitely recommend studying with group for the tests and talking to TA's, it's a huge help. I would definitely take this professor again.
A lot of work and reading for a class that shouldn't be that hard.

Dr. Reeder is awesome! He cares about his students and takes time to get to know their names and faces. He is willing to help with your essays and is considerate with reading quizzes. There is weekly reading, but it never gets unmanageable. Overall, Dr. Reeder's real one.

Reeder is a fantastic lecturer. He prepared students for the exams made the reading relevant, etc. That said I'm a straight A, 4.0 student. I was doing well in this class but missed a class activity for a university excused dance performance. After that, my grades tanked, and he was really closed off when I would go to talk to him outside of class.

Attendance is not mandatory but is somewhat enforced by unannounced (no makeup) pop quizzes. Only had one midterm which was easy; we were practically given the exam beforehand by the study guide. Reeder is a fun guy and makes connections with the class easily. Only part that sucks is the amount of reading. Had to write three papers but were easy.

I love Dr. Reeder. He has a pretty balanced (perhaps leaning conservative) approach to U.S. History. It's a rigorous class (~100 pages of reading a week) but he makes the class super fun and is very clear on what he expects. He listens to student feedback and is willing to help you. If you do not mind the work load, I would recommend taking him.

Strives to help you understand what brought about historical events and understand why certain aspects of history thrive/survive over others. You do have the usual key terms, events, and people of history but you dig deeper to understand why history unfolded the way it did. He is willing to spend time on anything that will help the class succeed.

I loved 460 with Dr. Mitchell. Our class size was small, and we had a lot of fun! I can tell she really cares about what she is teaching and her PT background made this class is feel like an intro to PT school.

I took 440 and 460 from Prof Mitchell and she is amazing! There are times in class where it feels like she expects the students to know/ think more than she has taught us, but it just shows that she is eager to help us learn and apply the material. She goes over the outline and what to expect on the exams which is very helpful.

Professor Mitchell really cares about her students and is willing to meet outside of class to go over tests and explain difficult subjects. It can be hard at first to figure out the structure of the tests, but just focus on the labs and pay attention to her powerpoints and you'll do well. 80% of your grade is exams.

Professor Mitchell helps you know what is going to be on her exams, and a lot of what is on them lines up with the lab material, but her lecturing is very choppy and she gets hard to follow on complicated subjects. There are times it feels she doesn't really know what she's talking about, but other times she knows it all.

There is a lecture and lab portion. The only thing for graded as part of the lecture are the 5 tests. There are quizzes, assignments, and tests for the lab. This class is very test heavy and is a lot of memorization. The lab tests are simply recall and you must say the exact wording they are looking for. Just make sure you prepare for the tests.

This class was way more challenging than I had anticipated. There are only exams and a few lab assignments to earn points. At the end of the semester, we only had two days to learn 70+ slides of new material before taking the final. It felt like she ran out of time to teach us and then threw it on the exam anyways. Would take it from someone else.

Prof Mitchell is a great teacher, but if you don't come to class it is difficult to keep up. She did a great job explaining the bodily functions and HER test questions were more straight forward. However, there were 2 other professors teaching too, which made the tests harder.

Mitchell is one of my favorite professors I have had at BYU. She is super clear about what will be on the test, she is really funny and I thought class was pretty entertaining. Sometimes the way she explains things is a little confusing, but when that happens she encourages the class to work together to understand better.

Knows her stuff, but a terrible teacher. Horrible organization, not clear what is going to be on a test, and her "clarifications" are more confusing. Was combative with student questions and felt embarrassed when her inconsistencies were questioned. Easy class, so if you take it from her, just don't show up and you'll have a much better experience.

She is very straight forward as to what she will be testing on. If you attend the lectures you'll be fine. She wants you to get a good grade so if you have any questions or concerns she will be sure to help you figure it out!

She cares a lot but the lecture portion of the class was unorganized and caused confusion as to what exactly would be on the exams. Its hard to say how much of the disorganization had to do with the COVID situation. The exams were fair but I did better on the lab stuff than the lecture material. The class is doable but not my fav professor.

I don't usually leave reviews of professors, but I absolutely loved Dr. Mitchell and this class. You definitely have to put work into the class, but it's an upper level class and that's to be expected. Dr. Mitchell is amazing and genuinely cares about her students and their understanding. She also includes a lot of clinical applications

I LOVE Mitchell! She's been my favorite teacher by far at BYU. She has some mean ratings on here but she is so kind and caring to her students. I've never done a rating before but I am doing this one because I feel the need to offset these mean ones. She cares about the clinical application of things, not just memorizing pointless info.
Mitchell is awesome. She's really good at explaining difficult concepts, funny, and gets to know her students. One of my favorite classes at BYU.

Mitchell is an interesting, funny teacher who wants to make sure you do well. Showing up to class really helps because during lecture she clearly hints at what will be test material. She likes using scenarios that demonstrate clinical importance, which I thought was super interesting. Clinical applications are discussed in class so no need to worry

Dr. Mitchell is great! She is funny and engaging in class, and a very nice professor. She likes to incorporate the organ systems as a whole and test on application questions, but she is still very clear in class what she will test you on. If you understand anatomy well you will do great in her class!

Dr. Mitchell is great. She highlights the things of clinical importance. Her tests can be difficult, but certainly not tricky. Her lectures and reviews are designed to prepare you for her tests. An A is doable but you do need to put in some effort. I would definitely take her again

Mitchell is very straight forward. Attendance isn't mandatory, but you should go because she'll pretty much tell you exactly what's on the test. She is understanding and will work with you and your schedule. Grades mainly on tests.

She seemed alright at first,but then things got weird and halfway into the semester she called me into her office and said I was plagiarizing answers to questions from quizlet,which wasn't the case at all. I explained I was using answers from her class notes,but she didn't hear me out/care. This was the worst experience I ever had at BYU.

One of my favorite teachers at BYU.  She really cared about how I was doing and was so willing to be available for extra help.  I went to her office several times, and she always responded to emailed questions right away.  One time we were having a study group and I emailed her a question and she called me on my cell to discuss the material.
I loved this class.  She was a wonderful professor and was very clear!
Mitchell was a great teacher who really wanted to help her students learn. Despite being German, she is not cold at all. Favorite teacher so far, hands down.

I took 400 from Johnson, and 460 from Mitchell.  I honestly wish I had taken 460 from Johnson instead of Mitchell.  Johnson was clear and interesting, whereas Mitchell is very unclear, and even tricks herself on her quizzes and tests.  She and the class spent 20 mins arguing over a test question, which she later concluded was wrong.  Waste of time.

Didn't like her.  She didn't teach very well.  Just asked tons of questions before she taught the subject.  Has a stereotypical European personality and is a little cold.  Take it from Johnson.  He awesome!!

Coolest teacher in the WoRlD!!  I heard she has 345 facebook friends, wrestles bears, and walks on water.  Seriously, a very caring teacher who loves her work and cares for her students.  Everyone should take at least one class in their BYU career from Dr. Mitchell.  WahOoOoOoO!!!

I took both 400 and 460 from her and she was amazing. Not only was she funny but kept it clear and simple. For 460 she gives quizes that are easy if you study and she goes over everything you need to know before the exam. If you study then you'll get a good grade. Favorite teacher!
I really enjoyed Dr. Mitchell. Offers lots of extra credit and is willing to help in any way. Tests can be tricky- lots of memorization, but it's to be expected. Good class.

This should not be 0.5 credits. You do a presentation during class, attend 3 out-of-class events, have a counselor appointment then write about it. It was annoying and time consuming. The lectures made me want to fall asleep. They literally read information off the honors website and call it a "lecture." The assignment descriptions were confusing.

Prof Filimoeatu was absent a lot in Honors 110; the class was mostly taught by TAs. This class is a bog standard honors orientation and I found it a bit tedious. The best part of class was the honors activities-- don't miss the Halloween murder mystery. She seems really nice and the class served its purpose overall.

Honestly, this class could have been an email. It's not really anything against the teacher or honors program, I just think that this class is pointless. However, if you're wanting to join the honors program, and you have to take this class, then it really isn't the worst thing in the world and it is extremely easy.
Drop the honors program. This class gave me the time to perfect my Seterra skills. Not much else.

Vika didn't get much time to teach (only one class per week and many of those were taken up by class or guest presentations), but when she did it was fairly clear. Unfortunately, she never seemed very invested in the class, particularly because she had her TAs do all the communication and grading.

This class is basically a run-down of what to do in the honors program. Vika is nice and cares about her students, so I'm glad I took this class. However, the group assignments are really frustrating, and you have to fight to get your group to work. Make sure you pay attention to the event requirements because it is graded. It's an easy class.

Vika is really awesome! The class itself was a little boring, but it was interesting to learn about different options in the Honors program. You could also work on other assignments during class. Overall super chill and Vika is really easy to talk to. I would highly recommend taking HONRS 110 with HONRS 120.

She was awesome. Super caring and approachable. The class itself is SO BORING, and the group project was a little frustrating for me, but it's an easy A. Would highly recommend taking 110 and 120 concurrently!!!

She is so awesome! I found her to be a caring and respectful instructor, and she wanted us to succeed and have a good understanding and experience with the honors program. My only struggle with the class was working with our assigned groups, just because they were never available, and didn't care as much.
Chillest class in the world and you can work on other assignments during the lecture. Lectures are mainly just speakers sharing their projects or experiences.

The teacher was super kind and nice--definitely think the class could have been just for a term/half of the semester. Having a whole semester of this class was definitely a bit much and they were stretched thin of content (at least that's what it felt like)
She's a very nice person and a good teacher, but the class feels pointless. The group projects are hard to do because of the number of people that have to be involved in a very simple project.
She is a sweetheart and will help if you have any questions.

There were some group assignments but most of the group didn't have to do much of anything. It was fun to attend and get to know people, but you didn't really have to "learn." The expectations weren't totally clear on all the assignments, but you don't have to worry too much about them because will pass by doing the bare minimum anyways.
This class is super easy and the professor is great but the class is sooooo pointless and is a waste of time.
She is amazing and cares about us! This was such a happy, stress-free class.
Super simple class and is well organized. Although there were attendence quizzes, I only attended 2 lectures and could easily guess on them and get full credit.
Very easy class! Super informational about the Honors program! Had hardly any homework and caused me 0 stress

Vika is amazing! Super personable and kind, learned my name within the first week and always stops and says hello. The class itself is jokingly easy (Pass/Fail system), not meant to be a real grade but an intro to the Honors program.

This was a super easy pass/fail class that you have to take as an intro to the honors program. She teaches you what classes you will have to take, prepping to think about writing a thesis, all the honors program activities, etc. Basically just once a week learning information about what the honors program is like.

Vika is so sweet and does exactly what is needed for this class. My only complaint is with the course itself; it's not really necessary and shouldn't be required for those who are all-in the honors program, but it's a good overview for those who want to dip their toes in the water first.

If you are a living breathing human who can sit in a chair and answer a couple of weekly questions, you will pass. The assignments are easy but you do have to actually do them. Anyone could teach this stuff, but Vika is really nice and warns you when anything is due. Take HONRS120 at the same time to see what honors really like.
It was such an easy and chill class

This class is a pass/fail 0.5 credit class so it doesn't require almost anything, honestly you don't have to pay much attention to the lectures- just enough to get the answers to the attendance questions. Vika is really sweet though, and excited about the Honors Program. I loved her class!

This class is all about understanding the Honors program at BYU. It is a good introduction, and definitely made me want to continue with program for the next couple of years. It is super easy to get a pass for this class.

This class is a simple intro to the Honors program. You can find out if you really want to stay in the program and get to know a lot of people in the Honors faculty. I took this concurrently with 120, which I recommend, so you can get accepted immediately into the Honors program. Assignments are clear: follow the instructions and get 100!
Dr. Wilding is a great professor, but 311 is a cornucopia of random safety and environmental facts. Sometimes it's hard to know what's on the test.

Dr. Wilding has been my favorite teacher at BYU. He teaches super clearly and tests based on what you've been taught. He is absolutely fair about everything he does and does an excellent job of organizing an engineering class. He is a totally quality teacher, and I wish I could take more classes from him.

ChEn 311 was one of the most eye-opening classes I took at BYU. It gave me more work than I thought it should, but I also learned a lot. Dr. Wilding is such a good guy and definitely there to help you. He inspires you to be a great engineer.

The others are correct, in that lectures are rambly, monotonous, and mostly cover what's on the class review sheets, which are posted online. I am passing as a result of grit and Paul's Online Math Notes. Great guy, not a good lecturer. At least it's not much homework and you can take notes into the frequent exams. If he's your speed, have fun.

Dr. Soloviev is a great professor and I highly recommend taking his classes. It was difficult at times to understand because of his accent but I found that I was able to understand the material just fine. He's very accessible outside of class and holds test reviews if you want extra help. He also draws connections to applications of the material.
Vladimir Soloviev, more like Chadimir Soloviev

Dr. Soloviev is one of the most brilliant mathematicians I've met. While he didn't do as many example problems as I'd have liked in his lectures, I quite enjoyed the course structure (1 assignment per week, self-graded, tests every 3 weeks), and he is more than willing to accommodate students who reach out to him.

In class, he just lectures the whole time and he usually only does derivations with no actual examples. He kind of just rambles on and on, I think I fell asleep almost every class. However, he prints out summaries each day for class and review sheets for tests. He also let us take a page of notes into tests. Overall, he really cares and is helpful

A relatively dry lecturer, but explained the content well. Very smart guy, adds pretty interesting anecdotes about the history of what we are learning to put it in context. He prepares a lot of material for students in this class, which was helpful. He has summary sheets for every class, as well as for every midterm.

Dr. Soloviev is from the Ukraine, so sometimes his accent is hard to understand. The best part of his class is how organized it is; he prepares class summaries for each lecture that have exactly what you need for the homework and tests. It's a tough class, but not over-the-top. It's pretty reasonable.

I really enjoyed taking thermodynamics from Professor Soloviev and would definitely recommend him. He is extremely caring and knowledgeable. His accent can be difficult to understand, but it isn't too bad to get accustomed to it and honestly is extra incentive to closely pay attention lol

Pros: He wants us to succeed and understands the practical applications of math. He gives us useful cover sheets and the general equations rather than making us take time to derive the equations every time we want to solve a problem like the other class does. Cons: he is hard to understand sometimes, goes on tangents, and spends too long deriving.

He honestly really really cares about his students and if they learn the math! When you ask a question he will focus on you and answer it until you understand. If you ever want to talk to him outside of class he will take time for you and meet with you whenever works for you. Highly recommend!

Very hard class, but he teaches in a way that really boosts understanding. Always ready to answer questions. Can be hard to understand at times, but usually not bad. Makes lots of comparisons to the real world that actually relate to the material. The homework seems like a lot, but it helps prepare for the tests so much.

Dr. Solo is very smart.  His lectures are terrific because he presents very clearly and he adds exciting tangents -- mostly about European history that is related to the mathematicians  whose stuff we learn.  The class should be treated as a solid 4-credit class.  You'll want to put aside lots of time.

He's a really nice professor who is trying hard to make a Business Russian class interesting. The only problem is that, just like a Russian Business, the class is disorganized at times, some of the objectives aren't clear, and he essentially lets you grade yourself. The subject matter isn't super interesting, but it's ok. He is super friendly

He has thick accent, which you get over after a bit, but makes it hard. The class sometimes seems like a waste of time since he lectures from the notes available, and it's hard to tell the difference between what he taught any given day, and the day before that. He's very kind, and willing to help in office hours. Put in the work, & you'll do good.
Good proffesor!

I had a hard time learning from Solovjov. He does have a nice handout that summarizes the material, but lecture consists of him copying that handout on the blackboard. He rarely even turned around to talk to us.  Tests weren't too bad, but if you miss the ONE multiple choice question, the best grade you can get is a 66%.  Nice guy, hard class.

This class is obviously hard, but he is great at preparing you for the final. He has a strong accent so his lectures are hard to understand, but his tests, quizes, and handouts are all perfect preparation for the final. He also is very willing to help you outside of class. So yes it is difficult, but he also does a great job.

I don't think there could be a more clear presentation of Heat Transfer.  He hands out a summary sheet with all of the equations on it.  The test problems are exactly like the homework problems, and are open book! He fields questions, allows time to share experiences where the subject has been useful... the quizzes are group quizzes.  Very nice man

Dr. Solovjov is a heat transfer man.  Therefore, the differential equations were all applied to heat transfer.  I am not a heat transfer man, so I found this course difficult.      He is jovial and willing to help.  Quirky world traveller from Siberia.  I really like him as a professor.
Very hard to understand, doesn't teach well at all.

BYU is looking into ways that they can clone Dr. Guthrie and have him be the instructor for every class on campus. Course assignments, projects and tests are all clearly outlined and organized. Grades are received promptly, and he is an exceptional lecturer and teacher. Dr. Guthrie is hands down the best professor in the CE department.

Dr. Guthrie is an amazing teacher and getting an A is not hard & that jazz but what I wanted to say here is he is one of THE BEST MEN I have ever known. He is kind and helpful. I had a personal concrete project where I needed the help of an experienced engineer; he quickly helped me and followed up. You are gaining an amazing mentor and friend.

He is passionate about the subject and uses a variety of methods to demonstrate principles to the class. He cares about his students. The lab reports are difficult, but manageable. Homework isn't all that hard, but it is frequent. The tests were online and weren't too hard.
Great professor. knows what he is talking about. his labs are graded harshly but gives you an option to resubmit

Dr. Guthrie is awesome. He structures his class in a very organized way and grading criteria is very clear. He genuinely cares about his students and wants them to succeed. The labs each week are a little long but not too bad. He makes himself very available so make sure to take advantage of that. He always shares his testimony in class as well.
Professor Guthrie is a great professor however his assistant that he has grade assignments is terrible. She graded insanely harshly and would take off large amounts of points for small mistakes.
Great teacher. Really knows his stuff!
I took Dr. Guthrie's introductory concrete class last semester. It was well-run and informative, but not too interesting in my opinion.
Exceptional professor. He's hard but that's because he's good.

Dr. Guthrie expects a lot out of his students, but his expectations are not unreasonable. This isn't a class that you can just coast through. You're going to have to work but it is worth it!  I worked hardf and really enjoyed this class.

Give him another chance after 306 (305B). I hated 305 but LOVE his teaching style in all of his other classes.  He cares about his students a ton and will help you with outside- class issues as well.  Realize that 305 is the first really difficult class you take, so it is unfair to judge him on a teacher from it.

If you have reservations about Dr. Guthrie from 305B (306) please give him another chance.  I did not enjoy 305B, but wanted to learn more about pavement so I took this class and I learned a ton!  He clearly explains the material and the grading seemed a bit calmer than 305B.

Went into this class excited to learn about concrete, but came out of it unlearned and bitter.  Tests were extremely difficult and students can only do well if they know what to write down on the notecards he gives you before the test.  Labs were in groups, but graded very difficult as well.  Miserable experience, glad it's over.

The greatest professor I have ever had in my life. He is not easy, have high expectation and standard, but you learn a lot from him. He is always willing and trying to help beyond academic means. I am taking his CE 505 now, and the only reason that I am taking it is because he is teaching it.

His 305 class (2006) was ridiculous. The only CE class I received < B+. Tests were a collection of his best attempts at trying to trick us. Class avg. was < 65 on every test. The worst were the lab reports where 5 points were penalized for any gramatical errors, including commas! Class avg was < 70 for each lab. He loved Utah St. and TAMU, not BYU.

His 305 class is very time consuming the first couple of weeks but once you make it through that things are not too bad. He is a very good teacher and class is always worth going to. Homework and tests aren't too bad. The most difficult part of the class is the lab reports.
I did not find him very helpful. And he is making CE 305 class more difficult than it should be. The labs will take you to much time, and he will take off points for a coma.

interesting material but the lab reports are difficult.  They are very time consuming and the grader was nit picky.If you don't have things just right in your report or homework then your grade is horrible.  Plan on several hrs for reports, memos not that bad.Homework is simple for the most part.Pay attention to detail for the exams(T/F & matchin)

Wade is such a great professor! You did have to do a lot of reading throughout the term, but the questions that were assigned to each reading were very manageable. He is a very helpful professor and is willing to help you find answers to the things that you are interested in when it comes to course content.  The final at the end was handwritten.

Wade was really fun to learn from. You could always tell that he is passionate about performance studies. There is a lot of reading from the textbook and reading questions to make sure you have done it. The lectures in class clarified a lot of concepts and provided examples that were crucial on the tests. The midterm and final are online!

He tries to get most of the reading done in the beginning of the semester, but it's mostly easy from there.  Class was full of good discussions, and I loved the final performative project (not everyone needed to perform, but it was a fun option).

Wade really tries to get to know everyone throughout the class. He wants to make sure you are learning so make sure to just ask questions if needed, he won't mind at all. You can tell he's passionate about what he teaches. Just read what you need to and show up to class. The homework level varies; if you don't procrastinate, it's an easy class.

There is a lot of reading different Finnish texts, including some of the oldest ones like Kanteletar and Kalevala, but if you have read any scriptures in Finnish then they are a breeze. If you are extraordinarily fast, you could do the readings in 10 minutes. Reading all the different texts is pretty fun and my Finnish has definitely grown.  10/10

Wade was a fantastic prof. His classes were super interesting and relaxed. There was a bit of reading but as long as you turn in the assignment you get full points. The final was easy as long as you memorized a few names and years. He also has a god-tier English vocabulary and uses crazy academic words extemporaneously in discussion. 10/10

I had an A most of the semester until I did really bad on the final. The final was probably harder than my anatomy tests. HW for every class period, 3 papers (one in Finnish), a project, and a final. Don't take this class unless you want to get the Scandinavian studies minor. You'll have to work for your A (94%). Prof. H. is a good guy though

I really liked Prof. Hollingshaus, he had solid lectures and the review days were really fun. I feel like I understood the material and that I can use it in future classes. It was also nice because he related things to the real world, not just theatre. Overall I don't have much to say other than he is a solid professor and has a good class.

Easiest class I've ever taken. This course is intended for theatre related majors, but as a film major that didn't negatively impact my experience. Each week a staff member shares their personal journey in the arts and you submit 3 things you learned. The main grade is putting together a grad plan, which you might as well get credit for it.

Dr. Hollingshaus is very knowledgeable about many things. His lectures can be interesting, but they can be boring and drag on. In this class, he wants you to share "your experience" with the readings. He cares about how you feel about your grade and the class content. Still, he wants you to be creative and write good papers.

Dr. Hollingshaus really tries to engage with students. But he often comes off as condescending and pious in his literary interpretations. As far as a humanities professor goes, he is probably a solid choice though.

Homework is time-consuming and often not available until less than a day before it is due. It has to be a physical copy turned in at the beginning of class. Homework is based on the reading and the exams are based on science (NOT what you discussed in class) - memorize the study guide. Hollingshaus is so understanding and a great teacher, though.

Performance Studies is incredibly abstract, vague, and confusing but also very interesting and intriguing. Wade does the best with it that anyone can as he is published on the subject. He is, however, now been promoted to Head of the Theatre and Media Arts department so likely won't be teaching nearly as much anymore, so jump on any opportunities.
Great professor. Makes everything very clear and very interesting. Great class.

Wade is a great teacher! I, personally, find the 115 class to be extremely confusing at times but he and his TA are willing to work with you. The homework is fairly simple, the reading is a little extensive sometimes. Still a very fun class overall.

I took TMA 115 and Book of Mormon from Prof. H, and he is one of the best teachers around.  Does so well at making the material interesting and teachable, and keeps class entertaining.  DEFINITELY take his classes.

Professor H is soooo awesome!  He does his best to teach you the material and make sure you understand it.  The reading can be a little dry but it's always short, and his tests are taken at home.  I loved this class, it was so interesting and I looked forward to going to class each day.

Dr. Hollingshaus gives lots of reading and writing assignments but he grades fairly easy. I really enjoyed the class although it did require a lot of time outside of class. That being said, I finished the class with a very high A. If you do the work, you will get a good grade.
This professor is really flexible and great. The class isnt too hard because they're all done on learning suite. Homework isnt too time consuming but you have to do a lot of reading.

I have had Wade for 3 classes.  Always willing to work with students and he cares about how everyone is doing.  He also realizes that the world does not revolve around his class and is willing to work with his students.  Wonderful professor!

Great professor, great guy.  Not so great of a class. This is not the easiest Civ credit out there. TONS of reading and assignments to go with every one, so if you miss one it makes a big difference in your grade. But if you're more dedicated than me, you'll be fine. Wade is a great professor-super knowledgeable, funny, and cares about the students

He's insightful, fun, and gets the entire class involved in deep discussions about subject material. Shows awesome clips in class of things that pertain to theatre and its historical background. He's one of my favorite professors by far-- and he knows me by name which is also awesome.

Incredible. I took the class because I thought it'd be an easy civ. credit. It wasn't easy but I learned a ton, and Prof. Hollingshaus is incredible. Great sense of humor, totally understanding if you have crazy circumstances and can't turn things in. Learns the names of like 100 students. I'm very impressed.
No Comments

I like Dr. Paxton as a teacher, but 113 is the worst class ever. He grades lab reports very harshly (or rather, his AI does) and will not give you any points back. Make sure to pick a good TA cause they help you with experiments and grade your notebook. The midterm and final had us simply memorizing stuff from experiments, which I did not expect.

Paxton is a nice guy (who doesn't answer his emails), but the class is poorly structured. Labs are fun, but reports are graded very harshly and Paxton doesn't answer clearly when you ask for help/explanations. The midterm is manageable, but the final is extremely difficult. Overall, a lot of work for little credits and grades don't reflect effort.

Chem 113 with Dr. Paxton was really hard. The lab reports are such a huge part of your grade and so harshly graded that doing bad on a few (which is inevitable) is really hard to come back from. Be prepared to spend lots of time on this class, more than a 2 credit class should be. He's okay, not super accessible or helpful but a nice guy.

TAKE IT FROM PAX! Some labs aren't going to be as fun, but I only disliked 1 lab out of 15. Lab reports are hard if you don't know what you're doing, so pay attention to 112 and lectures. Do the reading / hw before so you know what you're doing. Midterm is on Experiments 1-10 and Final is on 11-15. If you love hands-on work, you'll love this class.

Dr. Paxton is awesome! He cares about his students and knows his stuff. He gets tripped up in little mistakes when he's doing stuff in front of 100 people but if you go to his office hours when something doesn't make sense you will be in the clear. This class is math heavy, and there was maybe 1 thing on his exams that I hadn't seen before going in

Chemistry is such a hard subject, and he taught it in a way that made the most enjoyable it could be. He would know his students by name who participated a lot, played music before class, and had accessible office hours to find him for questions. The practice exams were key for succeeding on exams and PRACTICE EVERY DAY. Read the syllabus :).

Dr. Paxton is a really funny guy, and he really does try to be a great professor. This class is just so hard,
tests are very hard, does give practice exams that are similar enough to the real deal.
He is a very good professor, but his tests are really hard. If you study and do the practice tests, you will do fine. I loved the content and Professor Paxton explains tough concepts really well.

Dr. Paxton is very kind and wants you to succeed! This class will take a lot of effort- the tests and quizzes take lots of preparation. Although it's a tough class, Dr. Paxton makes up for it with exciting lectures and plenty of goofy dad-jokes.

I loved this class. Dr. Paxton is super fun and very helpful. You won't really know your grade until it comes out after the term. The midterm and final are hard, don't underestimate the value of simply memorizing the procedure. You have to ask him specific questions, general ones won't get the answer you want but he is helpful if you are specific.

Dr. Paxton is the best Chem 106 professor at BYU. He teaches hard concepts as best as they can be taught. His practice exams are previous exams so if you know how to do those you'll likely be good on the final. Most of all, he is helpful when you are struggling.

I hated this class .He wasted lab time daily with unhelpful lectures and never answered questions well, even if answers hugely impacted grades (rambled about "the beauty of science"). As much as I agree, being graded on nearly only accuracy and precision with no grace given for mistakes, this made class frustrating. Grades don't reflect effort.

Lab class. Very difficult class and a very hard A. It was his first time teaching 113 and It showed because he wasn't able to answer a lot of questions but he was a very good lecturer and I learned a lot in his lectures. The labs were very difficult and the class is very hard to get an A without a curve they implement at the end of the semester.
I always loved Dr. Paxton's lectures, but I felt like he could have done a lot better in preparing us for his exams.

Overall this class is incredibly hard, and he clearly knows his stuff. But, I don't feel like he completely taught everything that showed up on the tests. In general, most things were gone over, but many of the short answer questions were not.

Chem 106 is difficult no matter who teaches it. Dr. Paxton is your best shot at an A. Out of the four midterms, I got a 78, 82, 84, and 87. And then I got a 94 on the final and finished with an A- in the class. Midterms are difficult but manageable. He works hard to make sure you understand the concepts and also shows an effort to learn your name.

Dr Paxton is amazing. He is super helpful and super caring. I had a horrible grade for the first half of the semester and I started going to his office hours and he was so helpful. He is so good at remembering everyone's names and making sure that you are being as successful as possible. Make sure you do the practice tests and just memorize them.

Dr. Paxton is easily the best professor for CHEM 106. He's great at making difficult topics easier to understand. Sadly, 50 minutes of lecture isn't enough to cover everything you need to know, so go to his office hours and TA lab. Do practice, practice, practice and ask as many questions as you can. His practice tests are also awesome!!!

Professor Paxton is an okay professor, but with the large class size, it was hard for him to manage. People constantly talked over him in lectures, and his lectures were unclear about what we needed to know. Four midterm exams and one comprehensive final, which make up most of your grade. They make this class hard to weed out pre-meds.

I loved Dr. Paxton's class, despite having dreaded doing CHEM106 after having taken CHEM105. He had great lectures. Not doing homework definitely brought my grade down, so do it! The tests could be hard (+ not curved), but practice tests are very helpful + similar to the tests. Recitation quizzes are important. Overall great prof for a hard class.

Dr. Paxton was unable to effectively communicate the material. His lectures were often unclear, and lacked the depth needed to grasp the concepts. I found myself struggling to keep up, and had to do most of my learning outside of class through various resources. Despite my efforts to reach out for additional help, I was met with indifference.
A great professor for a super hard class. He is there for the students

I found Dr. Paxton's lectures so helpful! He simplifies complicated concepts and effectively builds on ideas to help you understand the reason behind the equations. He is very generous with his grading and you get points on exams even for incorrect answers if you get some steps right. The homework and reading expectation was very reasonable.

Chem 106 is a difficult class, but Dr. Paxton is a good professor. He clearly cares about his students and is willing to answer questions after class, thru email, and in office hours. It's still a lot of work, but he tries his best to explain it well and make it interesting (experiments in lecture). Do the homework and DO THE PRACTICE TESTS.

It's difficult, but manageable. The readings are well spread out and there isn't an overwhelming amount of work. The topics can be difficult to understand, but lectures can help clear them up. This class is very math based, more than 105, but there are less topics to go over. Professor Paxton had a great energy and helped clarify every question.

Paxton is just the happiest guy ever. He clearly loves his job and his students a lot. He includes a quote at the start of every lecture, sometimes spiritual, sometimes not, but it's always inspirational. He explains things clearly and is always happy to help you. He also has the most awesome demonstrations. Such an awesome professor.

Really great guy! He genuinely wants students to understand, succeed in, and love chemistry. He would take time to answer everyone's questions in lecture. He was very accessible outside of class, and was very flexible when I had a concern pop up. I actually understood chem this semester and did well in the class-- I had an A up until the last exam.

Dr. Paxton is a really nice guy! Clearly loves chemistry and wants you to understand things. We tended to run out of time during lectures and got behind the homework schedule. If you don't have a strong chemistry background (like AP Chem) you might find this class difficult. The TAs are all awesome and the tests were pretty fair, just a hard class!

I struggle with chemistry a lot.  I have had to retake 111,105,107, and this was my third time retaking Chem106. Dr. Paxton was the first and only professor I had that seemed to understand that chemistry doesn't just click for everyone, he would go around asking students personally how he could help them understand, he was so genuine and helpful.

The GPA distribution for this class looks like a population pyramid for a developing country. My educational experience was also that of a developing country. Take from someone else, unless you like feeling unprepared for all your exams, no corrections/curves, and dispersed explanations in class. Worst class I've taken at BYU by a long shot.

Dr. Paxton's was a decent professor and taught well, but he never covered the concepts covered by the homework until the day it was due, which was problematic. I ended up teaching myself most of the material from the textbook in order to complete the homework. He also doesn't provide test curves or regrades which can make it difficult to get an A.

Paxton did a good job covering topics in lecture and preparing students for the homework. That being said, like other chem classes, extracurricular studying is a must-do in order to do well on tests. Paxton was a bit slow but consistent in responding to emails, and his office hours were very helpful. Extra credit opportunities were present/sparce.

Cool guy, but his TAs are better at teaching chemistry than he is. That being said, he's a solid choice. He drops a lot of low grades, including one midterm. The practice exams were extremely helpful for me. The final was pretty intense though, & was very different from the midterms. He's got a good sense of humor & does a devotional every class.
Just a very hard class and he didn't do the best at explaining. Good guy but a hard class. if you want a good grade work with the TAs.

Professor Paxton is one of the best chemistry teachers at BYU. His expectations are clear, and reasonable. His course is challenging, but he gives lots of resources for student success. If you put in the work, getting a good grade is completely possible. Also, don't get the textbook, you never use it. Otherwise, 10/10. Solid choice.

Dr. Paxton is one of the best lecturers in the Chemistry department. He is able to teach things clearly and is super helpful if you go to his office hours. His tests are very reasonable and fair and the course load is what you should expect for a 3 credit chemistry class. I'm so glad that I took Chem 106 from Dr. Paxton, I highly recommend him!!!!

If you want to spend the whole semester teaching yourself through YouTube, this prof is for you! He would often admit that he had explained a topic wrong. I felt unprepared for the exams and hardly understood the topics that were covered. The homeworks and practice exams dont match with what he tests about.

If you are at BYU for chemistry AND your dad is not a chemist, apply somewhere else. This class is literally a speed run, and I feel that the chemistry professors do not care about teaching quality.
