This class is terrible, the TA's were useless. BUT! Kimball is  the best American Heritage professor. I actually enjoyed lectures, he was interesting and hilarious. He is a good guy who is really pretty funny.

Professor Kimball keeps the class interesting and ties in some jokes here an there. By talking to other students, I've found that he has less reading assignments than other ahtg professors. You still learn a ton, and the tests are hard. I still would recommend him over the other professors because you learn so much but don't have quite as much hw.

American Heritage is going to be hard no matter who you take it from.  That said, Kimball is a great professor, and his lectures are genuinely interesting.  The only points in the class come from weekly quizzes, a couple essays, and the tests.  Not easy to get an A in.
He's a good teacher and nice, but the class is pretty hard. Easier compared to the other AHTG classes though. Go to the Review Room.

Loved going to class. I felt like the tests weren't what he said they'd be though. He said they would be mostly conceptual but I found that the second test had a lot of random facts that didn't seem important. Overall I liked the class and Dr. Kimball is awesome.

Not as difficult as everyone makes it out to be. I got an A in this class. to do well on those "impossible" tests just study your notes along side your book. Great lectures and really knows his stuff. The tests are relatively fair, but the final was difficult. Use the review room if you suck at history
Kimball is awesome! It is true that the material that you cover and read is not really what the tests are about. The class is brutal, but Kimball makes the lectures fun and entertaining.

Professor Kimball is hilarious and brilliant. He always made class interesting, but lectures are mandatory if you want to do well on the tests. Book reading is pretty much optional..but I found that it helps a lot with the quizzes. I loved Kimball though!

okay here's the deal. You will learn a lot of interesting stuff, stuff that will never be on your tests. I could never figure out how to study for this class. Quizzes are fine, just read. Essays are fine too. Tests are a totally different story. I still got a B, but how I did is still unknown. Buena Suerte my good fellow students.

Professor Kimball is really funny. His lectures are pretty interesting. There are quizzes every week in lab that aren't bad as long as you do the reading. There are three papers that are pretty easy. The tests are impossible, so study hard even though you probably wont do that good. Go to class, do well on the quizzes and papers, and you'll be fine

Dr. Kimball is a really good professor as long as you read the book.  Weekly quizzes in lab and 3 tests which are mostly lecture material.  A couple of papers that aren't too bad but otherwise, a pretty easy class!
This class is pretty simple. Read the book and it will all be well. I never used the review room (except to get papers looked at) and I did really well.

Dr. Kimball is a great teacher! He is interesting and engaging in his lectures. He does several object lessons in class that are really helpful. My advice: go to the American Heritage Review Room on a weekly basis! It is extremely helpful. Go to class and study. Test and quizzes challenge you but aren't impossible. Dr. Kimball is the best choice.
Prof. Kimball is a great lecturer. He has a unique sense of humor that is very fun. His tests are all MC and he teaches from the book. Go to TA lab and you'll be fine.

Powerpoints were not clear. He doesn't put enough details into his powerpoints and he doesn't post powerpoints online so dont miss class. Had to get help from TA's a LOT! Tests were INSANELY HARD! In my opinion the tests were unfair because he plays the "two answers are right, but one is better" game. To be honest, it's my least favorite class...

My favorite professor at BYU so far! Let me point out that I am a very average student, I'm not stupid, but no one would ever call me a genius. He was super clear to me and has fabulous video clips every lecture that really helped me get the point. As long as you go to any review your TA has and put in a decent amount of study time you'll be fine.
Amazing class.  His choice in books was excellent.  Tough tests, but I learned a ton!

Horrible class. If you can think logically, you won't like this class. Tests are ridiculously hard and questions are biased. When reviewing your test all the TAs will tell you, "You should infer that from the textbook." When you read through your textbook, it is nowhere close to what was on the test. Professor is VERY liberal and pushes his agenda
Great teacher, loved him.  Very articulate and was always available for the students.  The tests were really rough.

Kimball is a great teacher, although he is a little intimidating. American Heritage is not as bad as everyone says. Just make sure you listen, take good notes, study hard and read the text. The review room is very helpful. I got an A. Those who complain how hard it is are those who put off reading, don't listen or freak themselves out about tests.

My favorite professor of the semester! Dr. Kimball is really funny, and I found his lectures extremely helpful. I would (and do) tell anyone to take American Heritage from him if they can. He is hilarious, but class was still extremely productive. This class isn't easy, but if you study and keep up on the reading you'll do fine.

horrible...he tried too hard to be funny and failed completely...his teaching style might be relevant for some but it put me to sleep because we accomplished virtually nothing in class. DO NOT take from him. a good TA is pretty much the only hope you have of succeeding

The rumors are true; American Heritage is in no way an "easy" class. You must understand the concepts taught in class, but Professor Kimball teaches them in a way that students can understand. He uses object lessons, and he encourages questions. You must study outside of class to do good. Also, having a good TA can make all the difference.
Dr. Kimball is HILARIOUS!  I loved his class!  He's easy to follow and he makes class interesting :).

Ridiculous.  his lectures were weird, and sometimes a little offensive.  He wasted time trying to be funny and it was really hard comprehending anything that came out of his mouth.  his tests are stupid.  they are so hard.  I only learned from the review sessions.  i just did not think he was very good at teaching...

The lectures were entertaining.  He does a good job of keeping you interested.  The tests are impossible.  But I think you will find that with all the American Heritage classes.  I'd take it from him just so you can survive the lectures.

Dr. Kimball is awesome! He is so funny, and he makes sure to explain everything really well. I enjoyed his class a lot, even though the tests were hard. He makes sure to explain every concept thoroughly and he's very open to questions. Great class, I would definitely recommend him as a teacher.

Kimball's classes are interesting and fun to attend; he makes a lot of jokes. I do have a roommate that hates that, so if you're not into that, don't take him. He makes the information relatable with good examples and media clips. By the nature of the class, the tests are hard but if you take good notes from the book and lecture, you should be fine

It was a relief to have a teacher who was more moderate than conservative. The class was interesting overall. Kimball's lectures were funny. The TA lab was good, depending on your TA. The tests were hard and tricky though. Studying is mandatory.

I took almost every class Dr. Kimball teaches because he made everything interesting, applicable, and yes--enjoyable.  He does not give an easy A, but he does make striving for one as interesting and fun as possible.  He brings out the best in students, and we love him for it.
Class was interesting and he was a nice guy. Moderate politically which was refreshing. Tests were hard but the curve straightened out grades. I would recommend him.

Professor Kimball is very good. His jokes and media clips break up the monotony of lecture. He knows his history. The tests are not bad AS LONG AS YOU STUDY, but have a few subjective questions each. Some lame lazy people complain about the class and how hard it is but they don't study. Weekly quizzes come straight from the readings. Take Kimball.

Kimball is a great professor. He makes the class very interesting and enjoyable...take lots and lots of notes and pay attention, and you'll be good to go! You have to take the class, so take it from Kimball

Dr. Kimball has very interesting lectures and I felt that I learned a lot from the class.  However, his tests are ridiculously subjective. On most questions you have to think, "What does Dr. Kimball want me to think that he's thinking that I'm thinking that he's thinking?".  The verbiage on the tests will trip you up.

I never read the textbook, but attended all the labs and lectures. The quizzes at the labs are easy if you read the textbook. The tests are tricky and I love history, but when the answer choices go up to j that's a bit ridiculous. It's a GE.

This class is pretty difficult. Tests are incredibly hard, but they get a little easier throughout the semester. Grades are based on a curve,so your 58 on a test will probably end up being a B. Read before lecture, and take lots of notes on the lectures and you should be able to pull at least a B.

This is a tough class but not impossible. If you take notes and do all the reading you will be fine. The review room is also available, I didn't need it but it was there to help. Dr Kimball keeps his lectures upbeat, a lot of video clips keep it interesting. Not a real heavy work load just weekly reading and a couple essays. Tests are challenging.
this class is sooooo hard! if you think you're ready for the test, you're not. start studying way ahead of time and make sure to do the readings for the quiz,also a good TA can make a big difference!

Lecture is fun and you learn a lot.  But I'll be honest.  I am not a freshman, and I am on scholarship-I am not an idiot. But this course was the bane of my existence. I studied for hours and got 50% scores on tests...and that was above average. It's a 100 level class!  I think there is a problem with the course.  But the teacher and TAs are great!

I did not miss a single lecture all semester. Funny thing is I didn't learn a thing from him. All he did for his lectures was go through a PowerPoint during which there were a lot of awkward silences. Thinks he is pretty funny, but he's really not if you think about it. Tests are TOUGH with averages around 55-60%. Try someone else.

Bro Kimball is very entertaining and his lectures are interesting and clear. His tests are pretty difficult however...you MUST know the material thoroughly to do well on them. If you can handle a challenge, then Kimball's a good choice.
way hilarious. way smart. and sometimes even inspirint :)
He's very entertaining.  The tests suck and don't truly show your comprehensive understanding of the course but lectures were fun.
Kimball was an awesome professor. Just go to class and take good notes and study and you will do fine in his class.

excellent teacher. lectures were always interesting, tests were very fair. TA was helpful, but I think I would have just as fine with a crappy one. some people think this class is really hard. it's not. if you do the reading and take good notes in lecture, an A is very possible. previous experience with the material helps, ex. ap gov and ap econ

SUPER hard class, study time for tests run about 5 hours. No joke. He's pretty entertaining as a lecturer, but my TA graded really hard on the essays and the average test score was about a 60%. This class is insanely hard. Unrealistically so.

Dr. Kimball is the best professor I have had at BYU. His lectures are interesting, he tries to keep the readings interesting, and he encourages questions and discussion. He is extremely helpful if you go to his office. Sports history was different than I expected, but definitely worth it.

The lectures were fun, but the tests were ridiculous. If year after year students average a score of 60%, it is not a well-written test. Also, my TA was terrible. A good TA can make all the difference!

He is a very interesting teacher and is great to listen to for lecture. The textbook is necessary, especially when studying for tests but he gives you a study guide that really helps if you're willing to put in a little time.
mmm

The class was somewhat of a disappointment for me. Dr. Kimball is very funny, but the class left me unsatisfied in learning. The midterm and final were both 95% based on the textbook; class time was almost a waste. The chapters in the book are too long to read completely, so use a study group before tests. First midterm timed. No long papers.

good teacher, tries to lighten up the class. Plays the devil's advocate a little too much, leaving the impression that somehow socialism and communism are superior ideologies than liberty and capitalism.

Is Professor Kimball a commie? I swear the guy is out to convince his students that the USA isn't the greatest country in the world. This is BYU. We believe in God and Country. Not the propaganda of liberal profesors.
This was an interesting class. The writing assignments were graded a little strictly but that's what the class is for. The readings were great! Never a dull moment in class. Great discussions!

Very tough class, with very tough grading of writing, but that is what the class is about.  This class taken from any professor would easily have been very boring, but the readings that he chooses are very well written, and Professor Kimball is very entertaining. I went to talk to him several times and he was by far the most helpful professor.

Dr. Kimball is an amazing teacher!  He's a way funny guy and his classes are quite entertaining.  If you need to take 200, he's one of the best.  Not the easiest prof that I've ever had, but he definitely wants you to do well and does everything he can to help you.
I hate history but Kimball made this class one of the best experiences i've had at BYU!  I looked forward to every lecture and still apply what I learned in class.  Definitely worth taking!
The tests are hard, but I really always looked forward to coming to that class. He is very knowledgable and passionate about our history. I would definately recommend Dr. Kimball to anyone.

Hist 200 is a sucky class, but Kimball is great. I wouldn't take it from anyone else. He is really willing to help you in any way he can. He knows the class is hard, so he does his very best to help you survive and still get the skills you need. He is way funny and helps make the class less stressful.

Dr. Kimball rocks my world! I loved this class SO much. His lectures are totally interesting, entertaining, and inspiring. I could not wait for lecture every week. He makes you want to learn. I changed my major to history because of him. Take A Htg and take it from Dr. Kimball. Do the reading, take good notes, go to TA reviews, and you'll be fine.

American Heritage sucks, there is no doubt about it but since it's a GE there is no way out of it. However Prof. Kimball made it really enjoyable. His lectures were great, he's so funny and he kept me awake. The tests are hard, and really require a lot of work, it's also really helpful if you get a good TA. I feel like I learned a lot in his class

I enjoyed the class and the lectures.  Do your reading, go to your labs, set up study groups and you'll do fine.  Dr. Kimball is funny, spiritual, helpful, always willing to answer your questions, and able to make hard concepts easy to understand.  Take American Heritage from him and you'll be better off then others. It takes work, but this IS college after all.

The best lecturer I have had. Very funny; utilizes a lot of video clips to explain things; interesting material. I couldn't have hoped for better in professors. The key to getting a good grade in the class is simply being a good student; many do not do well because they are unprepared freshman. It will require effort!

Dr kimball is a smart guy but that is all. his tests ask alot of opinionated questions that dont make sense. his essays are knickpicked to have to include every little detail. im just glad i passed the class and will never have to take it again. i suggest taking the alternative to having to take american heritage with him

Prof. Kimball is a great lecturer! I loved going to class. Be prepared to take a lot of notes. The tests are hard- the multiple choice isn't too bad, but the essays and identification questions are killer. My TA was ok, the class was ok, but Professor Kimball and his lectures were great! I ended up with a B-. Not too bad.

If anyone watches Smallville and has a crush on Lex Luther, take Am. Heritage from Kimball! He not only looks very much like Lex, (especially at the distance which you'll be seeing him from) but he sounds a ton like him as he speaks too! He is way interesting and seems very smart. The tests were way hard, but I passed them, so they're doable.

Kimball was a fun guy. He made the class really interesting, but his tests are tricky. Multiple choice wasn't too bad, but the essays and ID questions require you to state every tiny little detail with exactness about every little thing or you get no points. Labs were ok, my TA wasn't the greatest. I'm pretty happy with my B.
Prof. Kimball is a great lecturer, but this class is very difficult. I always enjoyed the class, but the tests were extremly difficult.  Don't expect an A in this class.

Dr. Kimball was great. The lectures were interesting and worth attending. He is a funny and intelligent guy and is interested in your success. However, the class is difficult and the tests are hard. The final was pretty intense, but not impossible. This was a great class.

Dr. Kimball is funny and smart, and his lectures are very good.  However, American Heritage is just plain hard! The tests are difficult, but grades are on a curve.  Go to labs-it's easy points.  If you're going to take American Heritage I'd highly recommend Dr. Kimball.
Great teacher. Teaches well, funny, and makes class interesting. You do have to work though.
Professor Kimball was probably the best Professor I've had.  He is way awesome...hard class, but well worth it.
Dr. Kimball was as good as I would expect an American Heritage professor to be. The class wasn't amazing, but I really enjoyed it. I wouldn't see any reason to avoid Dr. Kimball in any way.

This a killer class!! The lectures are enjoyable and the labs are easy points, but the tests are tricky and hard! If you are going to take the class be ready for extremely hard tests! Dr. Kimball is a nice guy with a great sense of humor. He makes the lectures fun!

This class sucked.  The first two tests were pretty hard, but the final was ridiculously impossible.  My TA was horrible.  She didn't know how to teach if her life depended on it.  The lectures were ok, but overall... a horrible class.  I learned a lot though.  Don't take this class if you can help it.  Take Poly Sci or something else instead.

This was a great Class! The tests were hard, but luckly they are graded on a curve. Doctor Kimball is  a great teacher and really knows how to teach. Great class. However, if you get a bad TA, transfer to a different section as a bad TA can make the lab experience miserable.

Everybody has to take A Htg, so take it from Dr. Kimball.  Lectures are amazing!  But be warned, tests are hard.  Make sure you understand the concept behind the definitions.  Go to lecture, lab, and stay on top of the reading.  Make sure you understand the general concept of all his major points.

Captivating and inspiring lectures. It's all powerpoint with many movie clips to demonstrate his points. GREAT class...study, go to lab, read the book and you will do fine. His LECTURES are amazing and I found myself leaving inspired as a better, more loyal person! he is also REALLY HILARIOUS! Sold 12 doughnuts to a class of 800...that was funny!
Awesome, awesome professor.  Lectures were great and inspiring.  Very smart and funny. As with most classes, if you study you'll do well.

Dr.Kimball is awesome. i loved his lectures, very entertaining and interesting.i loved learning from him. the class is very reading intensiveand has 4-5 essays and service..study hard and you'll do ok.don't let the ta s scare you..good luck!
Awesome teacher, didn't think I would like this class but I did. Definitely need to study though, to do well.
Kimball is AMAZING!  If you need to take American Heritage... take it from no one else!  He makes the class enjoyable and entertaining, yet so insightful!
He is a really good teacher.  He cares that we all do well in the infamous American Heritage class.  I love going to lecture because of his witty comments and humor.  He knows his stuff.
Professor Kimball really makes boring stuff become interesting, and he relates it to our time with video clips and stuff, and i love that. funny guy too. great class
Professor Kimball makes history come alive, with his dry humor, insightful video clips, and interesting lectures. His class is now one of my favorites!

Prof. Kimball is such a great teacher. He makes the lectures so interesting. This class has been my favorite class, and I think a lot of it has to do with the way he teaches. The tests are hard, but just study a lot and you should be fine. My favorite class of all time!
I really enjoyed this class... he made is so personal and fun.. i would recommend him for any history class!

The subjuct is just a hard subject no matter what, yet Kimball does a good job in presenting the material and does cover everything that he puts on the test.  The class is hard, but kimball is a fair and good teacher.  His classes are very enjoyable, just be ready to study.

Kimball is one of my favorite teachers ever.He has a passion for what he does. I love the video clips he shows, because it really does help everyone understand better. And he is Hilarious!! I love his dry humor!! All of this makes him strikingly attractive, in a very Governmental Agent way (with the shaved head and dark rimmed glasses) Love him!!
Excelent teacher. He knows his topic and makes it interesting. You will have to work in his class, but it is well worth it.  I would highly recomend him for American Heritage or U.S. History

It's a shame that all of you people had to have Kimball for AHtg; large lectures and defined curriculum really are not his thing. I had him for a small history class on something he really loves and he's about the best you'll find at BYU or anywhere else, for that matter.
Awesome teacher. Very Funny and you learn a lot too.  You need to study, but nothing on the test is unexpected.

Killer tests. Amazing lectures!!! Fun teacher, makes history interesting. Mark Patterson was the BEST TA ever! I learned a lot from Prof. Kimball- but he'll be the first to admit its a very demanding class and should be a 400 level.

Great Professor. His lectures are great. The class is hard. The key is to take really good notes in class. I noticed that lectures were key. Also:study in groups. This is key.If you can get together in a small group and discuss the material, it makes it easier. This helped my roommate and I get A's.

The work for this class was ridiculous. He was not a very interesting teacher. He would often poke fun and tease the students. If I am in class, I am there to learn, not be bothered by a dumb teacher. He was definately not a great teacher. His tests were terrible. I do not recommend him at all!!!
Really hard class.  Kimball makes a boring subject kind of fun.  I learned a lot, studied at least 10 hours for each test, and only made a B.  This class is really hard.

He made the lectures fun and interesting so i never wanted to fall asleep. on the downside the test  were very hard i always felt like no matter how  hard i studied it never helped. i didn't think the book was any help at all, just kept you busy.

This class was ridiculous. The lectures were interesting but the busywork assigned was atrocious. The tests were more trivial and the grading procedures were unfair. Avoid this course and take the Econ Poly Sci option. The TA's are horrible for the course

Class was rewarding. It is a very hard class and really helps one dig deep into the Heritage of America. Proffesor Kimball's enthusiasm helps students get excited about the subject. The class is dang hard though no matter who you take it from.
Great lectures, but the tests are killer.  Lots of busy work in labs.
This was a very difficult class, but he made it a fun to take.

While the lectures were interesting and entertaining, I found the book to be poorly written and the tests to be abominably difficult, even after laborious and extensive study. There was a great deal of busywork.
Awesome teacher. He makes the lectures interesting and fun to go to. Great sense of humor.
He's funny and makes what would normally be a boring and stressful class interesting.
He's hot. He's sporty. He's leisurely. He's da bomb!
Good sense of humor, fair grader

Dr. Christensen was perfect for teaching this class on Taiwan as an expert in the field with extensive experience working in Taiwan and China in the State Dept., and also serving as the de facto U.S. ambassador to Taiwan. Super interesting lectures. Expectations for midterm and final are very clear (IDs, short essay). You pick your term paper.
Awesome class. He's very inspiring, and this class is an easy A. He's an easy grader, but if you put effort into assignments, you'll be fine. I would recommend it.
The class with Professor Duncan was really chilling. This class does not require attendance. If you put effort into the class assignments and final projects, you will get full points for the class.

Great professor, very caring, and assigns very little assignments.  Easy grader, and his classes are super inspirational and are all discussion based.  You'll learn a lot from his class, and you'll always want to attend even though attendance isn't mandatory.
Professor Duncan was an awesome professor he really know what he is teaching he is a really easy grader. He really cares about his students.

Professor Duncan is seriously the kindest man you will ever meet, although I technically never met him bc I took this class through zoom. The class is focused on your own personal spiritual growth rather than knowing random obscure things about the church which I LOVE
Professor Duncan was awesome! He cares about his students and gives amazing lectures that include class discussions!

He is the best religion professor that I have taken here at BYU. He made class enjoyable and really cares about all his students. If you have a chance to take his class do it! Only one assignment a week on a conference talk to share an insight. NO TESTS!!!

Professor Duncan is an incredible teacher and made Eternal Families enjoyable and engaging. He is very organized and upfront with assignments and wants everyone to get an A. I genuinely wanted to attend class because of how interactive it is and because of his thoughtful insights on various topics.

Do you need an easy religion class? Take REL C 200 from Brother Duncan! He is very kind and respectful, and there is basically no homework outside of class aside from one small project, some weekly readings, and a weekly quiz. Take this class!

Professor Duncan is the best! He's relaxed and makes the class easy and fun if you show up and listen. Assignments are all short and really easy, including super short final project. Professor Duncan knows the question to any random scenario you throw at him, and remains objective on controversial topics, which is refreshing in the SFL major.

Prof Duncan is truly an angel on this earth. Every class I am amazed at how kind and sweet he is!! He cares so much about his students and always wants to be the best teacher he can. I am super picky about professors and I LOVE this man. TAKE THIS CLASS!!!!

I LOVED this class! Professor Duncan is the most humble and kind guy ever, and he makes this class so easy, yet so engaging and inspiring! Weekly "quizzes" (just share your learning experiences in the class and at home), easy project, piece-of-cake exams, and he is such a light grader. This will be one of the best classes you will ever take.

Prof. Duncan is a sweetheart. He cares so much about our success as a student. There are no tests, just unit quizzes and a final presentation. He's a very light grader. Despite that you learn a lot. My knowledge of family laws increased significantly! Definitely worth your time to take.
Super easy class grading wise, just do the little bit of homework and the one project. I still learned a lot in his class, and I would definitely take it again.

By far one of the best classes I have taken at BYU. I learned so much about the family in the context of the law, and I loved going to class every day. Very few assignments, and they are fun and help you learn more about the course. I recommend this course to every SFL major I know and Brother Duncan is seriously amazing!

Come to class, learn about the law, email him a few sentences about what you learned (or questions you have), and that's it! Online midterm & final (a few questions, if you went to class it'll be super easy), and a 3 pg paper about a law you like/dislike/or would change. No homework. He's pretty funny and what you learn is interesting. worth it.

One of my favorite professors and classes. You're encouraged to ask questions. He will spend time making sure he answers it fully. If open-ended discussion annoys you I wouldn't recommend. Tests are open note and he goes over the study guide really well. There is also one Short paper, and reflection due each class. Easy and enjoyable.

I really enjoyed this class, but at the same time, it was incredibly difficult. Dr. Harrison's review days were lifesavers on quizzes and tests. It's important to get help when needed, this would have helped me get a higher grade. I loved this class, Dr. Harrison is a good choice, but make friends in the class and use the TAs, they will save you!

Lectures are a hit or miss tbh. I felt like he went into obscure details a lot, but when it came to relevant stuff that would show up on exams or HW, there was very little examples. I had to teach myself a lot outside of lectures to complete the HWs. However tests did feel very fair. You were allowed a note sheet on the exams and they felt doable.
Difficult to work with
Straightforward class. Just need to show up. Dr. Harrison's lecture on ethics was great.
Dr Harrison has clear expectations and well-prepared lectures. He cares about his students and went through a lot of effort to make things fair when the testing center messed up a test print job.
Fantastic professor that really cares about teaching well. He makes efforts to inspire and clearly outlines expectations in his class. There was a lot of homework.

LOVE dr. fails!!! he genuinely loves his students so much. he wrote the textbook so he basically teaches from memory which is so respectable tbh. sometimes things aren't clear during class, but if you ask him for clarification he is so helpful. 100% take this class from him!

Always left class astonished at what I had just sat through. His class model gives you 0% ability to use outside of class time to know what he wants you to know. Absurd tests. Realistically no way to memorize that and get A. Any questions? No.-Just continuous state of confusion. Accessible and "willing"? Yes. Not helpful at all. Not room enough akí

Dr. Fails is hardcore--he wants you to learn, and he doesn't give busywork. He's awesome, because he wants you to know the material! You're required to read and learn the material before you come to class so that class will just be review. Some classes were just reading the textbook. Tests are take home and every 2 weeks. Lots of work, learned much

Didn't learn anything. Lectures are trash, basically just reading the textbook. The textbook is subpar, he wrote it... the tests suck and he seems like he doesn't want anyone to get a good grade in the class. All of my friends were averaging 75% on the pruebas. You basically just have to rewrite the textbook verbatim for the pruebas. -10/10

This has been one of the hardest classes that I have taken at BYU, but it is so worth it. He is kind of a tough grader, but I thought all of his grades were fair. You could definitely tell that he really cared for each of the students. He was also really funny. I felt like the entire class got super close with him throughout the professor.

I got a lot more than I bargained for with this class. I didn't pay too much attention  so I found it to be pretty difficult. 7 take home tests and 100MC final, and so much reading. The prof literally wrote the book so he knows his stuff but he is looking for the exact phrasing used in his book. Not for your average Spanish major/minor

For the first 3/4 of the semester, he would just read from the book and "explain it" and they were the most boring lectures I've ever sat through. Granted, it was my own fault for not paying attention, but it's kinda hard to when there's no way to be involved when he just talks the whole time. Final was super hard and confusing even tho it was MC.

Horrible class. If you're looking for an interesting/helpful/manageable class stay away from this one. The textbook is very long and roundabout, the questions are trick questions with very specific answers that he is looking for. NOBODY IN THIS CLASS GOT AN A. The highest grade was an A-, the average for the final was a 61%. Take something else.

Professor Fails knows his stuff but is a mediocre teacher. It might be just because everything went online this semester, but all class was was reading from the textbook. The content is actually interesting, but he makes the class boring. There's lots of reading which is manageable, but I wish there was more actual practice of pronunciation.

The textbook takes 40 double-columned pages just to talk about 3 vowels. He expects you to read this much before every class. This is not an easy class to just finish up the language certificate. I don't know if this part is just because we're online or not, but there is no actual practice in improving your accent even though that's the final exam.

I'm extremely impressed by the quality of teaching and care of Profesor Fails. He is extremely knowledgable, his textbook is gold for anyone trying to perfect their spanish pronunciation, and he beleives in the students. He has a way of making sure things get understood and are clear for everyone, even the small questions. I would again.

Dr. Fails is one of my favorite professors of all time. He was such a patient teacher, and his extensive knowledge of the Spanish language is flawless. His exams were take home, and he promised a pizza party if everybody scored 100% on one of the daily quizzes. He's so inspiring, a former mission president, and overall a really awesome teacher.

AMAZING! Dr. Fails is "THE top professor in his field in the entire U.S., but he'll never tell you it". Take home tests (minus the final exam) but closed book (he immediately puts so much trust in you). Quick paced but won't move on until everyone is comfortable. Teaches the STUDENT, not just the lesson. Only points come from tests and attendance.

Dr. Fails is by far the BEST professor I have ever had. That's not to say that his class was a walk in the park, but he really cares about his students. He knows his stuff and he focuses on the learning experience of each individual. Even if the whole class understands something, he will stop everything to explain it to you. GREAT PROF.

He's a great teacher and really knows his stuff, but this is not a class for the casual Spanish minor like me. This is an intensive linguistics course, and I wish I had known that going in. So, if you're a Spanish major or are really into linguistics, take it. I felt so confused half the time. And the take-home tests are very tough.

If you are taking 326, he is THE BEST! Even all of the other Spanish professors will tell you that. He knows his stuff and you will learn a TON! If you want to improve your pronunciation, TAKE IF FROM HIM. Trust me. He will show you how to pronounce everything correctly and your accent improve drastically! You won't regret taking it from him.

BEST PROFESSOR EVER. I honestly cannot say enough good things about him. I have taken 2 classes from him, and would take more if he taught more. He cares about his students and will help in any way he can. Very accessible outside of class. Tests are easy if you'll just sit down make time for them. They are take home tests, but require several hours

Dr. Fails really knows his stuff but the class was rough. Top advice: take notes on EVERYTHING he says (pictures of the diagrams on the board helped a lot). Create a GoogleDoc to study as a class and write out the answers in advance for the test. He is really good about helping students outside of class if needed. Practice phonetic transcriptions!

BEST PROFESSOR i have EVER had at BYU. He wrote the textbook for the course, but doesn't rub in how smart he is. Whenever we didn't understand, he stopped instructing, walked over and helped you 1 on 1 until you felt comfortable. He wouldnt move on until you got it. Take home tests, allowed to look up and memorize test answers before taking tests

All of the class material is from the textbook that he wrote. There were 5 take home exams and 1 final. Straightforward, but you cover a significant amount of material and it's a pretty in-depth treatment of phonetics and phonology. Not an 'easy' class, but definitely not impossible.

Dr. Fails is great! This was my second class from him, and I have enjoyed it both times. If you do the work, you will get the grade. Tests are simple if you study for them and your class does the reading. He is very helpful during office hours and is patient. There is a lot of information in the class, but it is definitely doable. Great professor!

Dr. Fails is one of the smartest people I know. He has an answer for EVERYTHING! Much of class was used to answer students'  questions. He is a great and inspirational teacher. The class is not super easy though. There is a lot of homework, and his tests are difficult.
He is a really good teacher. He knows what he is talking about and is fairly good at transmitting information. His class is not the easiest but you do learn a ton.

This was my first and last Spanish Class. The entire semester was spent learning sentence diagramming that had nothing to do with the final. I still wonder why.... Verb Quizzes every day. Book work every time. Tests are open book but not easy. He really does care and will take time to help you after class.

Fails is a great teacher and you'll learn a ton in his class if you put the effort in. He is really easy going and knows his stuff and is always willing to explain something and help the students out. Just be ready to do the homework, which takes some time, but the tests were take home and open book. I learned a ton, and enjoyed class overall.

Professor Fails is a great professor. You learn A LOT about Spanish whether you served a mission or not. He explains things very clearly and grades on a slight curve usually. He loves his students and he's extremely personal. He'll know your name within the first few weeks usually.

Brother Fails is awesome! His Spanish is impeccable and he knows his stuff. He respects and loves each student and no question is dumb. He's great for one on one help and will take all the time you need in class. There is a lot of homework but if you keep up it's doable. He is a spectacular teacher. Also, attendance is necessary.

Make sure you do the readings! Dr. Fails is extremely knowledgeable and gives great in-class lectures, but he expects students to have prepared for class by reading the material first. You learn a lot of material, which makes tests hard, but they're take home tests and if you study like he asks you to you'll do fine.

If you are going to be a spanish major, then he will really help. But his class isn't easy, with lots of rough reading and homework assignments. There is a quiz every day. The tests are open book, which is really nice. Nice guy, but I felt like his way of explaining things didn't really connect well to me. (Lots of sentence diagraming, etc.)

Dr. Fails is extremely smart. he knows so much about spanish, it is amazing. unfortunately he hardly spent time in class teaching us. He expected us to teach ourselves and spent most of class on procedures. Class was very fun but tests were hard because he did not prepare us. he is great, but i would suggest another teacher. not an easy A
Great teacher, always willing to help. He teaches things very clearly and completely. He is a great teacher and he expects you to know the material. Awesome.

This Professor is incredible. I had a lot Spanish experience prior to taking him and yet he made the world of the Spanish language so new and enthralling. He knows his stuff and class is so interesting and entertaining that they are not to be missed. One of the best professors around

Dr. Fails is definitely one of the more difficult professors of SPAN 321, but he is also one of the best. It's hard, but you like going to class. I'd never thought a lecture about Spanish grammar could be so enthralling. If you want an easy 'A', don't do it--but if you want to like the class, take it with him. An A is possible, just requires work.

This is a hard class, we had 7 tests plus the final in the semester. However, I learned a lot about phonetics and pronunciation. I feel like the work you put into it is worth it. Just study, go to class, and you will be fine. I loved taking this class, it showed me another perspective on the Portuguese language.

Fails is a good professor.  Make sure to go into lectures with a defibrillator.  You could go into a coma during lecture.  Be prepared to memorize like nobody's business.  He'll prepare you really well for the tests, which are hard, but totally doable.

Great professor! He knows the course material well (he wrote one of our main text books) and he taught it in a way that managed to keep most of the class engaged (the entire class time was spent on lectures). The tests are very hard and cover a ton of material, but are very straightforward.

He's intense. You'll learn in his class but will have to study a lot for an A. Many  people think with the Spanish learned in the mission it would be an easy A, but there were native Spanish speakers who didn't even get an A. All tests besides the final are written so you have to know your stuff. He'll teach you a ton but expects you to know a ton

Professor fails is a great teacher! I always enjoyed attending his classes because he kept them exciting. The first test I took I didnt do well on because I tried to memorize the whole text book. His tests will be easy if you focus on memorizing the "cuadros" that he has through the chapters. I did that and aced the rest of my tests! Great class!
He wrote the manual for mine so he expects a lot, and that you write close to what he says on the tests. Very useful,learned a lot. Not an easy class

He is a great teacher but focused alot on the linguistics of Spanish.  I was very displeased with his form of grading and examinations.  The Final is a departamental multiple choice and was much easier than every one of his tests.  Which took place every two weeks

Great teacher, one of the best I have ever had, but he expects a lot!!! Very difficult, a lot of work out of the book, tests every 2 weeks, essays every 2 as well. Great if Spanish is your major, but not worth it otherwise.

Prof. Fails is NOT the teacher you should even consider taking unless you are majoring in Spanish. His class takes way, way, way more effort than the other professors classes. He is very prideful, and not very nice. You will learn more in his class, but it will cost you.

Took this class thinking it would be fun as a Port major.  First part of the semester was out of his packet. Then it was just him talking and taking tons of notes and probably once every 2 weeks was a written test that took forever. I recommend a googledoc and everyone write in their notes. A native brazilian was still confused with what he taught.

He's a great prof and explains things really well. I learned so much from him and he clarified those "MTC Spanish rules" which are false! His tests are all written tests except final exam. Verb conjugation quiz every class period. If you really want to learn something, take this class from him. If you want an easy A, go with a different prof.

Best professor I've ever had. Extremely clear and reasonable in his grading. Also, he is very helpful and always willing to help any student to understand. I would recommend this professor above all others. :)

I LOVED THIS CLASS! it was my favorite class to go to during the semester! Profe Fails has an answer for everything! he's a crack up! and explains things very well. If you pay attention in class and study the vocab its easy to get a good grade and to learn a lot. I highly recommend taking this class from him!
Sometimes I felt lost, but Prof. Fails is always willing to help and explain. Subject isn't super exciting, but I don't think there is anyone better to teach this class.
Competently taught phonetics with decent rigor.  A fair teacher with a clearly outlined course.  Willing to answer questions and knowledgable in his field.

Brother Fails was an awesome professor! He is extremely helpful and was able to explain concepts in a very comprehensible way. Simply go to class, read the text and do the work and you will actually learn the material.

Looking back now at the end of my college career, Dr. Fails is one of the absolute best professors I had at BYU.  He ignited a love for Spanish linguistics that I never thought I would have.  He is always willing to receive you in his office to answer your questions, he is funny, strict about keeping the honor code, and he loves his students

This class really requires a lot of preperation. There is a lot of homework assignments and projects due, something every week. The tests are not difficult, but they are long and cover lots and lots of information. He is a good teacher, but be advised that this is not a very hands-on class; mostly theory.

This class requires a bit of work, and I don't really care for the Ladefoge textbook he uses, but his lectures are interesting enough. I don't recommend taking it at 8:00 am b/c he starts every class with a quiz, and I came late pretty often. He provides study guise that cover all of the material you will need to know for the test.

I love the man, he's a clean-shaven Santa Claus, but this class was horrible! We had another faculty member sub one day, and everyone marvelled over how much we learned. Dr. Fails has a lot of Spanish in his head but has a hard time teaching it to students. Possible to do well in this class, yes, but actually learning something? Hmm.

I loved Dr. Fails. He was interesting, he taught clearly, and I felt like I got really interested in the subject because of him. He really knows his stuff. His tests are hard, but not too bad if you study. I highly recommend him. I had the 8:00 class, and I never once fell asleep.

This class is unbearably boring.  His system of handing in homework is complicated. You must hand in each assignment twice. His tests are very long and hard. Be prepared to write essays for his tests.

he does cover A LOT of info thru the semester.  but he knows his stuff.  he has always been very willing to help me and guide me in my studies.  he is a pretty low-key guy unless you get him talking about cougar or texas football.

I loved Fails. He was always willing to meet w/ me and answer my questions which I think is what saved me in the class. He's a GENIUS, and so sometimes he rambles about random things, but I seriously learned so much. Awesome professor.

Horrible experience, and I love phonetics.  Vague class examples/topics, and he can get quite snarky about people who are not on time -- I regularly skipped class rather than arrive late, which really tanked my grade (yeah, those "easy little quizzes"...).
If you're taking an 8:00, be prepared to sleep. Fails is a nice guy, but dull. The class is pretty easy if you keep on top of things.

Fails is a pretty good teacher, but it's the review sessions with the TA that save you. He gives a review guide for every test, and if you know that back to front, you'll do fine. Easy quizzes every day at the beginning of class, though, so if you have trouble being on time...probably not for you.

Prof Fails was entirely unnotable. I dropped the class cause I was bored with it (and it was too early:)). But you know what you are getting- its fairly predictable and Fails seems like a nice enough guy.

This class is so chill. Tests are open note and take home - I got 95-100% on all of them without studying at all. Homework is really light. There are quizzes you have to do during class, so you should go to class. I never minded going, Professor Jensen is so kind and always made little jokes which was funny and made class a more interesting.

Professor Jensen is a super nice guy, and you can tell that he knows what he's talking about. Sometimes the lectures can be hard to follow, but you get multiple attempts on pretty much everything, and the TA labs are really good.

I totally recommend Dr. Jensen!!!! Our tests were open-note and even open-lecture-slides. He helps you understand exactly what you need to know. And he's funny and will throw in jokes or spiritual thoughts.
Professor Jensen was good at explaining the concepts and always made sure to answer and explain any questions asked during or after lectures.
Professor Jensen is very nice and truly cares for his students. You get multiple attempts on every homework and even the tests. TAs are also very helpful and nice.

I learned hardly anything in this class. Lectures were confusing and anything I learned, I learned in the TA Lab. GO TO THE TA LAB, it'll save your grade. You get multiple attempts on almost everything, even the final, and exams are open note. However, that only really helps if you understand the content. Some of your lowest scores will be dropped.

I love Dr. Jensen! Even though it was a big class, I felt seen as a student-- he remembered my name! He is personable, deeply knowledgeable, and teaches in a clear, accessible way. His of real-world experience and stats jokes made this class fantastic! I was nervous for this general, but Dr. Jensen made it easy and enjoyable! 1000% recommend!

Dr. Jensen is super caring and respectful. His assignments have multiple tries and you only keep your highest score (4 tries per homework, 2 per exam). He also has some in-class analysis assignments that were fun and collaborative (you can work in a group or alone). His lectures were sometimes easy to zone out, but the class is pretty easy.

This class is like every other stats class, so there are not a ton of differences. This teacher, though, makes sure the class understands the topics before moving on to the next. He gave time in class to do the longer assignments and get help from the TAs. He is only an adjunct teacher, so he doesn't teach all the time.

Professor Jensen is very nice and willing to work with you if you reach out to him. He has awesome TA's and works a lot with them. If you pay attention in class, the assignments and tests are not overly hard. He allows multiple tries for homework and tests. I would completely take another course from him. Be willing to ask for help if you need it.

So many times I came to class, expecting a lesson, only to get stories and stories from Dr. Wilson's career. She is experienced, she is knowledgeable, but I fear her pride in her incredible career is inhibiting her from caring about the students and the profession as much as she may have used too.

Dr. Wilson is one of the best teachers I've ever had. My favorite class thus far. She has a bad rap as a tough teacher, but I have never had another professor who has shown so much genuine interest in me, as a student and a person. She gets an F from me as a teacher. I didn't feel she cares about her students as much as the program

I took two classes with Dr. Wilson.Her grading, seemingly fair on the syllabus, is arbitrary and uneven.She regularly creates a toxic environment.I left most classes either fuming or in tears.Her warnings of the "real world" didn't match the "real world" job I went to every day.My boss was supportive, encouraging, and understanding.Wilson was not.

The most important thing if you want to succeed in Dr. Wilson's class is to go to her office hours. She may not be very clear during class but you can almost guarantee a decent grade if you check it over with her first.

She will review all of your work before you turn in. Do it. Stay on top of your reading and study guides. Choose group mates carefully. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS DURING A TERM. There is simply too much work and you have to start projects before you have really learned how to do them. But, she is well-known in the field, you can learn a lot.
Tons of busy work. Ridiculous quizzes. In class, Dr. Wilson asks questions to the class with one answer pre-planned in her head, which makes class a big guessing game of what she's thinking.

For those of you who have to take PR because you are a comms minor (exact boat I'm in right now), DON'T TAKE THIS CLASS FROM HER. PR is the most useless part of the minor, IMO, so the amount of work required completes outweighs the benefits of doing well in this class

She is a really good teacher in the way that she makes you love PR. However, it is true that it is a quite hard class. Worth it? i think so, i learned too much with her. Talk to her about your assignments, she is really helpful! hard exams though.

Laurie Wilson is THE woman when it comes to PR. She is a master. BUT you WILL have to study your tail off for your precious A. And you WILL learn A TON. Advice: #1-do the reading. No, really. Stop mentally arguing with me because you will be sorry come pop quiz time. #2-choose your group campaign members like you would your eternal companion. Yes.

Dr. Wilson is the queen of PR. Her class was hard, but I don't regret taking it. (I got an A!) There are two major assignments, a group campaign and a case analysis.  I brought both to her the week before the due date, and she made corrections and I got a 100. By the time you're done with this class you WILL be ready for the program.

DO NOT take this class from her unless you are VERY serious about PR. This is a hard class and it is very demanding. This class must become a big part of your life. Dr. Wilson doesn't mess around and she is very blunt. Pop quizzes are her favorite thing. BUT she is very willing to meet with you one-on-one for extra help.
She is a nice lady, but she is VERY tough on grades. Dont let her know you want to go into anything other than PR! PR is her whole world. Be preapred for a rigourous semester.

This was one of the hardest classes that I've ever taken.  That being said though, Dr. Wilson is also more willing to meet with her students than I've ever seen in a professor.  She expects tons of perfect work, but is willing to help you get your assignments up to par.  She will always return e-mails and has an open door policy for meetings.

You will have to work to understand the concepts she teaches. Definitely not an easy A. However, she is a great teacher, she cares for her students and want them to learn, understand and think for themselves. If you have any question about assignments or anything visit her or email her, she is really helpful. Lots of extra credit opportunities!

Welcome to the real world! People who didn't do well in this class are just plain lazy. Yes, she requires a lot, but she is very helpful. If you take advantage of her offer to look over assignments before they're due, you'll get near perfect every time. A challenge for sure, but Dr. Wilson is more than fair, knowledgeable and helpful.

She really was hard, but I felt SO prepared to get into the major.  She has individual interest in every student.  Yes, she is not completely up-to-date with new media, but she will teach you the real foundation of PR so well that you will be prepared for the real world.  Excellent.

Professor Wilson is a consummate professional. She knows her stuff inside and out, but focuses on the essential elements of PR. She expects a lot, but you learn a ton. Those that are looking to coast (in 485 or 235) will not enjoy her. I had her for both. The students that whine about her are typically the lazy ones. Take her if you want to learn.

I was a rare I.S. taker of this course.  Prof. Wilson gave me great feedback throughout and saved my rear @ the end by grading things fast even though I didn't deserve it--and dis so of her own free will w/out my asking.  My few personal interactions with her have all been positive and I have the utmost respect for her.  Shove it, all ye who whine!
She is a good teacher and I enjoyed the class.  She comes off strict and hard, but is a cool lady.  Make sure you meet deadlines!

Smart but completely condescending & arrogant.   Doesn't have a clue about new media/social media. Awful.

Not my style! She is condescending and rude.  She spent more time crying about 'office politics' or talking about swine flu than she did teaching applicable material. She knows her stuff, but is arrogant. She wrote her own text book and requires you to basically memorize it. 485 is a capstone that should be a positive experience; however, listing to an out dated teacher is not the most educational experience. I would look for another teacher.

Professor Wilson is brilliant! She truly knows what she's talking about and is a captivating teacher. You have to try, but she really wants you to do well and offers to proofread assignments and gives extra credit. If you're going to take comms 235, take it from her.

Excellent professor. Knows her stuff and has years of work experience to prove it. She is a strong woman, sticking to her standards and giving a good work load, but you'll learn a ton from her. The best...ever. Stop looking for a handout and actually try and learn something.... sheesh people... you are all lazy.
She was a great teacher. I enjoyed the class and learned so much. She was willing to help me out whenever i had a question and is such a kind person. She really cares about how you do in the class.

She was definitely NOT my favorite teacher. I can't blame her for my poor grade, but her teaching style was incredibly difficult for me to follow and understand. She really expects you to memorize the textbook. You must do ALL of your reading, it is very extensive, and you MUST meet with her ouside of class to even have a hope of doing well.

There is work to be done but she's fair and super friendly. If you do each assignment a day or two early and take it in to her office (with an appointment) she'll mark up your assign and tell you exactly what to change. You will get nearly perfect on every assignment. Tests were reasonable. This class was my first A in four years at BYU

If you are really into have extremely hard tests, projects, and group evaluations...take this class! You are expected to basically memorize the text. She sits down throughout all lectures. She grades really hard for introduction class. It's not a enjoyable class whatsoever!

Very opinionated.. she's always right. She wrote part of your textbook hence she knows it Really really well. Its almost as though she expects you to know how public relations works Before taking the "intro to public relations" class. This class convinced me Not to got into PR.

Dr. Wilson knows her stuff. She's really intimidating at first and takes public relations seriously, so she expects you too as well. She's up front about what you have to do to get a good grade. Dr. Wilson is a great teacher. She knows what she is talking about from her own experience. If you read the text and pay attention in class, you will do just fine. SHE GETS AN F! HOOOOOOOORRIBLE!

The worst teacher I have ever had.  The biggest waste of time.  I don't think she knows where she is half the time.  If you want to take an 11 page final with 6 essay questions, 45 short answer and matching...then by all means take the class!!!!

So she basically takes easy material and complicates it because she is unorganized and forgets things real easily.  The mark of a good teacher is one who takes complicated material and teaches a student to understand it.  SHE DOES THE OPPOSITE!!!

Wow, I did get an A in this class, but I do NOT recommend it!  The material is interesting, but Dr. Wilson is a BAD professor.  Nice person, but BAD BAD BAAAAAAD teacher. OK, all of the people that said Dr. Wilson is a bad teacher need to grow up. She is amazing. Never before have I had a teacher who explains things as they are. oh my goodness. I could not have been more frustrated with this class. The lectures were pointless, she taught test material AFTER the test, and treated us like criminals, or at least ignorant, rude children. Do not take this class from Dr. Wilson.

If you are thinking of going into PR, take 235 from someone else.  If you are looking for PR as just a filler class, take it from someone else.  I lost all desire to go into PR because of this woman.  Completely uninspiring.  She requires you to read and remember every detail about the book.  It's nuts!

I loved Dr. Wilson! She is an expert in public relations and tries to share not only the information about the field but personal experiences. She cares for each student individually and is always ready to help if you are struggling with a concept. I would recommend taking this class from her.

Professor Wilson is wacky.  She started yelling at a student who was using a laptop because she thought she was surfing the internet.  She started calling her rude and embarrasing this poor girl...and it turned out she was only taking notes, not surfing the internet!  WEIRD PROFESSOR!

This professor does not enjoy her job and is rude and condescending to students. It's unfortunate that she chose to go into teaching.  She teaches an introductory class and tries to make you hate the subject.  Avoid this teacher.  One of the worst profs I've ever had.
DO NOT TAKE CLASSES FROM HER! She does  not how to teach at all.
DON’T take classes from her. YOU WILL REGRET ABOUT IT. Do not waste your time. You will find yourself attending to a boring class, having a hard time with the class, and learning nothing.

Treats you like a 5 yr old-condescending to her students.  Will reduce your grade if your cell phone goes off.  She deducts from your grade if you're absent, yet she was absent for 2 weeks - for being sick!  Very unfair teacher...in every way

This professor is kind but an extremely tough grader. She expects near-perfection on every assignment with little room for error. I LOVE SISTER JAYNES! Experienced, gives great feedback, cares so much about her students. It's very easy to get an A if do what's asked (4 hours practice each week, playing assignments). So helpful learning to play for congregations!

She tries her best but is very unprofessional. I didn't understand how much work this one credit class would be when I signed up but it was very time-consuming. I was dissuaded from pursuing a music minor further after this class

Prof Jaynes is awesome! She's very passionate about what she teaches, and she knows her stuff really well. It gets a little heavy on homeworks, but once you get use to how the curse works it is pretty easy. Attendence is not mandatory so that is a plus to me.

It was okay. The topics are interesting, especially for medical fields, but expect a lot of work. The grading felt very skewed. I followed the rubric and gave my best effort every time. One project took four hours and I received a 10%, which felt more like a grade for not trying at all.

She had almost weekly zooms that were not required, but you were able to join which were super helpful. She was always more than willing to help students out, especially if their previous performance in the class showed that they worked hard. The only thing that tripped me up was that almost half of the final was just latin roots.

Professor Hernandez was a great professor and I learned a lot from the content! I would highly recommended taking it especially if you're a Spanish speaker who wants to go into the medical field. Easy A but entirely useless. You rush through every unit and are never tested on it. This is exactly what an online course should be in my opinion, the structure is clear and for the most part you can accomplish the tasks on your own time. Profe Hernández is attentive and helpful. She was very respectful as a teacher, but not involved in the class.  There was so much busy work to do and I feel like I learned very little.  The final was difficult to study for because she gave us very few resources and the material we were tested on felt random.

Professor Pena is the best for this class, she is a native Spanish speaker and studied medicine which makes he very knowledgeable and the best Spanish teacher! the online course was clear and easy to follow and get an A. She cared for the students and was willing to help when I reached for help.

She was detached from the class, with little involvement. She did not grade assignments which were needed to complete other assignments til the last day that they were due. I submitted a paper early and it took 4 weeks to get it graded. No help from the TA's and the exams are just the reading quiz questions

Professor Pena is the best Spanish instructor at BYU! Her online class is so interesting and organized. Very easy to navigate and understand. She is caring and responsive to your concerns. Don't hesitate on taking this class!

This class was great! Very informative and easy. The TA David was super great and patient. There are quite a few assignments, but they're not too time-consuming or difficult. Would definitely recommend!

This class is super helpful for learning medical terms! Ultimately, you get out what you put in, like most Spanish classes at BYU. As long as you stay up to date and communicate with the TAs, the class is super straight forward. Just make sure you read all of her announcements because she tells you exactly what to study for the upcoming tests.

Profesora Pena de Hernandez was pretty good. The class seemed to be geared more toward understanding the latino culture in a medical setting rather than medical terminology in Spanish, but you do get a little bit of that. Profe Hernandez is awesome! Her class is super well organized and you end up learning a lot if you put the work in. An A is not hard if you turn everything in on time and get all the weekly assignments done. The final is really straight forward and is super simple if you've payed attention all year.

This was a pretty easy class and you get out what you put into it! It was super doable to just skim the readings and do the online quizzes (I've taken a medical terminology class in english before). She is very accessible and willing to work with you on your grade! I would recommend, especially if you're going into the medical field!
I really enjoyed this class! Honestly one of my favorites. I was able to learn a lot.  She's super nice and cares about every student. I recommend this class 100%

At first, I couldn't understand my grade but quickly learned that if you pay attention to the instructions and follow them an A is obtainable. Amazing class!

Professor Hernandez is very good at communicating with students who genuinely want to earn a good grade in the course. She made me love the Spanish language even more. If you set out to succeed in her class with personal motivation, you will do well, and you will enjoy it. It's pretty easy too. I would recommend taking it from her.

I liked this professor a lot! Her online class is very well organized and is very easy and not too time consuming. Very easy A if you are self-motivated to get stuff done.

This class is full of busy work that takes a lot of time but doesn't develop your language skills. There are a lot of group discussions. This class is a waste to anyone actually hoping to learn. Online class is disorganized, and material is never tested (until the final, which is easy). Pretty easy to blow through the whole week's assignments in a few hours and then forget about it all. All that being said, it is an easy A.

Honestly I didn't learn anything from this class. You rush through a lot of material that you are never tested on, and the class just feels very disorganized. I love her! she takes her of her students and cares about what she is teaching!, I would totally her class again. mandatory attendance and fast to reply students emails.i learned a lot in her class

Dr. Hovanski is solid. This was his first time teaching MFGEN 130. I just didn't love his teaching style. Everything is open book and open note, so you're chilling. Dr. Hovanski is awesome! He is very organized and had tons of wisdom bits he'd drop on us all the time. He did cancel a bunch of lectures this semester, guess he got busy. The homework and quizzes are not difficult. The labs sometimes could be, but the TAs were great.

Dr Hovanski is probably my favorite professor in the manufacturing engineering department. He is an awesome professor. His class can be a bit tough (mostly the latter half), but it is a rewarding challenge. Professor Glassett is one of the most kind, understanding professors I have ever had. He will help if you have questions, responds to emails, and truly cares for his students. Profe Glassett is awesome. This was one of the best Spanish classes I've ever taken! He is really good at explaining Spanish concepts to English native speakers. He understands the student from the Spanish and the English side. There is an easy quiz almost everyday, but do not forget to study for it. I would definitely recommend this class!

Loved profe glassett, very reasonable, accepts late work, hilarious, loved coming to class. I never missed a class but he will work with you to do make up work. The difficult thing about the class is that there is a lot of quizzes and busy work, miss a lot and it'll hurt your grade.
Professor Glassett was always willing to help and offer support in anyway that he possibly could. He's funny too. Really sharp, and loves what he does.
So grateful I had Professor Fox! Made learning Python so fun. BYU Marriott could use more professors like him.
